AI.conclusion: By transforming affordance grounding from a purely output-constrained objective into attention-grounded spatial reasoning, SpatialAfford demonstrates that explicit attention alignment is a key enabler for compact VLMs to achieve competitive affordance grounding performance.

title: RadYOLO: Computationally Efficient 3D Object Detection and Segmentation in CT and MRI
summary:
Object detection and segmentation in three-dimensional medical images is a very active area of research. However, most proposed deep learning models carry a high computational cost, and only few aim to be broadly applicable, achieve high detection performance, and remain fast to execute on resource-constrained hardware. To address this gap, we present RadYOLO, a 3D extension of YOLO11 tailored to medical images. We compare it with nnU-Net and nnDetection on five datasets comprising CT and MRI data with varying object sizes and prevalence. RadYOLO's detection performance surpasses that of nnDetection on four of five datasets and is comparable on one. Compared to nnU-Net, RadYOLO performs better on lesion detection tasks, while nnU-Net excels at detecting large organs when precise localization is required. When rough object localization is sufficient, RadYOLO matches or outperforms nnU-Net on all five datasets. Regarding inference time, RadYOLO is 8-46x faster than nnU-Net on a GPU. Compared to nnDetection the speedup is even higher. When executed on a CPU, RadYOLO's inference runs within seconds (still faster than nnU-Net on a GPU) offering a significant advantage for clinical and edge-device deployment.
  RadYOLO repository: https://github.com/FraunhoferMEVIS/RadYOLO

AI.tldr: RadYOLO is a 3D extension of YOLO11 for medical image detection/segmentation that achieves competitive performance with nnU-Net and nnDetection while being 8-46x faster, making it suitable for resource-constrained clinical deployment.
AI.motivation: Most deep learning models for 3D medical image detection/segmentation have high computational costs. Few approaches achieve broad applicability, high detection performance, AND fast execution on resource-constrained hardware simultaneously, creating a gap this work addresses.
AI.method: RadYOLO extends YOLO11 to 3D for medical images. It is compared against nnU-Net and nnDetection on five datasets covering CT and MRI data with varying object sizes and prevalence.
AI.result: RadYOLO surpasses nnDetection on 4/5 datasets and matches on one. It beats nnU-Net on lesion detection tasks, while nnU-Net is better for large organs requiring precise localization. With rough localization, RadYOLO matches or outperforms nnU-Net on all datasets. RadYOLO is 8-46x faster than nnU-Net on GPU and even faster than nnDetection, with CPU inference in seconds (still faster than nnU-Net on GPU).
AI.conclusion: RadYOLO offers a practical trade-off between detection performance and computational efficiency, providing a significant advantage for clinical and edge-device deployment in 3D medical imaging.

title: Test-time Adaptation of Pelvic Bone Segmentation Models via Dynamic Reliability-Guided
comment: Provisionally accepted for presentation at MICCAI 2026
summary: Reliable pelvic bone segmentation (PBS) from CT is essential for robot-assisted pelvic trauma surgery, yet deploying a source-trained model to a new hospital suffers from severe performance degradation due to cross-center domain shifts. While test-time adaptation (TTA) enables online model adaptation without accessing source data, existing methods show limited effectiveness for PBS, facing challenges including boundary degradation, anatomical inconsistency under domain shifts, and voxel-level class imbalance. To address these challenges, we propose a novel closed-loop dynamic Reliability-Guided TTA framework (ReGA) for PBS. Specifically, we introduce a pseudo-label reliability criterion termed Segmentation Inference Consistency Evaluation (SICE), which jointly measures region overlap and boundary deviation via dropout-based ensemble predictions. Based on SICE, a trust-weighted refinement module adaptively updates features to mitigate boundary errors in pseudo-labels. Furthermore, a confidence-weighted region-level contrastive learning strategy is proposed to enforce anatomical consistency. Finally, ReGA follows the teacher-student (TS) scheme to alleviate voxel-level class imbalance. Experiments on three heterogeneous 3D pelvic CT datasets demonstrate that ReGA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art TTA methods, enabling effective adaptation of the source-trained PBS model to unseen clinical domains. The code is available at https://github.com/Ren-ling/ReGA.

AI.tldr: Proposes ReGA, a closed-loop reliability-guided test-time adaptation framework for pelvic bone segmentation in CT, addressing cross-center domain shifts via a novel pseudo-label reliability criterion (SICE), trust-weighted refinement, and confidence-weighted contrastive learning.
AI.motivation: Source-trained pelvic bone segmentation models suffer severe performance degradation when deployed to new hospitals due to cross-center domain shifts. Existing test-time adaptation (TTA) methods are limited for PBS due to boundary degradation, anatomical inconsistency, and voxel-level class imbalance.
AI.method: Introduces a Segmentation Inference Consistency Evaluation (SICE) criterion using dropout-based ensembles to jointly measure region overlap and boundary deviation. A trust-weighted refinement module adaptively updates features to reduce boundary errors, a confidence-weighted region-level contrastive learning strategy enforces anatomical consistency, and a teacher-student scheme alleviates voxel-level class imbalance.
AI.result: Experiments on three heterogeneous 3D pelvic CT datasets show ReGA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art TTA methods, enabling effective adaptation of source-trained PBS models to unseen clinical domains.
AI.conclusion: ReGA provides an effective closed-loop TTA framework for reliable pelvic bone segmentation under cross-center domain shift, with code publicly available.

title: GuideGround: VLM-guided Semantic Understanding and Viewpoint-aware Reasoning for 3D Visual Grounding
summary: 3D visual grounding aims to localize the target object in a 3D scene from a natural language query, requiring both fine-grained semantic understanding and viewpoint-dependent spatial reasoning. Existing methods typically formulate semantic understanding as an auxiliary closed-set object classification task and rely on multi-view feature aggregation for viewpoint reasoning, limiting semantic generalization and weakening viewpoint-specific evidence. We observe that vision-language models naturally provide complementary capabilities through open-vocabulary semantic understanding and global scene perception. Based on this insight, we propose GuideGround, a VLM-guided framework that complements rather than replaces task-specific grounding models by leveraging VLMs for semantic enhancement and viewpoint-specific hypothesis verification. Specifically, we replace auxiliary closed-set object classification with VLM-generated object semantic descriptions to enhance semantic understanding. Meanwhile, instead of directly aggregating multi-view representations, we preserve viewpoint-specific grounding hypotheses through per-view grounding and explicitly verify them using VLMs across candidate viewpoints. Extensive experiments on the ReferIt3D benchmark demonstrate that GuideGround consistently outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods. Comprehensive ablation studies further confirm the effectiveness of both the proposed semantic understanding and viewpoint reasoning strategies.

AI.tldr: GuideGround is a VLM-guided framework for 3D visual grounding that uses vision-language models to complement task-specific grounding models, replacing closed-set object classification with VLM-generated semantic descriptions and verifying viewpoint-specific grounding hypotheses across candidate viewpoints instead of directly aggregating multi-view features, achieving state-of-the-art results on ReferIt3D.
AI.motivation: Existing 3D visual grounding methods rely on closed-set object classification for semantic understanding and multi-view feature aggregation for viewpoint reasoning, which limits semantic generalization to open-vocabulary queries and weakens viewpoint-specific evidence.
AI.method: GuideGround leverages VLMs in two ways: (1) it replaces auxiliary closed-set object classification with VLM-generated object semantic descriptions to enhance semantic understanding, and (2) it preserves viewpoint-specific grounding hypotheses through per-view grounding and explicitly verifies them using VLMs across candidate viewpoints rather than directly aggregating multi-view representations.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on the ReferIt3D benchmark demonstrate that GuideGround consistently outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods. Ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of both the semantic understanding and viewpoint reasoning strategies.
AI.conclusion: VLM-guided frameworks that complement rather than replace task-specific grounding models can effectively improve both semantic understanding and viewpoint-dependent spatial reasoning in 3D visual grounding.

title: Unleashing the Power of Text: Text-Guided Flow Matching for Image Fusion under Complex Degradations
summary: Infrared-visible image fusion under realistic degradation scenarios is a challenging task, as degradations not only cause a loss of reliable modality-specific information in observed images but also hinder the fusion process. Recent studies indicate that text can provide prior information about degradation characteristics, complementing the limited evidence available from corrupted input images and facilitating fusion. However, existing methods typically inject fixed global text representations into visual features, making it difficult for textual guidance to adapt to spatially varying degradations, local structures, and thermal saliency. To this end, we propose TGFusion, a text-guided latent-space flow matching framework that unifies degradation suppression and cross-modal fusion. TGFusion encodes task, degradation, and generation cues into structured prompts. To fully exploit these priors, we design a Prompt-conditioned Multi-stream Joint Flow Transformer that represents text as an independent semantic stream alongside fusion, visible, and infrared streams. Joint attention enables token-level bidirectional interaction and layer-wise updating among semantic and visual representations, allowing degradation semantics to dynamically guide reliable information selection and fusion latent generation. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks and complex degradation scenarios demonstrate that TGFusion achieves superior or competitive performance in perceptual quality, image naturalness, structural-detail preservation, and infrared-saliency retention, while remaining robust across diverse single and compound degradations.

AI.tldr: TGFusion is a text-guided latent-space flow matching framework for infrared-visible image fusion under realistic degradation conditions, using structured text prompts and a Prompt-conditioned Multi-stream Joint Flow Transformer to enable dynamic, spatially-adaptive textual guidance for joint degradation suppression and cross-modal fusion.
AI.motivation: Real-world infrared-visible image fusion faces spatially varying degradations that obscure modality-specific information and hinder fusion. Existing text-guided fusion methods inject fixed global text representations into visual features, which cannot adapt to local degradation patterns, structures, or thermal saliency variations.
AI.method: TGFusion encodes task, degradation, and generation cues into structured prompts and employs a Prompt-conditioned Multi-stream Joint Flow Transformer that treats text as an independent semantic stream alongside fusion, visible, and infrared streams. Joint attention enables token-level bidirectional interaction and layer-wise updating between semantic and visual representations for dynamic guidance of reliable information selection and fusion latent generation.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on public benchmarks and complex degradation scenarios show TGFusion achieves superior or competitive performance in perceptual quality, image naturalness, structural-detail preservation, and infrared-saliency retention, with robustness across diverse single and compound degradations.
AI.conclusion: TGFusion demonstrates that spatially-adaptive, token-level text guidance in a flow matching framework effectively unifies degradation suppression and cross-modal fusion, outperforming existing methods in realistic degraded scenarios.

title: DocPO: Advancing Document Policy Optimization via Tailored Step-Aware Rewards
comment: 14 pages. Accepted to the 34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM Multimedia 2026). Yunhao Wang and Binghong Wu contributed equally
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) for document parsing often relies on reference-based rewards rooted in edit distance (e.g., tree edit distance), yet it remains hard to optimize in the high-accuracy regime because such rewards become weakly discriminative: near-correct outputs receive very similar scores, providing limited learning signal for hard cases. We propose Step-Aware Annealing (SAA), a plug-and-play reward sharpening mechanism that progressively increases reward curvature during training, amplifying subtle quality differences among high-scoring samples while preserving stability in early learning. Built on SAA, we introduce DocPO, a document policy optimization framework with element-specific, reference-based rewards anchored by edit-distance signals: normalized string edit distance (NED) for text, tree edit distance similarity (TEDS) for tables, and a hybrid Rubric+edit reward for formulas. Experiments on OmniDocBench and DocElemHard show that SAA consistently improves GRPO-style RL across document elements over non-annealed rewards, without requiring additional human supervision for reward construction.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes Step-Aware Annealing (SAA), a reward sharpening mechanism that progressively increases reward curvature during RL training for document parsing, and introduces DocPO, a document policy optimization framework with element-specific reference-based rewards (NED for text, TEDS for tables, Rubric+edit for formulas). Experiments show SAA consistently improves GRPO-style RL across document elements without extra human supervision.
AI.motivation: Existing RL for document parsing relies on edit-distance-based rewards that become weakly discriminative in the high-accuracy regime—near-correct outputs receive very similar scores, providing limited learning signal for hard cases, making optimization difficult.
AI.method: SAA is a plug-and-play reward sharpening mechanism that progressively increases reward curvature during training, amplifying subtle quality differences among high-scoring samples while maintaining stability in early learning. DocPO builds on SAA with element-specific reference-based rewards anchored by edit-distance signals for text, tables, and formulas.
AI.result: Experiments on OmniDocBench and DocElemHard show that SAA consistently improves GRPO-style RL across document elements compared to non-annealed rewards.
AI.conclusion: SAA provides a simple, plug-and-play way to sharpen weak rewards for document parsing RL, improving performance without requiring additional human supervision for reward construction.

title: Hybrid-Domain Posterior Sampling for Inverse Problems via Latent Flow Matching
summary: Latent Flow Models have revolutionized compressed-space image synthesis, yet their application to high-fidelity inverse problems remains bottlenecked. In this paper, we trace this dilemma to a fundamental geometric limitation of pre-trained autoencoders, which we term \emph{First-Order Manifold Blindness}. Severe decoder compression (e.g., retaining only $\sim\!2\%$ of the original degrees of freedom) produces a rank-deficient Jacobian, rendering high-frequency measurement residuals in its orthogonal complement invisible to latent gradients even when the decoder can represent the target image. To overcome this bottleneck, we propose Hybrid-Domain Posterior Sampling (HDPS), a decoupled inference framework that disentangles physical measurement consistency from semantic prior modeling. HDPS diverges into the pixel space, leveraging Langevin dynamics to absorb precise orthogonal measurement gradients, and subsequently projects these structural corrections back onto the generative manifold. An optimization-based latent alignment is introduced to filter pixel-space artifacts while avoiding the semantic drift of direct encoding. Extensive experiments on diverse inverse problems demonstrate that HDPS establishes a new state-of-the-art, successfully recovering the high-frequency structural precision that latent-only solvers inherently discard. The code is available at \href{https://github.com/74587887/HDPS}{https://github.com/74587887/HDPS}.

AI.tldr: HDPS is a hybrid-domain posterior sampling framework that overcomes "First-Order Manifold Blindness" in latent flow models for inverse problems by decoupling physical measurement consistency (handled via pixel-space Langevin dynamics) from semantic prior modeling (handled via latent-space optimization-based alignment), achieving state-of-the-art results on diverse inverse problems.
AI.motivation: Latent flow models excel at compressed-space image synthesis but struggle with high-fidelity inverse problems because pre-trained autoencoders suffer from a fundamental geometric limitation called First-Order Manifold Blindness: severe decoder compression produces rank-deficient Jacobians, making high-frequency measurement residuals in the orthogonal complement invisible to latent gradients.
AI.method: HDPS (Hybrid-Domain Posterior Sampling) is a decoupled inference framework that: (1) diverges into pixel space and uses Langevin dynamics to absorb precise orthogonal measurement gradients, and (2) projects these structural corrections back onto the generative manifold via an optimization-based latent alignment that filters pixel-space artifacts while avoiding semantic drift from direct encoding.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on diverse inverse problems demonstrate that HDPS establishes a new state-of-the-art, successfully recovering high-frequency structural precision that latent-only solvers inherently discard.
AI.conclusion: HDPS effectively bridges the gap between latent and pixel domain solvers for inverse problems, overcoming the rank-deficient Jacobian bottleneck of pre-trained autoencoders and enabling high-frequency structural recovery that was previously inaccessible to latent-only approaches.

title: DiffuseAgent-MI: Distributionally-Grounded,Tool-Integrated Self-Evolving Agents for Faithful Visual Reasoning
comment: 11 pages, 9 figures, accepted by ICML 2026 manitrack
summary: Tool-integrated vision-language agents have made remarkable progress on compositional and multi-step visual reasoning. Yet their outputs frequently exhibit unfaithfulness: the stated reasoning path diverges from the computation that actually produced the answer, undermining reliability in safety-critical applications. We present DiffuseAgent-MI, a self-evolving agent whose perceptual grounding is governed by a KL-minimal energy model over feature units, providing a distributional view of visual mechanistic interpretability. The agent learns an energy landscape that softly constrains generated samples to lie near the native prior conditioned on the chosen interpretable unit, closing the gap between the explanation and the internal representation. A verifier then supplies trajectory-level faithfulness rewards, and a repair branch re-conditions the energy when the verifier flags an unfaithful step. On GeoQA, SciVis, VQA-v2 and an in-house multimodal reasoning set, DiffuseAgent-MI improves accuracy by up to 5.1 points over prior self-evolving agents while more than doubling mutual-information faithfulness and human-interpretability agreement. Our analysis shows the energy term and the verifier are complementary: the former guarantees distributional faithfulness, the latter trajectory-level faithfulness, and only their combination closes both gaps.

AI.tldr: DiffuseAgent-MI is a self-evolving vision-language agent that uses a KL-minimal energy model over feature units for perceptual grounding, with a verifier providing trajectory-level faithfulness rewards and a repair branch for re-conditioning. It improves accuracy by up to 5.1 points and more than doubles faithfulness metrics across multiple benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Tool-integrated vision-language agents show progress on compositional reasoning but often produce unfaithful outputs where the stated reasoning diverges from the actual computation, which is unreliable for safety-critical applications.
AI.method: The agent learns an energy landscape that softly constrains samples near the native prior conditioned on chosen interpretable units (KL-minimal energy model over feature units). A verifier supplies trajectory-level faithfulness rewards, and a repair branch re-conditions the energy when unfaithful steps are flagged.
AI.result: On GeoQA, SciVis, VQA-v2 and an in-house multimodal reasoning set, DiffuseAgent-MI improves accuracy by up to 5.1 points over prior self-evolving agents, while more than doubling mutual-information faithfulness and human-interpretability agreement.
AI.conclusion: The energy term and verifier are complementary: the energy guarantees distributional faithfulness while the verifier ensures trajectory-level faithfulness, and only their combination closes both gaps.

title: Zero-Cost Virtual RNA: Approximating Immunotherapy Signatures via Cross-Modal WSI Retrieval
comment: Accepted to MIDL 2026 Short Paper track
summary: Identifying the ``Inflamed'' immunophenotype in Gastric Adenocarcinoma predicts immunotherapy response but requires an expensive 10-gene RNA signature. While deep learning on standard H\&E slides offers a scalable alternative, conventional binary classifiers oversimplify continuous RNA data and introduce label noise. To resolve this, we propose VITA (VIrtual Transcriptomic Approximation). By aligning H\&E and RNA into a joint latent space during training, VITA requires only standard H\&E at inference to retrieve morphologically similar historical cases and approximate the continuous RNA signature. Achieving 0.72 classification accuracy and a 0.66 Spearman correlation, VITA provides a cost-effective ``virtual transcriptomics'' pre-screening tool that preserves the continuous phenotypic spectrum without requiring genomic sequencing.

AI.tldr: VITA (VIrtual Transcriptomic Approximation) is a deep learning method that aligns H&E slides and RNA signatures in a joint latent space during training, allowing inference from H&E alone to retrieve morphologically similar historical cases and approximate continuous RNA signatures for predicting immunotherapy response in gastric adenocarcinoma. It achieves 0.72 classification accuracy and 0.66 Spearman correlation.
AI.motivation: Identifying the "inflamed" immunophenotype in gastric adenocarcinoma predicts immunotherapy response but requires an expensive 10-gene RNA signature. Deep learning on standard H&E slides offers a scalable alternative, yet conventional binary classifiers oversimplify continuous RNA data and introduce label noise. A more nuanced, cost-effective approach is needed.
AI.method: VITA aligns H&E images and RNA data into a joint latent space during training. At inference, it requires only standard H&E slides to retrieve morphologically similar historical cases, from which it approximates the continuous RNA signature—preserving the phenotypic spectrum instead of forcing binary classification.
AI.result: VITA achieves 0.72 classification accuracy and a 0.66 Spearman correlation for continuous RNA signature approximation.
AI.conclusion: VITA provides a cost-effective "virtual transcriptomics" pre-screening tool that preserves the continuous phenotypic spectrum without requiring genomic sequencing, serving as a scalable alternative for immunotherapy response prediction.

title: DrawAI: Agentic Benchmark and Workflow for Making Raster Images Editable
summary: Recent image-generation models and multimodal agents can produce high-quality visuals for increasingly complex visual communication tasks. Yet their raster outputs remain difficult to use directly because meaningful content and relationships are flattened into pixels, preventing users from inspecting, modifying, rearranging, or reusing individual components. We formulate image-to-editable reconstruction, which recovers a structured, directly manipulable artifact from a raster image while preserving its visual and semantic content. The central challenge is to jointly satisfy Fidelity and Editability, which often trade off in practice. To study this task, we introduce DrawAI, comprising an agentic benchmark, DrawAI-Bench, and a reconstruction workflow, DrawAI-Flow. DrawAI-Bench spans scientific figures, presentation slides, posters, and diagrams, combining real and AI-generated images to reflect practical visual-creation scenarios. It evaluates Fidelity and Editability through a hybrid protocol of 39 criteria: deterministic rule-based metrics measure properties with direct correspondences, while asset-specific vision-language rubrics capture semantic and perceptual qualities for which exact matching is misleading. Besides, we propose DrawAI-Flow, a two-stage agentic workflow in which a Parser Agent turns extracted elements evidence into an explicit reconstruction plan, and a Reconstruction Agent realizes the plan as executable graphics code through an iterative code-render-validate-revise loop. On DrawAI-Bench, we systematically evaluate thirteen models across five agent harnesses to study the effects of model capability, harness choice, and workflow design. The results show that reconstruction quality and costs vary substantially across model-harness configurations, while DrawAI-Flow consistently improves editable structure.

AI.tldr: Introduces image-to-editable reconstruction task and DrawAI, comprising DrawAI-Bench (a benchmark with 39 hybrid evaluation criteria across scientific figures, slides, posters, and diagrams) and DrawAI-Flow (a two-stage agentic workflow for reconstructing raster images into executable graphics code).
AI.motivation: Modern image-generation models produce high-quality raster images, but these pixel-based outputs cannot be easily inspected, modified, or reused because meaningful content is flattened into pixels. There is a need to recover structured, directly manipulable artifacts from raster images.
AI.method: Proposes DrawAI with two components: (1) DrawAI-Bench evaluates Fidelity and Editability via 39 criteria using rule-based metrics plus asset-specific vision-language rubrics; (2) DrawAI-Flow is a two-stage agentic workflow with a Parser Agent (creates reconstruction plan from extracted elements) and a Reconstruction Agent (generates executable graphics code via an iterative code-render-validate-revise loop).
AI.result: Systematically evaluated thirteen models across five agent harnesses. Reconstruction quality and costs vary substantially across model-harness configurations, and DrawAI-Flow consistently improves editable structure.
AI.conclusion: Editable reconstruction of raster images is a challenging task requiring a trade-off between fidelity and editability, and the DrawAI framework provides a systematic way to study and improve this capability through agentic workflows.

title: Test-Time Curriculum for Open-Set AIGC Detection
summary: AI-generated image detectors deployed in open-world environments inevitably face distribution shifts as new and stronger generative models continue to emerge. Although existing methods improve cross-generator generalization through better representations or training data construction, they typically follow a static train-once-and-deploy paradigm and cannot adapt after deployment. In this work, we study open-set AIGC image detection from a test-time adaptation perspective. We propose Test-Time Curriculum (TTC), a simple and model-agnostic framework that adapts a detector on unlabeled test data through curriculum-based self-training. TTC starts from highly reliable pseudo-labeled samples and progressively incorporates harder yet informative cases, while enforcing class-balanced selection to reduce biased updates under generator shift. To further improve pseudo-label quality, we introduce Cross-Scale Pseudo-Label Refinement, which aggregates complementary evidence across multiple resolutions for more reliable adaptation, and applies noisy-or fusion at inference to strengthen final predictions. In addition, we construct AIGCGuard, a new benchmark containing 3,100 representative real images and 124,000 generated images from 40 of the most advanced open-source and proprietary text-to-image models. Extensive experiments on five benchmarks show that TTC substantially improves overall detection performance under diverse unseen-generator shifts, establishing a practical and effective test-time adaptation framework for open-set generated image detection.

AI.tldr: TTC is a test-time adaptation framework for AI-generated image detection that adapts pre-trained detectors on unlabeled test data via curriculum-based self-training, improving robustness to distribution shifts from new generative models.
AI.motivation: AI-generated image detectors face distribution shifts in open-world deployment as new generative models emerge, but existing methods use a static train-once-and-deploy paradigm that cannot adapt after deployment.
AI.method: Test-Time Curriculum (TTC) adapts detectors on unlabeled test data through curriculum-based self-training, starting from reliable pseudo-labels and progressively incorporating harder samples with class-balanced selection. Cross-Scale Pseudo-Label Refinement aggregates evidence across multiple resolutions for better pseudo-labels and uses noisy-or fusion at inference. A new benchmark AIGCGuard is constructed.
AI.result: Experiments on five benchmarks show TTC substantially improves detection performance under diverse unseen-generator shifts. The AIGCGuard benchmark contains 3,100 real images and 124,000 generated images from 40 text-to-image models.
AI.conclusion: TTC establishes a practical and effective test-time adaptation framework for open-set generated image detection, addressing the static deployment limitation of existing detectors.

title: Beyond Token-Level Cross-Entropy: Fréchet Distributional Post-Training for Autoregressive Image Generation
summary: Autoregressive image generators are commonly pretrained with token-level cross-entropy under teacher forcing, yet evaluated by the distributional quality of decoded images. This creates an objective mismatch, because categorical errors have unequal image-level consequences, and a context mismatch, because inference conditions on model-generated histories. We introduce FD-loss post-training, which adapts a pretrained discrete generator using representation-space Fréchet distance as the sole objective. A dual-pass scheme first constructs detached rollout contexts through gradient-free generation under the model's native inference configuration, then performs differentiable replay with a probability-level straight-through estimator (STE) that preserves hard argmax decoding in the forward pass while propagating image-level gradients through temperature-scaled probabilities. Only the generator is updated, while the tokenizer and feature extractors remain frozen. Across eight completed configurations from four generator families on class-conditional ImageNet at $256\times256$, FD-loss post-training reduces FID and $\mathrm{FD}_{r6}$ by 41.4% and 52.0% on average. The strongest FID result improves from 2.42 to 1.43 without adding parameters or inference steps.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces FD-loss post-training, a method that adapts pretrained discrete image generators using representation-space Fréchet distance as the sole training objective, addressing the mismatch between token-level training and distributional evaluation in autoregressive image generation.
AI.motivation: Autoregressive image generators are pretrained with token-level cross-entropy under teacher forcing, but evaluated by distributional quality of decoded images. This creates two problems: (1) an objective mismatch since categorical errors have unequal image-level consequences, and (2) a context mismatch since inference conditions on model-generated (not ground-truth) histories.
AI.method: The method uses a dual-pass scheme: (1) a first pass constructs detached rollout contexts through gradient-free generation under the model's native inference configuration, and (2) a second pass performs differentiable replay using a probability-level straight-through estimator (STE) that preserves hard argmax decoding in the forward pass while propagating image-level gradients through temperature-scaled probabilities. Only the generator is updated; tokenizer and feature extractors remain frozen.
AI.result: Across eight configurations from four generator families on class-conditional ImageNet at 256×256, FD-loss post-training reduces FID and FD_r6 by 41.4% and 52.0% on average. The strongest FID result improves from 2.42 to 1.43 without adding parameters or inference steps.
AI.conclusion: FD-loss post-training effectively bridges the gap between token-level pretraining and distributional evaluation, significantly improving image generation quality across multiple model families without architectural changes or additional inference cost.

title: Relax Within, Balance Across: Geometry-Guided Load Balancing for Vision-Language Mixture-of-Experts
comment: 22 pages, including appendices. Code available at https://github.com/ZiangWu-77/ReBA
summary: Vision-language MoE batches contain different numbers of image and text tokens. Image resolution, image count, tiling, and prompt length all change this token mix. We call the standard token-level Switch auxiliary loss Std-Aux. Std-Aux balances only the mixed load, so large image and text load errors can cancel at one mix. On our main model, the same trained router shows more than a fivefold change in load imbalance across image resolutions. We hold the image and text load profiles fixed and derive the exact load curve as the token mix varies. The image-text load gap controls sensitivity to the token mix. Physical preprocessing can also change the conditional profiles. The fixed-profile law excludes such changes. To design a remedy, we examine the router input structure. Image and text occupy distinct regions, while visual tokens group strongly by source image. The modality boundary motivates separate image and text terms. The image boundary motivates one equal-weight routing instance per image. ReBA, or Relax Within, Balance Across, implements both choices. Across four split backbones, ReBA lowers load on every reported benchmark input while keeping mean task accuracy comparable to Std-Aux. ReBA also lowers average load over the tested range and worst physical load under resolution and tiling shifts. Code is available at https://github.com/ZiangWu-77/ReBA.

AI.tldr: The paper identifies failures of standard token-level Switch auxiliary loss (Std-Aux) in vision-language MoE models, where load imbalances vary >5x across image resolutions due to mixed image/text token loads canceling each other. The authors propose ReBA (Relax Within, Balance Across), which separates image and text load balancing and applies equal-weight routing per image, reducing load across benchmarks while maintaining comparable accuracy.
AI.motivation: Standard token-level Switch auxiliary loss balances only the mixed load of image and text tokens, allowing large errors in each modality to cancel out at certain token mixes. This causes severe load imbalance variability (fivefold change) across image resolutions in vision-language MoE models, degrading efficiency.
AI.method: The paper derives an exact load curve as a function of token mix, showing the image-text load gap controls sensitivity. They analyze router input structure, finding image and text occupy distinct regions with visual tokens grouped by source image. Based on these boundaries, ReBA introduces separate image and text balancing terms, plus one equal-weight routing instance per image.
AI.result: Across four split backbones, ReBA lowers load on every reported benchmark input while keeping mean task accuracy comparable to Std-Aux. ReBA also reduces average load over the tested range and worst physical load under resolution and tiling shifts.
AI.conclusion: ReBA provides a robust remedy for load balance in vision-language MoE by leveraging modality and image source boundaries in router input structure, improving load stability without sacrificing accuracy.

title: Element-Aware Group Learning for E-Commerce Image Generation
summary: Recent advances in image generation and editing have made prompt quality a key bottleneck for e-commerce creatives. Vision-language models (VLMs) can generate image-editing prompts from product images and metadata, but further improving their prompt-writing capabilities requires post-training with feedback from the generated images. Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) is a natural framework for such outcome-level reward optimization. However, it assigns credit only at the full-prompt level, even though image quality often depends on specific design elements such as composition, background, and the presentation of selling points. Existing fine-grained credit assignment methods typically require step-level supervision or learned critics. To address this, we propose EAGLE-GRPO (Element-Aware Group Learning for E-Commerce Image Generation), which decomposes the group-centered reward over predefined elements. We cast element-level credit assignment as a kernel ridge regression problem and derive a closed-form solution, without additional rollouts or separate credit-assignment models. This yields interpretable per-element advantages and more precise policy updates. Experiments show that EAGLE-GRPO sustains performance gains over more training steps before plateauing and generates prompts that produce higher-quality e-commerce images than competitive VLM prompt-writing baselines.

AI.tldr: EAGLE-GRPO is a fine-grained credit assignment method for RL-based prompt generation in e-commerce image editing, decomposing group-level rewards into element-level advantages via closed-form kernel ridge regression without extra models or rollouts.
AI.motivation: GRPO assigns credit only at the full-prompt level, but image quality depends on specific design elements (composition, background, selling points). Existing fine-grained methods need step-level supervision or learned critics, which are costly or unavailable.
AI.method: Decompose the group-centered reward over predefined elements and formulate element-level credit assignment as kernel ridge regression, deriving a closed-form solution that yields interpretable per-element advantages for more precise policy updates.
AI.result: Experiments show EAGLE-GRPO sustains performance gains over more training steps before plateauing and produces higher-quality e-commerce images than competitive VLM prompt-writing baselines.
AI.conclusion: Element-aware credit assignment improves training stability and prompt quality for e-commerce image generation without requiring extra supervision or models.

title: Representation Transfer of Foundation Models for Ultra-Widefield Retinal Imaging
summary: Despite the widespread adoption of foundation models as feature extractors for medical imaging, relatively little is understood about how different pretraining strategies influence the transferability of learned representations to weakly supervised ophthalmic imaging tasks. We investigate this question in ultra-widefield (UWF) retinal imaging by evaluating foundation model representations within a patch-based multiple instance learning (MIL) framework for disease classification on UWF images. We compare Vision Transformer encoders pretrained with supervised, Masked Autoencoder (MAE), and self-distillation objectives, while keeping the downstream aggregation architecture unchanged. Within a controlled comparison of ViT-B encoders pretrained on ImageNet-1k, the choice of pretraining objective substantially influenced frozen representation transfer, with supervised and self-distillation-based models outperforming MAE. A contemporary DINOv3 model pretrained at a larger scale achieved the strongest overall performance, with a quadratic weighted kappa of 0.863 for five-class diabetic retinopathy grading, comparable with DINOv1. Attention analysis further revealed distinct patch-aggregation behaviours associated with the different pretrained representations, while partial fine-tuning substantially reduced the performance gap for MAE. These findings suggest that pretraining strategy influences both representation transferability and the subsequent aggregation of patch-level evidence within MIL, resulting in differences in downstream classification performance.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how different pretraining strategies for vision foundation models affect transferability to weakly supervised ophthalmic imaging tasks, specifically evaluating ViT encoders (supervised, MAE, self-distillation) within a patch-based MIL framework for UWF retinal disease classification. Results show pretraining objective substantially influences frozen representation transfer, with supervised and self-distillation models outperforming MAE; a large-scale DINOv3 model achieved the best performance (kappa=0.863), and partial fine-tuning reduced the gap for MAE. Pretraining strategy affects both representation transferability and patch-aggregation behavior within MIL.
AI.motivation: Despite widespread use of foundation models as feature extractors in medical imaging, little is understood about how different pretraining strategies influence the transferability of learned representations to weakly supervised ophthalmic imaging tasks, particularly in ultra-widefield retinal imaging.
AI.method: Evaluation of ViT-B encoders pretrained with supervised, MAE, and self-distillation objectives within a patch-based multiple instance learning (MIL) framework for disease classification on UWF images, keeping downstream aggregation architecture unchanged, with controlled ImageNet-1k comparison and a larger-scale DINOv3 model.
AI.result: Pretraining objective substantially influenced frozen representation transfer, with supervised and self-distillation models outperforming MAE; DINOv3 achieved the strongest overall performance with kappa=0.863 for five-class diabetic retinopathy grading, comparable to DINOv1; attention analysis revealed distinct patch-aggregation behaviors; partial fine-tuning substantially reduced the MAE performance gap.
AI.conclusion: Pretraining strategy influences both representation transferability and the subsequent aggregation of patch-level evidence within MIL, resulting in differences in downstream classification performance in weakly supervised ophthalmic imaging.

title: InstancePin: Instance-Addressable Layout-to-Image Diffusion via Coordinate Pinning
summary: Layout-to-image diffusion models have achieved impressive semantic controllability by conditioning generation on category-level segmentation maps. However, such category-aligned control is not necessarily instance-addressable: multiple nearby objects from the same category are often treated as a shared semantic region, leading to ambiguous boundaries, averaged appearances, and feature confusion among instances. This limitation is particularly evident in urban scene synthesis, where small and crowded pedestrians or vehicles require fine-grained instance separation while preserving global scene consistency. In this paper, we propose InstancePin, an instance-addressable layout-to-image diffusion framework that pins each object instance with an explicit coordinate anchor. Instead of directly injecting instance masks into the pretrained backbone, InstancePin introduces an independent instance-aware adapter to preserve the category-level generation prior while learning instance-specific spatial control. For each instance, its center coordinate is encoded with Fourier features and projected into a coordinate token, which serves as a spatial anchor queried by latent image features through coordinate pinning attention. To make these anchors spatially meaningful, we further supervise the coordinate attention maps with instance regions, encouraging each coordinate token to activate its corresponding object area. Finally, an instance-mask guided fusion module routes pretrained backbone features to non-instance regions and adapter features to instance regions, enabling local instance refinement without sacrificing global semantic fidelity. Extensive experiments on Cityscapes demonstrate that InstancePin mitigates instance entanglement in dense layouts and improves both image fidelity and semantic consistency.

AI.tldr: InstancePin is an instance-addressable layout-to-image diffusion framework that pins each object instance with explicit coordinate anchors, using an instance-aware adapter with coordinate pinning attention and instance-mask guided fusion to mitigate instance entanglement in dense urban scene synthesis.
AI.motivation: Existing layout-to-image diffusion models control generation via category-level segmentation maps, which lack instance-addressability. Multiple nearby objects of the same category are treated as a shared semantic region, causing ambiguous boundaries, averaged appearances, and feature confusion—particularly problematic in dense urban scenes with small, crowded pedestrians and vehicles.
AI.method: InstancePin introduces an independent instance-aware adapter alongside the pretrained backbone. Each instance's center coordinate is encoded with Fourier features into a coordinate token, serving as a spatial anchor. Coordinate pinning attention allows latent image features to query these anchors, and the attention maps are supervised with instance regions to ensure spatial activation. An instance-mask guided fusion module routes backbone features to non-instance regions and adapter features to instance regions for local refinement while preserving global semantics.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on Cityscapes show that InstancePin mitigates instance entanglement in dense layouts and improves both image fidelity and semantic consistency compared to baseline methods.
AI.conclusion: Instance-addressable control via explicit coordinate anchors effectively resolves instance-level confusion in dense layout-to-image generation, achieving better fidelity and semantic quality without disrupting category-level priors.

title: Diagnosing Under-Development of Irreversible Processes in Video Generation
summary: Many physical attributes are \emph{irreversible}: ice melts but does not re-freeze, paper chars but does not un-burn. Do video generators respect this? We show the question is hard to measure, and that what can be measured reliably is \emph{development} rather than reversal. Metrics of local reversal are null-degenerate: a per-clip violation rate scores $0.50$ on pure noise, and a variance-normalized reversal residual sits at its noise ceiling. What survives null-testing is a two-part protocol: progress (a directional attribute correlation) and a stasis rate. Under this protocol, generated video separates cleanly from real footage, and the gap is human-validated. Across seven text-to-video models, real reference footage advances ($ρ{=}{+}0.40$, $35\%$ static) while every generator shows near-zero progress and $92$--$100\%$ stasis; nine annotators rate real footage far above generated ($2.75$ vs.\ $0.99$ on a $0$--$4$ scale). The reliable finding is \emph{under-development}: generators barely advance irreversible attributes rather than reversing them. As a complementary mechanism, we show that post-hoc readout guidance is gameable, whereas enforcing monotonicity by construction in a disentangled attribute latent removes the gameable readout, validated in controlled and semi-synthetic settings.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether text-to-video generators respect irreversible physical attributes (e.g., ice melting). The authors show that simple reversal metrics are flawed (null-degenerate), and propose a two-part protocol measuring progress and stasis rate. Real footage shows clear progress, while seven video generators show near-zero progress and 92-100% stasis, indicating under-development rather than reversal of irreversible attributes.
AI.motivation: Video generators may not respect irreversible physical processes, but this is hard to measure due to methodological issues. Existing local reversal metrics fail null-testing (e.g., scoring 0.50 on noise). The paper aims to find reliable measurement protocols to determine whether generators respect or violate irreversibility.
AI.method: The authors propose a two-part protocol: (1) progress measurement via directional attribute correlation, and (2) a stasis rate. They validate this against null testing. They also compare post-hoc readout guidance (shown to be gameable) with a construction-based approach enforcing monotonicity in a disentangled attribute latent, validated in controlled and semi-synthetic settings.
AI.result: Real reference footage shows positive progress (ρ=+0.40, 35% static), while all seven text-to-video models show near-zero progress and 92-100% stasis. Human annotators rate real footage significantly higher (2.75 vs. 0.99 on a 0-4 scale). The reliable finding is under-development: generators barely advance irreversible attributes. Post-hoc readout guidance is shown to be gameable, while construction-based monotonicity enforcement is not.
AI.conclusion: Video generators do not reverse irreversible attributes; they under-develop them—failing to advance physical processes rather than violating their directionality. The proposed two-part protocol provides a robust, null-tested measurement framework, and construction-based monotonicity enforcement offers a more reliable mechanism than post-hoc readout guidance.

title: Where Does Generative Difficulty Reside? An Empirical Study of Target Representations
comment: TL;DR: Across pixels, SD-VAE, DINOv2, and MAE, we find that target representations are not interchangeable: they shift difficulty between contextual modeling, per-token denoising, and guidance, producing distinct optimization and diversity trade-offs
summary: The target representation defines the distribution an image generator must learn, yet it is often treated as an interchangeable interface. This assumption is particularly questionable for continuous masked generators, which combine contextual inference from visible tokens with conditional modeling of each missing token. We study raw pixels, SD-VAE latents and DINOv2 as well as MAE representation-autoencoder features within a unified masked autoregressive rectified-flow model. Under a shared ImageNet training budget, these spaces exhibit distinct optimization and inference regimes. DINOv2 converges fastest in both iterations and computation but benefits strongly from a wider local denoiser and direct context fusion. Pixels optimize substantially more slowly and require a different prediction, masking, and guidance configuration. MAE reconstructs images more faithfully and exhibits clear semantic clustering, yet produces generations substantially worse than DINOv2. The representations also respond differently to classifier-free guidance and occupy distinct precision-recall trade-offs. Together, our results show that compression, reconstruction fidelity, token dimensionality, and visible semantic clustering do not individually predict generative behavior. Instead, target representations redistribute difficulty across contextual modeling, per-token denoising, and inference-time distributional control.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how different target representations (raw pixels, SD-VAE latents, DINOv2 features, and MAE features) affect continuous masked autoregressive generative models, showing that each representation creates distinct optimization and inference regimes that cannot be predicted by any single property like compression or reconstruction fidelity.
AI.motivation: Target representations are often treated as interchangeable interfaces in image generation, but this assumption is questionable for continuous masked generators that combine contextual inference and conditional modeling. The paper aims to understand how different target spaces affect generative behavior.
AI.method: The authors train a unified masked autoregressive rectified-flow model on ImageNet across four target representations: raw pixels, SD-VAE latents, DINOv2 features, and MAE representation-autoencoder features. They systematically compare optimization speed, computational efficiency, prediction/masking/guidance configurations, and generative quality.
AI.result: DINOv2 converges fastest in iterations and computation but needs a wider local denoiser and direct context fusion. Pixels optimize much slower and require different configurations. MAE reconstructs faithfully and shows semantic clustering but produces worse generations than DINOv2. Representations respond differently to classifier-free guidance and occupy distinct precision-recall trade-offs.
AI.conclusion: Compression, reconstruction fidelity, token dimensionality, and semantic clustering do not individually predict generative behavior. Instead, target representations redistribute difficulty across contextual modeling, per-token denoising, and inference-time distributional control, meaning representation choice is a critical design factor rather than an interchangeable detail.

title: WiFuse: An Attention Mechanism for Human Activity Recognition using Fused CSI Amplitude and Delay-Doppler Channel Features
summary: Recently, Wi-Fi sensing has played a significant role in Human Activity Recognition (HAR), as it enables the detection of various activities using only Wi-Fi signals, ensuring privacy and remaining non-intrusive for the user. However, environmental characteristics such as reflective surfaces, hardware offsets, and other physical impairments affect recognition by the neural network, subsequently causing errors and significantly reducing model accuracy. To overcome this problem we present the WiFuse framework, a dual-stream Channel State Information (CSI) framework for human activity recognition (HAR) that pairs denoised time-domain amplitude variations with 2D-FFT-derived Delay-Doppler motion representations computed from the sanitized channel phase. The fused representation feeds a hybrid ResNet-Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) neural architecture augmented with channel and spatio-temporal attention, where the ResNet extracts spatial-spectral features and the TCN models long-range temporal dependencies; a decoupled two-stage transfer learning strategy is employed to improve optimization stability and feature reuse. We conduct extensive experiments on two public datasets, including comparisons against state-of-the-art methods and alternative hybrid architectures, ablation studies, and cross-dataset and domain-adaptation evaluations. The proposed framework reaches an overall accuracy of up to 95.28% across the four environments of the XRF55 dataset and up to 98.20% on the multi-user Wi-MIR dataset. Overall, the results indicate that combining amplitude and Delay-Doppler representations within a dual-stream strategy, enhanced by transfer learning, improves recognition performance under conditions that typically degrade deep neural networks, such as class overlap, multipath propagation, noise, and interference.

AI.tldr: WiFuse is a dual-stream CSI-based framework for human activity recognition that combines denoised time-domain amplitude features with 2D-FFT-derived Delay-Doppler representations from sanitized channel phase, feeding a hybrid ResNet-TCN architecture with channel and spatio-temporal attention, enhanced by two-stage transfer learning. It achieves up to 95.28% accuracy on XRF55 and 98.20% on Wi-MIR datasets.
AI.motivation: Wi-Fi sensing for HAR is privacy-preserving and non-intrusive, but environmental factors such as reflective surfaces, hardware offsets, and physical impairments degrade neural network recognition accuracy, motivating a more robust framework.
AI.method: WiFuse employs a dual-stream CSI framework pairing denoised time-domain amplitude variations with 2D-FFT-derived Delay-Doppler motion representations from sanitized channel phase. The fused representation feeds a hybrid ResNet-TCN architecture with channel and spatio-temporal attention, where ResNet extracts spatial-spectral features and TCN models long-range temporal dependencies, augmented by a decoupled two-stage transfer learning strategy.
AI.result: The framework achieves up to 95.28% accuracy across four environments of the XRF55 dataset and up to 98.20% on the multi-user Wi-MIR dataset, with extensive experiments including comparisons against state-of-the-art methods, ablation studies, and cross-dataset/domain-adaptation evaluations.
AI.conclusion: Combining amplitude and Delay-Doppler representations in a dual-stream strategy enhanced by transfer learning improves recognition performance under conditions that typically degrade deep neural networks, such as class overlap, multipath propagation, noise, and interference.

title: PixelSR: Efficient Screen Content Super-Resolution via Pixel Classification
summary: Screen content images are generally composed of texts and graphics. Compared to natural images, these man-made images contain a large quantity of sharp but repetitive structures. However, existing works in screen content super-resolution underutilize the special characteristics of screen content, leaving a large room to improve model performance and speed up. In this paper, we propose PixelSR, a simple yet effective method to improve super-resolution performance but with faster inference speed. To improve model performance, we classify pixels via pixel binning to compute content attention in the training phase. Specifically, after binning pixels into content-dependent groups, content attention is aggregated from pixel features within each group to introduce a content-dependent and non-local receptive field for every pixel. In the testing phase, we utilize the properties of self-repetitiveness and redundancy in screen content to speed up inference without the loss of model performance. We divide targeted high-resolution pixels into three types, which are unique pixels, repeated pixels, and background pixels for each test image. We conduct conventional network processing on unique pixels and cache their predictions in the on-the-fly lookup table. For repeated pixels which have appeared in unique pixels, we directly retrieve prediction results from the lookup table without network processing. For background pixels, we use the nearest neighbor algorithm to generate high-resolution pixels. The on-the-fly lookup table is cleaned and repeats the procedure above for the next test image. Experiments show our PixelSR achieves state-of-the-art performance with shorter inference time in screen content super-resolution.

AI.tldr: PixelSR is a screen content super-resolution method that improves performance by using pixel binning to compute content-dependent attention during training, and speeds up inference by classifying pixels into unique, repeated, and background types—using a lookup table for repeated pixels and nearest-neighbor for background pixels.
AI.motivation: Screen content images contain sharp but repetitive structures that existing super-resolution methods underutilize, leaving room for both performance improvement and faster inference. The authors aim to exploit the special characteristics of screen content.
AI.method: During training, pixels are binned into content-dependent groups and content attention is aggregated from pixel features within each group to provide a non-local receptive field. During testing, pixels are classified into three types: unique pixels (processed by the network), repeated pixels (retrieved from an on-the-fly lookup table), and background pixels (generated via nearest-neighbor algorithm). The lookup table is cleared per test image.
AI.result: Experiments show PixelSR achieves state-of-the-art super-resolution performance with shorter inference time on screen content images.
AI.conclusion: By leveraging the self-repetitiveness and redundancy of screen content, PixelSR demonstrates that both accuracy and inference speed can be simultaneously improved in screen content super-resolution.

title: Geometry-guided Emotion Modulation for Controllable and Photorealistic Emotional Talking Face Generation
summary: Audio-driven emotional talking face generation aims to synthesize realistic videos with expressive facial dynamics. However, existing methods struggle to balance controllability and visual fidelity. Although implicit representations capture rich semantics, they lack structural guidance, often resulting in averaged emotional expressions. In contrast, explicit geometric methods offer better control over facial expressions but tend to sacrifice high-frequency texture details. To address it, we propose GemTalk, a diffusion-based framework that combines the semantic richness of implicit representations with the structural precision of explicit geometric priors. We introduce a Vision-guided Audio Emotion Projection (V-AEP) module to extract implicit emotional lip and expression features. At the same time, a Diffusion-based Geometric Priors Generator (D-GPG) generates identity-aware blendshape coefficients as explicit structural priors. Crucially, our Geometry-guided Emotion Modulation (GEM) module leverages these geometric priors to recalibrate the magnitude of implicit features, enabling precise, continuous control over emotional expressions, especially emotion intensity, without sacrificing visual quality. Extensive experiments show GemTalk achieves superior performance in photo-realism, and facial emotional dynamics.

AI.tldr: GemTalk is a diffusion-based framework for audio-driven emotional talking face generation that combines implicit representations with explicit geometric priors to achieve both precise emotional control and high visual fidelity.
AI.motivation: Existing methods struggle to balance controllability and visual fidelity: implicit representations capture rich semantics but lack structural guidance (leading to averaged emotional expressions), while explicit geometric methods offer better control but sacrifice high-frequency texture details.
AI.method: GemTalk integrates three key components: (1) a Vision-guided Audio Emotion Projection (V-AEP) module extracts implicit emotional lip and expression features; (2) a Diffusion-based Geometric Priors Generator (D-GPG) generates identity-aware blendshape coefficients as explicit structural priors; (3) a Geometry-guided Emotion Modulation (GEM) module uses these geometric priors to recalibrate the magnitude of implicit features for precise, continuous emotional expression control.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show GemTalk achieves superior performance in photo-realism and facial emotional dynamics compared to existing methods.
AI.conclusion: By unifying implicit semantics with explicit geometric guidance, GemTalk enables precise emotional expression control (especially emotion intensity) without sacrificing visual quality, effectively resolving the controllability-fidelity trade-off in emotional talking face generation.

title: CopyCat: Improving Fine-Grained Subject Consistency in Subject-to-Image Models within Seconds
summary: Recent subject-to-image models have achieved impressive progress in personalized image generation, yet they still struggle to preserve fine-grained subject-specific details. A major reason is the lack of high-quality fine-grained identity supervision: real paired data are expensive to collect, while synthesized training pairs often preserve only coarse subject appearance and fail to capture subtle subject-specific details. In this work, we propose CopyCat, a lightweight model-refinement framework that improves fine-grained subject consistency within only a few seconds. CopyCat performs a one-time refinement of a pretrained subject-to-image model by attaching a lightweight Fine-grained Consistency LoRA (FCLoRA) and optimizing it using a single proxy image, which is used as both the conditioning image and the reconstruction target. This exact self-reconstruction objective substantially simplifies the optimization task, enabling effective fine-grained refinement within only a few seconds. The refinement is performed only once; the resulting model can be directly applied to diverse unseen reference subjects and prompts without further subject-specific optimization. We further revisit subject-to-image LoRA training in double-stream diffusion transformers and find that adapting only the visual stream consistently improves subject consistency. Extensive experiments on DreamBench and XVerseBench demonstrate consistent improvements in fine-grained subject consistency across representative subject-to-image models under both single- and multi-subject settings.

AI.tldr: CopyCat is a lightweight model-refinement framework that improves fine-grained subject consistency in subject-to-image generation by attaching a Fine-grained Consistency LoRA (FCLoRA) and optimizing it against a single proxy image via exact self-reconstruction, achieving refinement in seconds without per-subject optimization.
AI.motivation: Existing subject-to-image models struggle to preserve fine-grained subject-specific details due to the lack of high-quality fine-grained identity supervision. Real paired data is expensive to collect, and synthesized training pairs only capture coarse subject appearance, failing to retain subtle subject-specific details.
AI.method: CopyCat performs a one-time refinement of a pretrained subject-to-image model by attaching a lightweight Fine-grained Consistency LoRA (FCLoRA) and optimizing it using a single proxy image that serves as both the conditioning image and the reconstruction target. This exact self-reconstruction objective simplifies optimization, allowing fine-grained refinement in only a few seconds. The method also revisits LoRA training in double-stream diffusion transformers, finding that adapting only the visual stream improves subject consistency.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on DreamBench and XVerseBench demonstrate consistent improvements in fine-grained subject consistency across representative subject-to-image models under both single- and multi-subject settings.
AI.conclusion: The refinement is performed only once; the resulting model can be directly applied to diverse unseen reference subjects and prompts without further subject-specific optimization, establishing CopyCat as an efficient and effective solution for preserving fine-grained subject identity.

title: Breaking the Horizontal Prior: From Long-Tailed Orientation Bias to Roll-Robust Monocular Depth Estimation
comment: The code is publicly available on GitHub: https://github.com/KaihuaTang/Horizontal-Prior
summary: Despite recent advances in Monocular Depth Estimation, state-of-the-art depth foundation models remain vulnerable to robustness issues. Particularly, even slight camera rolls can result in substantial degradation in depth estimations. We attribute this problem to a previously overlooked phenomenon, termed the Horizontal Prior, which is a manifestation of long-tailed distribution bias: most training images are captured in approximately horizontal orientations due to human visual preferences and photographic habits. While intuitive remedies such as re-balanced data augmentation and horizon leveling provide partial improvements, they fail to fully address the issue. In this paper, we introduce Invariant Depth Constraint (ID-Constraint), a training-time supervision strategy that improves roll robustness by fine-tuning and jointly regularizing the depth backbone with a series of geometric and spatial reasoning tasks. These auxiliary objectives encourage the backbone to learn rotation-stable, depth-relevant representations, while the auxiliary prediction heads are discarded after training, leaving the original inference architecture unchanged. Extensive experiments on five benchmark datasets across four roll settings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Invariant Depth Constraint (ID-Constraint), a training-time supervision strategy that improves the roll-robustness of monocular depth estimation models by regularizing the depth backbone with auxiliary geometric and spatial reasoning tasks, addressing a phenomenon called the Horizontal Prior.
AI.motivation: State-of-the-art monocular depth estimation models suffer from significant performance degradation under even slight camera rolls. This is attributed to the Horizontal Prior—a long-tailed distribution bias where most training images are captured in approximately horizontal orientations due to human photographic habits. Existing remedies like data augmentation and horizon leveling only provide partial improvement.
AI.method: The proposed ID-Constraint is a training-time supervision strategy that fine-tunes and jointly regularizes the depth backbone with a series of geometric and spatial reasoning auxiliary tasks. These auxiliary objectives encourage the backbone to learn rotation-stable, depth-relevant representations, while the auxiliary prediction heads are discarded after training, keeping the original inference architecture unchanged.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on five benchmark datasets across four roll settings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving roll robustness for monocular depth estimation.
AI.conclusion: The ID-Constraint effectively addresses the previously overlooked Horizontal Prior issue, providing a training-time solution that enhances roll robustness without changing the inference-time architecture.

title: BRIC-Net: Boundary-Reliable Illumination-Color Interaction for Remote Sensing Image Deshadowing
summary: Shadows in remote sensing images obscure surface appearance and disrupt radiometric continuity, reducing the reliability of visual interpretation and downstream analysis. Remote sensing image deshadowing is an ill-posed inverse problem that requires spatially varying illumination recovery while preserving chromatic and radiometric consistency in non-shadow regions. Existing methods commonly rely on hard shadow masks for compensation or directly regress RGB intensities. Hard masks may inadequately model gradual penumbra variations and are sensitive to localization errors, often producing residual shadows or halo artifacts; direct RGB regression entangles illumination recovery with chromatic reconstruction and can introduce color casts. To this end, we propose the Boundary-Reliable Illumination-Color Interaction Network (BRIC-Net), which decouples these failures at different representation levels. A Lightness Reliability Prior (LRP) derives reliability-aware guidance from CIELAB statistics. Boundary-Adaptive Gated Mixing (BAGM) performs gated interpolation between shallow RGB and lightness features around uncertain transitions, while Spatial-Channel Mutual Modulation (SCMM) coordinates deeper spatial and channel responses for appearance-preserving illumination recovery. BRIC-Net achieves 29.46~dB full-image peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) on AeroDS-Syn and 27.96~dB on SRGTA. It also obtains the lowest Perception-based Image Quality Evaluator (PIQE) scores on AISD and AeroDS-Real. Region-wise evaluations and component ablations further support its effectiveness in shadow recovery and non-shadow preservation.

AI.tldr: BRIC-Net is a boundary-reliable illumination-color interaction network for remote sensing image deshadowing, using a Lightness Reliability Prior, Boundary-Adaptive Gated Mixing, and Spatial-Channel Mutual Modulation to decouple illumination recovery from chromatic reconstruction. It achieves state-of-the-art PSNR and PIQE scores on multiple benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing deshadowing methods use hard shadow masks that poorly model gradual penumbra variations and are sensitive to localization errors, or directly regress RGB intensities which entangle illumination recovery with chromatic reconstruction, leading to residual shadows, halo artifacts, or color casts.
AI.method: BRIC-Net introduces: (1) a Lightness Reliability Prior (LRP) for reliability-aware guidance from CIELAB statistics; (2) Boundary-Adaptive Gated Mixing (BAGM) for gated interpolation between shallow RGB and lightness features around uncertain transitions; and (3) Spatial-Channel Mutual Modulation (SCMM) for coordinating deeper spatial and channel responses in illumination recovery.
AI.result: BRIC-Net achieves 29.46 dB PSNR on AeroDS-Syn and 27.96 dB on SRGTA, and the lowest PIQE scores on AISD and AeroDS-Real. Region-wise evaluations and ablations confirm effectiveness in both shadow recovery and non-shadow preservation.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling illumination recovery from chromatic reconstruction, guided by reliability-aware priors and boundary-adaptive mechanisms, is effective for handling gradual penumbra and preserving radiometric consistency in remote sensing image deshadowing.

title: Proteus: A Truncation-Robust Entropy Model for Progressive LiDAR Compression
summary: LiDAR point clouds provide explicit, deterministic physical boundaries critical for collaborative safety-critical perception. However, wireless channels inherently impair and corrupt transmitted signals. Existing robust frameworks (such as deep JSCC or MDC) attempt to counter these channel impairments through statistical or parametric estimation, turning exact physical measurements into unverified algorithmic estimates. To address this, we propose Proteus, a learned LiDAR codec operating on 2D range images. By decoupling the frame representation into independent coders for the \textbf{sig}nificant range bit-planes (SIG) and the \textbf{ins}ignificant range bit-planes and attributes (INS), Proteus achieves overall stream-level truncation robustness. The non-truncatable SIG block encodes the most significant range bit-planes to establish a necessary, self-contained perceptual lower bound, below which the reconstructed point cloud is severely degraded. Meanwhile, INS employs bit-plane slicing representation and coding, ensuring that range truncation mathematically maps to a deterministic spatial precision degradation. Subordinate attributes are reconstructed via a hybrid lossless-predictive method, leveraging the decoded geometry as a strong structural prior for fine-grained approximation. Furthermore, strategic ordering within INS prioritizes geometry over attributes under bandwidth drops. Experimental results on the Waymo Open Dataset and SemanticKITTI demonstrate that Proteus tolerates up to approximately 70\% bitstream truncation, while outperforming established standards (G-PCC, Draco, and JPEG XL) and the representative learned compressor Unicorn under ideal channel conditions.

AI.tldr: Proteus is a learned LiDAR point cloud codec that achieves stream-level truncation robustness by decoupling frames into SIG (significant range bit-planes) and INS (insignificant bit-planes/attributes) coders, tolerating up to ~70% bitstream truncation while outperforming G-PCC, Draco, JPEG XL, and Unicorn.
AI.motivation: LiDAR point clouds are critical for safety-critical perception, but wireless channels corrupt transmitted signals. Existing robust frameworks (deep JSCC, MDC) use statistical or parametric estimation, converting exact physical measurements into unverified algorithmic estimates, which is undesirable.
AI.method: Proteus operates on 2D range images and decouples frame representation into: (1) SIG coder for significant range bit-planes, establishing a non-truncatable perceptual lower bound; (2) INS coder using bit-plane slicing for insignificant bit-planes and attributes, where truncation maps to deterministic spatial precision degradation. Attributes use hybrid lossless-predictive reconstruction, and INS prioritizes geometry over attributes under bandwidth drops.
AI.result: On Waymo Open Dataset and SemanticKITTI, Proteus tolerates up to ~70% bitstream truncation and outperforms established standards (G-PCC, Draco, JPEG XL) and the learned compressor Unicorn even under ideal (no-truncation) channel conditions.
AI.conclusion: By preserving exact physical measurements in a non-truncatable significant block and providing deterministic degradation semantics through bit-plane slicing, Proteus offers a robust alternative to statistical estimation-based robust codecs for safety-critical collaborative perception.

title: E2Pano: Learning Event-to-Panorama Image Reconstruction
summary: Event cameras offer microsecond-level temporal resolution and high dynamic range, potentially facilitating motion-blur-free panoramic imaging from fast rotational scanning. Nonetheless, existing optimization-based methods remain computationally demanding, while prior learning-based reconstruction methods are largely designed for perspective imagery and lack geometry-aware support for panoramic outputs. We present E2Pano, a geometry-guided event-to-panorama pipeline with an end-to-end learnable photometric reconstruction stage. Our framework preserves real spherical coordinates from geometric mapping throughout the pipeline, employs a lightweight enhancement module with frequency-domain supervision to bridge the event-image domain gap, and leverages a spherical Transformer with 3D positional embeddings for photometric reconstruction. Experiments on synthetic data and captured rotational scans show improved reconstruction quality and lower photometric reconstruction cost than optimization-based baselines, together with encouraging transfer to real captures under our acquisition protocol despite training purely on synthetic data. Additionally, we construct PanoScan, a dataset with 4,370 synthetic and 30 real-world panoramic scenes paired with event streams. Our dataset and code will be released.

AI.tldr: E2Pano is a geometry-guided event-to-panorama pipeline that reconstructs blur-free panoramic images from event cameras under rotational scanning, using a learnable photometric reconstruction stage with spherical coordinates preserved throughout and a spherical Transformer. It outperforms optimization-based baselines in quality and cost, and introduces the PanoScan dataset (4,370 synthetic + 30 real panoramic scenes with event streams).
AI.motivation: Event cameras can enable motion-blur-free panoramic imaging from fast rotational scans due to their microsecond temporal resolution and high dynamic range. However, existing optimization-based methods are computationally expensive, and prior learning-based approaches are designed for perspective imagery without geometry-aware support for panoramic outputs.
