AI.method: KAFR operates in three stages: (1) a fine-tuned YOLO model detects and segments surgical tools; (2) frames are adaptively selected based on tool displacement or velocity variation; (3) an X3D model classifies the selected frames into seven surgical phases.
AI.result: KAFR achieved a 91.0% F1 score using only 0.58% of frames for phase classification, representing approximately a seven-fold reduction compared to typical 4% frame sampling, while maintaining performance comparable to LoViT (90.2%) and Trans-SVNet (89.7%).
AI.conclusion: The results demonstrate that kinematics-based frame selection effectively transfers to the challenging laparoscopic environment, showing promise for reducing computational burden in surgical video analysis across domains.

title: One Query, Many Scales: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts for Efficient Hierarchical Cross-View Geo-Localization
summary: Cross-view geo-localization (CVGL) retrieves geo-tagged satellite imagery for a ground-view query. Most systems exhaustively search a flat, fixed-resolution gallery, incurring high cost over large areas and adapting poorly to satellite resolution changes. Autoregressive coarse-to-fine alternatives reduce comparisons but bind later predictions to earlier decisions and a predefined hierarchy. We introduce GeoMoE, a sparse mixture-of-experts dual encoder that decouples global multi-scale representation learning from local hierarchical search. Global multi-scale supervision and content-adaptive routing map ground and satellite images across resolutions into a globally comparable embedding space. At inference, each image is encoded once, and probabilistic beam search follows parent--child links to score a small candidate subset. Later levels reuse these descriptors rather than features generated by preceding levels, limiting feature-level error propagation and hierarchy coupling. We further introduce VIGOR-M, a four-city benchmark with an explicit parent--child satellite hierarchy and held-out half-step galleries for single-resolution, cross-resolution, and hierarchical evaluation. GeoMoE achieves 95.78% R@40m on Just Zoom In, 2.77 percentage points above the previous best, and 62.39% R@1 on VIGOR-M. The latter requires 0.885 MMAC/query for descriptor matching, 5.27% of an exhaustive L3 scan, while exceeding the strongest exhaustive baseline by 3.12 percentage points in R@1. One model trained on L1, L2, and L3 also outperforms a matched dense control across all six galleries and transfers to three withheld resolutions. By decoupling globally trained embeddings from local hierarchical search, GeoMoE jointly improves localization accuracy, search efficiency, and cross-resolution transfer.

AI.tldr: GeoMoE is a sparse mixture-of-experts dual encoder for cross-view geo-localization that decouples global multi-scale representation learning from local hierarchical search, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy and efficiency with a new VIGOR-M benchmark.
AI.motivation: Existing CVGL systems either exhaustively search flat fixed-resolution galleries (high cost, poor adaptation to resolution changes) or use autoregressive coarse-to-fine approaches that couple predictions to earlier decisions and predefined hierarchies. A decoupled approach is needed.
AI.method: GeoMoE uses a sparse mixture-of-experts dual encoder with global multi-scale supervision and content-adaptive routing to map ground and satellite images across resolutions into a shared embedding space. At inference, each image is encoded once, and probabilistic beam search follows parent-child links to score a small candidate subset while reusing prior descriptors to avoid error propagation.
AI.result: GeoMoE achieves 95.78% R@40m on Just Zoom In (2.77 pp above previous best) and 62.39% R@1 on VIGOR-M, requiring only 5.27% of the compute of exhaustive L3 scan while exceeding the strongest exhaustive baseline by 3.12 pp. A single model outperforms a matched dense control across all six galleries and transfers to three withheld resolutions.
AI.conclusion: By decoupling globally trained embeddings from local hierarchical search, GeoMoE jointly improves localization accuracy, search efficiency, and cross-resolution transfer.

title: ReACT-CLIP: Response-Aware Test-Time Defense for Vision--Language Models
summary: Training-free test-time defenses offer a practical way to improve the adversarial robustness of CLIP-style vision--language models without modifying the pretrained model. However, their correction strength is typically fixed for a narrow range of attack budgets, even though the attack budget is unknown at inference and the required correction varies across samples. We show that this mismatch causes existing defenses to degrade sharply as attacks strengthen. We introduce ReACT-CLIP, a response-conditioned test-time defense that separately determines how strongly each input should be corrected and whether defensive intervention is necessary. Our key observation is that the relative increase in CLIP visual-feature drift between low- and high-noise probes provides a graded, sample-specific proxy for correction demand. ReACT-CLIP maps this relative cross-noise drift to the Gaussian noise scale used to construct a stable, noise-averaged feature anchor, enabling the corrective reach to adapt to each input. To determine whether intervention is necessary, we further observe that clean inputs retain stable class-probability distributions under weak spatial augmentations, whereas adversarial inputs exhibit greater variation. ReACT-CLIP quantifies this variation using a prediction-instability score computed by Jensen--Shannon divergence and combines it with relative cross-noise drift to form the defensive intervention score. ReACT-CLIP requires no model or prompt training, and its correction-strength mapping is calibrated once and fixed across datasets and attack budgets. Across 12 downstream datasets, as well as ImageNet and its distribution-shifted variants, ReACT-CLIP delivers substantial robustness gains across diverse attack types and strengths while largely preserving clean accuracy.

AI.tldr: ReACT-CLIP is a training-free test-time defense for CLIP models that adapts correction strength per-sample by measuring relative cross-noise visual-feature drift, and decides whether intervention is needed via a prediction-instability score computed with Jensen-Shannon divergence under weak spatial augmentations.
AI.motivation: Existing training-free test-time defenses for CLIP use fixed correction strength for a narrow attack budget range, but attack budgets are unknown at inference and required correction varies per sample. This mismatch causes existing defenses to degrade sharply under stronger attacks.
AI.method: ReACT-CLIP computes a relative cross-noise drift (between low- and high-noise probes of visual features) as a sample-specific proxy for correction demand, mapping it to a Gaussian noise scale for constructing a noise-averaged feature anchor. A prediction-instability score (Jensen-Shannon divergence) under weak spatial augmentations is combined with the drift to form a defensive intervention score, deciding whether correction is necessary. No training is required; the correction-strength mapping is calibrated once and fixed.
AI.result: Across 12 downstream datasets, ImageNet, and distribution-shifted variants, ReACT-CLIP provides substantial robustness gains across diverse attack types and strengths while largely preserving clean accuracy.
AI.conclusion: ReACT-CLIP demonstrates that sample-adaptive, response-conditioned test-time defense can effectively handle unknown and varying attack budgets without model modification or training, overcoming the limitations of fixed-strength defenses.

title: PlantRig - From Bones to Branches: Adaptation of Autoregressive Rigging Models for Plant Skeletal Reconstruction
summary: Autoregressive rigging models such as UniRig and SkinTokens perform well on articulated characters, but their ability to generalize to plant structures remains largely unexplored, since plant topologies exhibit highly variable, non-canonical branching patterns that challenge learned skeletal priors. We evaluate these models for plant skeletal reconstruction using synthetic L-system-generated trees and real scanned data spanning monopodial, sympodial, whorled, and vine-like archetypes. Preliminary testing showed UniRig collapsing complex branching into near-linear chains, while SkinTokens preserved topology better but over-segmented branches and produced an unstable output space, so we focused on UniRig for its greater stability. Diagnosis traced the collapse to sampling-level suppression of branch tokens, and further analysis showed the frozen mesh encoder had limited sensitivity to structural variation, pointing to a geometric bottleneck in the tokenization pipeline rather than a purely learned bias. Building on these findings, we applied multi-round fine-tuning over multiple procedurally generated synthetic datasets. Across rounds, the model progressively recovered accurate branching topology and generalized beyond branch-only structures to plants with foliage, a harder case given the zero-thickness, mesh-normal-dependent geometry of leaves. The resulting model generalized well across diverse plant forms without leaf-specific architectural changes, indicating that targeted fine-tuning can substantially close the domain gap between character-rigging priors and plant skeletal structure. As such, our work points toward a viable path for automated plant rigging across both branch topology and foliage type, even those not considered in our findings.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether autoregressive rigging models (UniRig, SkinTokens) trained on articulated characters can generalize to plant skeletal reconstruction. UniRig was found more stable and was fine-tuned over multiple rounds on synthetic L-system trees, progressively recovering accurate branching topology and generalizing to foliage, closing the domain gap without architectural changes.
AI.motivation: Plant structures have highly variable, non-canonical branching patterns that challenge learned skeletal priors from character-rigging models. Whether existing autoregressive rigging models can generalize to plants remains unexplored, motivating an evaluation of their suitability for plant skeletal reconstruction.
AI.method: Evaluate UniRig and SkinTokens on plant skeletal reconstruction using synthetic L-system-generated trees and real scanned data across multiple plant archetypes (monopodial, sympodial, whorled, vine-like). Diagnose failure modes (branch token suppression, frozen mesh encoder bottleneck), then apply multi-round fine-tuning on procedurally generated synthetic datasets.
AI.result: UniRig initially collapsed branching into near-linear chains but progressively recovered accurate branching topology through multi-round fine-tuning. The model generalized to foliage (harder zero-thickness, mesh-normal-dependent geometry) without leaf-specific architectural changes, and generalized across diverse plant forms.
AI.conclusion: Targeted multi-round fine-tuning can substantially close the domain gap between character-rigging priors and plant skeletal structure, pointing toward a viable path for automated plant rigging across branch topology and foliage types.

title: Lethe: How Hard Is It to Forget? A Benchmark for Federated Unlearning in Medical Imaging
summary: Federated learning enables medical-imaging models to be trained across hospitals, and privacy law, most explicitly the GDPR ``right to be forgotten'', turns removing a hospital's, a class's, or a patient's influence from such a model into a federated unlearning problem. This need is most acute in medicine, where patients withdraw consent and hospitals leave collaborations. Yet nearly all unlearning evidence comes from natural images, whose heterogeneity and task structure differ sharply from clinical data, so it is unclear whether existing methods transfer, and no shared protocol covers clinical data. We present Lethe, a benchmark for federated unlearning in medical imaging. It evaluates twelve methods across eight task families, from classification and segmentation to denoising, cross-modality synthesis, and vision-language question answering, at three forgetting granularities and against a retrained gold standard on utility, privacy, and cost. The central result is that what separates methods is the difficulty of the forgetting request, not the method itself. The easy removals that dominate the literature leave the methods that preserve utility indistinguishable, while only hard ones separate them. More striking, on the many medical tasks that generalize across sites, forgetting a client barely changes task performance, leaving residual membership as the signal that must be erased.

AI.tldr: Lethe is a benchmark for federated unlearning in medical imaging, evaluating 12 methods across 8 task families (classification to vision-language QA) at three forgetting granularities. The key finding is that task difficulty, not the method, separates performance; easy removals leave methods indistinguishable, while hard removals discriminate them. On tasks generalizing across sites, forgetting a client barely affects performance, making residual membership the key signal to erase.
AI.motivation: Federated learning in medicine must comply with privacy law (GDPR "right to be forgotten"), requiring removal of a hospital's, class's, or patient's influence from models. However, existing unlearning evidence comes mostly from natural images with different heterogeneity and task structure, and no shared protocol covers clinical data, leaving uncertainty whether existing methods transfer to medical imaging.
AI.method: The authors present Lethe, a comprehensive benchmark for federated unlearning in medical imaging. It evaluates 12 unlearning methods across 8 task families (classification, segmentation, denoising, cross-modality synthesis, vision-language QA) at 3 forgetting granularities, comparing against a retrained gold standard on utility, privacy, and cost.
AI.result: Task difficulty, not the choice of method, is the primary differentiator. Easy removal requests (which dominate the literature) leave utility-preserving methods indistinguishable, while only hard requests separate them. On many medical tasks that generalize across sites, removing a client barely affects task performance, making residual membership the crucial signal that must be erased.
AI.conclusion: The benchmark reveals that current easy-only evaluations are insufficient for clinical settings; hard forgetting scenarios are needed to differentiate methods, and privacy-focused metrics (membership erasure) are essential, especially for cross-site-generalizing medical tasks where utility changes are minimal.

title: SSR: Similarity-Shift Refinement for Training-Free Object-Centric Masks
summary: Object-centric models often produce fragmented masks, boundary leakage, and incorrect region merging. We introduce Similarity-Shift Refinement (SSR), a training-free post-hoc method for improving object-centric masks with a frozen self-supervised Vision Transformer. SSR measures changes in pairwise patch similarity before and after self-attention value aggregation, retains positively strengthened relations, and constructs a sparse affinity graph. This graph propagates the initial soft slot assignments in a single refinement step, without retraining or modifying either model. Across natural-image, synthetic-video, and real-world-video benchmarks, SSR improves all-pixel Adjusted Rand Index in all 24 evaluated model-dataset combinations, with an average gain of 8.5 percentage points. Ablations show that value-space similarity shifts outperform query- and key-space variants as well as static Transformer affinities. However, texture-dense scenes may cause visually similar regions to be over-grouped. Overall, SSR provides a simple and transferable signal for training-free object-centric mask refinement.

AI.tldr: SSR is a training-free post-hoc refinement method that leverages frozen self-supervised ViT patch similarity shifts (before/after self-attention value aggregation) to build a sparse affinity graph, which propagates initial soft slot assignments in a single step. It improves object-centric masks across all 24 evaluated model-dataset combinations, with an average +8.5 percentage points in all-pixel ARI.
AI.motivation: Existing object-centric models frequently produce fragmented masks, boundary leakage, and incorrect region merging, motivating a need for effective mask refinement that does not require retraining or modifying the base models.
AI.method: SSR computes the change in pairwise patch similarity before and after self-attention value aggregation in a frozen self-supervised ViT. It keeps only positively strengthened relations, builds a sparse affinity graph, and propagates the initial soft slot assignments through it in a single refinement step—requiring no training.
AI.result: Across natural-image, synthetic-video, and real-world-video benchmarks, SSR improves all-pixel Adjusted Rand Index in all 24 model-dataset combinations, with an average gain of 8.5 percentage points. Ablations confirm value-space similarity shifts outperform query/key-space variants and static Transformer affinities.
AI.conclusion: SSR offers a simple, transferable, training-free signal for object-centric mask refinement, though texture-dense scenes may cause visually similar regions to be over-grouped.

title: From Patches to Evidence Balls: Class-Conditioned Evidence Retrieval for Few-Shot Whole Slide Image Classification
summary: Whole slide image (WSI) classification is an evidence-driven task, where diagnostic cues are often sparse, spatially organized, and class-dependent. Existing MIL and vision-language methods aggregate a large pool of patch features into a single global slide representation. Under few-shot supervision, limited slide-level labels make it difficult to learn a reliable aggregation mechanism that organizes sparse local cues into compact and coherent diagnostic evidence. Moreover, a shared slide representation compresses evidence supporting a candidate class and its alternatives into the same feature, limiting class-specific reasoning and interpretability. To address these issues, we propose EviBall, a class-conditioned evidence retrieval framework for few-shot WSI classification. EviBall organizes local patches into Evidence Balls through semantic-spatial assignment and center refinement, yielding compact and spatially coherent evidence units under weak supervision. It then uses task-specific class queries, including language-guided queries for morphology-oriented tasks and molecular-guided queries for molecular endpoint prediction, to retrieve supporting evidence balls and produce class-conditioned evidence representations for direct class-wise prediction. By introducing structured evidence units and task-relevant semantic guidance, EviBall reduces the reliance on learning an unconstrained global aggregation mechanism from scarce slide-level labels. It therefore reformulates few-shot WSI classification as structured evidence retrieval and competition among candidate classes. Extensive experiments across four morphology-oriented and molecular endpoint WSI tasks demonstrate that EviBall consistently outperforms conventional and vision-language MIL baselines under diverse few-shot settings, while providing spatially localized and class-specific evidence for each prediction.

AI.tldr: EviBall is a class-conditioned evidence retrieval framework for few-shot whole slide image (WSI) classification that organizes patches into Evidence Balls, retrieves supporting evidence via task-specific class queries, and performs class-wise prediction, outperforming MIL baselines across morphology and molecular tasks.
AI.motivation: Existing MIL and vision-language methods aggregate all patch features into a single global slide representation, which fails under few-shot supervision because limited labels make it hard to learn reliable aggregation of sparse diagnostic cues. Additionally, a shared representation compresses evidence for both target and alternative classes, limiting interpretability and class-specific reasoning.
AI.method: EviBall organizes local patches into Evidence Balls via semantic-spatial assignment and center refinement to form compact, spatially coherent evidence units. It then uses task-specific class queries (language-guided for morphology, molecular-guided for molecular endpoints) to retrieve supporting evidence balls and produce class-conditioned evidence representations for direct class-wise prediction, reformulating few-shot WSI classification as structured evidence retrieval and competition.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across four morphology-oriented and molecular endpoint WSI tasks show EviBall consistently outperforms conventional and vision-language MIL baselines under diverse few-shot settings, while providing spatially localized and class-specific evidence for each prediction.
AI.conclusion: By introducing structured evidence units and task-relevant semantic guidance, EviBall reduces reliance on learning unconstrained global aggregation from scarce labels, effectively addressing few-shot WSI classification with improved accuracy and interpretability.

title: SG-Layout: Structured Scene Graph-Guided Layout Generation with LLMs
summary: Understanding and generating spatially coherent layouts from natural language remains a fundamental yet challenging task for large language models (LLMs). Existing LLMs often struggle to capture explicit geometric relationships and structural dependencies between objects. To address this issue, we propose SG-Layout, a graph-guided layout generation framework that explicitly incorporates structured spatial knowledge into LLMs. SG-Layout follows a two-stage training paradigm: (1) a graph-language feature alignment stage, where a relational graph encoder and a projector are trained to map scene-graph embeddings into the LLM's linguistic space; and (2) an instruction tuning stage, where LoRA-based adapters enable efficient fine-tuning for instruction-driven layout generation while keeping the backbone frozen. We evaluate SG-Layout on image layout generation, indoor scene synthesis and robotic object rearrangement tasks. Experimental results show that SG-Layout improves spatial reasoning accuracy and geometric consistency over the compact open-source backbone, with particularly clear advantages in relation-dense and compositionally complex scenes. These results highlight the effectiveness of graph-structured feature alignment for enhancing controllable layout generation.

AI.tldr: SG-Layout is a graph-guided layout generation framework that incorporates structured spatial knowledge into LLMs via a two-stage training paradigm, improving spatial reasoning and geometric consistency across image layout, indoor scene synthesis, and robotic rearrangement tasks.
AI.motivation: Existing LLMs struggle to capture explicit geometric relationships and structural dependencies between objects when generating spatially coherent layouts from natural language descriptions.
AI.method: A two-stage training paradigm: (1) graph-language feature alignment, where a relational graph encoder and projector map scene-graph embeddings into the LLM's linguistic space; (2) instruction tuning with LoRA-based adapters for efficient fine-tuning while keeping the backbone frozen.
AI.result: SG-Layout improves spatial reasoning accuracy and geometric consistency over compact open-source backbones, with particular advantages in relation-dense and compositionally complex scenes across image layout generation, indoor scene synthesis, and robotic object rearrangement.
AI.conclusion: Graph-structured feature alignment is effective for enhancing controllable layout generation in LLMs.

title: CoT-Edit: Let CoT Guide Instruction Video Editing
summary: Text-driven instruction-based video editing in complex scenes remains challenging: purely textual prompts often fail to capture precise spatial relationships and physical constraints, resulting in target ambiguity and physically implausible outcomes. To address this, we propose a plan--guide--edit framework that explicitly bridges semantic intent and spatial execution. In our framework, a Chain-of-Thought (CoT)-enhanced multimodal large language model (MLLM) serves as a planner, performing structured reasoning over the video and instructions to derive a precise sequence of bounding boxes and attribute-enriched editing directives. These spatial priors then guide a box-conditioned mask generator, transforming ambiguous global retrieval into localized, context-aware refinement and producing masks that more accurately capture object scale, contact relationships, and placement. Building on these spatial and semantic signals, a diffusion-based editor integrates the masks, enriched instructions, and frame features to render high-fidelity edits that remain temporally coherent and spatially well aligned. Trained first in a modular manner and then jointly, our framework achieves superior performance with reduced data requirements, delivering precise localization in scenes with multiple similar objects and physically consistent object additions, and extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance over multiple strong baseline methods. More details are available at: https://github.com/flying-sky999/CoT-Edit

AI.tldr: This paper proposes CoT-Edit, a plan-guide-edit framework for text-driven instruction-based video editing that uses a CoT-enhanced multimodal LLM planner to derive spatial bounding boxes and editing directives, a box-conditioned mask generator for localized refinement, and a diffusion-based editor for temporally coherent, high-fidelity edits, achieving state-of-the-art performance in complex scenes with multiple similar objects.
AI.motivation: Purely textual prompts in instruction-based video editing fail to capture precise spatial relationships and physical constraints, leading to target ambiguity and physically implausible outcomes in complex scenes. There is a gap between semantic intent and spatial execution that existing methods cannot bridge.
AI.method: A three-stage plan-guide-edit framework: (1) a CoT-enhanced MLLM planner performs structured reasoning to derive precise bounding box sequences and attribute-enriched editing directives; (2) a box-conditioned mask generator converts global retrieval into localized, context-aware refinement producing accurate masks; (3) a diffusion-based editor integrates masks, enriched instructions, and frame features for temporally coherent and spatially aligned rendering. Training is modular first, then joint.
AI.result: Superior performance with reduced data requirements, precise localization in scenes with multiple similar objects, physically consistent object additions, and state-of-the-art results over multiple strong baselines.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly bridging semantic intent and spatial execution through spatial priors (bounding boxes and masks) effectively addresses the limitations of purely text-driven video editing, demonstrating that a plan-guide-edit paradigm improves both accuracy and physical plausibility.

title: MiniWorld: Democratizing the Training of Video World Models from Scratch
summary: Video world models predict future observations conditioned on historical observations and control signals, enabling long-horizon generation through autoregressive state transitions. Unlike conventional video generation models that primarily capture visual appearance and motion, video world models learn the underlying dynamics governing environment evolution under agent actions, providing a foundation for embodied AI and interactive simulation. Recent progress has largely relied on adapting pretrained video generation models through post-training or distillation. Although effective, these approaches often require complex training pipelines, substantial computational resources, and suffer from the mismatch between bidirectional pretraining and causal streaming inference. Recent studies have shown that training autoregressive video world models from scratch is feasible and scalable. However, the community still lacks a lightweight, transparent, and fully reproducible baseline trainable end-to-end with modest computational resources. We present MiniWorld, a reproducible framework for training streaming video world models from scratch. MiniWorld employs a block-causal Video Diffusion Transformer trained with Flow Matching in the latent space of a pretrained Video VAE. Building on Diffusion Forcing, it adopts a chunk-wise non-decreasing noise schedule and two-stage continued training to improve temporal modeling and stability. During inference, MiniWorld combines a rolling KV cache with pipelined asynchronous denoising for efficient streaming generation under bounded computation. The entire model can be trained within several days on a single 8-GPU server. By releasing the training and inference codebase and pretrained checkpoints, we hope MiniWorld will facilitate future research on video world modeling.

AI.tldr: MiniWorld is a reproducible framework for training streaming video world models from scratch, using a block-causal Video Diffusion Transformer with Flow Matching, chunk-wise noise scheduling, and efficient streaming inference with KV caching and pipelined denoising—all trainable on a single 8-GPU server in days.
AI.motivation: Existing video world models rely on adapting pretrained video generation models, which requires complex pipelines, high compute, and suffers from bidirectional-pretraining vs. causal-inference mismatch. While training from scratch is feasible, there is no lightweight, transparent, fully reproducible end-to-end baseline that runs with modest computational resources.
AI.method: MiniWorld uses a block-causal Video Diffusion Transformer (Video DiT) trained with Flow Matching in the latent space of a pretrained Video VAE. It builds on Diffusion Forcing with a chunk-wise non-decreasing noise schedule and two-stage continued training for temporal modeling and stability. At inference, it combines a rolling KV cache with pipelined asynchronous denoising to enable efficient streaming generation under bounded computation.
AI.result: The full model can be trained within several days on a single 8-GPU server, and the framework is fully reproducible with released training/inference codebase and pretrained checkpoints.
AI.conclusion: By providing a lightweight, transparent, and reproducible baseline, MiniWorld aims to facilitate future research on video world modeling and lower the barrier to entry for the community.

title: InteracVid: Building a Real Interactive Audio-Visual Response Dataset from Live-Chat Videos
summary: Large language models have made text the default medium for human--AI interaction, buttext alone cannot express the full range of responses required by multimodal assistants,avatars, and embodied agents. While recent audio-video generative models can synthesizehigh-fidelity synchronized content, existing supervision is largely \emph{descriptive}:models are trained to render captions rather than to produce audio-visual responsescaused by external user interactions. We introduce \textbf{InteracVid}, \emph{the firstopen-source large-scale dataset that addresses this missing supervision}, so that everysample couples a preceding audio-visual context and an external stimulus with the realinteractive response that follows. We design a metadata-aware pipeline that extractsinteractive clips from long, noisy livestreams, yielding over \textbf{454K}context-query-response triplets from more than \textbf{59K} livestream videos andspanning conversation-centered, object-centric, procedural, embodied, and screen-basedscenarios. A ten-rater human study confirms that the extracted interactions are causal,natural, and temporally complete for both genuine and reconstructed queries. On aheld-out benchmark of \textbf{100} genuine live-chat queries, fine-tuning on InteracVidimproves both interaction planning and audio-video response generation, and anindependent human evaluation reproduces the system ranking and the conclusions obtainedwith our automatic judge. These results highlight interaction-structured data as acritical foundation for interactive multimodal generation.

AI.tldr: InteracVid is the first open-source large-scale dataset providing causal context-query-response triplets for interactive audio-visual generation, extracted from 59K+ livestream videos to yield over 454K triplets spanning diverse interaction scenarios, with human-validated quality and demonstrated improvements in interaction planning and audio-video response generation.
AI.motivation: Existing audio-video generative models are trained on descriptive supervision (rendering captions) rather than causal supervision (responses caused by external user interactions), creating a missing supervision gap for interactive multimodal assistants, avatars, and embodied agents that must respond to real-world stimuli.
AI.method: A metadata-aware pipeline extracts interactive clips from long, noisy livestreams, coupling preceding audio-visual context and an external stimulus (query) with the real interactive response that follows, producing context-query-response triplets spanning conversation-centered, object-centric, procedural, embodied, and screen-based scenarios.
AI.result: Over 454K context-query-response triplets from 59K+ livestream videos; a ten-rater human study confirms interactions are causal, natural, and temporally complete; on a 100-genuine-query held-out benchmark, fine-tuning on InteracVid improves interaction planning and audio-video response generation, with independent human evaluation reproducing system rankings.
AI.conclusion: Interaction-structured data is a critical foundation for interactive multimodal generation, as it provides the missing causal supervision needed to train models that produce audio-visual responses caused by external user interactions rather than mere descriptive renderings.

title: Think in Sets for Streaming Video Token Compression
summary: Streaming VideoLLMs process frames causally while visual tokens grow continuously, making compression essential for controlling prefilling latency and memory. Existing training-free methods independently rank tokens, ignoring marginal-gain interactions among retained tokens. We argue that streaming video token compression should instead be formulated as set selection, where each candidate is valued by what it adds beyond the tokens already retained. Unlike existing set-wise methods designed for offline tasks, streaming makes causal, frame-by-frame pruning decisions, so modeling cross-frame interactions requires an explicit historical reference. This creates a reference-set dilemma: the reference must adequately represent previously conveyed content while remaining bounded for real-time inference. We introduce NovaCov, to our knowledge the first training-free, plug-and-play set-wise token compressor designed for streaming video. NovaCov maintains a capacity-bounded, recency-weighted Historical Reference Bank and optimizes a dual-branch submodular coverage objective that preserves representative current-frame content while prioritizing information insufficiently covered by history. Both branches are facility-location functions, so greedy selection retains the classical (1-1/e) approximation guarantee. Across streaming and offline benchmarks, NovaCov outperforms existing training-free compression methods, retaining 99.6% of ReKV accuracy while reducing LLM prefilling latency by 46%.

AI.tldr: NovaCov is the first training-free, plug-and-play set-wise token compressor for streaming video LLMs. It maintains a capacity-bounded, recency-weighted Historical Reference Bank and uses a dual-branch submodular coverage objective to preserve current-frame content while prioritizing information not well covered by history, achieving 99.6% of ReKV accuracy with 46% prefilling latency reduction.
AI.motivation: Streaming VideoLLMs face unbounded growth of visual tokens, making compression essential. Existing training-free methods independently rank tokens and ignore marginal-gain interactions among retained tokens. The key insight is that streaming token compression should be formulated as set selection where each candidate is valued by its additive contribution beyond already retained tokens. However, streaming's causal, frame-by-frame nature creates a reference-set dilemma: the historical reference must represent prior content while remaining bounded for real-time inference.
AI.method: NovaCov introduces a set-wise token compression framework with two key components: (1) a capacity-bounded, recency-weighted Historical Reference Bank that represents previously conveyed content while remaining bounded for real-time inference, and (2) a dual-branch submodular coverage objective that preserves representative current-frame content while prioritizing information insufficiently covered by history. Both branches use facility-location functions, which enables greedy selection to retain the classical (1-1/e) approximation guarantee.
AI.result: Across streaming and offline benchmarks, NovaCov outperforms existing training-free compression methods, retaining 99.6% of ReKV accuracy while reducing LLM prefilling latency by 46%.
AI.conclusion: NovaCov demonstrates that formulating streaming video token compression as set selection with explicit historical reference modeling yields superior results compared to independent token ranking approaches, achieving near-lossless accuracy with substantial latency reduction.

title: DynActiveGS: Active Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Scene Reconstruction
summary: We present DynActiveGS, a dynamic-aware active reconstruction framework based on 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) for autonomous exploration in dynamic environments. The framework incrementally reconstructs a 3D Gaussian scene representation while suppressing motion-corrupted observations through online uncertainty prediction and uncertainty-weighted Gaussian optimization. A key component of DynActiveGS is the explicit decomposition of uncertainty into structural uncertainty and motion-induced uncertainty, which enables the system to distinguish under-reconstructed static regions from dynamically unreliable areas. Based on these uncertainty fields, DynActiveGS performs dynamic-aware viewpoint selection and dynamic-constrained path planning to favor informative yet stable observations during exploration. The resulting system forms a unified closed-loop pipeline for robust active reconstruction in dynamic scenes. Extensive experiments on challenging dynamic benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over existing active reconstruction baselines in reconstruction accuracy, completeness, rendering quality, and exploration efficiency.

AI.tldr: DynActiveGS is a dynamic-aware active reconstruction framework based on 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) for autonomous exploration in dynamic environments. It incrementally reconstructs 3D Gaussian scenes while suppressing motion-corrupted observations via online uncertainty prediction and uncertainty-weighted optimization. The framework decomposes uncertainty into structural and motion-induced components, enabling dynamic-aware viewpoint selection and dynamic-constrained path planning in a unified closed-loop pipeline. Experiments show consistent improvements over existing baselines in accuracy, completeness, rendering quality, and exploration efficiency.
AI.motivation: Existing active reconstruction methods for 3DGS-based autonomous exploration typically assume static environments, but real-world scenes contain dynamic objects that corrupt observations and degrade reconstruction quality. The paper addresses this gap by explicitly modeling and suppressing motion-induced uncertainty during active exploration.
AI.method: The framework incrementally reconstructs 3D Gaussian scenes with online uncertainty prediction and uncertainty-weighted optimization to suppress motion-corrupted observations. It explicitly decomposes uncertainty into structural uncertainty (under-reconstructed static regions) and motion-induced uncertainty (dynamically unreliable areas). Based on these uncertainty fields, it performs dynamic-aware viewpoint selection and dynamic-constrained path planning, forming a unified closed-loop pipeline.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on challenging dynamic benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over existing active reconstruction baselines in reconstruction accuracy, completeness, rendering quality, and exploration efficiency.
AI.conclusion: DynActiveGS provides a robust unified pipeline for active reconstruction in dynamic scenes by explicitly distinguishing and handling structural versus motion-induced uncertainty, leading to improved reconstruction and exploration performance over existing methods.

title: 3DZip: Spatial-Aware Feature Diversity-Guided Token Compression for 3D Question Answering
comment: Accepted to ECCV 2026. Project page: https://cvsp-lab.github.io/3DZip
summary: Recent 3D vision-language models (3D VLMs) construct geometry aware tokens by projecting 2D visual features into world coordinates, enabling spatial reasoning for tasks such as 3D question answering. However, this design generates thousands of tokens per scene, resulting in substantial computational and memory overhead. While token compression has been extensively studied in 2D VLMs, existing approaches rely on semantic relevance or attention-based selection that overlook the structured spatial nature of 3D tokens. Moreover, redundancy in 3D representations cannot be resolved by spatial proximity alone, as object-level token imbalance persists even after spatial aggregation. To address this, we propose 3DZip, a three-stage token compression framework that first applies coarse voxelization to remove point-level redundancy, then selects anchor tokens based on feature-space diversity via a Determinantal Point Process, and finally merges remaining tokens under spatial constraints to preserve geometric coherence. Experiments on three 3D question answering benchmarks demonstrate that 3DZip consistently outperforms existing compression methods, retaining 94.7% of the original performance with only 128 tokens, achieving a $1.92\times$ faster inference speed.

AI.tldr: 3DZip is a three-stage token compression framework for 3D vision-language models that reduces thousands of geometry-aware tokens to just 128 while retaining 94.7% of original performance and achieving 1.92× faster inference.
AI.motivation: 3D VLMs generate thousands of tokens per scene by projecting 2D visual features into world coordinates, creating substantial computational and memory overhead. Existing 2D token compression methods rely on semantic relevance or attention-based selection that overlook the structured spatial nature of 3D tokens, and spatial proximity alone cannot resolve object-level token imbalance.
AI.method: 3DZip is a three-stage token compression framework: (1) coarse voxelization to remove point-level redundancy, (2) anchor token selection based on feature-space diversity via a Determinantal Point Process (DPP), and (3) merging remaining tokens under spatial constraints to preserve geometric coherence.
AI.result: Experiments on three 3D question answering benchmarks show 3DZip consistently outperforms existing compression methods, retaining 94.7% of original performance with only 128 tokens and achieving 1.92× faster inference speed.
AI.conclusion: 3DZip demonstrates that a spatial-aware, multi-stage compression approach effectively handles the unique redundancy patterns in 3D representations, enabling efficient 3D VLMs without significant performance loss.

title: QuerySplat: Decoupling Geometry and Appearance Representations in 3DGS Prediction
summary: While feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables efficient 3D reconstruction, achieving high-fidelity rendering remains challenging. Existing pixel-aligned approaches suffer from spatial inflexibility and massive structural redundancy, whereas query-based methods lack 3D priors and entangle geometry with appearance, yielding blurry, pose-dependent results. To overcome these deficiencies, we propose \textbf{QuerySplat}, a feed-forward 3DGS framework driven by geometric priors and explicit appearance decoupling. Specifically, we design a dual-branch query-based decoder: the geometry branch leverages a pretrained Vision Geometric Model for spatial understanding, which intrinsically endows QuerySplat with pose-free modeling capabilities, while the appearance branch recovers high-frequency details through a dedicated pathway separated from geometric attribute regression. Extensive experiments demonstrate that QuerySplat mitigates the blurry rendering issues of early query-based models and consistently outperforms pixel-aligned approaches in rendering fidelity. On the challenging DL3DV benchmark, it achieves state-of-the-art novel view synthesis performance, with average PSNR gains of 2.30 dB and 1.04 dB over the best pose-free and pose-required baselines, respectively. Project Page: https://inspatio.github.io/querysplat.

AI.tldr: QuerySplat is a feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting framework with a dual-branch query-based decoder that separates geometry (guided by a pretrained Vision Geometric Model for pose-free spatial understanding) from appearance (dedicated high-frequency detail recovery), achieving state-of-the-art novel view synthesis on DL3DV with 2.30 dB and 1.04 dB PSNR gains over the best pose-free and pose-required baselines.
AI.motivation: Existing feed-forward 3DGS methods fall short: pixel-aligned approaches suffer from spatial inflexibility and structural redundancy, while query-based methods lack 3D priors and entangle geometry with appearance, leading to blurry and pose-dependent rendering.
AI.method: QuerySplat employs a dual-branch query-based decoder. The geometry branch incorporates a pretrained Vision Geometric Model to provide spatial understanding and pose-free modeling capabilities, while a separate appearance branch recovers high-frequency details independently from geometric attribute regression.
AI.result: QuerySplat mitigates blurry rendering of early query-based models, beats pixel-aligned approaches in fidelity, and achieves state-of-the-art performance on the DL3DV benchmark with average PSNR gains of 2.30 dB over best pose-free and 1.04 dB over best pose-required baselines.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling geometry from appearance with geometric priors effectively addresses both blurriness and pose-dependency in feed-forward 3DGS, establishing a new state of the art in novel view synthesis.

title: Fruit-HSNet: A Machine Learning Approach for Hyperspectral Image-Based Fruit Ripeness Prediction
summary: Fruit ripeness prediction (FRP) is a classification-based agricultural computer vision task that has attracted much attention, thanks to its wide-ranging advantages in agriculture field for both pre-harvest and post-harvest management. Accurate and timely FRP can be achieved using machine/deep learning-based hyperspectral image classification techniques. However, challenges including the limited availability of labeled data and the lack of robust methods generalizable to various hyperspectral cameras and fruit types can compromise the effectiveness of hyperspectral image-based FRP. Addressing these challenges, this paper introduces Fruit-HSNet, a machine learning architecture specifically designed for hyperspectral classification of fruit ripeness. Fruit-HSNet incorporates a spatio-spectral feature extraction module based on Fourier Transform and central pixel spectral signature followed by learnable feature fusion and a classifier optimized for ripeness classification. The proposed architecture was evaluated using the DeepHS Fruit dataset, the largest publicly available labeled real-world hyperspectral dataset for predicting fruit ripeness, which includes five different types of fruits-avocado, kiwi, mango, kaki, and papaya-captured with three distinct hyperspectral cameras at various stages of ripeness. Experimental results highlight that Fruit-HSNet substantially outperforms existing deep learning methods, from baseline to state-of-the-art models, with improvements of 12%, achieving a new state-of-the-art overall accuracy of 70.73%.

AI.tldr: Fruit-HSNet is a machine learning architecture for hyperspectral fruit ripeness classification that uses a Fourier Transform-based spatio-spectral feature extraction module with central pixel spectral signatures, followed by learnable feature fusion and an optimized classifier. It achieves 70.73% overall accuracy on the DeepHS Fruit dataset, outperforming existing methods by 12%.
AI.motivation: Fruit ripeness prediction is important for agriculture but faces challenges including limited labeled data and lack of robust methods that generalize across different hyperspectral cameras and fruit types.
AI.method: Fruit-HSNet uses a spatio-spectral feature extraction module based on Fourier Transform and central pixel spectral signatures, followed by learnable feature fusion and a classifier optimized for ripeness classification.
AI.result: Fruit-HSNet outperforms existing baseline and state-of-the-art deep learning methods by 12%, achieving a new state-of-the-art overall accuracy of 70.73% on the DeepHS Fruit dataset.
AI.conclusion: The proposed Fruit-HSNet demonstrates significant improvements in hyperspectral fruit ripeness classification and generalizes across multiple fruit types and hyperspectral cameras.

title: It's the Decoding Format, Not the Perturbation: Auditing Consistency-Based Selection for Vision-Language Test-Time Scaling
summary: Test-time scaling lifts large language model reasoning by sampling many candidate solutions and selecting among them, yet the same recipe transfers poorly to vision-language models (VLMs): recent work shows that simple majority voting beats selection methods built on the model's own self-verification, apparently because at the selection layer an image-grounded answer and a confident guess from the language prior look the same. A natural fix is to make the selection signal one that cannot be computed without the image. We study Perturbation Grounded Selection (Pgs), a label-free, training-free rule that scores each candidate by whether the model re-derives it under label-preserving perturbations of the input (cropping, background masking, mild photometric or geometric jitter); Pgs recovers majority voting when the perturbation set is empty. The decisive question is not whether Pgs beats chain-of-thought only majority voting, but whether the perturbation term adds anything once decoding format and budget are controlled. We therefore introduce a format-matched control (MatchedCtrl): the same short, no-CoT draws spent on the original image. Across TextVQA, MATH-Vision, MMMU, and ViLP, with a Qwen headline (three-seed means) and LLaVA-OneVision coverage in matched-budget selector tables, Pgs appears to beat plain majority voting by up to +31.8 points on TextVQA (Qwen), but MatchedCtrl tracks or exceeds Pgs within noise on every benchmark, including the vision-required ViLP; no Qwen category shows a significant gain over this control. The stability gap is real and image-dependent (up to +0.48), yet does not predict per-instance wins. The result is negative and diagnostic: perturbation consistency is at best a partial diagnostic of visual dependence and, on its own, not a usable selection signal once format is controlled; gains reported against CoT-only majority voting overstate such methods.

AI.tldr: Perturbation Grounded Selection (Pgs), a training-free method that scores candidate VLM answers by re-derivation under image perturbations, fails to beat a matched-format majority voting control across four benchmarks, revealing that perturbation consistency is at best a partial diagnostic of visual dependence and not a usable selection signal.
AI.motivation: Test-time scaling works for LLMs via sampling and selection, but transfers poorly to VLMs because self-verification selection fails to distinguish image-grounded answers from confident language-prior guesses. The paper seeks an image-grounded selection signal that cannot be computed without the image.
AI.method: Proposes Perturbation Grounded Selection (Pgs): score each candidate by whether the model re-derives it under label-preserving input perturbations (cropping, background masking, photometric/geometric jitter). Introduces a format-matched control (MatchedCtrl) using the same short, no-CoT draws on the original image to ensure gains are attributable to the perturbation term rather than decoding format or budget.
AI.result: Pgs beats CoT-only majority voting by up to +31.8 points on TextVQA, but MatchedCtrl tracks or exceeds Pgs within noise on every benchmark including vision-required ViLP. No significant gains over the control observed; the stability gap is real and image-dependent (up to +0.48) but does not predict per-instance wins.
AI.conclusion: The result is negative and diagnostic: perturbation consistency is at best a partial diagnostic of visual dependence and not a usable selection signal once format is controlled. Gains reported against CoT-only majority voting overstate such methods.

title: VaRS-Doc: Interpretation-Aware Variant Representations via Latent Self-Probing for Visual Document Retrieval
summary: Visual document retrieval has recently become increasingly important in applications such as enterprise search, scientific literature discovery, and retrieval-augmented generation. These applications depend on efficiently identifying query-relevant pages across large collections of visually rich documents. Existing methods commonly adopt late-interaction architectures that encode and index documents offline to enable scalable and low-latency online retrieval. Despite its efficiency, this paradigm requires each document to be encoded into a fixed representation before the query is known. However, the same content in a visual document may induce different interpretations depending on the query intent, which a fixed representation struggles to capture. Yet postponing document encoding until the query arrives would incur prohibitive online retrieval latency. To address this gap, we propose VaRS-Doc, a visual document retrieval framework that diversifies document representations by enabling the model to actively explore variant latent interpretations during document encoding, while preserving efficient late-interaction retrieval in which each query adaptively selects the best-fit representation. We further introduce a two-stage training strategy that encourages the model to capture complementary semantic interpretations and prevents it from falling back to train a single dominant representation. Experiments on visual document retrieval benchmarks show that VaRS-Doc achieves state-of-the-art retrieval performance, offering a practical solution to the mismatch between query-agnostic document encoding and query-specific retrieval needs. Code is available at https://github.com/bokufa/VaRS-Doc.

AI.tldr: VaRS-Doc is a visual document retrieval framework that diversifies document representations by actively exploring variant latent interpretations during encoding, while preserving efficient late-interaction retrieval where queries adaptively select the best-fit representation.
AI.motivation: Existing late-interaction retrieval methods encode documents offline into fixed representations before queries are known, but the same visual document content can be interpreted differently depending on query intent. This mismatch between query-agnostic encoding and query-specific needs limits retrieval quality.
AI.method: VaRS-Doc diversifies document representations by having the model explore variant latent interpretations during document encoding, while maintaining late-interaction retrieval where each query adaptively selects the best-fit representation. A two-stage training strategy encourages complementary semantic interpretations and prevents collapse to a single dominant representation.
AI.result: Experiments on visual document retrieval benchmarks show VaRS-Doc achieves state-of-the-art retrieval performance.
AI.conclusion: VaRS-Doc offers a practical solution to the mismatch between query-agnostic document encoding and query-specific retrieval needs, providing state-of-the-art performance without sacrificing retrieval efficiency.

title: From Forest to Future Capital: Tracking Land Cover Change in Ibu Kota Nusantara (IKN) from 2021 to 2026 with PlanetScope Imagery
summary: Indonesia's relocation of its political and administrative capital from Jakarta to Ibu Kota Nusantara (IKN) has been framed around a ``Forest City'' vision, yet rapid construction within the Core Government Area (KIPP) raises concerns over land conversion, vegetation loss, and carbon stock decline. This study applies remote sensing techniques to systematically assess land use and vegetation cover change in KIPP from 2021 to 2026 using PlanetScope SuperDove satellite imagery. Cloud-free mosaics were prepared and analysed through spectral indices, including the Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), Normalised Difference Red Edge (NDRE), and Normalised Difference Water Index (NDWI), alongside supervised land use and land cover (LULC) classification using a Support Vector Machine algorithm. Results show substantial environmental transformation, with mean NDVI declined by 17.1\%, total carbon stock decreased by 0.28\%, developed land expanded by 672\%, and total vegetation declined by 18.1\%. Vegetation loss was most extensive between 2023 and 2024, although a temporary recovery in NDVI and carbon stock occurred from 2024 to 2025 as active clearing slowed and development shifted towards already-cleared land. Overall, the findings demonstrate that remote sensing provides an effective approach for monitoring the environmental impacts of large-scale urban development, while highlighting the need for higher-resolution, hyperspectral, and SAR-based methods to improve detection of construction stages and plantation-related land cover changes.

AI.tldr: This study uses PlanetScope SuperDove satellite imagery and remote sensing techniques (NDVI, NDRE, NDWI indices, and SVM-based LULC classification) to assess land use and vegetation changes in the Core Government Area (KIPP) of Indonesia's new capital IKN from 2021-2026, revealing significant environmental transformation including a 17.1% decline in mean NDVI, 18.1% vegetation loss, and 672% expansion of developed land, with the most severe vegetation loss occurring between 2023-2024.
AI.motivation: The relocation of Indonesia's capital to IKN, despite its "Forest City" framing, raises concerns about land conversion, vegetation loss, and carbon stock decline due to rapid construction in the Core Government Area, motivating a systematic assessment of these environmental impacts using remote sensing.
AI.method: Cloud-free mosaics from PlanetScope SuperDove satellite imagery (2021-2026) were analyzed using spectral indices including NDVI, NDRE, and NDWI, alongside supervised LULC classification employing a Support Vector Machine algorithm to track land use and vegetation cover changes.
AI.result: Mean NDVI declined by 17.1%, total carbon stock decreased by 0.28%, developed land expanded by 672%, and total vegetation declined by 18.1%. Vegetation loss was most extensive between 2023-2024, though a temporary recovery in NDVI and carbon stock occurred from 2024-2025 as development shifted toward already-cleared land.
AI.conclusion: Remote sensing provides an effective approach for monitoring environmental impacts of large-scale urban development, though higher-resolution, hyperspectral, and SAR-based methods are needed to better detect construction stages and plantation-related land cover changes.

title: A Benchmark Dataset for MLLM-Generated Image Detection: GPT Image2 & Nano Banana2
summary: The realism of images generated by multimodal large language models (MLLMs), such as GPT Image2 and Nano Banana2, has improved rapidly in recent years. Compared with early generative models, current models have made clear progress in text rendering. They can produce high-quality images that closely resemble real-world application scenarios. The enhanced generation capabilities of current MLLMs pose increasingly severe challenges to AI-generated image detection. Detection is no longer limited to identifying obvious artifacts left by early generators. Instead, it requires systematic and realistic benchmarks for the new generation of generated content. However, most existing benchmarks are still built around early generative models and cannot fully evaluate the forensic challenges introduced by high-quality and multi-form generated images. To address this gap, this paper constructs a benchmark dataset for detecting images generated by MLLMs. The benchmark covers several realistic application scenarios and adopts three generation protocols to simulate direct generation, reference-based reconstruction, and local editing. Based on this benchmark, we evaluate detector degradation from traditional scenarios to MLLM-generated images and analyze false positive rates and false negative rates across three sample types, revealing the failure modes of existing methods. We further propose a structural-artifact-prior-guided dual-stream prompt framework (SAP-DSP) as a strong baseline. SAP-DSP uses dual-stream prompt learning and structure-aware routing fusion to improve representation learning. Extensive experiments show that the proposed benchmark exposes the performance degradation of existing detectors on high-quality generated images, while SAP-DSP achieves more stable detection results on this benchmark. Our code and dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/xbrainnet/SAP-DSP.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a new benchmark dataset for detecting AI-generated images from multimodal large language models (MLLMs), covering realistic scenarios with three generation protocols (direct generation, reference-based reconstruction, local editing). It evaluates existing detector degradation on high-quality MLLM images, analyzes failure modes, and proposes SAP-DSP, a structural-artifact-prior-guided dual-stream prompt framework that achieves more stable detection results.
AI.motivation: Current MLLMs like GPT Image2 and Nano Banana2 can generate highly realistic images with accurate text rendering, making AI-generated image detection increasingly challenging. However, most existing benchmarks are built around early generative models and cannot fully evaluate the forensic challenges posed by new-generation high-quality and multi-form generated content.
AI.method: The paper constructs a benchmark dataset covering realistic application scenarios with three generation protocols (direct generation, reference-based reconstruction, and local editing). It evaluates detector degradation from traditional to MLLM-generated images, analyzes false positive/negative rates across three sample types, and proposes SAP-DSP, a dual-stream prompt learning framework with structure-aware routing fusion as a strong baseline.
AI.result: The proposed benchmark exposes performance degradation of existing detectors on high-quality MLLM-generated images. SAP-DSP achieves more stable detection results on this benchmark compared to existing methods.
AI.conclusion: The benchmark provides a more realistic and systematic evaluation platform for detecting MLLM-generated images, and the proposed SAP-DSP framework demonstrates more robust detection performance. The code and dataset are publicly released for the research community.

title: Rethinking Video Token Compression with a Global Codebook: Learning Once, Compressing Everywhere
summary: Video large language models (Video-LLMs) represent videos as dense sequences of visual tokens, whose length grows with the temporal and spatial extent of the input. These tokens often contain substantial redundancy arising from repeated visual patterns, leading to unnecessary computation in the subsequent language-model processing. Existing token compression methods, including pruning and merging, perform compression online during inference, repeatedly incurring additional computation for each input video and often relying on model-specific designs that limit their generality, we instead rethink this paradigm by shifting the costly compression process offline. We propose \textbf{ONCE}, a plug-in video token compression framework that introduces an offline-to-online paradigm: a frequency-aware global codebook is learned once in the visual feature space and reused for lightweight online compression through codebook lookup and aggregation, reducing repeated per-video computation and the need for model-specific compression designs. Extensive experiments across multiple video understanding benchmarks and against diverse compression baselines demonstrate that our approach achieves a strong accuracy-efficiency trade-off, maintaining competitive performance while achieving the lowest inference latency among compared methods.

AI.tldr: ONCE is a plug-in video token compression framework that shifts compression from expensive online computation to an offline stage by learning a frequency-aware global codebook in visual feature space, reused via lightweight codebook lookup and aggregation during inference to reduce redundancy in Video-LLMs with minimal latency cost.
AI.motivation: Video-LLMs generate dense, redundant visual tokens whose length grows with input size, causing unnecessary computation. Existing compression methods (pruning/merging) operate online per video, which is computationally costly and often model-specific, limiting generality.
AI.method: ONCE adopts an offline-to-online paradigm: a frequency-aware global codebook is learned once offline in the visual feature space, then reused for lightweight online compression via codebook lookup and aggregation, avoiding per-video repeated computation and model-specific designs.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across multiple video understanding benchmarks show ONCE achieves a strong accuracy-efficiency trade-off, maintaining competitive performance while achieving the lowest inference latency among compared compression baselines.
AI.conclusion: Shifting token compression offline via a reusable global codebook provides an effective, general, and efficient solution for reducing redundancy in Video-LLMs without sacrificing accuracy.

title: Astrolabe: Spherical-Map Guidance Across Diffusion Pipelines for Full-Body Capture from Unconstrained Images
summary: Full-body capture from unconstrained photographs requires global correspondence across arbitrary views, poses, crops, and occlusions. Yet pose, geometry, and foundation features estimated in this setting are too unreliable for dense matching or appearance transfer, while diffusion rectifiers and optimization pipelines expose no common interface for consuming such uncertain correspondence. Our insight is that correspondence need not be locally accurate: its coarse viewpoint and body layout can still organize how a diffusion prior adapts and guides reconstruction. We introduce \emph{Astrolabe}, a host-portable adapter built on frozen viewpoint-guided spherical maps (SPH). A fixed bounded transform converts SPH into a spatial noise shift, which is matched during prior adaptation and reused during downstream denoising or score-distillation guidance in both pipeline categories. When a rectifier exposes a reference router, the same target/reference SPH additionally supplies coarse compatibility scores to select native appearance features; router-free optimization uses only the shared shift path. Astrolabe therefore follows one SPH--shift--adapt--guide process without dense warping or a learned control branch. Across Puzzle-IOI and 4D-Dress, it improves all reported image metrics in both hosts and all paired Puzzle-IOI geometry metrics; image gains extend to rear views, while 4D-Dress geometry remains stable overall.

AI.tldr: Astrolabe is a host-portable adapter that converts coarse viewpoint-guided spherical maps into spatial noise shifts, enabling diffusion priors to adapt and guide reconstruction from unconstrained full-body photographs without requiring dense matching or learned control branches.
AI.motivation: Full-body capture from unconstrained photos requires global correspondence across arbitrary views, poses, crops, and occlusions, but pose, geometry, and foundation features in this setting are too unreliable for dense matching or appearance transfer. Existing diffusion rectifiers and optimization pipelines have no common interface for consuming such uncertain correspondence.
AI.method: Astrolabe uses a frozen viewpoint-guided spherical map (SPH) that is converted into a spatial noise shift via a fixed bounded transform. This shift is matched during prior adaptation and reused during denoising or score-distillation guidance. When a rectifier has a reference router, target/reference SPH supplies coarse compatibility scores to select native appearance features; router-free optimization uses only the shared shift path. The whole process follows a single SPH→shift→adapt→guide pipeline without dense warping or learned control branches.
AI.result: Across Puzzle-IOI and 4D-Dress benchmarks, Astrolabe improves all reported image metrics in both host pipelines and all paired Puzzle-IOI geometry metrics. Image gains extend to rear views, while 4D-Dress geometry remains stable overall.
AI.conclusion: Coarse-level viewpoint and body-layout correspondence from SPH is sufficient to organize how a diffusion prior adapts and guides full-body reconstruction, achieving consistent improvements across both rectifier and optimization-based pipelines.

title: TurboClear: One-Step Object-Effect Removal via Region-Calibrated Distribution Matching and Fusion
summary: Recently, diffusion-based removal methods have achieved promising visual quality in removing both target objects and their associated effects. However, they typically rely on multi-step denoising, leading to high inference cost. Directly applying existing one-step distillation methods is also suboptimal, since their global objectives lack explicit region-wise calibration and may weaken the asymmetric edit-and-preserve behavior required by object-effect removal. To address these challenges, we propose TurboClear, a one-step SDXL-based object-effect removal model. During training, we design Region-Calibrated Distribution Matching (RDM) for region-aware distillation to preserve the teacher model's asymmetric edit-and-preserve behavior. Furthermore, we propose Learnable Spatial Fusion (LSF) for lightweight inference-time fusion. Extensive experiments show that TurboClear significantly improves inference efficiency while maintaining competitive visual quality. TurboClear reduces the computational overhead by up to $40.04\times$ compared to ObjectClear, and by up to $665\times$ against the Flux-based method OmniPaint, all while maintaining comparable or better visual removal quality. Code is available at https://github.com/GuoCalix/TurboClear.

AI.tldr: TurboClear is a one-step SDXL-based object-effect removal model that achieves significant inference speedup (up to 40x vs ObjectClear, 665x vs OmniPaint) while maintaining competitive visual quality, using Region-Calibrated Distribution Matching for region-aware distillation and Learnable Spatial Fusion for lightweight inference-time fusion.
AI.motivation: Existing diffusion-based removal methods achieve good visual quality but rely on multi-step denoising, leading to high inference costs. Directly applying one-step distillation methods is suboptimal because their global objectives lack explicit region-wise calibration and weaken the asymmetric edit-and-preserve behavior required for object-effect removal.
AI.method: Proposes TurboClear, a one-step SDXL-based object-effect removal model. During training, it uses Region-Calibrated Distribution Matching (RDM) for region-aware distillation to preserve the teacher model's asymmetric edit-and-preserve behavior. For inference, it proposes Learnable Spatial Fusion (LSF) for lightweight inference-time fusion.
AI.result: TurboClear significantly improves inference efficiency while maintaining competitive visual quality. It reduces computational overhead by up to 40.04x compared to ObjectClear and up to 665x against the Flux-based method OmniPaint, while maintaining comparable or better visual removal quality.
AI.conclusion: The proposed region-calibrated distillation and learnable spatial fusion enable a one-step diffusion model for object-effect removal that is dramatically more efficient than prior multi-step methods without sacrificing visual quality.

title: UDT: Reconciling U-Nets and Diffusion Transformers with Data-Adaptive Token Reduction
summary: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) have emerged as a core architecture in generative modeling due to their scalability and adaptability to multimodal tasks. DiTs comprise isotropic transformer blocks, and learn representations progressively across depth, where the denoising objective drives later layers to focus on fine-detail reconstruction. This results in degraded representation quality and an imbalanced encoder-decoder behavior. Prior approaches such as representation alignment (REPA) mitigate this by encouraging stronger early representations via training regularization. Alternatively, U-Net-style DiT architectures introduce explicit multi-scale encoder-decoder structures for improved convergence. But they build on standard U-Net wisdom via learnable operators for spatial downsampling, which are not well-suited to transformer architectures, introducing inefficiencies and compatibility issues with components such as cross-attention and representation regularization. In this work, we propose UDT, a U-Net diffusion transformer that combines the representation power of DiTs with the encoding-decoding benefits of U-Nets, through data-adaptive token merging for downsampling and upsampling, while preserving the DiT token dimension. Our baseline UDT architecture outperforms existing U-Net DiTs and achieves performance comparable to REPA across all model sizes. Furthermore, using architectural optimization and REPA, UDT outperforms SiT's 7.9 FID at 1400 epochs (w/o CFG) within 40 epochs (~ 40x faster convergence) for XL model size on 256x256 ImageNet. Finally, it achieves strong image generation performance with CFG, reaching FID of 1.38 (320 epochs) with SD-VAE and 1.35 (500 epochs) with VA-VAE, providing a new backbone for DiTs with strong empirical benefits.

AI.tldr: UDT is a U-Net style Diffusion Transformer that combines DiT representation power with U-Net encoding-decoding benefits through data-adaptive token merging for down/up-sampling, achieving REPA-comparable performance and ~40x faster convergence than SiT.
AI.motivation: DiTs have imbalanced encoder-decoder behavior and degraded representation quality at later layers due to denoising objectives. Existing fixes (REPA via training regularization, or U-Net style structures with learned spatial downsampling) are limited—the latter introducing inefficiencies and compatibility issues with transformer components.
AI.method: UDT employs a U-Net diffusion transformer using data-adaptive token merging for downsampling and upsampling while preserving the DiT token dimension, avoiding learnable operators that are poorly suited to transformers.
AI.result: UDT outperforms existing U-Net DiTs, matches REPA performance across model sizes, achieves SiT's 7.9 FID at 1400 epochs within 40 epochs (~40x faster convergence) on 256x256 ImageNet XL, and reaches FID 1.38 (SD-VAE) and 1.35 (VA-VAE) with CFG.
AI.conclusion: UDT provides a new backbone for DiTs with strong empirical benefits, combining the strengths of both U-Net and transformer architectures.

title: Ranking Image Fusion the Way Humans Do: A Learned Pairwise Preference Metric for Infrared-Visible Fusion Assessment
summary: Infrared-visible image fusion (IVIF) has no ideal fused reference, so fusion algorithms are routinely ranked by scalar objective metrics that formalize different proxies for information transfer, structure, or source similarity. These proxies often disagree with the judgment that ultimately matters: given the same sources, which of two fused results does a human prefer? Direct pairwise comparison is an established reference protocol for relative subjective assessment, but its cost grows quadratically with the number of algorithms, which prevents routine use. We present the Learned Perceptual Image Fusion Measure (LPIFM), a source-conditioned model that operationalizes the human A/B/Tie comparison protocol as a repeatable, scalable surrogate. LPIFM jointly observes the infrared source, the visible source, and two fused candidates, and predicts whether candidate A is better, candidate B is better, or the two are perceptually equivalent. Supervision comes from a new dense preference corpus that covers every unordered comparison among a broad pool of fusion methods on the scenes of a public benchmark, labeled under a blinded, randomized, two-stage protocol with expert adjudication. Across scene- and method-generalization settings, LPIFM tracks human pairwise decisions closely and reproduces the tie-aware Bradley-Terry rankings derived from human labels; on full method pools it surpasses the strongest conventional metric by a wide margin in both pairwise accuracy and ranking correlation. We release the annotated preference dataset, together with the LPIFM model weights, source code, and evaluation code, to support preference-aligned IVIF assessment. LPIFM offers a practical instrument for human-aligned method comparison and ranking at scale.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces LPIFM (Learned Perceptual Image Fusion Measure), a source-conditioned model that predicts human A/B/Tie preferences between two infrared-visible fused outputs, trained on a new dense preference corpus, achieving significantly better alignment with human pairwise judgments than conventional objective metrics.
AI.motivation: Infrared-visible image fusion (IVIF) lacks a ground-truth fused reference, so algorithms are ranked by scalar objective metrics that often disagree with actual human preferences. Direct human pairwise comparison is the gold standard but scales quadratically with the number of fusion methods, preventing routine use.
AI.method: LPIFM is a source-conditioned model that jointly takes the infrared source, visible source, and two fused candidates as input, predicting whether candidate A is better, candidate B is better, or they are perceptually equivalent. It is trained on a new dense preference dataset built via a blinded, randomized, two-stage labeling protocol with expert adjudication, covering all unordered pairwise comparisons among fusion methods on public benchmark scenes.
AI.result: LPIFM closely tracks human pairwise decisions across scene- and method-generalization settings, reproduces tie-aware Bradley-Terry rankings from human labels, and surpasses the strongest conventional metric by a wide margin in both pairwise accuracy and ranking correlation on full method pools.
