AI.conclusion: LPIFM provides a practical, scalable, and human-aligned instrument for IVIF method comparison and ranking, with released resources including the annotated preference dataset, model weights, source code, and evaluation code.

title: Beyond Symmetric Fusion: Exploiting Task-Dependent Modality Strengths for RGB-Event Small Object Detection
summary: State-of-the-art RGB-Event detectors improve the detection of small, fast-moving objects by combining complementary features from RGB and Event data, yet they typically fuse the two modalities into a unified representation for both localization and classification. Such a task-symmetric design is inconsistent with the intuition that the two modalities should play different roles according to their task-specific strengths. To examine this issue, we conduct a modality-specific evaluation and find that the relative advantage of the two modalities reverses across tasks: Event data are substantially more effective for class-agnostic localization, whereas RGB data provide stronger category evidence within localized target regions. Motivated by this task-dependent asymmetry, we propose an Asymmetric Event-RGB Object Detection Transformer (AERODet). During class-agnostic localization, Scale-wise Uncertainty-aware Reliability Estimation (SURE) calculates the relative reliability of the two modalities from their objectness response heatmaps and accordingly calibrates their contributions when the decoder aggregates multimodal features. Once the candidate boxes are obtained, Task-Decoupled Semantic Refinement (TDSR) decouples classification from localization and uses RGB RoI features for fine-grained classification. Extensive experiments on FRED and NeRDD demonstrate that AERODet achieves state-of-the-art performance. In particular, it surpasses the strongest RGB-Event baseline by 10.7 mAP points on the FRED challenging split.

AI.tldr: AERODet is an asymmetric RGB-Event object detection transformer that leverages task-dependent modality asymmetry—using Event data for class-agnostic localization and RGB data for classification—achieving state-of-the-art results, including a 10.7 mAP improvement over the strongest baseline on FRED.
AI.motivation: Existing RGB-Event detectors fuse both modalities symmetrically for both localization and classification, which contradicts the empirical finding that Event data excel at class-agnostic localization while RGB data provide stronger category evidence. The paper motivates a task-asymmetric design based on this observed reversal of modality advantages.
AI.method: AERODet comprises two components: (1) Scale-wise Uncertainty-aware Reliability Estimation (SURE) computes relative reliability of the two modalities from objectness heatmaps to calibrate their contributions during multimodal feature aggregation for localization; (2) Task-Decoupled Semantic Refinement (TDSR) decouples classification from localization and uses RGB RoI features for fine-grained classification.
AI.result: AERODet achieves state-of-the-art performance on FRED and NeRDD datasets, surpassing the strongest RGB-Event baseline by 10.7 mAP points on the FRED challenging split.
AI.conclusion: Task-asymmetric fusion—using Event data for localization and RGB for classification—is more effective than symmetric fusion, validating the task-dependent modality asymmetry hypothesis and providing a new design paradigm for RGB-Event detection.

title: SPAE: Spectrally Guided Autoencoder for Pretrained Visual Latents
summary: Latents from vision foundation models (VFMs) are semantically rich and well suited for visual understanding. Recent representation autoencoder methods such as RAE have shown that they can provide promising latent spaces for image generation. However, VFM latents remain difficult to model directly: DiT-generated latents exhibit spectral mismatch with encoder latents, especially in high-frequency components. Our channel-wise spectral analysis further reveals that these high-frequency components are diffusely distributed across latent channels and entangled with semantic information, making the latent space difficult for DiT to model. To address these challenges, we propose SPAE, latent adaptation framework for generation. Specifically, SPAE employs a compact bottleneck to distill stable semantic information while suppressing high-frequency components, thereby improving the alignment between DiT-generated latents and encoder latents. In addition, we apply a channel-wise masking strategy to promote the decoupling of semantic information and high-frequency details across bottleneck channels. Experiments show that SPAE achieves a favorable balance among visual understanding, generation quality, and reconstruction fidelity.

AI.tldr: SPAE is a latent adaptation framework that addresses the spectral mismatch between vision foundation model (VFM) latents and DiT-generated latents by using a compact bottleneck to distill semantic information while suppressing high-frequency components, combined with channel-wise masking to decouple semantics from high-frequency details, achieving a favorable balance across understanding, generation, and reconstruction.
AI.motivation: VFM latents are semantically rich and good for understanding, but difficult to model directly for generation due to spectral mismatch between DiT-generated latents and encoder latents, especially in high-frequency components that are diffusely distributed across channels and entangled with semantic information.
AI.method: SPAE employs a compact bottleneck to distill stable semantic information while suppressing high-frequency components, and applies a channel-wise masking strategy to promote decoupling of semantic information and high-frequency details across bottleneck channels.
AI.result: SPAE achieves a favorable balance among visual understanding, generation quality, and reconstruction fidelity.
AI.conclusion: SPAE effectively adapts VFM latents for generation by addressing the spectral mismatch problem, enabling high-quality generation while preserving the semantic richness of VFM latents.

title: Remember-R1: Mitigating Long-Context Visual Forgetting through Reinforcement Learning
summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) increasingly rely on long chain-of-thought reasoning for complex tasks. However, as reasoning sequences lengthen, models may gradually rely less on visual evidence and more on accumulated textual context, leading to visual forgetting. Existing approaches do not directly constrain how visual evidence is used and maintained along the original reasoning trajectory, leaving long-context visual forgetting insufficiently addressed. To address this issue, we propose Remember-R1, a reinforcement learning framework that mitigates long-context visual forgetting by applying process-level supervision directly on the original reasoning trajectory. Specifically, Remember-R1 introduces rewards that encourage broader coverage of matched visual keywords, stronger persistence of visual dependence in later reasoning steps, and greater focus on question-relevant image regions. Experiments across multiple model scales and diverse multimodal benchmarks demonstrate that Remember-R1 consistently improves reasoning performance. Additional analyses further show that it slows the decline of visual attention during generation, supporting its effectiveness in mitigating long-context visual forgetting.

AI.tldr: Remember-R1 is a reinforcement learning framework that mitigates long-context visual forgetting in multimodal large language models by applying process-level supervision directly on the original reasoning trajectory, using rewards that encourage broader visual keyword coverage, persistent visual dependence, and focus on question-relevant image regions.
AI.motivation: As MLLMs generate longer chain-of-thought reasoning sequences, they tend to rely less on visual evidence and more on accumulated textual context, causing visual forgetting. Existing approaches do not directly constrain how visual evidence is used and maintained along the original reasoning trajectory.
AI.method: Remember-R1 is a reinforcement learning framework that applies process-level supervision directly on the original reasoning trajectory, introducing rewards that encourage: (1) broader coverage of matched visual keywords, (2) stronger persistence of visual dependence in later reasoning steps, and (3) greater focus on question-relevant image regions.
AI.result: Experiments across multiple model scales and diverse multimodal benchmarks show consistent improvement in reasoning performance. Analyses demonstrate that Remember-R1 slows the decline of visual attention during generation, confirming its effectiveness in mitigating long-context visual forgetting.
AI.conclusion: Remember-R1 effectively addresses long-context visual forgetting through trajectory-level process supervision, improving reasoning performance across model scales while slowing the decay of visual attention during long reasoning sequences.

title: SphereVideo: Prototype-anchored Hyperspherical Boundary for Continual AI-generated Video Detection
summary: AI-generated video (AIGV) detection aims to distinguish real videos from AI-generated ones. In practice, detectors trained on existing data often fail to generalize to newly emerging generative models, making this task challenging. Therefore, continual learning (CL) is essential for improving the adaptability. However, CL frameworks for this task remain underexplored. To this end, we propose SphereVideo, a novel CL framework for AIGV detection built on two key observations. First, real videos exhibit a compact feature distribution. Based on this, we encourage real video features to cluster around a real prototype on a hypersphere while repelling AI-generated samples, thereby establishing a decision boundary. This prototype serves as a stable anchor for CL, regulating boundary evolution and mitigating catastrophic forgetting. Second, existing methods tend to rely solely on spatial artifacts as shortcuts. To enhance temporal modeling, we introduce a strategy that models the temporal dynamics of real data at both frame and clip levels. By strengthening real data modeling, this strategy further facilitates learning a real prototype and forming a stable decision boundary. Moreover, we construct a comprehensive and challenging benchmark. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SphereVideo achieves an improved plasticity-stability trade-off, outperforming prior methods by 3.08% on seen data and 4.00% on unseen AI-generated data.

AI.tldr: SphereVideo is a novel continual learning framework for AI-generated video (AIGV) detection. It builds a decision boundary by clustering real video features around a stable prototype on a hypersphere while repelling AI-generated samples, and enhances temporal modeling at frame and clip levels. It outperforms prior methods by 3.08% on seen data and 4.00% on unseen data.
AI.motivation: AIGV detectors trained on existing data fail to generalize to newly emerging generative models. Continual learning is essential for adaptability, but CL frameworks for AIGV detection remain underexplored.
AI.method: SphereVideo proposes a CL framework based on two key observations: (1) real videos exhibit compact feature distributions, so real features are clustered around a real prototype on a hypersphere while repelling AI-generated samples to form a decision boundary; this prototype acts as a stable anchor for CL to regulate boundary evolution and mitigate catastrophic forgetting. (2) A strategy that models temporal dynamics of real data at both frame and clip levels to avoid relying solely on spatial artifacts, strengthening real data modeling to facilitate learning the real prototype. A comprehensive benchmark is also constructed.
AI.result: SphereVideo achieves an improved plasticity-stability trade-off, outperforming prior methods by 3.08% on seen data and 4.00% on unseen AI-generated data.
AI.conclusion: SphereVideo demonstrates that prototype-anchored continual learning combined with temporal modeling at frame and clip levels effectively improves AIGV detection under evolving generative models.

title: Asleep at the Wheel: JEPA's Limitations in Evaluating Novel Driving Data
summary: Modern autonomous-driving fleets record far more video than human reviewers can inspect. This motivates the need for an automatic clip triage mechanism, to surface rare and review-worthy clips, so that driving models can be fine-tuned to better handle unideal circumstances. We test a label-free approach that scores clips by the prediction-error "novelty" of a self-supervised joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA); a frozen V-JEPA video encoder is paired with a lightweight predictor head to reconstruct masked clip embeddings, and clips whose embeddings are hard to predict are flagged as interesting. Evaluated under a realistic protocol that trains on one dataset and tests against footage from others, this approach appears highly effective. We show that this apparent success is actually a domain-shift consequence: on a fair benchmark drawn from a single dataset, this mechanism collapses to chance and is on par with simple no-training baselines. A lightly supervised probe on the same frozen embeddings results in almost double the average precision, indicating that the bottleneck is indeed the self-supervised objective, rather than the representation. We present this as a study for evaluating the effectiveness of self-supervised learning, where cross-dataset protocols can silently reward domain separation over novelty.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates a label-free clip triage system for autonomous driving that uses frozen V-JEPA video embeddings with a lightweight predictor head to flag "novel" (hard-to-predict) clips. While it appears highly effective under cross-dataset evaluation, the authors demonstrate this is an artifact of domain shift, not true novelty detection—on a fair single-dataset benchmark the approach collapses to chance. A lightly supervised probe achieves nearly double the average precision, showing the self-supervised objective is the bottleneck rather than the representation itself.
AI.motivation: Autonomous driving fleets record vastly more video than human reviewers can inspect, motivating the need for automatic clip triage to surface rare, review-worthy clips so driving models can be fine-tuned on unideal circumstances. The authors aim to test whether a label-free, self-supervised novelty-scoring approach can effectively identify such clips.
AI.method: The approach scores clips by prediction-error novelty: a frozen V-JEPA video encoder is paired with a lightweight predictor head that reconstructs masked clip embeddings. Clips with poorly predictable embeddings (high prediction error) are flagged as interesting. The method is evaluated under a realistic cross-dataset protocol (train on one dataset, test on others) and also on a fair single-dataset benchmark, comparing against simple no-training baselines and a lightly supervised probe on the same frozen embeddings.
AI.result: Under the cross-dataset protocol the method appears highly effective, but this success is revealed to be a domain-shift consequence. On a fair single-dataset benchmark, the mechanism collapses to chance and performs on par with simple no-training baselines. A lightly supervised probe on the same frozen embeddings achieves almost double the average precision.
AI.conclusion: The self-supervised objective is the bottleneck in this clip triage task, not the underlying representation. The paper serves as a cautionary study for evaluating self-supervised learning, demonstrating that cross-dataset protocols can silently reward domain separation rather than actual novelty detection.

title: Driver2Map: Imitating Human Driving for Online High-Definition Map Construction
summary: High-definition (HD) maps are essential for autonomous driving systems. In constructing such maps, onboard multi-view camera images, standard-definition maps and satellite images provide crucial information. However, due to the modality and perspective differences among these data sources, existing methods often struggle to effectively align and fuse them, making online HD map construction still challenging. To address these issues, we propose Driver2Map, an online HD map construction model inspired by human drivers. Unlike existing HD map construction models that utilize only two modalities, our Driver2Map can simultaneously exploit three modalities. Specifically, we propose a "two-stage alignment" strategy to reduce spatial misalignment across different modalities. Additionally, we introduce "Pose-Guided BEV Fusion", a BEV (bird's-eye-view) generation module that leverages camera pose information to adaptively weight multi-view features, thereby effectively suppressing cross-view feature overlap during BEV generation. Also, we design a "Pretrained Prior for Map Refinement" module to refine the initial prediction by learning map structure priors, thus improving the HD map prediction under dynamic occlusions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Driver2Map outperforms existing methods on both IoU and AP metrics.

AI.tldr: Driver2Map is an online HD map construction model that integrates three modalities (multi-view cameras, standard-definition maps, satellite images) using a two-stage alignment strategy, a Pose-Guided BEV Fusion module, and a pretrained prior refinement module, outperforming existing methods on IoU and AP metrics.
AI.motivation: Existing HD map construction methods struggle to effectively align and fuse heterogeneous data sources due to modality and perspective differences, and prior models only utilize two modalities, making online HD map construction challenging.
AI.method: Driver2Map simultaneously exploits three modalities. It proposes: (1) a two-stage alignment strategy to reduce spatial misalignment across modalities, (2) Pose-Guided BEV Fusion that uses camera pose information to adaptively weight multi-view features and suppress cross-view overlap during BEV generation, and (3) a Pretrained Prior for Map Refinement module that learns map structure priors to refine initial predictions under dynamic occlusions.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrate that Driver2Map outperforms existing methods on both Intersection-over-Union (IoU) and Average Precision (AP) metrics.
AI.conclusion: Inspired by human drivers, the multi-modal fusion and alignment approach in Driver2Map effectively improves online HD map construction accuracy, setting a new state-of-the-art performance.

title: DeVIT: Low-Power Vision Transformer Acceleration Using Delta Computation
summary: The emergence of transformer-based deep learning models has brought unprecedented performance across various domains, particularly in natural language processing and computer vision. However, deploying these models, especially on resource-constrained devices, poses significant challenges due to their high computational complexity and large memory size and bandwidth requirements. This complexity has led researchers to use low-bit model weights to reduce memory usage and improve efficiency. In addition to reducing processing and memory demands, quantization introduces another useful property: value locality, where the extremely large number of parameters are restricted to a limited range of values. To fully take advantage of this locality, this paper presents DeVIT, an acceleration method for vision transformers that leverages differential computation to enable multiplier-less matrix multiplication.

AI.tldr: DeVIT is an acceleration method for vision transformers that leverages low-bit weight quantization's value locality to enable multiplier-less matrix multiplication through differential computation, reducing memory and computational demands for deployment on resource-constrained devices.
AI.motivation: Transformer-based models, especially vision transformers, face significant deployment challenges on resource-constrained devices due to high computational complexity, large memory footprint, and bandwidth requirements. While low-bit weight quantization reduces memory usage and improves efficiency, the authors recognize that quantization also creates "value locality"—where numerous parameters are restricted to a limited range of values—and aim to exploit this property for further acceleration.
AI.method: DeVIT (Differential Vision Transformer) leverages differential computation to enable multiplier-less matrix multiplication by exploiting the value locality introduced by low-bit weight quantization, thereby reducing both memory and computational costs.
AI.result: The paper introduces DeVIT as an acceleration method that enables multiplier-less matrix multiplication for vision transformers, though specific quantitative results are not detailed in the abstract.
AI.conclusion: DeVIT demonstrates a novel approach to accelerating vision transformers by combining low-bit quantization with differential computation to eliminate expensive multiplication operations, making transformer deployment more feasible on resource-constrained hardware.

title: Prompt-Driven Simulation with Feature Perturbation for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Object Detection
summary: Data augmentation, which simulates diverse visual variations to expand the source distribution and induce synthetic domain shifts, is a simple yet effective strategy for mitigating severe domain shifts and limited labeled target data in cross-domain few-shot object detection (CD-FSOD). Existing approaches rely on conventional data augmentation, such as Color-Jitter, Mosaic, and background-centric adaptation (e.g., Domain-RAG), which are limited in modeling complex domain shifts and often lead to suboptimal performance. In this paper, we propose PSP-FSOD, a principled framework that integrates prompt-driven domain simulation with feature perturbation regularization to improve generalization in CD-FSOD. To enable controllable domain synthesis, we design a prompt-driven strategy that leverages the visual grounding capability of large VLMs to jointly model foreground and background variations, generating semantically consistent yet domain-diverse training samples. Moreover, we adopt a grounding-aware generation scheme that guides object placement and alleviates semantic-spatial misalignment, thereby improving foreground adaptation. To ensure training stability and robustness, we further introduce a noise-induced feature perturbation mechanism that injects Gaussian noise into multi-scale intermediate features with distribution correction, encouraging consistent predictions under perturbations and reducing reliance on domain-specific cues. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PSP-FSOD produces high-quality domain-diverse supervision and learns domain-invariant representations, consistently improving performance across CD-FSOD benchmarks.

AI.tldr: PSP-FSOD is a framework for cross-domain few-shot object detection that uses prompt-driven domain simulation with VLMs and feature perturbation regularization to generate domain-diverse training samples and learn domain-invariant representations, improving generalization across CD-FSOD benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing data augmentation approaches (e.g., Color-Jitter, Mosaic, Domain-RAG) are limited in modeling complex domain shifts and often lead to suboptimal performance in cross-domain few-shot object detection.
AI.method: (1) A prompt-driven strategy leveraging large VLMs' visual grounding to jointly model foreground and background variations, generating semantically consistent yet domain-diverse samples. (2) A grounding-aware generation scheme that guides object placement to avoid semantic-spatial misalignment. (3) A noise-induced feature perturbation mechanism injecting Gaussian noise into multi-scale intermediate features with distribution correction for training stability.
AI.result: PSP-FSOD produces high-quality domain-diverse supervision and learns domain-invariant representations, consistently improving performance across CD-FSOD benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Prompt-driven domain simulation combined with feature perturbation regularization is an effective way to improve generalization in cross-domain few-shot object detection.

title: PixVL: Self-Supervised Training of Pixel-Level MLLMs via a Unified Mask--Text Consistency Cycle
summary: Recent studies develop pixel-level multimodal large language models (MLLMs) that support both Region Segmentation and Region Understanding, extending multimodal interaction from whole images to specific objects and regions. However, these methods face two fundamental challenges. First, the scarcity of high-quality mask--text pairs leaves abundant mask annotations without corresponding language supervision. Second, discrepancies in supervision formats and learning-signal densities induce optimization interference between Region Segmentation and Region Understanding. To address these challenges, we propose PixVL, a self-supervised post-training framework that introduces a unified Mask--Text Consistency Cycle, enabling pixel-level MLLMs to generate and self-verify regional descriptions and learn from unlabeled data. We found that direct cycle based solely on geometric reconstruction is unreliable because re-segmentation IoU does not faithfully reflect the semantic quality and referring sufficiency. PixVL therefore introduces confuser-aware semantic verification, which uses the model's confidence when it correctly chooses the target among highly similar candidate regions, and assigns zero reward to an incorrect choice. Meanwhile, PixVL performs cross-view verification using temporally separated video frames or geometrically transformed image views, preventing cyclic learning from collapsing to positional and shape shortcuts. Finally, a quality-coupled bidirectional learning strategy uses the highest-reward description to guide Text-to-Mask learning. This strategy transforms Region Understanding and Region Segmentation from competing tasks into mutual generators and verifiers. Experiments demonstrate that PixVL improves both region understanding task and segmentation task.

AI.tldr: PixVL is a self-supervised post-training framework for pixel-level multimodal large language models (MLLMs) that unifies Region Segmentation and Region Understanding via a Mask-Text Consistency Cycle, using confuser-aware semantic verification and cross-view verification to learn from unlabeled data and improve both tasks.
AI.motivation: Pixel-level MLLMs supporting both Region Segmentation and Region Understanding face two challenges: (1) scarcity of high-quality mask-text pairs leaving many mask annotations without language supervision, and (2) discrepancies in supervision formats and learning-signal densities causing optimization interference between the two tasks.
AI.method: PixVL introduces a unified Mask-Text Consistency Cycle enabling pixel-level MLLMs to generate and self-verify regional descriptions from unlabeled data. It uses confuser-aware semantic verification (rewarding the model's confidence when correctly selecting targets among similar candidate regions, zero reward for incorrect choices) and cross-view verification (using temporally separated video frames or geometrically transformed views) to prevent collapse to positional/shape shortcuts. A quality-coupled bidirectional learning strategy uses the highest-reward description to guide Text-to-Mask learning, transforming the two tasks into mutual generators and verifiers.
AI.result: Experiments demonstrate that PixVL improves both region understanding and region segmentation tasks.
AI.conclusion: By converting Region Understanding and Region Segmentation from competing tasks into mutually reinforcing generators and verifiers, PixVL effectively addresses the data scarcity and optimization interference challenges in pixel-level MLLMs.

title: CORTIVA: Candidate-Score Fusion of Complementary Visual Teachers for EEG- and MEG-to-Image Retrieval
comment: 31 pages, 19 figures; includes supplementary information. Code: https://github.com/Fuyunhan/CORTIVA
summary: Decoding visual experience from non-invasive brain activity is central to neuroscience and brain-computer interfaces. Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) offers fine spatial detail, but its slow hemodynamics and burdensome acquisition limit temporally resolved decoding. Electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetoencephalography (MEG) provide millisecond resolution, making image retrieval compelling: identify the viewed image from one neural response and a fixed candidate bank. Contrastive alignment to pretrained visual representations enables zero-shot retrieval from EEG and MEG, but most systems collapse heterogeneous visual supervision into a single embedding before ranking. This early consolidation imposes one similarity geometry on every candidate order and removes encoder-specific disagreements from the final ranking. We propose CORTIVA, a candidate-score fusion framework that preserves this complementary evidence. Three decoding routes are aligned to heterogeneous visual targets, score the same indexed candidates independently, and combine only their temperature-scaled score vectors before ranking. On the 200-way THINGS-EEG2 benchmark, CORTIVA reaches 73.5% Top-1 and 95.3% Top-5 across ten participants, exceeding the strongest reported baseline by 10.3 and 5.4 percentage points. With a modality-specific neural encoder, the same fusion principle reaches 42.4% Top-1 on THINGS-MEG. Matched route-removal retraining and four weight controls demonstrate that CORTIVA's gain arises from integrating complementary route scores and persists with uniform weighting, without requiring a specialized weighting rule. Independent DINOv2 analyses further reproduce the local error neighborhoods and posterior neural-visual correspondence. These results establish candidate-score fusion as a simple and testable alternative to embedding-level consolidation for neural image retrieval.

AI.tldr: CORTIVA is a candidate-score fusion framework for neural image retrieval that aligns three decoding routes to heterogeneous visual targets, scores candidate images independently, and combines temperature-scaled score vectors before ranking—achieving 73.5% Top-1 on THINGS-EEG2 and 42.4% Top-1 on THINGS-MEG, outperforming embedding-level consolidation baselines.
AI.motivation: Existing contrastive alignment approaches for zero-shot image retrieval from EEG/MEG collapse heterogeneous visual supervision into a single embedding before ranking, imposing one similarity geometry on all candidate orders and removing encoder-specific disagreements from the final ranking.
AI.method: CORTIVA fuses candidate scores from three independently aligned decoding routes to heterogeneous visual targets. Each route scores the same indexed candidates independently, and only the temperature-scaled score vectors are combined before ranking, preserving complementary evidence across encoders.
AI.result: On 200-way THINGS-EEG2, CORTIVA achieves 73.5% Top-1 and 95.3% Top-5 (beating the strongest baseline by 10.3 and 5.4 points). With a modality-specific encoder on THINGS-MEG, it reaches 42.4% Top-1. Gains persist under uniform weighting, and DINOv2 analyses confirm error neighborhoods and neural-visual correspondence.
AI.conclusion: Candidate-score fusion is a simple, testable alternative to embedding-level consolidation for neural image retrieval, showing that preserving complementary route evidence rather than early consolidation yields substantial accuracy gains.

title: Harnessing Adversarial Distillation to Customise Debiased, Disease-Specific Pathology Foundation Models for Breast Cancer
comment: 11 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables. Accepted to MICCAI 2026 (early accept)
summary: Pathology foundation models (PFMs) provide strong tissue representations and have become central to digital pathology. However, deployment in disease-specific settings is limited by 1) the high computational cost of billion-parameter PFMs and 2) distribution mismatch and non-biological bias inherited from pan-cancer, multi-centre pre-training, including site-specific signatures and imbalanced disease prevalence. These factors can encourage shortcut learning and under-emphasise subtle morphology required for reliable modelling of a specific cancer type. We present SmartStu (a Smart Student), a framework to customise compact, breast-cancer-specific PFMs via distillation whilst mitigating confounding. SmartStu distils representations from multiple teacher PFMs into a lightweight student backbone. Crucially, we introduce adversarial distillation that leverages a dedicated noise model trained to predict nuisance, edge-dominated cues on the distillation set. Using this noise model as a counterexample, the adversarial objective encourages the student to recognise, yet suppress, features predictive of nuisance targets. We further incorporate multi-teacher ensemble distillation and an auxiliary self-supervised objective with artefact injection. We validate SmartStu on three external cohorts (Yale HER2, SLN-Breast, and BRACS) with multiple tiny backbones. SmartStu yields breast-cancer-specific PFMs that are over $30\times$ smaller than general PFMs whilst largely preserving, and sometimes improving, downstream performance measured by balanced accuracy (bAcc) and AUC. Code is available at https://github.com/zwchen03/advDistall.

AI.tldr: SmartStu is a framework that distills representations from multiple large pathology foundation models into compact, breast-cancer-specific student backbones using adversarial distillation to suppress non-biological nuisance cues (e.g., site-specific signatures, edge-dominated artifacts), achieving over 30x smaller models with preserved or improved downstream performance.
AI.motivation: General pathology foundation models (PFMs) are impractical for disease-specific deployment due to: (1) high computational cost of billion-parameter models, and (2) distribution mismatch and non-biological bias (site-specific signatures, imbalanced disease prevalence) inherited from pan-cancer, multi-centre pre-training, which encourage shortcut learning and under-emphasise subtle morphology needed for reliable cancer-specific modelling.
AI.method: SmartStu (Smart Student) distills knowledge from multiple teacher PFMs into a lightweight student backbone. Key components include: (1) adversarial distillation using a dedicated noise model trained to predict nuisance, edge-dominated cues, which acts as a counterexample to encourage the student to recognise yet suppress nuisance-predictive features; (2) multi-teacher ensemble distillation; and (3) an auxiliary self-supervised objective with artefact injection.
AI.result: Validated on three external cohorts (Yale HER2, SLN-Breast, BRACS) with multiple tiny backbones. SmartStu produces breast-cancer-specific PFMs over 30x smaller than general PFMs while largely preserving, and sometimes improving, downstream performance measured by balanced accuracy (bAcc) and AUC.
AI.conclusion: SmartStu demonstrates that compact, cancer-specific foundation models can be efficiently created via adversarial distillation that mitigates confounding, achieving strong performance at a fraction of the computational cost of general PFMs.

title: Understanding Synergistic Interactions among Pathology Foundation Models via Adaptive Fusion
summary: Pathology foundation models (PFMs) provide strong tile-level representations via self-supervised pre-training on large-scale pathology images. Yet, PFMs are developed under diverse and often opaque data, architecture, and objective choices, inducing latent representational biases that limit robustness and obscure what each model specialises in. We present AdaFusion, a lightweight adaptive fusion framework that integrates complementary signals from multiple frozen PFMs through (1) low-dimensional feature compression and (2) a sample-conditioned gating module that reweights model-wise (and optionally channel-wise) contributions. Beyond improving predictive accuracy, AdaFusion provides contribution-driven interpretation that offers evidence consistent with model-specific preferences and synergistic interactions across tissue phenotypes. We evaluate AdaFusion on three public benchmarks spanning treatment response prediction, prostate cancer grading, and spatial gene expression inference. AdaFusion consistently outperforms individual PFMs and other fusion baselines, while providing interpretable tissue visualisation which aligns model preferences with morphological patterns. Code is available at: https://github.com/xyx-98/PathoOracle.

AI.tldr: AdaFusion is a lightweight adaptive fusion framework that combines multiple frozen pathology foundation models (PFMs) via low-dimensional feature compression and sample-conditioned gating, outperforming individual PFMs and other baselines on three benchmarks while providing interpretable, contribution-driven tissue visualizations.
AI.motivation: PFMs are pre-trained under diverse, often opaque choices (data, architecture, objectives), introducing latent representational biases that limit robustness and obscure what each model specializes in. A method is needed to integrate complementary signals while exposing model-specific contributions.
AI.method: AdaFusion integrates multiple frozen PFMs through (1) low-dimensional feature compression and (2) a sample-conditioned gating module that reweights model-wise (and optionally channel-wise) contributions, enabling adaptive fusion and contribution-driven interpretation.
AI.result: AdaFusion consistently outperforms individual PFMs and other fusion baselines across treatment response prediction, prostate cancer grading, and spatial gene expression inference, while providing interpretable tissue visualization consistent with model-specific preferences and synergistic interactions.
AI.conclusion: AdaFusion demonstrates that lightweight adaptive fusion with sample-conditioned gating can improve predictive accuracy over individual PFMs and yield interpretable insights into model specialization and tissue-level morphological patterns.

title: FineMoLA: Towards Fine-Grained Motion-Language Alignment from Clip-Level Supervision
summary: Text-conditioned human motion generation has made rapid progress with the emergence of large-scale motion--language datasets. However, even datasets with rich long-form descriptions typically provide supervision only at the clip level, without explicit temporal correspondence between motion frames and language. This limits fine-grained motion--text grounding and temporally precise generation. We propose FineMoLA, a weakly supervised framework that learns fine-grained frame--phrase correspondence directly from clip-level annotations. Our method first segments long-form descriptions into action-bearing phrases, and then formulates motion--language alignment as an optimal transport problem, which naturally models many-to-many relations between motion frames and text under global constraints. With entropic regularization and Sinkhorn iterations, FineMoLA efficiently infers pseudo frame-level alignments without human labeling. Experiments on SnapMoGen demonstrate that the learned alignments outperform baselines in motion--text grounding.

AI.tldr: FineMoLA is a weakly supervised framework for fine-grained frame-phrase motion-language alignment, using optimal transport with entropic regularization to learn temporal correspondence between motion frames and text from clip-level annotations only.
AI.motivation: Existing motion-language datasets provide only clip-level supervision without explicit temporal correspondence between motion frames and language descriptions, limiting fine-grained motion-text grounding and temporally precise generation.
AI.method: FineMoLA segments long-form descriptions into action-bearing phrases, then formulates motion-language alignment as an optimal transport problem that captures many-to-many relations between frames and text under global constraints. Entropic regularization with Sinkhorn iterations enables efficient pseudo frame-level alignment inference without human labeling.
AI.result: Experiments on SnapMoGen demonstrate that the learned alignments outperform baselines in motion-text grounding.
AI.conclusion: Weakly supervised optimal transport-based alignment can recover fine-grained frame-phrase correspondence from clip-level annotations, improving motion-text grounding without requiring manual labeling.

title: Training-Free Out-of-Distribution Detection for Pathology Whole-Slide Images
comment: Under review. The code is available in https://github.com/muskahya/ZIO
summary: Safe deployment of AI methods in medicine requires robust guardrails that detect when input data deviate from the training distribution to ensure that models provide predictions only within their scope of expertise and abstain otherwise. Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection can provide such safeguards and is extensively studied in general computer vision. Yet, it remains underdeveloped in computational pathology, where gigapixel whole-slide images (WSIs), subtle differences between disease subtypes, and variability in tissue preparation pose unique challenges for conventional OOD methods. We propose ZIO, a training-free, multimodal OOD detector for pathology WSIs that leverages vision--language pathology foundation models (FMs). ZIO constructs text and visual prototypes of in-distribution classes and integrates their complementary information through a prototype shrinkage mechanism to derive OOD scores. We provide the ZIO formulation for both slide- and patch-level FMs. We evaluate ZIO across diverse clinically relevant domain shifts, including rare diseases and near-OOD settings. Extensive evaluation of over 14,700 WSIs from five independent consortia shows that ZIO consistently outperforms both unimodal prototypes and 40 state-of-the-art OOD methods. These results demonstrate the benefits of multimodal representation for OOD detection and pave the way towards safer AI deployment in clinical practice.

AI.tldr: ZIO is a training-free, multimodal OOD detector for pathology whole-slide images that leverages vision-language foundation models, combining text and visual prototypes via a prototype shrinkage mechanism to outperform 40 state-of-the-art OOD methods across 14,700+ WSIs from five independent consortia.
AI.motivation: OOD detection is critical for safe AI deployment in medicine but remains underdeveloped in computational pathology due to gigapixel WSIs, subtle disease subtype differences, and tissue preparation variability that challenge conventional methods.
AI.method: ZIO constructs text and visual prototypes of in-distribution classes using vision-language pathology foundation models, integrates complementary information through a prototype shrinkage mechanism to derive OOD scores, and supports both slide- and patch-level formulations.
AI.result: Evaluation across 14,700+ WSIs from five independent consortia shows ZIO consistently outperforms both unimodal prototypes and 40 state-of-the-art OOD methods across diverse clinically relevant domain shifts including rare diseases and near-OOD settings.
AI.conclusion: Multimodal representation significantly benefits OOD detection in pathology, and ZIO paves the way toward safer AI deployment in clinical practice.

title: PackingGPT: 3D Packing Agent for Real Furniture in Last-Mile Delivery
summary: 3D bin packing rectangular items into standardised containers to maximise space utilisation under geometric shipping automation. Loading a furniture purchase into a personal vehicle is the same task, but under more complex conditions that standard container loading algorithms ignore. This paper addresses the physically stable placement under these realistic conditions with heterogeneous boxes (e.g. varying dimensions and weights) and occupied containers (e.g. groceries). This paper provides a real-world benchmark dataset and baseline model for the Heterogeneous furniture-in-vehicle packing task. The dataset uses real furniture company flat-pack packaging data covering a large number of catalogue products via family-level extrapolation with diversity length, widths, heights, and weights. We also propose a PackingGPT framework for packing as a sequential placement inspired by the Lego assembly process, where heterogeneous boxes of varying dimensions (bricks) are placed step-by-step into the irregular remaining cargo space (creations). Five baseline packing methods were tested on our dataset without considering the Centre-of- Mass (CoM) constraints. In sedan car simulations, 10-40% of placed boxes failed the stability check on average. When the LLP model was trained on packing sequences with CoM constraints enforced during placement, the failure rate dropped to 0.67% (SUV-500).

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a real-world benchmark dataset and PackingGPT framework for the heterogeneous furniture-in-vehicle packing task, addressing physically stable placement of boxes with varying dimensions/weights in partially occupied containers under Centre-of-Mass constraints.
AI.motivation: Standard container loading algorithms ignore the complex conditions of loading furniture into personal vehicles, such as heterogeneous box sizes/weights, occupied containers, and physical stability constraints. Existing methods fail stability checks 10-40% of the time when tested without Centre-of-Mass constraints.
AI.method: The authors create a benchmark dataset from real furniture company flat-pack packaging data with family-level extrapolation. They propose PackingGPT, a sequential placement framework inspired by Lego assembly, where heterogeneous boxes (bricks) are placed step-by-step into irregular remaining cargo space. They also train an LLP (Large Language Model/Placement) model with CoM constraints enforced during placement.
AI.result: Baseline packing methods failed stability checks for 10-40% of placed boxes on average in sedan car simulations. When the LLP model was trained on packing sequences with CoM constraints enforced during placement, the failure rate dropped to 0.67% for SUV-500 scenarios.
AI.conclusion: The proposed PackingGPT framework with CoM-aware training significantly improves physical stability in heterogeneous furniture-in-vehicle packing, reducing stability failure rates to near-zero, demonstrating the importance of incorporating physical constraints into packing sequence generation.

title: Long-Horizon Embodied Decision-Making via Multimodal Memory Compression
summary: Agents are increasingly expected to act not only as task executors, but also as decision-makers on behalf of human users. This shift requires agents to accumulate evidence over long horizons, interpret implicit user preferences, and compare multiple candidates under partial observations. In this work, we propose DunphyBench, a new benchmark for evaluating agents on long-horizon human-centered embodied decision-making, where the agent must navigate through multiple embodied housing environments and make decisions that align with multi-dimensional human preferences. Unlike standard embodied reasoning tasks that often focus on procedural planning or immediate goal completion, our setting requires agents to integrate multimodal, multi-source input into coherent knowledge that supports complex reasoning across long horizon. The evaluation results reveal that there is a substantial gap between current agents and human performance. Furthermore, our diagnosis of state-of-the-art VLM-driven agents reveals that memory management is one of the bottlenecks, where raw multimodal history introduces noise that hinders decision quality. Motivated by this finding, we design MeMento, a preference-conditioned multimodal memory compressor that selectively compresses decision-relevant information from long-horizon history based on user preferences with a fixed set of memory tokens. Experiments show that MeMento helps VLM-driven agents improve accuracy by 7.18%, while reducing memory usage by 85.38% compared to the strongest baseline.

AI.tldr: DunphyBench is a new benchmark for long-horizon human-centered embodied decision-making, and MeMento is a preference-conditioned multimodal memory compressor that improves VLM-driven agent accuracy by 7.18% while reducing memory usage by 85.38%.
AI.motivation: Agents are shifting from task executors to human decision-makers, requiring long-horizon evidence accumulation, interpretation of implicit user preferences, and comparison of multiple candidates under partial observations. Existing benchmarks focus on procedural planning or immediate goal completion rather than complex human-centered decision-making.
AI.method: The paper proposes DunphyBench, a benchmark where agents navigate multiple embodied housing environments and make decisions aligned with multi-dimensional human preferences. It also designs MeMento, a preference-conditioned multimodal memory compressor that selectively compresses decision-relevant information from long-horizon history using a fixed set of memory tokens.
AI.result: Evaluation reveals a substantial gap between current agents and human performance. MeMento improves VLM-driven agent accuracy by 7.18% while reducing memory usage by 85.38% compared to the strongest baseline. Diagnosis identifies memory management, particularly noisy raw multimodal history, as a key bottleneck.
AI.conclusion: Memory management is a critical bottleneck in long-horizon human-centered embodied decision-making, and preference-conditioned compression of multimodal history can significantly improve both decision quality and memory efficiency.

title: VGER: Voxel-Guided Global Event Ranking for Event Cloud Attribution
summary: Event cameras produce sparse and asynchronous event streams that provide rich spatio-temporal information for efficient perception. Recent advances in event-based models have demonstrated strong performance by directly modeling asynchronous events without dense frame reconstruction. However, identifying the event-level evidence behind their predictions is crucial for improving model transparency and reliability. Directly adapting point-level saliency methods from point clouds provides fine-grained attribution but overlooks event-specific spatio-temporal structures. To address this limitation, we propose Voxel-Guided Global Event Ranking (VGER), a training-free attribution framework for point-based event cloud networks. VGER combines event-level gradient evidence with task-aware voxel perturbation evidence, transferring regional contribution into event-level attribution scores while preserving fine-grained resolution. Furthermore, VGER introduces a unified event ranking strategy, where high-ranked events are expected to be prediction-critical and low-ranked events are expected to have limited influence on predictions. We evaluate VGER on three event-based benchmarks with PointNet, PointNet++, and EventMamba. Across nine dataset-backbone settings, VGER consistently improves both high-tail and low-tail deletion performance over point-level saliency baselines.

AI.tldr: VGER is a training-free attribution framework for point-based event cloud networks that combines event-level gradient evidence with task-aware voxel perturbation evidence to produce unified event rankings, improving model interpretability for event cameras.
AI.motivation: Existing point-level saliency methods adapted from point clouds provide fine-grained attribution for event-based models but overlook event-specific spatio-temporal structures, limiting model transparency and reliability.
AI.method: VGER combines event-level gradient evidence with task-aware voxel perturbation evidence, transferring regional (voxel-level) contribution into event-level attribution scores while preserving fine-grained resolution, and introduces a unified event ranking strategy where high-ranked events are prediction-critical and low-ranked events have limited influence.
AI.result: Across nine dataset-backbone settings (PointNet, PointNet++, EventMamba on three event-based benchmarks), VGER consistently improves both high-tail and low-tail deletion performance over point-level saliency baselines.
AI.conclusion: VGER effectively bridges fine-grained event-level attributions with spatio-temporal voxel context, offering a training-free and generalizable approach to interpret event-based models.

title: Slot2Text: Object-Centric Visual Tokenization for Efficient and Spatially Traceable Surgical MLLMs
summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLM) for surgical scene understanding typically inject hundreds of dense visual tokens into a language model, leading to costly inference and limited spatial traceability for generated answers. We present Slot2Text, a dual-mode surgical MLLM that replaces dense representations of visual input with a compact set of regions encoded as slot latents. Instead of relying on contrastive alignment of the visual encoder with language, Slot2Text groups self-supervised vision features into a few regions--slots that are consumed by the language model as area-labeled visual tokens. Slot2Text-Fast uses the slot prefix to answer surgical questions. Slot2Text-Reason also identifies and locates areas relevant for reasoning, linking language outputs to corresponding slot tokens, masks or regions. Experiments on multiple visual question answering and visual grounding benchmarks show that Slot2Text-Fast is competitive with state-of-the-art baseline at a much lower cost, reducing the average total token consumption by a 91.8\% and the visual prefix from 1,295 to 47 tokens (a 96.4\% reduction). Slot2Text-Reason trades additional tokens and latency for explicit area identities, locations, and traceable spatial evidence. These results establish compact slot latents as an efficient default visual interface for surgical MLLMs, with grounded reasoning invoked when greater spatial traceability is required.

AI.tldr: Slot2Text is a dual-mode surgical multimodal large language model (MLLM) that replaces dense visual token representations with compact slot latents, reducing visual tokens from 1,295 to 47 (96.4% reduction) and total token consumption by 91.8% while remaining competitive with state-of-the-art baselines on VQA and visual grounding benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Dense visual token injection in surgical MLLMs leads to costly inference and limited spatial traceability, motivating the need for a more efficient yet spatially accountable visual representation.
AI.method: Slot2Text groups self-supervised vision features into compact region slots consumed by the language model as area-labeled visual tokens. Two modes are proposed: Slot2Text-Fast (uses slot prefix for efficient surgical QA) and Slot2Text-Reason (identifies and locates reasoning-relevant areas, linking outputs to slot tokens/masks/regions).
AI.result: Slot2Text-Fast matches state-of-the-art performance at much lower cost, reducing average total token consumption by 91.8% and visual prefix from 1,295 to 47 tokens (96.4% reduction). Slot2Text-Reason trades additional tokens/latency for explicit spatial evidence and traceability.
AI.conclusion: Compact slot latents serve as an efficient default visual interface for surgical MLLMs, with grounded reasoning used when higher spatial traceability is required.

title: Towards Compact Unified Multimodal Tracking: Synergizing Knowledge Distillation with Structural Pruning
summary: Unified multimodal object tracking has achieved remarkable robustness by leveraging complementary sensor data (e.g., RGB, Thermal, Depth), yet the heavy computational burden of state-of-the-art models hinders their deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. In this work, we identify the prediction head as a critical but often overlooked efficiency bottleneck. By strategically streamlining the decoder architecture, we unlock the potential for real-time inference but simultaneously introduce a capacity gap between the lightweight student and the heavy teacher. To resolve this, we conduct a systematic analysis of 17 distillation strategies and introduce a Dual-Alignment Distillation framework. Our key insight is that effective compression requires decoupling knowledge transfer into two complementary streams: (1) Spatial Representation Alignment, which employs feature distillation to sharpen the student's spatial focus on foreground targets ("Where to track"); and (2) Semantic Distribution Alignment, which utilizes logit-based distillation to align decision boundaries and transfer discriminative dark knowledge ("What to track"). Extensive experiments across five benchmarks demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms complex state-of-the-art methods. Notably, our distilled model achieves 91.5% MPR on RGBT234 and operates at 54 FPS on a single RTX 4090, representing a 5x speedup over the teacher model while maintaining superior accuracy.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a Dual-Alignment Distillation framework for compressing unified multimodal object tracking models. By streamlining the decoder/prediction head architecture and decoupling knowledge distillation into Spatial Representation Alignment (feature-based "where to track") and Semantic Distribution Alignment (logit-based "what to track"), the approach achieves 5x speedup (54 FPS) over the teacher model while maintaining superior accuracy (91.5% MPR on RGBT234).
AI.motivation: State-of-the-art unified multimodal object trackers (RGB, Thermal, Depth) are robust but computationally heavy, hindering deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. The prediction head is identified as a critical but overlooked efficiency bottleneck, and compressing it creates a capacity gap between the lightweight student and heavy teacher that needs to be addressed.
AI.method: The method consists of: (1) Streamlining the decoder/prediction head architecture to unlock real-time inference; (2) Conducting a systematic analysis of 17 distillation strategies; (3) Introducing a Dual-Alignment Distillation framework that decouples knowledge transfer into two complementary streams: Spatial Representation Alignment using feature distillation to sharpen spatial focus on foreground targets ("where to track"), and Semantic Distribution Alignment using logit-based distillation to align decision boundaries and transfer discriminative dark knowledge ("what to track").
AI.result: The approach significantly outperforms complex state-of-the-art methods across five benchmarks. The distilled model achieves 91.5% MPR on RGBT234 and operates at 54 FPS on a single RTX 4090, representing a 5x speedup over the teacher model while maintaining superior accuracy.
AI.conclusion: Effective model compression for multimodal tracking requires decoupling knowledge transfer into complementary spatial and semantic alignment streams, demonstrating that lightweight student models can outperform heavier counterparts when properly distilled, enabling real-time deployment on edge devices.

title: GaussianSelector: Lightweight Human-Guided Object Selection in 3D Gaussian Splatting with Graph Optimization
summary: Selecting a complete 3D object from a reconstructed scene with minimal user effort is essential for practical scene editing and embodied interaction. Existing 3DGS-based methods either retrain the Gaussian representation to embed per-object labels, or build dense multi-view SAM observations, both requiring heavy computation and dense viewpoint coverage that is rarely available in practice. We present GaussianSelector, a training-free framework for interactive 3D object selection from sparse views and sparse scribble guidance. Operating directly on native Gaussian primitives, we coarsen dense Gaussians into geometrically coherent superpoints and construct a continuity-weighted graph using appearance and spatial cues. Sparse user scribbles are lifted into 3D via visibility-aware transmittance coverage, and selection is solved as a global graph-cut energy minimization that propagates sparse evidence to a complete 3D object. This design naturally supports multi-round refinement, where users iteratively correct the selection from additional viewpoints to progressively improve the result. Experiments demonstrate that GaussianSelector achieves competitive selection quality against state-of-the-art multi-view SAM-based methods, while requiring significantly fewer interaction views and substantially lower computational overhead. These properties make it well suited for human-in-the-loop 3D scene editing and 3D asset extraction in real-world deployment scenarios.

AI.tldr: GaussianSelector is a training-free framework for interactive 3D object selection from sparse views and sparse scribbles, operating directly on Gaussian primitives via graph-cut energy minimization.
AI.motivation: Existing 3DGS-based object selection methods require retraining Gaussian representations or dense multi-view SAM observations, both demanding heavy computation and dense viewpoint coverage that is often unavailable in practice. A lightweight, interactive selection approach is needed for practical scene editing.
AI.method: The framework coarsens dense Gaussians into geometrically coherent superpoints, constructs a continuity-weighted graph using appearance and spatial cues, lifts sparse 2D scribbles into 3D via visibility-aware transmittance coverage, and solves selection as a global graph-cut energy minimization. It supports multi-round refinement from additional viewpoints.
AI.result: GaussianSelector achieves competitive selection quality against state-of-the-art multi-view SAM-based methods while requiring significantly fewer interaction views and substantially lower computational overhead.
AI.conclusion: The method's efficiency and low interaction requirements make it well suited for human-in-the-loop 3D scene editing and 3D asset extraction in real-world deployment scenarios.

title: Probing the 3D Object-Level Understanding of Pre-Trained Detection Transformers
summary: Detection transformer models, including DETR and its extensions, learn to output a set of object-level embeddings that can be simultaneously decoded into 2D bounding boxes and class distributions. In this paper, we investigate what pre-trained 2D detection transformers understand about the 3D properties of objects. Specifically, we investigate the extent to which properties including the depth of objects from the camera and the 3D location of objects relative to the camera can be recovered from object-level embeddings using linear and non-linear probes. Across a range of detection transformer models, our results show a surprisingly strong and previously unknown ability of 2D DETR models to represent useful information about the 3D properties of objects, despite the complete lack of 3D supervision during model pre-training.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether 2D detection transformer models (like DETR) implicitly encode 3D object properties—specifically depth and 3D location relative to the camera—within their object-level embeddings, finding surprisingly strong 3D information despite no 3D supervision during pre-training.
AI.motivation: The authors want to understand what pre-trained 2D detection transformers implicitly understand about 3D properties of objects, despite being trained only with 2D supervision.
AI.method: The paper uses linear and non-linear probing techniques on object-level embeddings extracted from various detection transformer models (DETR and its extensions) to recover 3D properties including depth and 3D object locations relative to the camera.
AI.result: The results reveal a surprisingly strong and previously unknown ability of 2D DETR models to represent useful 3D object information, across a range of detection transformer models.
AI.conclusion: 2D detection transformers implicitly encode meaningful 3D object information despite having no 3D supervision during pre-training, suggesting these models capture more spatial understanding than previously recognized.

title: Rolling Shutter Camera Self-Calibration
summary: Rolling shutter (RS) cameras are widely used in consumer devices, but their row-wise exposure causes distortions under motion, making geometric 3D vision problems dependent on both camera intrinsics and readout time ratio. Existing RS calibration methods rely on calibration targets or specialised hardware, limiting their use in unconstrained settings. We present the first self-calibration method for RS cameras that directly estimates camera intrinsics and the readout time ratio from image sequences, without requiring calibration targets. The method is implemented as a self-calibrating bundle adjustment (BA), which critically depends on the RS imaging model. We combine two known complementary models. The first formulates RS imaging as continuous-time trajectory estimation under a row-wise pose representation. The second interprets RS images as temporally distorted global shutter (GS) images and requires to estimate correction fields. The combination is non-trivial and results in a unified dual-projection model, in which each 3D point is simultaneously constrained at both row-dependent and reference timestamps along a shared continuous trajectory, enforcing stronger geometric and temporal consistency. Extensive simulations analyse the applicability of several implementations under varying conditions, and real data experiments demonstrate the accuracy, robustness, and practical effectiveness of the proposed approach.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first self-calibration method for rolling shutter (RS) cameras that estimates camera intrinsics and readout time ratio directly from image sequences without calibration targets, implemented as a self-calibrating bundle adjustment using a unified dual-projection model.
AI.motivation: Existing RS camera calibration methods rely on calibration targets or specialized hardware, limiting their use in unconstrained real-world settings. Since RS cameras are ubiquitous in consumer devices and their row-wise exposure causes motion distortions that affect geometric 3D vision, there is a need for calibration methods that work without special equipment.
AI.method: The method is implemented as a self-calibrating bundle adjustment (BA) that combines two complementary RS imaging models: (1) continuous-time trajectory estimation with row-wise pose representation, and (2) interpreting RS images as temporally distorted global shutter (GS) images requiring correction fields. These are unified into a dual-projection model where each 3D point is constrained at both row-dependent and reference timestamps along a shared continuous trajectory, enforcing stronger geometric and temporal consistency.
AI.result: Extensive simulations analyze the applicability of several implementations under varying conditions, and real data experiments demonstrate the accuracy, robustness, and practical effectiveness of the proposed approach.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method achieves RS camera self-calibration (intrinsics and readout time ratio) without calibration targets, validated through both simulations and real-world experiments showing its practical effectiveness in unconstrained settings.

title: UCBound-Net: Uncertainty-Guided Boundary-Aware Continual Learning for Domain-Incremental Ultrasound Segmentation
comment: Accepted at the MICCAI 2026 CLiMeM Workshop
summary: Continual learning in clinical imaging faces a dual challenge: a model must assimilate knowledge from new anatomical domains while retaining representations learned from prior tasks, a problem known as catastrophic forgetting. Existing mitigation strategies, including regularization and knowledge distillation, treat all spatial regions equally, ignoring the fact that prediction uncertainty is strongly correlated with the propensity for forgetting. We introduce UCBound-Net, a continual segmentation framework that exploits Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout uncertainty as a spatial proxy for forgetting risk. Our method contributes three synergistic components: (i) uncertainty-weighted boundary distillation, which amplifies the knowledge transfer signal at high-entropy regions of the frozen teacher; (ii) uncertainty-calibration regularization, which explicitly penalizes overconfident erroneous predictions; and (iii) uncertainty-guided exemplar selection, a memory buffer that preferentially stores samples whose boundary regions exhibit the highest predictive entropy. Evaluated on a sequential domain-incremental benchmark comprising breast ultrasound (BUSI, Task 1) followed by thyroid ultrasound (TN3K, Task 2), UCBound-Net reduces forgetting relative to naive fine-tuning, achieving a backward transfer (BWT) of -0.098 compared with -0.173, while obtaining an average Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 0.755 across both tasks. The proposed framework outperforms baseline methods without requiring task-boundary supervision. An ablation study further demonstrates that each component contributes independently to forgetting mitigation, providing a practical pathway toward uncertainty-aware continual learning for clinical image segmentation.

AI.tldr: UCBound-Net is a continual segmentation framework that uses MC Dropout uncertainty as a spatial proxy for forgetting risk, incorporating three synergistic components—uncertainty-weighted boundary distillation, uncertainty-calibration regularization, and uncertainty-guided exemplar selection—to mitigate catastrophic forgetting in domain-incremental clinical imaging, achieving a BWT of -0.098 vs -0.173 for fine-tuning and 0.755 average DSC across breast and thyroid ultrasound tasks.
AI.motivation: Continual learning in clinical imaging is challenged by catastrophic forgetting when assimilating new anatomical domains. Existing mitigation strategies (regularization, knowledge distillation) treat all spatial regions equally, ignoring that prediction uncertainty strongly correlates with forgetting propensity.
AI.method: UCBound-Net leverages Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout uncertainty as a spatial proxy for forgetting risk, with three components: (i) uncertainty-weighted boundary distillation amplifying knowledge transfer at high-entropy regions of the frozen teacher, (ii) uncertainty-calibration regularization penalizing overconfident erroneous predictions, and (iii) uncertainty-guided exemplar selection preferentially storing samples with highest boundary predictive entropy in the memory buffer.
AI.result: On a sequential domain-incremental benchmark (BUSI breast ultrasound → TN3K thyroid ultrasound), UCBound-Net reduces forgetting (BWT of -0.098 vs -0.173 for fine-tuning) with an average DSC of 0.755 across both tasks, outperforming baselines without task-boundary supervision. Ablations confirm each component independently contributes to forgetting mitigation.
AI.conclusion: UCBound-Net provides a practical, uncertainty-aware pathway toward continual learning for clinical image segmentation, demonstrating that explicitly leveraging spatial uncertainty can effectively mitigate catastrophic forgetting without requiring task-boundary supervision.

title: ST-LoRA: Single Trajectory LoRA Ensemble for Uncertainty Aware Agricultural Segmentation
comment: Submitted to Computers and Electronics in Agriculture (Elsevier). Currently under review (first revision round)
summary: Reliable decision-support in digital agriculture requires accurate predictions and well-calibrated uncertainty estimates, particularly for dense prediction tasks such as semantic segmentation. Ensemble methods provide strong uncertainty quantification, but their computational and memory demands limit practical use, while single-model approximations often trade off uncertainty quality for efficiency. We propose ST-LoRA, a parameter-efficient ensemble framework that builds diverse ensemble members from a single training trajectory by combining Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) with snapshot ensembling. Each member shares a frozen pretrained backbone and differs only in lightweight low-rank adapters, reducing trainable parameters to under 10% of the full model while preserving ensemble diversity. We evaluate across two agricultural datasets - GrowliFlower-L (cauliflower, open field) and BUP20 (sweet pepper, glasshouse) - using SegFormer and Mask2Former, covering in-distribution performance, calibration under distribution shift, and out-of-distribution detection. Ablations show feed-forward layers, not attention layers, are the critical LoRA target for dense prediction, contrary to the attention-only convention from language models. ST-LoRA matches or exceeds full-rank ensembles in segmentation accuracy and calibration across both datasets and architectures, while substantially reducing training time, inference latency, memory footprint, and storage requirements. Against efficient baselines - Snapshot Ensemble, MC Dropout, and Deep Deterministic Uncertainty - ST-LoRA consistently matches or outperforms them in image/pixel-level OoD detection, calibration stability under shift, and cross-seed variance, with far fewer parameters and lower compute. These results show LoRA-efficient ensemble adaptation is a highly effective, practical approach for uncertainty-aware agricultural vision systems.

AI.tldr: ST-LoRA combines Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) with snapshot ensembling to create diverse ensemble members from a single training trajectory for uncertainty-aware semantic segmentation in agriculture. It shares a frozen pretrained backbone and trains only lightweight low-rank adapters (<10% of parameters), matching or exceeding full-rank ensembles in accuracy and calibration while drastically reducing compute, memory, and latency.
AI.motivation: Reliable decision-support in digital agriculture requires both accurate predictions and well-calibrated uncertainty estimates for dense prediction tasks. Ensemble methods provide strong uncertainty quantification but are computationally and memory-intensive, while single-model approximations sacrifice uncertainty quality for efficiency.
AI.method: ST-LoRA builds diverse ensemble members from a single training trajectory by integrating Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) with snapshot ensembling. Each ensemble member shares a frozen pretrained backbone and differs only in lightweight low-rank adapters, keeping trainable parameters under 10% of the full model. Evaluated on two agricultural datasets (GrowliFlower-L and BUP20) using SegFormer and Mask2Former, with ablations identifying feed-forward layers (not attention layers) as the critical LoRA target for dense prediction tasks.
AI.result: ST-LoRA matches or exceeds full-rank ensembles in segmentation accuracy and calibration across both datasets and architectures while substantially reducing training time, inference latency, memory footprint, and storage. It consistently outperforms efficient baselines (Snapshot Ensemble, MC Dropout, Deep Deterministic Uncertainty) in image/pixel-level OoD detection, calibration stability under shift, and cross-seed variance, with far fewer parameters and lower compute.
AI.conclusion: LoRA-efficient ensemble adaptation is a highly effective, practical approach for uncertainty-aware agricultural vision systems, offering a strong trade-off between ensemble diversity, computational efficiency, and uncertainty quantification quality.

title: Recursive Vision Language Models for General Symbolic Reasoning
summary: Hard symbolic-reasoning tasks such as Sudoku, maze pathfinding, and ARC remain challenging for LLMs due to their fixed-depth autoregressive reasoning, which limits systematic search, refinement, and backtracking. While recursive models such as Hierarchical Reasoning Model (HRM) and Tiny Recursive Model (TRM) address this limitation through iterative latent-state refinement, they are typically task-specific and do not leverage pretrained language priors. We propose R-Qwen, a recursive reasoning framework built upon a pretrained Qwen backbone. R-Qwen repeatedly refines a candidate solution through programmatic self-recursion and deep supervision, combining the structured iterative computation of recursive models with the linguistic and reasoning priors of pretrained LLMs. We further adapt Hierarchical Supervision Weighting (HSW) to autoregressive models by exponentially weighting losses across recursive steps. HSW reduces gradient variance by at least 50\%, improves the signal-to-noise ratio of stochastic gradients, and accelerates convergence. Across eight challenging benchmarks, R-Qwen consistently outperforms prior recursive reasoning models and substantially larger LLMs while using a comparable number of trainable parameters. Notably, on ARC-AGI dataset, our model achieves a 27.6\% improvement over the baseline, highlighting the effectiveness of recursive refinement for general symbolic reasoning. These results suggest that recursive reasoning mechanisms and pretrained language model priors are complementary approaches for improving symbolic puzzle-solving. Code and models will be released after acceptance.

AI.tldr: R-Qwen is a recursive reasoning framework built on a pretrained Qwen backbone that refines candidate solutions through programmatic self-recursion and deep supervision, combining recursive computation with pretrained LLM priors. It achieves strong results across eight benchmarks, including a 27.6% improvement on ARC-AGI.
AI.motivation: LLMs struggle with hard symbolic-reasoning tasks because their fixed-depth autoregressive reasoning cannot support systematic search, refinement, and backtracking. While recursive models (HRM, TRM) address this via iterative latent-state refinement, they are task-specific and fail to leverage pretrained language priors.
AI.method: R-Qwen repeatedly refines a candidate solution via programmatic self-recursion and deep supervision on a pretrained Qwen backbone. It also adapts Hierarchical Supervision Weighting (HSW) to autoregressive models by exponentially weighting losses across recursive steps, which reduces gradient variance by at least 50% and improves convergence.
AI.result: R-Qwen outperforms prior recursive reasoning models and substantially larger LLMs across eight benchmarks with comparable trainable parameters. On ARC-AGI, it achieves a 27.6% improvement over the baseline. HSW reduces gradient variance by at least 50% and improves signal-to-noise ratio of stochastic gradients.
AI.conclusion: Recursive reasoning mechanisms and pretrained language model priors are complementary for improving symbolic puzzle-solving, demonstrating that combining both approaches yields strong performance gains in general symbolic reasoning tasks.

title: STAR-VLM: Spatiotemporal Grounding Vision-Language Models for Motion and Velocity Estimation via Automotive Radar Supervision
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are emerging as a key component of embodied intelligence, with growing applications in auto-labeling and end-to-end autonomous driving. However, existing approaches for improving spatiotemporal reasoning in VLMs often rely on complex preprocessing pipelines, expensive human annotations, or synthetic data, which limit scalability and introduce potential sim-to-real gaps. Moreover, although these methods have improved spatiotemporal understanding, they still lack strong metric reasoning capabilities for dynamic scenes, such as estimating object motion in real-world units. Prior work has explored LiDAR-based metric depth supervision to enhance spatial perception, but it does not directly address temporal reasoning.
