We introduce STAR-VLM, an automotive radar-supervised framework that enhances spatiotemporal VLMs with motion reasoning and metric velocity estimation for autonomous driving. Automotive radar is a low-cost and widely deployed sensor that provides complementary spatiotemporal supervision through range and Doppler measurements. By leveraging these measurements as label-free ground truth during training, STAR-VLM improves the metric spatiotemporal reasoning ability of VLMs. Through experiments on driving scenarios, we show that STAR-VLM achieves state-of-the-art performance on both motion classification and metric velocity estimation, outperforming even task-specific methods designed for each task. These results highlight automotive radar as a scalable and cost-effective source of supervision for building metric-aware spatiotemporal VLMs for real-world autonomous driving.

AI.tldr: STAR-VLM is an automotive radar-supervised framework that enhances vision-language models with metric motion reasoning and velocity estimation for autonomous driving, using radar range and Doppler measurements as label-free ground truth during training.
AI.motivation: Existing VLM approaches for spatiotemporal reasoning rely on complex preprocessing, expensive human annotations, or synthetic data that limit scalability and create sim-to-real gaps. Furthermore, these methods lack metric reasoning capabilities (e.g., estimating object motion in real-world units), and prior LiDAR-based depth supervision does not address temporal reasoning.
AI.method: STAR-VLM leverages automotive radar as a low-cost, widely deployed sensor to provide complementary spatiotemporal supervision through range and Doppler measurements. These measurements serve as label-free ground truth during training to improve the metric spatiotemporal reasoning abilities of VLMs.
AI.result: STAR-VLM achieves state-of-the-art performance on both motion classification and metric velocity estimation in driving scenarios, outperforming even task-specific methods designed for each task.
AI.conclusion: Automotive radar serves as a scalable and cost-effective supervision source for building metric-aware spatiotemporal VLMs for real-world autonomous driving applications.

title: Enhancing Visual Perception in Foggy Conditions via Multiclass Fog Density Modeling
summary: Autonomous driving (AD) systems have advanced rapidly over the past decade; however, robust perception under adverse weather conditions remains a major challenge, particularly in dense fog. In this work, we investigate fog-aware perception using synthetically generated fog data derived from the Waymo dataset. To support fog simulation, depth images are generated using an iterative learning approach. We consider five fog-density levels: clear, light fog, moderate fog, heavy fog, and very heavy fog. Instead of training a single unified model across all conditions, we train separate perception models for each fog-density level. Experimental results show that density-specific training improves performance in severe fog conditions. In particular, for the very heavy fog class, recall improves from 0.076 to 0.232, corresponding to an absolute gain of 15.6 percentage points. These findings suggest that deploying multiple specialized models, rather than a single general-purpose model, can improve perception robustness for autonomous vehicles under challenging visibility conditions. Future work will extend this strategy to additional sensing modalities, including LiDAR and radar, and evaluate generalization across diverse weather scenarios.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates fog-aware perception for autonomous driving using synthetically generated fog data from the Waymo dataset, and shows that training separate perception models for each fog-density level (rather than a single unified model) significantly improves performance, especially in very heavy fog (recall improving from 0.076 to 0.232).
AI.motivation: Robust perception under adverse weather conditions, particularly dense fog, remains a major challenge for autonomous driving systems, which motivates exploring fog-aware perception strategies.
AI.method: Synthetically generate fog data from the Waymo dataset using depth images produced via an iterative learning approach; consider five fog-density levels (clear through very heavy fog); train separate perception models for each fog-density level instead of a single unified model.
AI.result: Density-specific training improves performance in severe fog conditions. For very heavy fog, recall improves from 0.076 to 0.232, an absolute gain of 15.6 percentage points.
AI.conclusion: Deploying multiple specialized models rather than a single general-purpose model can improve perception robustness for autonomous vehicles under challenging visibility conditions. Future work will extend to LiDAR and radar modalities and broader weather scenarios.

title: D^2-4DGS: Dual-Depth Guided Sparse-Camera 4D Gaussian Splatting
summary: Dynamic 4D Gaussian Splatting has emerged as an efficient representation for dynamic novel view synthesis through explicit scene modeling and real-time rendering. However, existing methods typically require dense multi-view videos for sufficient geometric constraints, making capture expensive and limiting sparse-camera deployment. Reducing input views lowers acquisition cost but weakens geometry supervision, often causing missing structures and floating Gaussians. Depth priors provide geometric cues, yet no single source offers both dense coverage and reliable geometry. Monocular depth provides dense structure but is scale-ambiguous and locally biased, whereas multi-view geometric depth provides incomplete anchors consistent with the reconstruction coordinate system. To exploit their complementarity, we propose D$^2$-4DGS, a sparse-camera dynamic 4D Gaussian Splatting framework guided by dual-source depth priors. We align monocular estimates with valid multi-view geometric depths and verify their consistency to identify reliable geometric anchors. These verified anchors support consistency-aware pruning and depth supervision, while verified geometric depths and aligned mono-only estimates provide candidate geometry for densification in under-reconstructed regions. Finally, RGB-D joint optimization improves appearance fidelity and geometric consistency under sparse-view supervision. Across all nine dataset--view settings, D$^2$-4DGS achieves the highest PSNR, improving by 1.33 dB on average over the best competing method in each setting.

AI.tldr: D^2-4DGS is a sparse-camera dynamic 4D Gaussian Splatting framework that leverages dual-source depth priors (monocular and multi-view geometric depth) to improve novel view synthesis under sparse camera setups, achieving state-of-the-art PSNR across nine dataset-view settings with 1.33 dB average improvement.
AI.motivation: Existing dynamic 4D Gaussian Splatting methods require dense multi-view videos for sufficient geometric constraints, making sparse-camera capture unreliable. Sparse views weaken geometry supervision causing missing structures and floating Gaussians, and no single depth source offers both dense coverage and reliable geometric consistency.
AI.method: The framework (1) aligns monocular depth estimates with valid multi-view geometric depths and verifies their consistency to identify reliable geometric anchors; (2) uses verified anchors for consistency-aware pruning and depth supervision; (3) leverages verified geometric depths and aligned mono-only estimates as candidate geometry for densification in under-reconstructed regions; (4) performs RGB-D joint optimization for appearance fidelity and geometric consistency under sparse-view supervision.
AI.result: Across all nine dataset-view settings, D^2-4DGS achieves the highest PSNR, improving by 1.33 dB on average over the best competing method in each setting.
AI.conclusion: Complementary depth priors from monocular and multi-view sources can effectively compensate for the lack of geometric supervision in sparse-camera dynamic 4D Gaussian Splatting, enabling high-quality dynamic novel view synthesis without expensive dense capture.

title: When Measurement Conventions Masquerade as Calibration Gains in Cardiac Digital Twins
comment: Accepted at the 2nd International Workshop on Digital Twin for Healthcare (DT4H 2026), held in conjunction with MICCAI 2026. 10 pages, 2 figures
summary: Cardiac digital twins convert clinical images into physiological measurements through observation operators, yet calibration studies often assume a fixed reference convention. Across four shared-backbone echocardiographic EF front-ends, phase conditioning appears to remove CAMUS baseline bias. Matched-reference analysis rejects this gain: singleplane ground-truth EF error is statistically indistinguishable across models, while single-plane ground-truth EF exceeds CAMUS biplane clinical EF by +6.30 points, explaining nearly all baseline bias. A prespecified EchoNet-Dynamic replication, with released data and our extractor aligned to the apical four-chamber plane, removes baseline overestimation and reverses the CAMUS ranking. We also quantify haemodynamic effects, conformal residual-width budgets, and EF-stratum changes, yielding a Convention-Aware EF Audit protocol that separates genuine observation operator calibration from measurement artefacts. GitHub: EjectionFraction-Bias-in-Cardiac-Digital-Twin.git

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that apparent bias in cardiac digital twin EF calibration stems from reference convention mismatches rather than observation operator flaws. Across four echocardiographic EF front-ends, phase conditioning removes CAMUS baseline bias, but matched-reference analysis shows this gain is illusory—single-plane ground truth EF exceeds CAMUS biplane clinical EF by +6.30 points. A prespecified EchoNet-Dynamic replication with released data removes overestimation and reverses CAMUS ranking. The authors propose a Convention-Aware EF Audit protocol to separate genuine calibration from measurement artefacts.
AI.motivation: Cardiac digital twins convert clinical images to physiological measurements via observation operators, but calibration studies typically assume a fixed reference convention, potentially conflating genuine model calibration improvements with artefacts caused by differing ground-truth EF reference conventions (e.g., single-plane vs biplane).
AI.method: The study compares four shared-backbone echocardiographic EF front-ends with phase conditioning, performs matched-reference analysis comparing single-plane versus biplane ground-truth EF, conducts a prespecified EchoNet-Dynamic replication with released data aligned to the apical four-chamber plane, and quantifies haemodynamic effects, conformal residual-width budgets, and EF-stratum changes via a Convention-Aware EF Audit protocol.
AI.result: Phase conditioning appears to remove CAMUS baseline bias, but matched-reference analysis reveals the gain is statistically insignificant—models are indistinguishable on single-plane ground truth. The +6.30 point difference between single-plane and CAMUS biplane clinical EF explains nearly all baseline bias. EchoNet-Dynamic replication removes baseline overestimation and reverses the CAMUS ranking.
AI.conclusion: Reference convention mismatches, not observation operator deficiencies, are the primary source of apparent EF baseline bias in cardiac digital twins. The proposed Convention-Aware EF Audit protocol provides a framework for separating genuine observation operator calibration from measurement artefacts.

title: Linear Multi-Timescale Retention as a Memory-Efficient Vision-Language Bridge
summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) face a critical computational bottleneck when processing high-resolution imagery due to the $O(N^2)$ memory complexity of Softmax Multi-Head Attention (MHA). While substituting MHA with independent Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) achieves $O(N)$ scaling, it strips the architecture of spatial sequence routing, severely degrading global scene understanding and object permanence. In this paper, we propose the Linear Multi-Timescale Retention (LIA-MTR) module, a memory-efficient cross-modal bridge. By integrating an ELU-based positive feature mapping with adaptive write-gating and log-linearly distributed recurrent decays, LIA-MTR mathematically compresses continuous visual sequences into bounded memory states. Theoretical analysis proves the architecture operates with strict $O(N)$ sequence-interaction complexity. Empirically, synthetic retrieval evaluations demonstrate that LIA-MTR flawlessly routes context across 16,000 tokens, eliminating the "Lost in the Middle" degradation typical of naive linear attention. Hardware benchmarking reveals infinite-context scaling capabilities, natively processing 262,144 visual patches within an 11.2 GB VRAM footprint, whereas standard MHA suffers out-of-memory failure at 16,384 patches. Furthermore, following instruction tuning on 665K conversational samples, LIA-MTR significantly outperforms an industry-standard MLP baseline on the MME benchmark (71.00% vs. 68.11%), driven by a 10% absolute improvement in object permanence and superior global semantic extraction. This work establishes a mathematically rigorous, computationally flat foundation for infinite-context Vision-Language integration.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes LIA-MTR, a memory-efficient attention alternative for Vision-Language Models that achieves O(N) linear scaling by compressing visual sequences into bounded memory states using ELU feature mapping, adaptive write-gating, and log-linear recurrent decays. It processes 262K visual patches in 11.2GB VRAM (vs MHA failing at 16K), improves MME to 71.00% vs 68.11% MLP baseline, and eliminates "Lost in the Middle" degradation up to 16K tokens.
AI.motivation: VLMs suffer from O(N²) memory complexity in softmax attention for high-resolution imagery. While linear MLP replacements achieve O(N) scaling, they lose spatial sequence routing, degrading global scene understanding and object permanence. The goal is to combine linear efficiency with attention-quality context routing.
AI.method: LIA-MTR integrates ELU-based positive feature mapping with adaptive write-gating and log-linearly distributed recurrent decays to compress continuous visual sequences into bounded memory states, achieving strict O(N) sequence-interaction complexity while maintaining context routing capability.
AI.result: The model routes context flawlessly across 16,000 tokens in synthetic retrieval tests, processes 262,144 visual patches within 11.2GB VRAM (MHA fails at 16,384), and after instruction tuning on 665K samples, achieves 71.00% on MME vs 68.11% for MLP baseline, with 10% absolute gains in object permanence.
AI.conclusion: LIA-MTR establishes a mathematically rigorous, computationally flat foundation for infinite-context Vision-Language integration, offering the efficiency of linear attention without sacrificing spatial sequence routing or object permanence.

title: Motion Beyond Morphology: Bootstrapping Cross-Category Motion Transfer from Abstract Motion Representations
summary: Video motion transfer aims to animate a target object using dynamics from a reference video. Existing formulations largely rely on fixed structural correspondence, which becomes ill-defined when reference and target objects differ substantially in morphology, articulation, or deformation mechanisms. We introduce Motion Beyond Morphology, a perspective that seeks to transfer motion beyond fixed structural correspondence, by preserving dynamics that remain meaningful across different target morphologies. To realize this, we propose a two-stage framework. Stage~I learns complementary multi-granularity abstract motion views and uses them to bootstrap cross-category video pairs that preserve transferable dynamics across diverse morphologies. Stage~II internalizes this supervision into direct reference-video-conditioned generation, removing the need for explicit motion extraction at inference. We further introduce OpenVMT-Dataset and OpenVMT-Bench for training and evaluating image- and text-conditioned motion transfer across Same, Near, and Far category gaps, and plan to release both upon acceptance. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art motion fidelity and target preservation. Project page: https://miniz233.github.io/MotionBeyondMorphology/

AI.tldr: Introduces Motion Beyond Morphology, a video motion transfer framework that moves beyond fixed structural correspondence to transfer dynamics across drastically different target morphologies (e.g., different categories), using a two-stage training approach with multi-granularity abstract motion views and direct reference-video-conditioned generation, along with new dataset and benchmark (OpenVMT).
AI.motivation: Existing video motion transfer methods rely on fixed structural correspondence between reference and target objects, which breaks down when the two differ substantially in morphology, articulation, or deformation—limiting transfer to same-category or structurally similar objects.
AI.method: Two-stage framework: Stage I learns complementary multi-granularity abstract motion views to bootstrap cross-category video pairs that preserve transferable dynamics; Stage II internalizes this supervision into direct reference-video-conditioned generation, removing explicit motion extraction at inference. Introduces OpenVMT-Dataset and OpenVMT-Bench for training/evaluation across Same, Near, and Far category gaps.
AI.result: Achieves state-of-the-art motion fidelity and target preservation, demonstrated through extensive experiments on the proposed OpenVMT-Bench.
AI.conclusion: Motion transfer can be generalized beyond fixed structural correspondence, enabling animation across morphologically distant objects while preserving both motion fidelity and target identity.

title: Mitigating Visual Degradation in MLLMs via Spatial-Spectral Visual Anchor Learning
comment: This paper has been accepted by ACM MM 2026
summary: Despite the progress of multimodal large language models (MLLMs), they continue to exhibit deficiencies in visual perception. Following visual instruction tuning, internal MLLM representations rapidly deviate from their original semantic states during inference, causing severe information degradation. While existing methods attempt to leverage external vision foundation models (VFMs) to align internal representations, we find that direct alignment with VFMs enhances visual semantics but fails to mitigate representation deviation. To address this, we propose Spatial-Spectral Visual Anchor Learning (SSVAL). The core of SSVAL is Visual Anchor Prompt Injection (VAPI), which introduces prompts that absorb rich knowledge from external VFMs during training, enabling them to serve as stable visual anchors that mitigate representation deviation during inference. Additionally, we incorporate auxiliary spatial and frequency-domain representation alignment losses to provide complementary vision-specific supervision at intermediate LLM layers. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SSVAL significantly outperforms existing methods. Code are available on our \href{https://msls38.github.io/SSVAL/}{project page}.

AI.tldr: SSVAL introduces Visual Anchor Prompt Injection with spatial-spectral alignment losses to stabilize MLLM internal representations during inference, mitigating the representation deviation problem that causes visual perception deficiencies.
AI.motivation: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) suffer from visual perception deficiencies because internal representations rapidly deviate from their original semantic states during inference after visual instruction tuning, causing severe information degradation. Existing approaches using external vision foundation models (VFMs) for direct alignment enhance visual semantics but fail to address the underlying representation deviation.
AI.method: SSVAL (Spatial-Spectral Visual Anchor Learning) consists of two key components: (1) Visual Anchor Prompt Injection (VAPI), which introduces prompts that absorb knowledge from external VFMs during training to serve as stable visual anchors that mitigate representation deviation during inference, and (2) auxiliary spatial and frequency-domain representation alignment losses that provide complementary vision-specific supervision at intermediate LLM layers.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrate that SSVAL significantly outperforms existing methods in mitigating representation deviation and improving visual perception capabilities of MLLMs.
AI.conclusion: Direct alignment with VFMs is insufficient because it enhances visual semantics without addressing representation deviation; instead, using VFMs as knowledge sources for visualization anchor prompts combined with spatial-spectral alignment supervision provides a more effective solution to stabilize MLLM representations during inference.

title: Dynamic Resolution Routing for Efficient Egocentric Grounding
summary: Egocentric visual grounding requires high-resolution inputs to localize small objects. However, scaling Multimodal Large Language Models to this domain is constrained by the excessive cost of visual token processing. We identify that current efficient strategies based on token reduction are unreliable for selecting object-centric spatial evidence. To overcome this, we propose SmartRes, a framework that performs efficiency optimization in the pixel space via dynamic resolution routing. SmartRes first encodes a low-resolution view for global context and uses a lightweight router to activate high-resolution patches in object-centric regions and constructs an order-preserving visual sequence. To further enable robust routing under severe foreground-background imbalance, we introduce a margin-regularized routing objective that increases foreground-background logit separation and improves foreground recall. Experiments on Ego4D and EgoIntention show that SmartRes reduces visual tokens by up to 67% while retaining 86.4% of full-resolution performance, and achieves up to 1.66X faster inference than state-of-the-art token reduction methods with higher accuracy. Furthermore, strong performance on small object grounding indicates the effectiveness of SmartRes towards egocentric applications. Code will be publicly available.

AI.tldr: SmartRes is a framework that performs efficiency optimization in pixel space via dynamic resolution routing for egocentric visual grounding, reducing visual tokens by up to 67% while retaining 86.4% of full-resolution performance and achieving up to 1.66X faster inference than state-of-the-art token reduction methods.
AI.motivation: Egocentric visual grounding requires high-resolution inputs to localize small objects, but scaling Multimodal Large Language Models to this domain is constrained by the excessive cost of visual token processing. Existing token reduction strategies are unreliable for selecting object-centric spatial evidence.
AI.method: SmartRes first encodes a low-resolution view for global context, uses a lightweight router to activate high-resolution patches in object-centric regions, and constructs an order-preserving visual sequence. It introduces a margin-regularized routing objective that increases foreground-background logit separation and improves foreground recall to handle severe foreground-background imbalance.
AI.result: On Ego4D and EgoIntention, SmartRes reduces visual tokens by up to 67% while retaining 86.4% of full-resolution performance, achieves up to 1.66X faster inference than state-of-the-art token reduction methods with higher accuracy, and demonstrates strong performance on small object grounding.
AI.conclusion: SmartRes demonstrates that efficiency optimization in pixel space via dynamic resolution routing is an effective alternative to token reduction for egocentric visual grounding, enabling efficient high-resolution processing with strong small-object grounding performance.

title: StreamTalk: Streaming Co-Speech Gesture Generation with Key-Pose Anchoring
summary: Real-time co-speech gesture generation must produce 3D motion clip by clip as speech arrives. Existing streaming methods are open-loop: each clip depends on past context, but the model cannot check or correct its trajectory. Small errors therefore accumulate and cause drift over long sequences. We observe that this failure is mainly caused by the lack of a forward constraint rather than poor short-clip quality. A plausible key pose at the end of each clip provides a destination anchor that limits drift. Based on this observation, we propose StreamTalk, a closed-loop framework with a periodic generate-retrieve-refine cycle. Streaming Pose-Guided Generation first predicts a coarse clip, retrieves a plausible tail pose from a speaker-specific motion database, and refines the clip using this pose before continuing to the next window. During training, Stochastic Anchor Masking randomly masks pose and translation frames, teaching the model to recover complete motion from sparse boundary conditions. A part-aware DiT separates hand, body, and translation streams to reduce interference between global displacement and local articulation. On BEAT2, StreamTalk achieves state-of-the-art FGD, reduces long-horizon drift relative to open-loop baselines, and runs in real time at 76 FPS. Project page: https://xiangyue-zhang.github.io/StreamTalk/.

AI.tldr: StreamTalk is a closed-loop framework for real-time co-speech gesture generation that prevents drift by periodically retrieving a plausible tail pose from a speaker-specific motion database and refining each generated clip, achieving state-of-the-art FGD on BEAT2 while running at 76 FPS.
AI.motivation: Existing streaming gesture generation methods are open-loop, where each clip depends only on past context without any forward constraint, causing small errors to accumulate and drift over long sequences. The authors observe that the primary cause of failure is the lack of a forward constraint rather than poor short-clip quality, motivating them to add a destination anchor.
AI.method: StreamTalk uses a periodic generate-retrieve-refine cycle: (1) Streaming Pose-Guided Generation predicts a coarse clip, (2) retrieves a plausible tail pose from a speaker-specific motion database as a destination anchor, and (3) refines the clip using this pose before continuing. Training employs Stochastic Anchor Masking to randomly mask pose and translation frames, teaching the model to recover complete motion from sparse boundary conditions. A part-aware DiT separates hand, body, and translation streams to reduce interference between global displacement and local articulation.
AI.result: On BEAT2, StreamTalk achieves state-of-the-art FGD, reduces long-horizon drift compared to open-loop baselines, and runs in real time at 76 FPS.
AI.conclusion: Adding a forward constraint through retrieved tail pose anchors effectively limits drift in streaming gesture generation, demonstrating that closed-loop control with destination anchors is a viable solution for long-horizon motion generation.

title: CRAFT: Compression via Recursive Adaptive Fusion of Video Tokens for Vision-Language Models
summary: In video understanding, vision-language models (VLMs) must ingest massive numbers of visual tokens, causing the computational and memory cost of the prefill stage to rise sharply. Such visual sequences are highly redundant along the spatio-temporal dimension, yet a high compression ratio is often accompanied by the loss of critical details. Existing token-compression methods either employ heuristic, training-free compression with limited content adaptivity or introduce additional modules that require expensive alignment training, leaving the trade-off between efficiency and adaptivity unresolved. To alleviate this limitation, we propose CRAFT: Compression via Recursive Adaptive Fusion of Video Tokens. CRAFT recursively merges tokens by decoupling parameter-free token selection from learnable token fusion: global similarity determines which tokens to merge, while a position-aware weighting module and a content-adaptive channel-wise gate learn how to fuse them. The whole compression pipeline is query-agnostic. Because every retained token is a linear combination of the original tokens, CRAFT preserves their true spatio-temporal coordinates and stays aligned with the pre-trained language model's input distribution. Experiments on multiple representative video benchmarks show that CRAFT consistently outperforms prior state-of-the-art token-compression methods. At about $8\times$ compression, it retains roughly $97\%$ of the backbone's average accuracy and shows significant efficiency improvement.

AI.tldr: CRAFT is a video token compression method that recursively merges visual tokens via parameter-free selection and learnable fusion, preserving spatio-temporal coordinates and achieving ~8x compression with ~97% accuracy retention.
AI.motivation: Video VLMs suffer from massive visual token counts, causing high prefill computational/memory costs. Existing token compression methods face a trade-off: heuristic training-free approaches lack content adaptivity, while learnable methods require expensive alignment training.
AI.method: CRAFT recursively merges tokens by decoupling parameter-free token selection (based on global similarity) from learnable token fusion (a position-aware weighting module and content-adaptive channel-wise gate). The pipeline is query-agnostic, and each retained token is a linear combination of original tokens, preserving true spatio-temporal coordinates and staying aligned with the pretrained LM's input distribution.
AI.result: CRAFT consistently outperforms prior state-of-the-art token-compression methods on multiple representative video benchmarks. At ~8x compression, it retains roughly 97% of the backbone's average accuracy with significant efficiency improvement.
AI.conclusion: By resolving the trade-off between efficiency and adaptivity, CRAFT demonstrates that recursive fusion with decoupled selection and learnable fusion can achieve high compression ratios while preserving critical details and model alignment.

title: StreamSplat: Streaming Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting
summary: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting enables efficient novel-view synthesis without per-scene optimization, but most existing methods assume a fixed set of context views and process them jointly. This limits their applicability to online scenarios where calibrated views arrive sequentially and the scene must be updated causally. We present \emph{StreamSplat}, a streaming feed-forward 3DGS framework that incrementally maintains a persistent geometry-grounded scene state and decodes it into renderable 3D Gaussians after each input chunk. StreamSplat centers on a \textbf{Voxel-Aligned Causal Cache (VACC)}, which stores historical 3D tokens in a memory-bounded voxel structure so that memory grows with explored scene geometry rather than stream length. To better reuse history during causal prediction, we introduce \textbf{History-Projected Depth Anchoring (HPDA)} to project cached geometry as depth guidance for current cost-volume estimation, and \textbf{Cache-Guided Feature Injection (CGFI)} to inject cached latent evidence into Gaussian-token regression. Experiments on DL3DV, RealEstate10K, and ScanNet show that StreamSplat remains competitive with state-of-the-art feed-forward 3DGS methods under sparse causal inputs, despite not using future views or full-scene context. More importantly, it scales to long input streams with 256, 512, and 1024 views where fixed-view baselines run out of memory, yielding sustained improvements in novel-view synthesis quality as more observations arrive. The code will be made publicly available upon acceptance.

AI.tldr: StreamSplat is a streaming feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that incrementally maintains a persistent geometry-grounded scene state, using a Voxel-Aligned Causal Cache (VACC) and associated mechanisms (HPDA, CGFI) to enable causal novel-view synthesis from arbitrarily long input view sequences without per-scene optimization or fixed-context assumptions.
AI.motivation: Existing feed-forward 3DGS methods assume a fixed set of context views and process them jointly, which limits their applicability to online/streaming scenarios where calibrated views arrive sequentially and the scene must be updated causally in real time.
AI.method: StreamSplat uses a Voxel-Aligned Causal Cache (VACC) to store historical 3D tokens in a memory-bounded voxel structure where memory grows with explored geometry rather than stream length. It introduces History-Projected Depth Anchoring (HPDA) to project cached geometry as depth guidance for cost-volume estimation, and Cache-Guided Feature Injection (CGFI) to inject cached latent evidence into Gaussian-token regression.
AI.result: On DL3DV, RealEstate10K, and ScanNet, StreamSplat remains competitive with state-of-the-art feed-forward 3DGS methods under sparse causal inputs, and scales to long streams (256, 512, 1024 views) where fixed-view baselines run out of memory, with sustained quality improvements as more observations arrive.
AI.conclusion: StreamSplat demonstrates that streaming feed-forward 3DGS is both feasible and effective, providing scalable novel-view synthesis for long sequential inputs without requiring future views or full-scene context, while maintaining competitive quality with non-streaming baselines.

title: Ground, Cover, and Refine: Evidence-Centric Frame Selection for Long-Video Question Answering
summary: Long-video question answering requires identifying sparse yet critical evidence from videos containing thousands of frames under a constrained visual-token budget. Existing methods either select query-aware frames in a single pass or rely on timestamped text solely as retrieval guidance, leading to two key limitations. First, selected frames tend to cluster around local relevance peaks, and once the budget is exhausted, omitted evidence cannot be recovered. Second, textual and visual evidence remain weakly aligned. We propose GCR, a training-free framework that casts fixed-budget frame selection as a joint evidence curation problem. Ground converts timestamped text into temporal events, selects query-relevant real frame anchors, and renders each event text onto its temporally aligned frame. Cover supplements grounded events with direct visual anchors for complementary visual evidence and applies global maximal marginal relevance to preserve diverse context. Refine revisits omitted temporal regions and replaces the weakest revisable context frame with a real-frame medoid---but only when the medoid offers greater evidence value. GCR maintains a fixed number of chronologically ordered frames and requires no VLM training or architectural modification. Experiments on LongVideoBench and Video-MME, across three 7B backbones and frame budgets of 8, 32, and 64, demonstrate consistent improvements in long-video QA. With the 7B LLaVA-OV backbone and 32 frames, GCR achieves 64.25% and 62.15% on the two benchmarks, outperforming the strongest reproduced baselines by 2.54 and 1.93 percentage points, respectively.

AI.tldr: GCR is a training-free framework for long-video question answering that casts fixed-budget frame selection as a joint evidence curation problem, combining grounded text-to-visual event anchoring with direct visual evidence supplementation and iterative refinement to achieve consistent improvements over baselines across multiple benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Long-video QA faces two key limitations in existing methods: (1) single-pass frame selection clusters around local relevance peaks, causing omitted evidence to be unrecoverable once the budget is exhausted; (2) textual and visual evidence remain weakly aligned. These issues prevent effective evidence discovery in videos with thousands of frames under constrained visual-token budgets.
AI.method: GCR consists of three components: (1) Ground converts timestamped text into temporal events, selects query-relevant real frame anchors, and renders event text onto temporally aligned frames; (2) Cover supplements grounded events with direct visual anchors for complementary evidence and applies global maximal marginal relevance to preserve diverse context; (3) Refine revisits omitted temporal regions and replaces the weakest revisable context frame with a real-frame medoid when it offers greater evidence value. The framework maintains chronologically ordered frames, requires no VLM training or architectural changes.
AI.result: On LongVideoBench and Video-MME, across three 7B backbones and frame budgets of 8, 32, and 64, GCR shows consistent improvements. With the 7B LLaVA-OV backbone and 32 frames, GCR achieves 64.25% and 62.15% on the two benchmarks, outperforming the strongest reproduced baselines by 2.54 and 1.93 percentage points respectively.
AI.conclusion: GCR demonstrates that joint evidence curation through grounded event anchoring, visual supplementation, and targeted refinement can effectively address the trade-offs in long-video frame selection, delivering consistent QA improvements without requiring model training or architecture changes.

title: FairForensics: Seeing Expressions and Parsing Demographics via Vision-Language Modeling for Generalizable Fair Deepfake Detection
summary: The challenge of fair deepfake detection (FDD) has attracted increasing attention. Existing fairness-enhanced detectors often suffer from suboptimal generalization to unseen manipulations and fairness across demographic groups. They are typically developed and evaluated on demographically imbalanced distributions, resulting in biased predictions toward minority groups. In this paper, we construct a novel demographically balanced FDD benchmark to train and evaluate the fairness of detectors under both balanced and imbalanced population scenarios. Additionally, we introduce a novel expression and demographic perceptual vision-language model, termed FairForensics, for generalizable fair deepfake detection. FairForensics conducts face forgery generalization enhancement and demographic-aware fairness regularization. During face forgery generalization enhancement, built upon the novel observation of significant distribution differences between pristine and forged expression vectors, we design an expression encoder to capture high-level expression-guided forgery patterns, and an expression-perceptual visual encoder that integrates global appearance and expression forgery features while mitigating identity bias using an identity-aware patch perturbation module. Under demographic-aware fairness regularization, we propose a demographic-guided language encoder to extract population-aware global language embeddings, which boosts the decoupling of forgery features from demographic information via vision-language alignment. We devise a population-aware prototype fairness objective to enforce both inter-class separability and intra-class alignment across demographic subgroups. Extensive experiments on our balanced demographic benchmark show that our method achieves the state-of-the-art in terms of generalization and fairness.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the challenge of fair deepfake detection (FDD) by constructing a demographically balanced benchmark and introducing FairForensics, a vision-language model that enhances face forgery generalization while enforcing demographic-aware fairness regularization through expression-guided forgery patterns and population-aware prototype fairness objectives.
AI.motivation: Existing fairness-enhanced deepfake detectors suffer from poor generalization to unseen manipulations and suboptimal fairness across demographic groups, largely due to development and evaluation on demographically imbalanced datasets that bias predictions against minority groups.
AI.method: FairForensics consists of two main components: (1) Face forgery generalization enhancement, which uses an expression encoder to capture high-level expression-guided forgery patterns and an expression-perceptual visual encoder integrating global appearance with forgery features while mitigating identity bias via an identity-aware patch perturbation module; (2) Demographic-aware fairness regularization, which uses a demographic-guided language encoder for population-aware global embeddings, with vision-language alignment decoupling forgery features from demographic information, plus a population-aware prototype fairness objective enforcing inter-class separability and intra-class alignment across subgroups.
AI.result: Experiments on the newly constructed demographically balanced benchmark demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in both generalization and fairness compared to existing methods.
AI.conclusion: The proposed demographically balanced benchmark and FairForensics framework effectively improve both generalization to unseen manipulations and fairness across demographic groups in deepfake detection, addressing key limitations of prior fairness-enhanced detectors.

title: Few-Shot Concept Prompt Learning for Segmentation Foundation Models via Visual Grounding
summary: Promptable segmentation foundation models (FMs) such as SAM3 and Medical SAM3 promise few-shot, interactively-specified segmentation for medical imaging through a natural language interface, yet their performance on clinical tasks falls well short of this promise. We posit that this shortfall is not an artefact of insufficient medical pretraining or imperfect prompt phrasing, but a structural limitation that will persist in any domain where paired image-text supervision is scarce, as it is across most clinical modalities. We further hypothesize that the limitation is specific to natural language as a control signal: a visually grounded prompt, learned directly from the target distribution, should recover the lost performance without additional image-text data or backbone retraining. We propose Few-Shot Concept Prompt Learning (FS-CPL), which learns a continuous concept prompt embedding $\mathbf{p}^* \in \mathbb{R}^{T \times d}$ from a small support set of $K$ image--mask pairs via mask supervision, with the encoder-decoder backbone frozen. Across four public benchmarks spanning ultrasound and endoscopy (BUSI, HC18, TN3K, CVC-Clinic), FS-CPL delivers absolute Dice improvements of up to $+0.62$ over canonical text prompts and is \emph{backbone-agnostic}: it lifts both vanilla SAM3 and the domain-specifically pretrained Medical SAM3, showing that visual concept prompting is complementary to in-domain pretraining.

AI.tldr: FS-CPL learns a continuous concept prompt embedding from K image-mask pairs to replace natural language prompts in promptable segmentation foundation models, achieving up to +0.62 Dice improvement over text prompts across four medical imaging benchmarks, while being backbone-agnostic and compatible with domain-specific pretraining.
AI.motivation: Promptable segmentation FMs (SAM3, Medical SAM3) underperform on clinical tasks, and the authors argue this is a structural limitation of natural language as a control signal in domains with scarce paired image-text supervision, not a pretraining or prompt phrasing issue.
AI.method: FS-CPL learns a continuous concept prompt embedding p* in R^{T×d} from a small support set of K image-mask pairs via mask supervision, with the encoder-decoder backbone frozen.
AI.result: Across four public benchmarks (BUSI, HC18, TN3K, CVC-Clinic), FS-CPL delivers absolute Dice improvements up to +0.62 over canonical text prompts, and works with both vanilla SAM3 and Medical SAM3, showing complementarity with in-domain pretraining.
AI.conclusion: Visual concept prompting is a complementary and effective alternative to natural language prompting for clinical segmentation, recovering performance lost due to scarce image-text supervision without additional pretraining data or backbone changes.

title: FAU at ImageCLEF 2026 Task on Multimodal Reasoning Robust Candidate Scoring and Concise Multilingual Visual Answering
comment: 16 pages, 3 figures, 7 tables. CLEF 2026 Working Notes, ImageCLEF 2026 Multimodal Reasoning Task
summary: We present our ImageCLEF 2026 Multimodal Reasoning system for the Visual Multiple Choice Question Answering (Visual MCQ) and Visual Open Question Answering (Visual OpenQA) subtasks. The challenge requires reliable reasoning over multilingual educational and scientific images with dense text, diagrams, charts, tables, formulas, and units, while enforcing strict answer formats. Our central finding is that robust output control is as important as model choice. For Visual MCQ, we replace fragile free-form generation with direct candidate label scoring from vision-language model logits, then combine complementary runs through score fusion and voting. For Visual OpenQA, we use image enhancement, concise final answer prompting, deterministic decoding, and targeted post-processing to remove reasoning traces and formatting artifacts. Without task-specific model training, our official submissions achieved third place in Visual MCQ with 0.7108 accuracy and first place in Visual OpenQA with 0.6488 COMET, 0.1391 BLEU, 0.2762 ROUGE L, and 0.2383 METEOR. The results highlight the practical value of inference engineering: careful scoring, ensembling, prompting, and cleanup can turn strong VLMs into reliable competition systems.

AI.tldr: The paper describes a system for ImageCLEF 2026 multimodal reasoning tasks, achieving 3rd place in Visual MCQ (0.7108 accuracy) and 1st place in Visual OpenQA by using inference engineering techniques like candidate label scoring, ensemble fusion, prompting, and post-processing—without any task-specific model training.
AI.motivation: Multimodal reasoning over educational and scientific images (with dense text, diagrams, charts, tables, formulas) is challenging, and the authors argue that robust output control is as important as model choice for reliable performance in such competition settings.
AI.method: For Visual MCQ, free-form generation is replaced with direct candidate label scoring from VLM logits, combined with score fusion and voting across runs. For Visual OpenQA, the system uses image enhancement, concise answer prompting, deterministic decoding, and targeted post-processing to strip reasoning traces and formatting artifacts.
AI.result: Achieved 3rd place in Visual MCQ with 0.7108 accuracy, and 1st place in Visual OpenQA with 0.6488 COMET, 0.1391 BLEU, 0.2762 ROUGE L, and 0.2383 METEOR scores—all without task-specific training.
AI.conclusion: Inference engineering—careful scoring, ensembling, prompting, and cleanup—can transform strong VLMs into reliable competition systems, highlighting that non-training interventions provide significant practical value.

title: Generative Brownian Bridge Diffusion In Motion Space For Enhanced Myocardial Strain Analysis
summary: Myocardial strain analysis of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) images provides an important tool for evaluating cardiac function. However, current techniques require either human-adjusted post-processing with suboptimal regional accuracy, or specialized and costly imaging acquisitions. In this paper, we propose to leverage the power of generative models to synthesize high-quality motion-derived strain values from routinely acquired CMR sequences. Specifically, we develop a novel Brownian bridge diffusion model in motion space to learn the probabilistic mapping between standard CMR motion estimated from widely adopted registration methods and highly accurate motion provided by advanced strain imaging techniques. To promote the fidelity of anatomical structure in the generation process, our model is conditioned on the corresponding CMR images. We validate our method on large-scale multi-center CMR datasets including subjects of paired standard cine CMR and advanced strain imaging acquisitions. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework significantly improves the accuracy of motion prediction and strain analysis from standard CMRs compared to existing learning-based approaches. Our research represents a new paradigm for potentially developing cost-effective, clinically deployable AI tools for cardiac function assessment with enhanced strain accuracy in busy clinical workflows. Our code is publicly available at anonymous.4open.science/r/Brownian-Bridge-strain-analysis-1140.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a novel Brownian bridge diffusion model that synthesizes high-quality myocardial strain values from routine cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) sequences, bridging the gap between standard registration-based motion estimates and advanced strain imaging motion data, conditioned on CMR images for anatomical fidelity.
AI.motivation: Current myocardial strain analysis from CMR requires either human-adjusted post-processing with poor regional accuracy, or specialized/expensive imaging acquisitions. The authors aim to enable cost-effective, clinically deployable strain analysis using routinely acquired CMR data.
AI.method: A Brownian bridge diffusion model is developed in motion space to learn the probabilistic mapping between coarse motion from standard registration methods and highly accurate motion from advanced strain imaging techniques. The model is conditioned on corresponding CMR images to preserve anatomical structure fidelity during generation.
AI.result: Validation on large-scale multi-center CMR datasets shows significant improvements in motion prediction and strain analysis accuracy over existing learning-based approaches.
AI.conclusion: The work introduces a new paradigm for cost-effective, clinically deployable AI tools for cardiac function assessment with enhanced strain accuracy in busy clinical workflows. Code is publicly available.

title: Generative AI and Foundation Models in Medical Image
summary: In recent years, generative AI has attracted significant public attention, and its use has been rapidly expanding across a wide range of domains. From creative tasks such as text summarization, idea generation, and source code generation, to the streamlining of medical support tasks like diagnostic report generation and summarization, AI is now deeply involved in many areas. Today's breadth of AI applications is clearly distinct from what was seen before generative AI gained widespread recognition. Representative generative AI services include DALL-E 3 (OpenAI, California, USA) and Stable Diffusion (Stability AI, London, England, UK) for image generation, ChatGPT (OpenAI, California, USA), and Gemini (Google, California, USA) for text generation. The rise of generative AI has been influenced by advances in deep learning models and the scaling up of data, models, and computational resources based on the scaling laws. Moreover, the emergence of foundation models, which are trained on large-scale datasets and possess general-purpose knowledge applicable to various downstream tasks, is creating a new paradigm in AI development. These shifts brought about by generative AI and foundation models also profoundly impact medical image processing, fundamentally changing the framework for AI development in healthcare. This paper provides an overview of diffusion models used in image generation AI and large language models (LLMs) used in text generation AI, and introduces their applications in medical support. This paper also discusses foundation models, which are gaining attention alongside generative AI, including their construction methods and applications in the medical field. Finally, the paper explores how to develop foundation models and high-performance AI for medical support by fully utilizing national data and computational resources.

AI.tldr: This paper provides an overview of generative AI technologies—including diffusion models for image generation and large language models (LLMs) for text generation—and their applications in medical support, while also discussing foundation models, their construction methods, and strategies for developing high-performance medical AI using national data and computational resources.
AI.motivation: Generative AI and foundation models have rapidly expanded across many domains including healthcare, fundamentally changing the framework for AI development in medical image processing. The paper aims to provide an overview of these technologies and their medical applications, while exploring how to leverage national data and computational resources to build high-performance medical AI.
AI.method: The paper is an overview/survey that covers: (1) diffusion models used in image generation AI, (2) large language models (LLMs) used in text generation AI, (3) their applications in medical support, (4) foundation models including their construction methods and medical applications, and (5) strategies for developing foundation models and high-performance medical AI using national data and computational resources.
AI.result: The paper presents a comprehensive overview of generative AI technologies (DALL-E 3, Stable Diffusion, ChatGPT, Gemini) and their medical applications, along with foundation model construction methods and their role in the medical field, culminating in a discussion of how to build high-performance medical AI at a national scale.
AI.conclusion: Generative AI and foundation models are fundamentally reshaping medical AI development. The paper concludes by proposing ways to develop high-performance medical support AI through the strategic utilization of national data and computational resources.

title: Entity-Aware Sequence Transduction for Player-Centric Ball Action Spotting
summary: Player-centric ball action spotting requires temporally precise event detection together with actor attribution in crowded, partially observed multi-agent sports videos. Existing Denoising Sequence Transduction (DST) baselines treat the player-role dimension as part of a flattened frame-level representation, which weakens the inductive bias for modeling player-specific temporal evolution and inter-player interactions. To address this limitation, we propose Multi-Entity Denoising Sequence Transduction (ME-DST). ME-DST keeps the role-slot dimension throughout encoding. It uses temporal attention to model the history of each role slot, and spatial attention to exchange information across role slots at each frame. This factorized design gives the model a direct structure for separating within-player evolution from inter-player context. We also add learnable role embeddings, tracking-derived tactical features, and fused visual predictions from X3D-L and Swin3D-S. Experiments on the FOOTPASS dataset show that ME-DST reaches a Micro F1 of 0.778. This improves the strongest official TAAD+DST baseline by 10.3 percentage points. Controlled ablations show that preserving the entity axis and encoding role identity are central to this gain. These results suggest that explicit entity modeling is an effective inductive bias for player-centric sports event understanding.

AI.tldr: ME-DST improves player-centric ball action spotting by keeping role-slot dimensions throughout encoding, using factorized temporal/spatial attention, achieving 0.778 Micro F1 on FOOTPASS (10.3 pp over baseline).
AI.motivation: Existing DST baselines flatten the player-role dimension into frame-level representations, which weakens the inductive bias needed to model player-specific temporal evolution and inter-player interactions in crowded, partially observed sports videos.
AI.method: ME-DST preserves role-slot dimensions throughout encoding, uses temporal attention for each role slot's history and spatial attention to exchange info across role slots per frame; adds learnable role embeddings, tracking-derived tactical features, and fused visual predictions from X3D-L and Swin3D-S.
AI.result: Achieves Micro F1 of 0.778 on FOOTPASS, improving the strongest official TAAD+DST baseline by 10.3 percentage points.
AI.conclusion: Explicit entity modeling is an effective inductive bias for player-centric sports event understanding; preserving the entity axis and encoding role identity are central to the gain.

title: UniSim-SLAM: Feed-Forward SLAM with Unified Sim(3) Optimization
summary: Recent geometric foundation models enable feed-forward inference for SLAM, but their predictions are strongly dependent on the input view set, which leads to geometric inconsistencies and trajectory drift when results are chained over long sequences. Online deployment further exposes a trade-off between the low latency of two-view tracking and the constraint richness of multi-view inference. We introduce UniSim-SLAM, an integrated system that runs lightweight two-view keyframe tracking in the frontend and performs periodic multi-view submap refinement in the backend. To combine predictions defined in heterogeneous local coordinates with inconsistent scales, we formulate a unified multi-level factor graph on $Sim(3)$ that jointly optimizes global keyframe poses and submap poses. The graph integrates temporal view-to-view odometry edges, view-to-submap bridge edges with depth-statistics scale anchoring, and submap-to-submap tie and scale constraints to enforce consistent similarity relations across submaps. Experiments on TUM RGB-D and 7-Scenes show that UniSim-SLAM achieves state-of-the-art accuracy in the uncalibrated setting, reducing trajectory error by $38.5\% $ on TUM RGB-D and $45.9\%$ on 7-Scenes compared to prior best results. Project page: https://vision3d-lab.github.io/unisim-slam/

AI.tldr: UniSim-SLAM is an integrated SLAM system that combines lightweight two-view keyframe tracking (frontend) with periodic multi-view submap refinement (backend), unified via a multi-level factor graph on Sim(3) that jointly optimizes global keyframe and submap poses with scale anchoring and consistency constraints, achieving SOTA accuracy in uncalibrated settings.
AI.motivation: Recent geometric foundation models enable feed-forward SLAM but their predictions depend heavily on input view sets, causing geometric inconsistencies and trajectory drift over long sequences. There is also an online deployment trade-off between the low latency of two-view tracking and the constraint richness of multi-view inference.
AI.method: The system uses lightweight two-view keyframe tracking in the frontend and periodic multi-view submap refinement in the backend. Predictions from heterogeneous local coordinates with inconsistent scales are combined using a unified multi-level factor graph on Sim(3) that jointly optimizes global keyframe poses and submap poses, integrating temporal view-to-view odometry edges, view-to-submap bridge edges with depth-statistics scale anchoring, and submap-to-submap tie and scale constraints.
AI.result: On TUM RGB-D and 7-Scenes, UniSim-SLAM achieves state-of-the-art accuracy in the uncalibrated setting, reducing trajectory error by 38.5% on TUM RGB-D and 45.9% on 7-Scenes compared to prior best results.
AI.conclusion: The proposed architecture successfully resolves the trade-off between latency and constraint richness by integrating two-view and multi-view inference in a unified Sim(3) factor graph framework, substantially improving SLAM accuracy over prior methods.

title: SpatialQuery: Benchmarking Geometry-Grounded Multi-Instance Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) achieve strong semantic understanding but remain unreliable in metric spatial reasoning, particularly when queries require comparing multiple instances of the same object category. We study this problem through the Closest-Instance Distance Query (CIDQ), where a model must identify the nearest visible candidate to a unique reference object and estimate their gravity-aligned floor-plane distance. We introduce SPATIALQUERY, a training- free framework for CIDQ reasoning from a single RGB image, together with SPATIALQUERY-1M, a benchmark containing over one million RGB-only question-answer pairs from 200 indoor scenes. SPATIALQUERY recovers instance-level metric geometry and transforms it into a canonical Bird's-Eye View through Scene Cubifying, which represents objects as uniformly sized, category-coded blocks to emphasize their relative floor- plane locations. We further propose Uncertainty-Aware Chain-of-Thought (UA-CoT) prompting, which incorporates geometry- derived per-instance uncertainty into the VLM reasoning process. Without task-specific fine-tuning or architectural modification, SPATIALQUERY with Qwen3-VL-8B achieves a Floor-MAE of 0.259 m, an Unc-Acc@0.3 m of 90.5%, and a proximity-decision accuracy of 84.18%, outperforming fine-tuned spatial specialists, general-purpose VLMs, and closed-source frontier models. Code, benchmark resources, and an interactive demo are available at https://namhai1810.github.io/SpatialQuery/.

AI.tldr: SPATIALQUERY is a training-free framework that enables vision-language models to perform metric spatial reasoning about closest-instance distances from single RGB images, using Scene Cubifying (canonical Bird's-Eye View representation) and Uncertainty-Aware Chain-of-Thought prompting. It achieves 0.259m Floor-MAE with Qwen3-VL-8B, outperforming fine-tuned specialists and closed-source models.
AI.motivation: VLMs excel at semantic understanding but fail at metric spatial reasoning, especially when queries require comparing multiple instances of the same object category (e.g., finding the closest instance to a reference).
AI.method: Two main components: (1) Scene Cubifying - recovers instance-level metric geometry from a single RGB image and transforms it into a canonical Bird's-Eye View with uniformly sized, category-coded blocks to emphasize relative floor-plane locations; (2) Uncertainty-Aware Chain-of-Thought (UA-CoT) prompting - incorporates geometry-derived per-instance uncertainty into the VLM reasoning process.
AI.result: With Qwen3-VL-8B, achieves Floor-MAE of 0.259m, Unc-Acc@0.3m of 90.5%, and proximity-decision accuracy of 84.18%, outperforming fine-tuned spatial specialists, general-purpose VLMs, and closed-source frontier models on the SPATIALQUERY-1M benchmark.
AI.conclusion: Training-free approaches with careful geometric preprocessing and uncertainty-aware prompting can surpass task-specific fine-tuning for metric spatial reasoning in VLMs, requiring no architectural modifications.

title: STC-Net: Electroluminescence-Based Solar Cell Crack Segmentation for Power Loss Estimation
summary: Accurate crack assessment in electroluminescence (EL) images is important for photovoltaic (PV) reliability analysis, yet existing segmentation methods often fail to capture the thin, elongated, and structurally constrained nature of crack defects. This paper proposes a Solar Topology Crack Network (STC-Net) that incorporates edge priors, spectral priors, and a boundary-topology refinement module to improve crack continuity and boundary preservation. The framework further extends segmentation to power-loss estimation by deriving a crack-associated inactive-area proxy from the predicted masks. Experiments on the PVEL-S dataset show that STC-Net achieves 95.98 MIoU, 98.01 MDice, and 98.00 MAcc during training, and 72.52 MIoU and 80.16 MDice on unseen test samples. These results demonstrate that STC-Net provides accurate crack localization while offering a practical link between EL-based defect segmentation and PV degradation assessment.

AI.tldr: STC-Net is a deep learning model that segments thin, elongated crack defects in electroluminescence (EL) images of solar panels by incorporating edge priors, spectral priors, and a boundary-topology refinement module, then extends segmentation to estimate power loss via a crack-associated inactive-area proxy. It achieves 95.98 MIoU during training and 72.52 MIoU on unseen test data from the PVEL-S dataset.
AI.motivation: Existing segmentation methods fail to accurately capture crack defects in EL images because cracks are thin, elongated, and structurally constrained, making accurate crack assessment critical for photovoltaic reliability analysis.
AI.method: STC-Net incorporates three key components: (1) edge priors to enhance boundary awareness, (2) spectral priors to capture frequency-domain characteristics, and (3) a boundary-topology refinement module to improve crack continuity and boundary preservation. The framework also derives a crack-associated inactive-area proxy from predicted masks to estimate power loss.
AI.result: On the PVEL-S dataset, STC-Net achieves 95.98 MIoU, 98.01 MDice, and 98.00 MAcc during training, and 72.52 MIoU and 80.16 MDice on unseen test samples.
AI.conclusion: STC-Net provides accurate crack localization in EL images and establishes a practical link between defect segmentation and PV degradation (power-loss) assessment.

title: When Extreme Darkness Meets Motion Blur: MeanFlow for Unified RAW Restoration
summary: Extremely low-light RAW enhancement aims to recover severely attenuated sensor signals, yet existing methods often focus on illumination and noise while overlooking the motion-induced degradations inherent in practical low-light imaging. We present a framework for robust extremely low-light RAW enhancement under realistic acquisition degradations. First, we introduce See in the Degraded Extremely Dark (SIDED), a new dataset that applies controlled motion degradation to extremely low-light RAW pairs while retaining their original sensor noise. Second, we propose a unified RAW tokenizer equipped with explicit domain-conditioned representation calibration to align extremely low-light and well-exposed RAW data, followed by a MeanFlow that performs enhancement in a single function evaluation. To our knowledge, this is the first work to formulate extremely low-light RAW enhancement under realistic motion-degraded acquisition and address it with MeanFlow. We further introduce a physics-guided refinement model to strengthen illumination--reflectance consistency, pixel fidelity, and color preservation without incurring additional inference cost. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our framework achieves state-of-the-art performance in extremely low-light RAW enhancement, and robustly handles coupled motion and noise degradations.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a framework for robust extremely low-light RAW enhancement that handles realistic motion-induced degradations, introducing the SIDED dataset with controlled motion degradation, a unified RAW tokenizer with domain-conditioned representation calibration, and a MeanFlow-based enhancement approach with a physics-guided refinement model.
AI.motivation: Existing extremely low-light RAW enhancement methods focus on illumination and noise but overlook motion-induced degradations that are inherent in practical low-light imaging scenarios.
AI.method: The framework includes: (1) SIDED dataset with controlled motion degradation on extremely low-light RAW pairs preserving original sensor noise, (2) a unified RAW tokenizer with explicit domain-conditioned representation calibration to align low-light and well-exposed RAW data, (3) MeanFlow for enhancement in a single function evaluation, and (4) a physics-guided refinement model for illumination-reflectance consistency, pixel fidelity, and color preservation without extra inference cost.
AI.result: The framework achieves state-of-the-art performance in extremely low-light RAW enhancement and robustly handles coupled motion and noise degradations.
AI.conclusion: This is the first work to formulate extremely low-light RAW enhancement under realistic motion-degraded acquisition and address it with MeanFlow, demonstrating robust performance on coupled motion and noise degradations.

title: G-Skin: Learning to Bind 3D Gaussians with Generative Visual Priors
summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting has achieved remarkable success in photorealistic and efficient rendering, leading to a rapid increase in 3D assets represented by 3D Gaussian primitives. Directly rigging these assets with arbitrary skeleton topologies is highly desirable. However, training a feed-forward skinning framework is infeasible due to the lack of high-quality 3D Gaussian rigging datasets. An alternative solution is to transfer mesh-based techniques to 3D Gaussian-based representation, but 3D Gaussian primitives are not restricted to the surface and lack explicit topological connectivity. Moreover, this kind of method suffers from poor generalization to unseen data due to its strong dependence on training data, while acquiring high-quality rigging data is prohibitively expensive. To address this challenging problem, we propose G-Skin, a novel generative skinning framework designed for expressive and high-fidelity animation with 3D Gaussian representation. To overcome this 3D data scarcity, we introduce a skeleton-controllable image generation model leveraging 2D vision foundation models to distill powerful motion priors into pseudo-guidance. Guided by these priors, we formulate an optimization pipeline incorporating geometry-aware regularizations, which stabilizes the learning process and ensures smooth, structurally coherent skinning weights. G-Skin also generalizes flexibly to the augmented variants of 3D Gaussian representation designed to mitigate animation-induced rendering artifacts. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of our approach, demonstrating clear advantages over state-of-the-art methods. Project page: https://yaoyx689.github.io/GSkin.html.

AI.tldr: G-Skin is a generative skinning framework for animating 3D Gaussian Splatting assets. It overcomes the lack of 3D rigging datasets by using a skeleton-controllable image generation model with 2D vision foundation models to distill motion priors, then optimizes skinning weights with geometry-aware regularizations to produce smooth, coherent animations.
AI.motivation: 3D Gaussian Splatting has become popular for photorealistic rendering, creating many 3D Gaussian assets. However, rigging these assets with arbitrary skeleton topologies is challenging because: (1) no high-quality 3D Gaussian rigging datasets exist for training feed-forward skinning frameworks, and (2) transferring mesh-based techniques to 3D Gaussian representation is problematic since Gaussian primitives lack surface restriction and explicit topological connectivity. Existing methods also suffer from poor generalization due to scarce, expensive rigging data.
AI.method: G-Skin introduces a skeleton-controllable image generation model that leverages 2D vision foundation models to distill motion priors into pseudo-guidance, circumventing the 3D data scarcity problem. Using these priors, it formulates an optimization pipeline with geometry-aware regularizations to stabilize learning and produce smooth, structurally coherent skinning weights. It also generalizes to augmented variants of 3D Gaussian representation designed to mitigate animation-induced rendering artifacts.
AI.result: Extensive experiments validate G-Skin's effectiveness, showing clear advantages over state-of-the-art methods in expressive and high-fidelity animation of 3D Gaussian representations.
AI.conclusion: G-Skin provides a practical solution for skinning 3D Gaussian assets with arbitrary skeleton topologies by leveraging 2D motion priors instead of expensive 3D rigging data, achieving superior animation quality and generalization to unseen data.

title: Learning Where to Look and How to Judge: Resolution-agnostic Image Quality Assessment with Quality-aware Saliency
comment: Accepted to the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR) 2026
summary: No-reference image quality assessment (NR IQA) has recently benefited from deep and multimodal models, yet many SOTA systems still violate at least one basic requirement: they either discard critical quality cues via aggressive resizing, fail to generalize across resolutions, cannot be jointly trained on heterogeneous IQA datasets with mismatched MOS scales, or require prohibitive computation. We present \textbf{ReLIQS}, a model for \textbf{Re}solution-agnostic \textbf{L}earning for \textbf{I}mage \textbf{Q}uality with \textbf{S}aliency, which is resolution-agnostic, preserves original-resolution quality cues, learns from multiple subjective studies, and remains computationally efficient and budget-adaptive. ReLIQS is a CLIP-based multiscale patch-driven architecture that learns both \emph{where to look} and \emph{how to judge} quality. Fixed-size patches are sampled across multiple resolutions, including the original resolution, and encoded with a CLIP vision backbone. A lightweight Perceptual Importance Estimator then predicts IQA-specific importance maps to select a small set of informative patches, and a Latent Quality Axis Module aggregates their embeddings into a single image-level score. Across authentic, synthetic, and AIGC benchmarks spanning diverse resolutions and distortions, ReLIQS generalizes better than strong CNN-, CLIP-, and MLLM-based baselines with matching or reduced computational cost.

AI.tldr: ReLIQS is a resolution-agnostic, computationally efficient NR IQA model that uses a CLIP-based multiscale patch-driven architecture with a Perceptual Importance Estimator to select informative patches and a Latent Quality Axis Module to aggregate quality scores, generalizing across diverse benchmarks while preserving original-resolution quality cues.
AI.motivation: Existing NR IQA systems violate basic requirements: they discard quality cues via aggressive resizing, fail to generalize across resolutions, cannot handle heterogeneous datasets with mismatched MOS scales, or require prohibitive computation.
AI.method: ReLIQS is a CLIP-based multiscale patch-driven architecture. Fixed-size patches are sampled across multiple resolutions (including original) and encoded with a CLIP vision backbone. A lightweight Perceptual Importance Estimator predicts IQA-specific importance maps to select informative patches, and a Latent Quality Axis Module aggregates embeddings into an image-level score.
AI.result: Across authentic, synthetic, and AIGC benchmarks spanning diverse resolutions and distortions, ReLIQS generalizes better than strong CNN-, CLIP-, and MLLM-based baselines with matching or reduced computational cost.
AI.conclusion: ReLIQS demonstrates that it is possible to build NR IQA systems that are resolution-agnostic, preserve original quality cues, learn from multiple subjective studies, and remain computationally efficient and budget-adaptive simultaneously.

title: IDraw: Artist Verification from Digital Drawing Images
summary: As digital drawings are increasingly shared online, reliable authorship verification has become important for protecting artists and resolving disputes. Yet when authorship is questioned, verification may have to rely only on the disputed drawing and reference drawings known to be created by the claimed artist. This setting is challenging for two reasons. First, artist-specific drawing behavior, such as pen pressure and movement speed, is informative but is not available from a completed drawing. Second, similarities in the depicted object or scene can obscure similarities arising from the artist. We propose IDraw, a framework that learns from drawings paired with tablet-pen sensor signals collected from separate training artists. This allows IDraw to infer drawing behavior from completed images during a later authorship dispute, without requiring sensor data from the artist being verified. IDraw also reduces the influence of drawing content by identifying information shared by drawings of the same object across different artists and suppressing it before comparing drawings. To support this approach, we construct the first multimodal dataset for digital drawing authorship verification, containing 1,110 drawings from 37 artists and 14 types of tablet-pen sensor signals. Evaluated on previously unseen artists across nine image-encoder backbones, IDraw consistently outperforms standard image-based verification and reduces verification error by up to 40%. These results demonstrate that inferring drawing behavior from completed images and suppressing drawing content improve digital drawing authorship verification.

AI.tldr: IDraw is a framework for digital drawing authorship verification that learns to infer drawing behavior (e.g., pen pressure, movement speed) from completed images using paired tablet-pen sensor data from separate training artists, and suppresses drawing-content similarities to improve verification accuracy by up to 40% over standard image-based baselines.
AI.motivation: Reliable authorship verification for digital drawings is important in practice, but when authorship is disputed, only the disputed drawing and reference drawings are available. Two challenges arise: (1) informative artist-specific behaviors like pen pressure and speed are not directly observable from completed images, and (2) similarities in depicted content can confound artist similarity signals.
AI.method: IDraw trains on drawings paired with tablet-pen sensor signals from separate artists, enabling it to infer drawing behavior from completed images at inference time without requiring sensor data from the verified artist. It also identifies and suppresses content-related information shared across drawings of the same object from different artists before comparing drawings. A new multimodal dataset with 1,110 drawings from 37 artists and 14 sensor signal types was constructed for this task.
AI.result: Across nine image-encoder backbones on previously unseen artists, IDraw consistently outperforms standard image-based verification, reducing verification error by up to 40%.
AI.conclusion: Inferring drawing behavior from completed images and suppressing drawing content both improve digital drawing authorship verification, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: SPECTRA: Band-Routed Embedding and Stage-Wise LoRA for Cross-Sensor Fine-Tuning of Geospatial Foundation Models
summary: Geospatial foundation models (GeoFMs), pretrained on large-scale geospatial data such as Earth observation (EO), climate, and weather data, have shown promising performance when fine-tuned on diverse downstream tasks. However, there are two challenges of adapting EO-pretrained GeoFMs to practical downstream datasets. The first challenge is how to handle spectral mismatch: pretrained patch embeddings expect a fixed set of input bands, whereas downstream sensors may provide different channels. The second challenge is how to reduce fine-tuning cost and make it efficient. While existing work has made efforts on these challenges individually, jointly improving fine-tuning performance under spectral mismatch while reducing adaptation cost remains underexplored. We propose SPECTRA, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning framework that addresses both spectral mismatch and adaptation cost. To handle spectral mismatch, SPECTRA introduces Band-Routed Embedding (BRE), which maps all available downstream bands into the band space expected by the pretrained GeoFM. By using BRE, all available bands in the downstream dataset are utilized to improve the selected-band input without changing the pretrained patch embedding interface. To reduce adaptation cost, SPECTRA further introduces a Stage-wise Transferability-aware LoRA (ST-LoRA) fine-tuning. ST-LoRA estimates stage-wise transferability before fine-tuning and assigns stage-specific LoRA ranks, concentrating trainable parameters on the stages with high transferability for the target task.
