Across three EO-pretrained GeoFMs and four downstream segmentation datasets, experiments show that BRE improves performance by utilizing all spectral bands, while ST-LoRA reduces trainable parameters compared with full fine-tuning and standard LoRA. Code is available at https://github.com/big-data-lab-umbc/SPECTRA.

AI.tldr: SPECTRA is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning framework for geospatial foundation models (GeoFMs) that addresses two challenges: spectral mismatch (downstream sensors providing different bands than pretrained models expect) and high fine-tuning cost. It introduces Band-Routed Embedding (BRE) to map all available downstream bands into the pretrained model's expected band space, and Stage-wise Transferability-aware LoRA (ST-LoRA) that estimates stage-wise transferability and assigns stage-specific LoRA ranks to concentrate trainable parameters where they matter most.
AI.motivation: GeoFMs pretrained on Earth observation data perform well when fine-tuned on downstream tasks, but two practical challenges hinder adaptation: (1) spectral mismatch between pretrained patch embeddings (which expect fixed input bands) and downstream sensor channels, and (2) high fine-tuning cost. While prior work addresses these issues separately, jointly handling spectral mismatch while reducing adaptation cost remains unexplored.
AI.method: SPECTRA introduces two key components: (1) Band-Routed Embedding (BRE) maps all available downstream spectral bands into the band space expected by the pretrained GeoFM, utilizing all available bands without altering the pretrained patch embedding interface; (2) Stage-wise Transferability-aware LoRA (ST-LoRA) estimates stage-wise transferability before fine-tuning and assigns stage-specific LoRA ranks, concentrating trainable parameters on high-transferability stages for the target task.
AI.result: Across three EO-pretrained GeoFMs and four downstream segmentation datasets, experiments show that BRE improves performance by leveraging all spectral bands, while ST-LoRA reduces trainable parameters compared to both full fine-tuning and standard LoRA.
AI.conclusion: SPECTRA effectively addresses both spectral mismatch and adaptation cost challenges in fine-tuning GeoFMs, achieving better performance through full spectral band utilization while reducing trainable parameter count via transferability-aware LoRA rank allocation. Code is publicly available.

title: Can Urban Blight Be Accessed with Vision-language Models: A Case Study in Detroit
summary: Addressing urban blight has seen increased focus in the past 15 years. Assessing urban blight is essential for guiding urban planning, targeting rehabilitation, and safeguarding public health, yet traditional residential blight surveys are difficult to maintain at scale due to the labor-intensive cost and long-term cycle. This study introduced a scalable framework for estimating residential blight using open-source large vision-language models on multiple views. Structured prompts guided models to evaluate housing attributes, including roof integrity, wall damage, and broken or boarded openings, producing both binary assessments and probabilistic estimates of disrepair. To evaluate the performance of these visual assessments, we compared professional human annotations of these features across several models, including an ensemble stacking approach based on XGBoost and a weighted scoring system. Results showed that (i) multiple street views can contribute to the improvement of accuracy, (ii) large vision-language models have different strengths of inference, (iii) the ensemble learner outperforms individual base models, enhancing robustness across all residential conditions and blight assessment. The practical application of the method allows low-cost tracking and management of housing stock conditions, providing a regularly updatable complement to traditional blight surveys.

AI.tldr: This study introduces a scalable framework for estimating residential blight using open-source large vision-language models on multiple street views. The framework evaluates housing attributes like roof integrity, wall damage, and broken/b boarded openings, and an ensemble approach (XGBoost-based stacking with weighted scoring) outperforms individual models in accuracy and robustness, enabling low-cost, regularly updatable blight assessment.
AI.motivation: Traditional residential blight surveys are labor-intensive and have long cycles, making them difficult to maintain at scale. There is a need for scalable, regularly updatable methods to assess urban blight for planning, rehabilitation, and public health.
AI.method: The study uses open-source large vision-language models on multiple street views with structured prompts to evaluate housing attributes (roof integrity, wall damage, broken/boarded openings), producing binary and probabilistic estimates. Performance is compared against human annotations using several models, including an ensemble stacking approach based on XGBoost and a weighted scoring system.
AI.result: (i) Multiple street views improve assessment accuracy, (ii) different large vision-language models have varying inference strengths, and (iii) the ensemble learner outperforms individual base models, enhancing robustness across all residential conditions and blight assessment.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method enables low-cost tracking and management of housing stock conditions, providing a regularly updatable complement to traditional blight surveys.

title: Pixel Ignores, Superpixel Sees: Adverse Weather Image Restoration via Semantic-Center SSM
summary:
Adverse weather image restoration aims to recover clear visibility from degraded images in complex weather conditions.
  Existing works attempt to address this problem by modeling relationships between pixels, however, this paradigm defies the spatially non-uniformity fact of degradations and learns non-discriminative features from semantic-conflict regions.
  In this paper, we propose SSR, a \textbf{S}emantic-center guilded \textbf{S}tate space model for image \textbf{R}estoration.
  The key idea of SSR is to shift the conventional scanning strategy of pixel-serial to semantic-guilded one.
  Specifically, we introduce a Superpixel-guided Selective Scan Mechanism ($\text{S}^3$M), which first partitions the image into perceptually coherent regions via superpixel clustering and then performs relations modeling within the semantic-related regions.
  Moreover, a Region-level Gating Mechanism (RGM) is developed to perform intra-region calibration by modulating degradation outliers within each semantic superpixel unit along the channel dimension.
  Extensive experiments on \textbf{6} well-established benchmarks demonstrate that SSR performs favorably against state-of-the-art models with competitive computational cost.

AI.tldr: SSR is a semantic-center guided state space model for adverse weather image restoration that uses superpixel clustering to group semantically coherent regions and performs relation modeling within those regions, achieving state-of-the-art results on 6 benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing adverse weather image restoration methods model relationships between pixels, which fails to account for the spatially non-uniform nature of degradations and learns non-discriminative features from semantic-conflict regions.
AI.method: SSR introduces a Superpixel-guided Selective Scan Mechanism (S3M) that partitions the image into perceptually coherent regions via superpixel clustering and models relationships within semantic-related regions, along with a Region-level Gating Mechanism (RGM) for intra-region calibration by modulating degradation outliers within each semantic superpixel unit along the channel dimension.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on 6 well-established benchmarks demonstrate that SSR performs favorably against state-of-the-art models with competitive computational cost.
AI.conclusion: Shifting from pixel-serial scanning to semantic-guided scanning in state space models improves adverse weather image restoration by respecting the spatially non-uniform nature of degradations and learning more discriminative features.

title: DecoupleGS: Interactive 3D Gaussian Splatting for End-to-End Autonomous Driving Testing
summary: End-to-end (E2E) autonomous driving algorithms require rigorous closed-loop validation in simulation environments offering high visual fidelity, strong interactivity, and real-time performance. Existing approaches, from game engines to static neural rendering, inherently trade off these requirements and struggle with the dynamic scene composition essential for E2E testing. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel decoupled 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) framework tailored for large-scale E2E evaluation. We fundamentally decompose scenes into a high-fidelity static background and manipulable dynamic agents using an object-centric canonical representation. To resolve resulting representational conflicts, we introduce three targeted modules: (1) asset compression via perceptual pruning and vector quantization for real-time traffic rendering; (2) map-guided geometric registration leveraging semantic topology to strictly align trajectories; and (3) proxy-based relighting transferring ambient illumination for seamless photometric integration. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DecoupleGS achieves a balanced fidelity-efficiency trade-off, improves metric and photometric consistency, and provides a practical closed-loop sensor simulation platform for E2E autonomous driving evaluation.

AI.tldr: DecoupleGS is a decoupled 3D Gaussian Splatting framework for end-to-end autonomous driving simulation that separates scenes into a static background and manipulable dynamic agents, introducing modules for asset compression, map-guided geometric registration, and proxy-based relighting to achieve balanced fidelity, efficiency, and realism in closed-loop evaluation.
AI.motivation: End-to-end autonomous driving algorithms need rigorous closed-loop validation in simulation environments that simultaneously offer high visual fidelity, strong interactivity, and real-time performance. Existing approaches (game engines to static neural rendering) trade off these requirements and cannot handle dynamic scene composition needed for E2E testing.
AI.method: The framework decouples scenes into a high-fidelity static background and manipulable dynamic agents using object-centric canonical representation. Three modules resolve representational conflicts: (1) asset compression via perceptual pruning and vector quantization for real-time traffic rendering; (2) map-guided geometric registration using semantic topology for trajectory alignment; (3) proxy-based relighting for seamless photometric integration via ambient illumination transfer.
AI.result: Experiments show DecoupleGS achieves a balanced fidelity-efficiency trade-off, improves metric and photometric consistency, and provides a practical closed-loop sensor simulation platform for E2E autonomous driving evaluation.
AI.conclusion: DecoupleGS bridges the gap between high-fidelity rendering and real-time interactive simulation, offering a practical solution for large-scale E2E autonomous driving evaluation in closed-loop environments.

title: LiveLight: Real-time Streaming Video Relighting with Interactive Control
comment: Accepted by TOG 2026. Project page: https://living-lighting.github.io
summary: We present LiveLight, the first diffusion-based framework for real-time streaming video relighting with interactive 3D lighting control. Achieving this is non-trivial, as it requires overcoming three critical challenges: effectively injecting dynamic 3D lighting into a diffusion model, maintaining high-fidelity generation under an extremely low NFE (Number of Function Evaluations) budget for real-time speed, and facilitating continuous streaming for interactive control. To address these pain points, we propose three key designs. First, for accurate lighting injection, we propose a lightweight adapter that feeds Multi-Plane Light Irradiance (MPLI) conditions-depth-aware irradiance maps encoding 3D lighting geometry-directly into the diffusion backbone. Second, to prevent rendering quality degradation at low NFEs towards real-time distillation, we introduce a geometry-guided feedback branch. This training-time constraint leverages a frozen geometry estimator to enforce depth- and normal-consistent relighting, ensuring geometrically plausible shading without adding inference overhead. Finally, to enable streaming interaction, we develop a progressive rolling-window strategy that maintains a denoising ladder of latent chunks at varying noise levels. By propagating intermediate states, this strategy guarantees temporal coherence and supports arbitrarily long video relighting with per-frame reference refresh. Extensive experiments on real-world and synthetic benchmarks demonstrate that LiveLight achieves state-of-the-art relighting quality while running at real-time speed, significantly outperforming offline baselines in temporal stability, lighting controllability, and user preference. To foster real-time interactive relighting research, we will publicly release our models, training data, and synthetic data generator.

AI.tldr: LiveLight is the first diffusion-based framework for real-time streaming video relighting with interactive 3D lighting control, using MPLI conditions, a geometry-guided feedback branch, and a progressive rolling-window strategy.
AI.motivation: Real-time video relighting with interactive 3D lighting control is challenging because it requires injecting dynamic 3D lighting into diffusion models, maintaining high-fidelity generation under an extremely low NFE budget, and enabling continuous streaming for interactive control—none of which existing methods fully address.
AI.method: Three key designs: (1) a lightweight adapter feeding Multi-Plane Light Irradiance (MPLI) conditions into the diffusion backbone; (2) a geometry-guided feedback branch using a frozen geometry estimator to enforce depth- and normal-consistent relighting during training; (3) a progressive rolling-window strategy maintaining a denoising ladder of latent chunks for streaming temporal coherence.
AI.result: LiveLight achieves state-of-the-art relighting quality at real-time speed, significantly outperforming offline baselines in temporal stability, lighting controllability, and user preference on real-world and synthetic benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: LiveLight demonstrates that diffusion-based real-time interactive video relighting is feasible, and the authors will release models, training data, and a synthetic data generator to foster further research.

title: Investigating Social Bias in Narrative Image Generation
comment: Accepted to GenAI4World Workshop at COLM 2026
summary: Text-to-image (T2I) generation models are increasingly embedded in applications such as media content creation and education, raising concerns about how their outputs may reproduce social biases. Prior work has shown that T2I models exhibit social biases, yet existing evaluations largely focus on a photo generation task. As a result, it remains unclear whether and how such biases manifest in more narrative visual formats, such as storyboards and comics, where characters and events are presented across multiple panels. In this work, we compare bias expression across photo, storyboard, and comic generation in six T2I models by adapting BBG, a text-based bias evaluation framework, to image generation. Our results show that proprietary models generate 25.9% biased outputs in photo generation on average, with biased outputs increasing by 9.6pp in storyboard generation and 18.2pp in comic generation. We also find that photos mainly encode biases through subtle visual cues, while storyboards and comics reveal them more explicitly through event sequencing, character positioning, narrative resolution, and textual elements. These findings show that biases that remain less visible in photo generation may surface in narrative visual formats, highlighting the importance of evaluating T2I systems with diverse visual formats beyond photo generation.

AI.tldr: This paper compares social bias expression across photo, storyboard, and comic generation in six T2I models by adapting the BBG bias evaluation framework. Results show biased outputs increase from 25.9% in photos to +9.6pp in storyboards and +18.2pp in comics, with narrative formats exposing biases through event sequencing, character positioning, and textual elements that remain less visible in photos.
AI.motivation: Prior bias evaluations of T2I models focus almost exclusively on photo generation, leaving it unclear whether and how social biases manifest in narrative visual formats like storyboards and comics where characters and events unfold across multiple panels.
AI.method: The authors adapted BBG (a text-based bias evaluation framework) to image generation and compared bias expression across photo, storyboard, and comic generation using six T2I models.
AI.result: Proprietary models produce 25.9% biased photo outputs on average, increasing by 9.6pp in storyboards and 18.2pp in comics. Photos encode biases through subtle visual cues, while narrative formats expose them explicitly via event sequencing, character positioning, narrative resolution, and textual elements.
AI.conclusion: Biases that are less visible in photo generation can surface more prominently in narrative visual formats, highlighting the need to evaluate T2I systems across diverse visual formats beyond photo generation.

title: Illuminating Visual Identity in Universal Multimodal Embeddings
summary: Universal Multimodal Embeddings (UMEs) aim to unify various modalities and tasks into a shared representation space. In recent years, this field has witnessed substantial progress driven by the development of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). However, a crucial capability, visual identity discrimination, remains underexplored in existing UME methods, despite its critical role in a wide range of tasks, including instance retrieval, re-identification, and identity preservation in AI-generated content. To bridge this gap, we propose a unified formulation for visual identity discrimination~(VisID) and introduce $\textbf{MVEB}$ ($\textbf{M}$ultimodal $\textbf{V}$isual Identity $\textbf{E}$mbedding $\textbf{B}$enchmark), a large-scale benchmark curated from both real-world and synthetic datasets to support evaluation and training. Furthermore, we present a simple yet effective learning framework that jointly optimizes general multimodal and visual identity representations through a carefully designed identity-aware sampling mechanism. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach successfully endows UMEs with strong identity discrimination capability and maintains competitive general multimodal performance. We believe this work not only illuminates a critical yet neglected capability, but also takes a step toward more holistic universal multimodal embeddings. Code and data are available at \href{https://chrisclear3.github.io/MVEB}{MVEB}.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes MVEB, a large-scale benchmark for visual identity discrimination in Universal Multimodal Embeddings (UMEs), along with a learning framework that jointly optimizes general multimodal and identity-aware representations through an identity-aware sampling mechanism, enabling UMEs to gain strong identity discrimination while maintaining general performance.
AI.motivation: Visual identity discrimination—the ability to recognize whether different modalities or instances refer to the same entity—is critical for tasks like instance retrieval, re-identification, and identity preservation in AI-generated content, yet existing UME methods largely overlook this capability.
AI.method: The authors introduce a unified formulation called VisID, construct a large-scale benchmark (MVEB) from both real-world and synthetic datasets, and propose a simple learning framework that jointly optimizes general multimodal and visual identity representations via an identity-aware sampling mechanism.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show the approach endows UMEs with strong identity discrimination capability while maintaining competitive general multimodal performance.
AI.conclusion: This work highlights a critical yet neglected capability in UMEs and takes a step toward more holistic universal multimodal embeddings, with code and data publicly available.

title: Parameter-Dynamic Adaptive Fusion and Calibration Network for RGBT Tracking
summary: Existing RGBT trackers typically employ fusion functions with fixed parameters across different targets and scenarios. Although dynamic-architecture methods improve fusion flexibility by selecting among predefined operations, they still cannot adapt the fusion parameters to the evolving target state. To address these issues, we propose a Parameter-Dynamic Adaptive Fusion and Calibration Network (PAFCNet) for RGBT tracking. PAFCNet dynamically generates target-conditioned parameters for multimodal fusion and temporal calibration, enabling the tracking process to adapt to target appearance variations and modality quality fluctuations. Specifically, we introduce a Target-Adaptive Hypernetwork (TA-HyperNet) that leverages template representations, which preserve stable target identity and recent appearance changes with less background interference, to generate target-conditioned parameters for subsequent fusion and calibration. Based on TA-HyperNet, we design a target-aware parameter-dynamic fusion module that uses the generated parameters to modulate the fusion process. This enables the fusion module to adapt to changes in target appearance and complex scene conditions. Furthermore, since spatio-temporal information propagation may accumulate tracking noise, we propose a dynamic spatio-temporal calibration module that employs TA-HyperNet to generate calibration parameters for spatio-temporal tokens. By dynamically calibrating historical information before propagation, the module improves the reliability of temporal representations. Experimental results demonstrate that PAFCNet achieves competitive performance on multiple RGBT tracking benchmarks.

AI.tldr: PAFCNet introduces a Parameter-Dynamic Adaptive Fusion and Calibration Network for RGBT tracking that dynamically generates target-conditioned parameters via a Target-Adaptive Hypernetwork (TA-HyperNet), enabling adaptive multimodal fusion and temporal calibration that respond to target appearance changes and modality quality fluctuations.
AI.motivation: Existing RGBT trackers use fusion functions with fixed parameters across different targets and scenarios. Although dynamic-architecture methods improve flexibility by selecting among predefined operations, they still cannot adapt fusion parameters to the evolving target state during tracking.
AI.method: PAFCNet consists of: (1) a Target-Adaptive Hypernetwork (TA-HyperNet) that generates target-conditioned parameters from template representations preserving stable identity and recent appearance changes; (2) a target-aware parameter-dynamic fusion module that uses generated parameters to modulate fusion adaptively; and (3) a dynamic spatio-temporal calibration module that generates calibration parameters for spatio-temporal tokens to recalibrate historical information before propagation, reducing accumulated tracking noise.
AI.result: PAFCNet achieves competitive performance on multiple RGBT tracking benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: By dynamically generating and applying target-conditioned parameters for both fusion and temporal calibration, PAFCNet effectively adapts RGBT tracking to target appearance variations and modality quality fluctuations, improving temporal representation reliability.

title: SecondOpinion: Anatomy-Aware Gated Reasoning for Efficient Medical Image Analysis
summary: Deep learning models for medical image analysis typically apply a fixed amount of computation to every input, regardless of case difficulty. Anatomy-guided dual-stream architectures have been shown to improve diagnostic performance, but they evaluate both streams unconditionally, even on cases a single stream could already resolve confidently. We propose SecondOpinion, a framework in which a fast primary stream processes every case, while a second, anatomy-guided stream is invoked only when GateKeeper, a gating mechanism trained explicitly as a binary correctness classifier, judges that the primary stream's prediction needs additional scrutiny, much as a clinician might seek a second opinion on a difficult case. When activated, the two streams are combined through a lightweight cross-attention fusion module. We evaluate SecondOpinion on a unified five-class chest X-ray dataset and a pelvic fracture dataset, the latter including a held-out, harder subset of fractures that are invisible on X-ray but confirmed via CT. SecondOpinion matches or exceeds prior state-of-the-art performance on both tasks, while activating its anatomy-guided stream on only 9.23% of chest X-ray cases, rising to 24.12% on visible fractures and 45.71% on invisible fractures, an activation rate that tracks task difficulty directly. These results suggest that supervising a gating signal toward correctness, rather than relying on unsupervised confidence, allows a model to allocate anatomical reasoning where it is actually needed.

AI.tldr: SecondOpinion is a framework where a fast primary stream processes every medical image, while a second anatomy-guided stream is selectively invoked only when a trained GateKeeper binary correctness classifier determines it is needed, matching or exceeding state-of-the-art performance while using the second stream on only a small fraction of cases (9.23% for chest X-rays, with higher rates for harder fracture cases).
AI.motivation: Deep learning models for medical image analysis apply fixed computation regardless of case difficulty. Anatomy-guided dual-stream architectures improve diagnostic performance but wastefully evaluate both streams unconditionally, even on easy cases a single stream could confidently resolve.
AI.method: SecondOpinion uses a fast primary stream on every case, with a GateKeeper gating mechanism trained explicitly as a binary correctness classifier to decide whether the primary stream's prediction needs further scrutiny. When activated, the second anatomy-guided stream is combined with the primary stream via a lightweight cross-attention fusion module.
AI.result: Evaluated on a unified five-class chest X-ray dataset and a pelvic fracture dataset (including a held-out harder subset of CT-confirmed fractures invisible on X-ray), SecondOpinion matches or exceeds prior state-of-the-art performance. It activates the anatomy-guided stream on only 9.23% of chest X-ray cases, 24.12% on visible fractures, and 45.71% on invisible fractures, with activation rates tracking task difficulty.
AI.conclusion: Supervising a gating signal toward correctness, rather than relying on unsupervised confidence, enables a model to allocate anatomical reasoning where it is actually needed, achieving state-of-the-art performance with significantly reduced computational cost from conditional stream activation.

title: DAVET: Denoising-Aware Visual Evidence Trajectory Allocation for Diffusion Vision-Language Models
summary: Diffusion vision-language models (dVLMs) iteratively denoise masked responses while conditioning each denoising step on visual evidence, making visual conditioning a substantial recurring inference cost. Unlike autoregressive decoding, diffusion generation repeatedly revisits the entire response as uncertainty evolves. Our analysis reveals that visual evidence demand is strongly step-dependent, motivating adaptive allocation across denoising steps. Existing inference acceleration methods operate through decoding-side strategies or visual token compression via pruning and merging, but do not explicitly treat visual evidence as a resource whose demand evolves across the diffusion process. Therefore, we present Denoising-Aware Visual Evidence Trajectory Allocation (DAVET), a training-free framework that allocates visual evidence according to the evolving generation state. Starting from a phase-conditioned evidence trajectory, the proposed allocation policy uses operation demand to set an evidence reserve whose allocation at each denoising step is modulated by trajectory risk. DAVET realizes the resulting budgets through a hierarchy of evidence views constructed from a single visual encoding, separating when and how much evidence is needed from how the evidence views are constructed. Evaluated on two representative dVLMs, LLaDA-V and LaViDa, across multiple visual-understanding benchmarks, DAVET achieves an average speedup of 1.55$\times$ with an average relative performance drop of 1.86\%, showing that denoising-aware visual evidence allocation can reduce visual conditioning cost while largely preserving generation quality.

AI.tldr: DAVET is a training-free framework that adaptively allocates visual evidence across denoising steps in diffusion vision-language models (dVLMs), achieving 1.55× average speedup with only 1.86% relative performance drop by treating visual evidence as a step-dependent resource.
AI.motivation: Diffusion VLMs repeatedly condition on visual evidence at every denoising step, making visual conditioning a major recurring inference cost. Unlike autoregressive models, diffusion revisits the entire response as uncertainty evolves, yet existing acceleration methods (decoding-side strategies or token compression) do not treat visual evidence as a resource whose demand evolves across the diffusion process. The paper identifies that visual evidence demand is strongly step-dependent, motivating adaptive allocation.
AI.method: DAVET is a training-free framework built on three components: (1) a phase-conditioned evidence trajectory as the starting allocation policy, (2) an evidence reserve set by operation demand, whose per-step allocation is modulated by trajectory risk, and (3) a hierarchy of evidence views constructed from a single visual encoding to decouple when/how much evidence is needed from how evidence views are built.
AI.result: Evaluated on LLaDA-V and LaViDa across multiple visual understanding benchmarks, DAVET achieves an average speedup of 1.55× with an average relative performance drop of only 1.86%.
AI.conclusion: Denoising-aware visual evidence allocation can substantially reduce visual conditioning cost in dVLMs while largely preserving generation quality, demonstrating that adaptive evidence allocation across diffusion steps is an effective and practical acceleration strategy.

title: Detail Continuation over a Trustworthy Coarse Scale for Autoregressive Super-Resolution
comment: Accepted by ACM Multimedia 2026. 10 pages, 8 figures. Code: https://github.com/BRL-SYSU/K2NSR
summary: Hallucination remains a persistent challenge in generative super-resolution (GSR), where reconstructed results may contain visually plausible yet weakly supported content, structural deviations, or unnatural textures with respect to the low-resolution (LR) input. Existing GSR methods have extensively explored the trade-off between perceptual realism and reconstruction fidelity, but the division between preserving reliable coarse-scale information and restoring more uncertain fine details is often handled implicitly within the overall restoration process. Visual autoregressive (VAR) modeling provides a natural opportunity to revisit this issue, as its coarse-to-fine next-scale prediction offers an explicit scale-wise generation interface. However, existing VAR-based SR methods still inherit the original full 1-to-$N$ autoregressive generation path, even though, for super-resolution, coarse-scale information in LR is often relatively more reliable, while long autoregressive chains may accumulate prediction errors. Motivated by these observations, we propose \textbf{K2N}, which reformulates VAR-based SR from full-path generation into a $k$-to-$N$ detail continuation process. Specifically, early coarse-scale states are established directly from LR, while only the remaining finer scales are restored autoregressively. Experimental results show that K2N remains competitive with the VARSR baseline on standard SR metrics, while exhibiting clearer advantages on hallucination-focused evaluation. These findings suggest that explicitly rethinking the generation path in a scale-wise manner can be a promising direction for improving the reliability of generative super-resolution. Our code will be released soon at https://github.com/BRL-SYSU/K2NSR.

AI.tldr: K2N reformulates VAR-based super-resolution from full 1-to-N autoregressive generation into a k-to-N detail continuation process, where coarse-scale states are established directly from LR input and only finer scales are restored autoregressively, reducing hallucination while maintaining competitive performance.
AI.motivation: Hallucination in generative super-resolution (GSR) produces visually plausible but weakly supported content. Existing methods implicitly handle the division between reliable coarse-scale information and uncertain fine details. VAR modeling offers an explicit scale-wise interface, but existing VAR-based SR methods still inherit the full 1-to-N autoregressive path despite coarse-scale LR information being more reliable and long autoregressive chains accumulating errors.
AI.method: K2N reformulates VAR-based SR into a k-to-N detail continuation process: early coarse-scale states are established directly from the LR input, bypassing autoregressive prediction for reliable scales, while only the remaining finer scales are generated autoregressively.
AI.result: K2N remains competitive with the VARSR baseline on standard SR metrics while showing clearer advantages on hallucination-focused evaluation.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly rethinking the generation path in a scale-wise manner is a promising direction for improving the reliability of generative super-resolution, and the findings suggest that separating reliable coarse-scale reconstruction from uncertain fine-scale restoration reduces hallucination.

title: PartMat: Material-Aware 3D Part Decomposition with a Single Global Latent
summary: Part-level 3D generation has recently attracted increasing attention for producing structured and editable 3D assets. However, existing methods typically decompose objects according to functional semantics rather than the editable material boundaries (e.g., fabric, wood, metal) required in practical 3D applications such as interior design. Additionally, current methods often generate parts independently, causing computational costs to scale linearly with the part count. To address these limitations, we present PartMat, an efficient material-aware 3D part decomposition pipeline that represents multi-part geometry with a single global latent. Given a reference image and a single whole-object geometry, PartMat decomposes the object into parts that follow material boundaries. First, we propose PartVAE to learn such a unified representation and decode all material parts in a single forward pass, thereby decoupling inference cost from the number of parts. Second, with this representation, a diffusion model is trained for part generation and refined via reinforcement learning for accurate material assignment and overlap suppression. Finally, to recover fine-grained geometric details, we introduce a sparse-voxel flow-matching model with part attention for geometry post-processing. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PartMat significantly outperforms existing baselines in material-aware decomposition accuracy and achieves comparable geometric quality, while maintaining efficient inference.

AI.tldr: PartMat is an efficient material-aware 3D part decomposition pipeline that uses a single global latent to represent multi-part geometry, enabling decomposition along material boundaries (fabric, wood, metal) rather than functional semantics, with inference cost decoupled from part count.
AI.motivation: Existing 3D part generation methods decompose objects by functional semantics rather than editable material boundaries needed for practical applications like interior design. Additionally, current methods generate parts independently, causing computational cost to scale linearly with part count.
AI.method: PartMat introduces: (1) PartVAE, a unified representation that decodes all material parts in a single forward pass; (2) a diffusion model for part generation refined via reinforcement learning for accurate material assignment and overlap suppression; (3) a sparse-voxel flow-matching model with part attention for geometry post-processing to recover fine-grained details.
AI.result: PartMat significantly outperforms existing baselines in material-aware decomposition accuracy, achieves comparable geometric quality, and maintains efficient inference.
AI.conclusion: PartMat addresses the gap in material-aware 3D part decomposition by providing an efficient pipeline that decouples inference cost from part count while achieving superior material-boundary accuracy and comparable geometric quality.

title: DeepVoyager-VL: Incentivizing Vision-in-the-Loop Search for Long-Horizon Multimodal Agents
summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have advanced visual understanding and reasoning, yet their static parametric knowledge limits their ability to address knowledge-intensive and dynamically evolving open-world problems. To move beyond this limitation, multimodal deep search has emerged as a key direction for open-world information access, evolving from single-turn factual retrieval toward long-horizon, multi-turn search guided by visual evidence. However, existing methods typically confine vision to the input or answer stage, overlooking its role in intermediate reasoning, and lack designs tailored to long-horizon interaction. Consequently, visual evidence rarely drives continued retrieval, constraining both interaction depth and reasoning span. To address these limitations, we propose DeepVoyager-VL, a long-horizon multimodal deep-search framework for vision-in-the-loop search. Specifically, we construct a multimodal event graph to drive data synthesis, yielding problems with intermediate visual dependencies and long reasoning chains. We then design an agent framework for active visual acquisition and on-demand image loading. Finally, we fine-tune models on the synthesized data without reinforcement learning. Extensive experiments across ten multimodal search benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

AI.tldr: DeepVoyager-VL is a long-horizon multimodal deep-search framework that keeps visual evidence active throughout the entire reasoning process (not just at input or answer stages), using a multimodal event graph for data synthesis, an agent framework for active visual acquisition and on-demand image loading, and fine-tuning on synthesized data—demonstrating effectiveness across ten benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing multimodal deep search methods confine vision to the input or answer stage, overlooking visual evidence's role in intermediate reasoning, and lack designs for long-horizon interaction—so visual evidence rarely drives continued retrieval, limiting interaction depth and reasoning span.
AI.method: (1) Construct a multimodal event graph to drive data synthesis, generating problems with intermediate visual dependencies and long reasoning chains. (2) Design an agent framework for active visual acquisition and on-demand image loading. (3) Fine-tune models on the synthesized data without reinforcement learning.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across ten multimodal search benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed DeepVoyager-VL framework.
AI.conclusion: DeepVoyager-VL successfully enables vision-in-the-loop long-horizon multimodal deep search, where visual evidence actively drives continued retrieval and reasoning throughout the entire search process.

title: MoCRA: Mixture of Compositional Rank-1 Atoms for 4K All-in-One Video Restoration
summary: Real-world video arrives hazy, rainy, dark, or noisy, and a deployable restorer faces three demands at once: no degradation label, native 4K output, and stability in playback. Existing methods answer them separately and break on the joint problem, because per-frame degradation readings flip between frames, downsampled proxies erase the rain and noise they are meant to remove, and dense temporal alignment does not fit 4K memory. No paired benchmark even poses that problem, so we build one. UHV-4K-AIO renders physically modeled haze, rain, sensor noise, and low light over the same 100 clean 4K clips with shared depth and motion, and its construction exposes the split MoCRA is built on: haze and low light survive aggressive downsampling, while rain and noise exist only at native scale. Band-matched compositional conditioning follows, spending conditioning capacity, computation, and supervision in the band where each degradation lives. One dictionary of rank-1 atoms, recomposed sparsely per frame, conditions both a once-per-clip coarse branch and a shallow native-resolution refiner, in 3.6M parameters and with no optical flow. Trained once for all four tasks, MoCRA takes the best task-mean PSNR of eleven retrained image and video baselines, holds warping error at the level of the flow-based video models while never estimating motion, and restores native 4K in under half a second, against 1.7 seconds for the fastest baseline.

AI.tldr: MoCRA is a single 3.6M-parameter model that jointly handles multi-degradation video restoration (haze, rain, noise, low light) at native 4K resolution without degradation labels or optical flow, trained once on a new UHV-4K-AIO benchmark.
AI.motivation: Real-world videos suffer from multiple degradations simultaneously, but existing methods address them separately and fail on the joint problem: per-frame degradation readings are unstable across frames, downsampled inputs erase fine-grained rain and noise, and dense temporal alignment is infeasible at 4K memory budgets. No paired benchmark exists for this joint problem, motivating both a new benchmark and a new architecture.
AI.method: The authors build UHV-4K-AIO, a benchmark with physically modeled haze, rain, sensor noise, and low light over 100 clean 4K clips sharing depth and motion. The benchmark construction reveals that haze and low light survive downsampling while rain and noise exist only at native scale, leading to band-matched compositional conditioning: a dictionary of rank-1 atoms sparsely recomposed per frame conditions both a once-per-clip coarse branch and a shallow native-resolution refiner. The model has 3.6M parameters and no optical flow estimation.
AI.result: Trained once for all four tasks, MoCRA achieves the best task-mean PSNR against eleven retrained image and video baselines, holds warping error at the level of flow-based video models without estimating motion, and restores native 4K in under half a second (versus 1.7 seconds for the fastest baseline).
AI.conclusion: MoCRA demonstrates that joint multi-degradation 4K video restoration is feasible with a compact model by exploiting the scale characteristics of different degradations and avoiding expensive temporal alignment, setting a new standard for deployable video restoration.

title: Decoupling semantics from vision: A framework for faithful visual-text compression evaluation
summary: Recent visual-text compression (VTC) methods, typified by DeepSeek-OCR, report impressive high token compression ratios for long-context modeling tasks by leveraging text-to-image rendering. However, existing evaluation protocols heavily rely on downstream task performance. Such evaluation metrics fail to accurately measure text preservation due to the strong inherent linguistic priors of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). In this work, we introduce a new evaluation framework that decouples MLLMs' capabilities to faithfully assess VTC quality. Within this framework, we further introduce the ZeroSense Benchmark to ensure low semantic correlation of testing samples. By eliminating textual dependencies, our benchmark guarantees that the evaluation results are purely reflective of VTC quality, unaffected by the semantic inference capabilities of downstream models. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets demonstrate that VTC quality and downstream task accuracy diverge significantly, highlighting the necessity of our decoupled evaluation framework.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a new evaluation framework that decouples MLLM capabilities from VTC quality assessment, along with the ZeroSense Benchmark that uses low semantic correlation samples to ensure evaluation results purely reflect VTC performance.
AI.motivation: Existing VTC evaluation protocols rely on downstream task performance, which fails to accurately measure text preservation because MLLMs have strong inherent linguistic priors that can compensate for poor VTC quality, masking the true compression quality.
AI.method: Introduces a decoupled evaluation framework that separates MLLM capabilities from VTC quality assessment, and the ZeroSense Benchmark with low semantic correlation testing samples to eliminate textual/linguistic dependencies so results purely reflect VTC quality.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across multiple datasets demonstrate that VTC quality and downstream task accuracy diverge significantly, validating that existing metrics are unreliable and the decoupled framework is necessary.
AI.conclusion: The paper highlights the necessity of a decoupled evaluation framework for VTC methods, arguing that current downstream-accuracy-based protocols are misleading and proposing ZeroSense as a more faithful benchmark for assessing visual-text compression quality.

title: Transformer Geometry Observatory TGO-III: Semantic Geometry Observatory
summary: With the widespread adoption of Vision Transformers in modern AI, the need to analyze their inherent representational behavior has become increasingly important. While most existing studies emphasize token geometries and training dynamics, the evolution of representational covariance structures and class-level geometric organization remains comparatively underexplored. In this work, we investigate semantic geometry and class separability as representations evolve across the layers of ViT-Small/16 through TGO-III: Semantic Geometry Observatory. It is a framework designed to analyze the emergence of semantic organization, feature evolution, and class-wise representation geometry throughout training. The framework employs multiple complementary observatories, including Linear Probe Accuracy, Fisher Ratio, Class Centroid Distances, Local Intrinsic Dimension, and Local PCA Rank, to quantify the progressive evolution of discriminative representations. Our analysis reveals that class representations become progressively more linearly separable, Fisher discriminability increases, class centroids move farther apart, and local representation manifolds exhibit structured class-dependent geometric complexity. These observations provide empirical evidence supporting the Semantic Expansion Hypothesis, suggesting that the manifold expansion observed in previous observatories is accompanied by the progressive organization of representations into increasingly discriminative semantic structures. Collectively, TGO-III extends the Transformer Geometry Observatory framework by establishing a direct connection between manifold geometry, covariance evolution, and semantic organization during Transformer training.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces TGO-III (Semantic Geometry Observatory), a framework for analyzing how semantic geometry and class separability evolve across layers of ViT-Small/16 during training. Using metrics like Linear Probe Accuracy, Fisher Ratio, Class Centroid Distances, Local Intrinsic Dimension, and Local PCA Rank, the authors show that class representations become progressively more linearly separable, discriminable, and geometrically structured, providing empirical support for the Semantic Expansion Hypothesis.
AI.motivation: While prior work on Vision Transformers has focused on token geometries and training dynamics, the evolution of representational covariance structures and class-level geometric organization remains underexplored. This paper addresses that gap by analyzing how semantic organization emerges as representations evolve through layers.
AI.method: The paper proposes TGO-III, a framework employing multiple complementary observatories (Linear Probe Accuracy, Fisher Ratio, Class Centroid Distances, Local Intrinsic Dimension, Local PCA Rank) to quantify progressive evolution of discriminative representations across layers of ViT-Small/16 during training.
AI.result: Class representations become progressively more linearly separable, Fisher discriminability increases, class centroids move farther apart, and local representation manifolds exhibit structured class-dependent geometric complexity. These findings empirically support the Semantic Expansion Hypothesis.
AI.conclusion: TGO-III extends the Transformer Geometry Observatory framework by establishing a direct connection between manifold geometry, covariance evolution, and semantic organization during Transformer training, showing that manifold expansion is accompanied by progressive organization into discriminative semantic structures.

title: Beyond Illumination: A Conditional Mutual Information-Guided Network for Low-Light Image Enhancement
summary: Low-light image enhancement (LLIE) seeks to restore structural fidelity, natural color rendition, and proper exposure from images captured under inadequate lighting conditions. Recent state-of-the-art approaches, such as CIDNet, adopt a dual-branch architecture comprising a chrominance (HV) branch and an intensity (I) branch to separately model decoupled chromatic and luminance information within the HVI color space. However, these methods overlook the mutual interaction between intensity and chrominance components, which inherently limits their representational capacity and leads to suboptimal enhancement performance. To address this limitation, we propose the Conditional Mutual Information-Guided Network (CMIG-Net), which leverages conditional mutual information as a principled metric to quantitatively assess the contribution of chrominance features conditioned on the available intensity information. In particular, we design a Conditional Mutual Information Calibration (CMIC) module that generates a conditional information map, enabling region-adaptive recalibration of chrominance representations according to local illumination statistics. Furthermore, we introduce a Dynamic Dual-branch Information Restoration (D2IR) module, which adaptively governs bidirectional information flow between the intensity and chrominance branches, guided by both the conditional prior and the instantaneous restoration state. Extensive experiments on paired LLIE benchmarks demonstrate that CMIG-Net consistently outperforms CIDNet, achieving up to a 0.619 dB gain in PSNR, with a 0.382 dB improvement specifically on the challenging Sony-Total-Dark dataset.

AI.tldr: CMIG-Net is a low-light image enhancement network that addresses the limitation of existing dual-branch approaches by using conditional mutual information to model the interaction between intensity and chrominance branches, achieving up to 0.619 dB PSNR improvement over CIDNet.
AI.motivation: Existing state-of-the-art LLIE methods like CIDNet use dual-branch architectures (chrominance and intensity) in HVI color space but overlook the mutual interaction between these components, which limits representational capacity and leads to suboptimal enhancement performance.
AI.method: CMIG-Net introduces two key modules: (1) a Conditional Mutual Information Calibration (CMIC) module that uses conditional mutual information to generate a conditional information map for region-adaptive recalibration of chrominance features based on local illumination; and (2) a Dynamic Dual-branch Information Restoration (D2IR) module that adaptively controls bidirectional information flow between intensity and chrominance branches using both conditional priors and instantaneous restoration state.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on paired LLIE benchmarks show CMIG-Net consistently outperforms CIDNet, achieving up to 0.619 dB gain in PSNR, with a 0.382 dB improvement on the challenging Sony-Total-Dark dataset.
AI.conclusion: Modeling the interaction between intensity and chrominance via conditional mutual information provides a principled and effective way to improve low-light image enhancement performance over existing decoupled dual-branch approaches.

title: GeoCore-9B: Towards Geo-Aware Generative Foundation Models in Earth Observation
comment: Please visit our project page at https://kaist-viclab.github.io/GeoCore-9B_site/
summary: Existing generative models for earth observation (EO) predominantly rely on fine-tuning natural image priors, which limits their scalability and introduces perspective biases that conflict with geospatial constraints. To address this, we introduce GeoCore-9B, a 9-billion-parameter generative foundation model, which is the first of its scale to be trained from scratch exclusively on EO data. Unlike previous EO foundation models, GeoCore-9B is built upon a Flow Matching-based Diffusion Transformer (DiT) and natively conditions generation on text descriptions and continuous geospatial metadata, including ground sample distances, latitudes, and longitudes. To overcome the convergence and spatial disorientation challenges of training at this scale, we propose a Geospatial Semantic Alignment loss. This objective distills structural Earth surface priors (e.g., terrain and urban areas) from a frozen specialist teacher network, constraining the diffusion latent trajectory during training without adding inference overhead. Pre-trained on the global-scale Git-10M dataset, GeoCore-9B demonstrates strong downstream versatility. Beyond standard proxy generative tasks, we show that GeoCore-9B can be effectively adapted for practical EO applications, including highly challenging tasks such as cloud removal and SAR-to-optical cross-modal translation. Extensive evaluations confirm that GeoCore-9B establishes new state-of-the-art performance in both visual fidelity and geographic structural accuracy.

AI.tldr: GeoCore-9B is a 9-billion-parameter generative foundation model trained from scratch exclusively on Earth observation data using a Flow Matching-based Diffusion Transformer. It natively conditions on text and continuous geospatial metadata, and uses a Geospatial Semantic Alignment loss to distill structural Earth surface priors from a frozen teacher network, achieving SOTA performance in visual fidelity and geographic structural accuracy, with successful adaptation to practical tasks like cloud removal and SAR-to-optical translation.
AI.motivation: Existing generative models for Earth observation rely on fine-tuning natural image priors, which limits scalability and introduces perspective biases that conflict with geospatial constraints. A dedicated EO-native generative foundation model is needed to overcome these limitations.
AI.method: GeoCore-9B is a 9B-parameter Flow Matching-based Diffusion Transformer (DiT) trained from scratch on the global-scale Git-10M EO dataset. It natively conditions on text descriptions and continuous geospatial metadata (ground sample distance, latitude, longitude). A proposed Geospatial Semantic Alignment loss distills structural Earth surface priors from a frozen specialist teacher network to constrain diffusion latent trajectories during training, without adding inference overhead.
AI.result: GeoCore-9B establishes new state-of-the-art performance in both visual fidelity and geographic structural accuracy across standard proxy generative tasks and practical EO applications, including highly challenging tasks such as cloud removal and SAR-to-optical cross-modal translation.
AI.conclusion: GeoCore-9B demonstrates that an EO-native generative foundation model trained from scratch at scale can outperform fine-tuned natural image priors, achieving strong downstream versatility and establishing a new paradigm for Earth observation generation.

title: SpatioLM: Towards General Physical Spatial Intelligence in Vision-Language Models
summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) perform well on commonsense reasoning tasks but struggle with visual spatial reasoning. Most existing solutions introduce extra 3D prior inputs or external spatial encoders, which increase complexity and degrade the underlying VLMs' general-purpose capabilities after spatial fine-tuning. To this end, we propose a parameter-efficient \textit{\textbf{Spatio}-vision \textbf{L}anguage \textbf{M}odels (SpatioLM)}, that enhances spatial intelligence without extra 3D prior inputs or third-party spatial encoders. Concretely, we design a plug-and-play and non-invasive spatio-vision module that elicits the spatial knowledge inherent in VLMs. Furthermore, we innovatively leverage pseudo depth and camera information as supervision to guide the model in learning physically coherent representations. Extensive experiments show that SpatioLM achieves significant improvements in diverse tasks, including spatial perception and understanding while effectively limiting the degradation of general capabilities. Notably, the model achieves an impressive score of 71.6 on the VSI-Bench (the first model to surpass 70). In addition, it attains competitive performance when transferred to embodied manipulation tasks. Code is available at \href{https://github.com/xiaomi-research/spatio-lm}{\faGithub~spatio-lm}.

AI.tldr: SpatioLM enhances VLM spatial reasoning through a parameter-efficient, plug-and-play spatio-vision module that elicits intrinsic spatial knowledge, using pseudo depth and camera information as supervision; it achieves 71.6 on VSI-Bench (first to surpass 70) with minimal degradation of general capabilities.
AI.motivation: VLMs excel at commonsense reasoning but struggle with visual spatial reasoning. Existing solutions rely on extra 3D priors or external spatial encoders, which increase system complexity and degrade general-purpose capabilities after spatial fine-tuning.
AI.method: SpatioLM proposes a parameter-efficient, plug-and-play, and non-invasive spatio-vision module that elicits the spatial knowledge already inherent in VLMs. It leverages pseudo depth and camera information as supervision to guide the model toward learning physically coherent representations, without requiring extra 3D priors or third-party spatial encoders.
AI.result: SpatioLM achieves significant improvements on diverse tasks including spatial perception and understanding while limiting degradation of general capabilities. It scores 71.6 on VSI-Bench (the first model to surpass 70) and attains competitive performance on embodied manipulation tasks.
AI.conclusion: SpatioLM demonstrates that VLM spatial intelligence can be effectively enhanced in a parameter-efficient manner by eliciting intrinsic spatial knowledge, offering a simpler alternative that preserves general-purpose capabilities and extends well to embodied manipulation scenarios.

title: PhotoHOI: Synthesizing 3D Hand-Object Interactions from a Single RGB Photograph
summary: Hand-object interaction (HOI) is a fundamental human behavior with broad applications in AR/VR, digital humans, and embodied interaction. Existing methods typically require predefined object geometry, object trajectories, or task-specific conditions, limiting their use with natural real-world inputs. To address this, we study a more practical problem of synthesizing 3D hand-object interaction sequences from a single RGB photograph and an open-vocabulary language instruction, and introduce PhotoHOI. PhotoHOI first uses a vision-language model to parse the input image and instruction into a structured task specification, including the interaction object, target region, and spatial relation. It then recovers a compact task-relevant 3D scene and plans a smooth collision-aware object trajectory based on the recovered object states, support relations, and surrounding scene geometry. To synthesize hand motion that generalizes to real-world photographs and unseen objects, it learns transferable task-conditioned contact and contact-conditioned grasp priors from large-scale affordance and HOI data. The grasp is further refined in a learned latent space, constraining the optimization to a plausible hand-pose manifold. Experiments on GRAB and H2O demonstrate improved contact quality and reduced penetration over representative baselines. Results on real-world photographs further demonstrate higher task success and scene consistency, together with generalization to unseen objects and open-vocabulary instructions.

AI.tldr: PhotoHOI synthesizes 3D hand-object interaction sequences from a single RGB photo and an open-vocabulary language instruction using a vision-language model, task-relevant 3D scene recovery, and learned contact/grasp priors.
AI.motivation: Existing HOI methods require predefined object geometry, trajectories, or task-specific conditions, limiting their applicability to natural real-world inputs. This paper addresses the more practical problem of generating HOI from a single photograph and a natural language instruction.
AI.method: PhotoHOI parses the image and instruction into a structured task specification via a vision-language model, recovers a task-relevant 3D scene, plans a collision-aware object trajectory, synthesizes hand motion using transferable task-conditioned contact and contact-conditioned grasp priors learned from large-scale data, and refines the grasp in a learned latent space.
AI.result: Experiments on GRAB and H2O show improved contact quality and reduced penetration over baselines. On real-world photos, it achieves higher task success, better scene consistency, and generalization to unseen objects and open-vocabulary instructions.
AI.conclusion: PhotoHOI demonstrates that practical HOI synthesis from a single photograph and language instruction is feasible, enabling natural input-driven interaction generation without predefined object or task conditions.

title: Assessing the Benefits of Combining Advanced Deep Learning Techniques for Post-Disaster Building Damage Assessment from UAV Imagery
comment: Accepted at ECMLPKDD 2026, 31 pages (including appendix), 18 figures
summary: Rapid and accurate post-disaster building damage assessment is essential, yet remains a challenging task. Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) imagery offers a timely and high-resolution view of affected areas, but existing Computer Vision (CV) models often demand large annotated datasets, generalize poorly across geographic regions and their assessment policies, and are confined to the specific tasks they were trained for. Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) offer a promising alternative through their strong reasoning and generalization capabilities, but fall short on precise, low-level perception tasks such as object detection and accurate bounding box generation. Furthermore, they often require a substantial amount of data for effective fine-tuning on domain-specific tasks. In this paper, we propose a hybrid framework that decouples detection from damage assessment, combining the precision of CV models with the reasoning power of LVLMs. A CV model first detects buildings and generates bounding boxes on the image that are then passed to an LVLM for damage classification and contextual interpretation. We evaluated our framework on two real-world benchmarks: RescueNet and FloodNet. In particular, the best combination under this framework accurately counts intact, partially damaged and completely destroyed buildings, surpassing isolated baselines by up to 2.1 R^2 points, while requiring only limited annotated data for the detection stage. Beyond reporting aggregate gains, we provide a detailed analysis of failure scenarios and edge cases, offering practical insights for practitioners and concrete directions for future work. Our source code and data are publicly available to the research community via the following repository: https://github.com/ungquanghuy-kddi/VLM_GDINO.git

AI.tldr: A hybrid framework combining CV-based building detection (with bounding boxes) and LVLM-based damage classification, evaluated on RescueNet and FloodNet benchmarks, outperforming isolated baselines by up to 2.1 R² points with limited annotation requirements.
AI.motivation: Rapid and accurate post-disaster building damage assessment is essential but challenging. Existing CV models need large annotated datasets, generalize poorly, and are task-specific, while LVLMs struggle with precise low-level perception like object detection and bounding box generation. LVLMs also require substantial fine-tuning data.
AI.method: The framework decouples detection from damage assessment: a CV model first detects buildings and generates bounding boxes, which are then passed to an LVLM for damage classification and contextual interpretation.
AI.result: Evaluated on RescueNet and FloodNet benchmarks; the best combination accurately counts intact, partially damaged, and completely destroyed buildings, surpassing isolated baselines by up to 2.1 R² points while requiring only limited annotated data for the detection stage. Includes detailed failure scenario and edge case analysis.
AI.conclusion: The hybrid approach effectively combines the strengths of CV models and LVLMs for post-disaster damage assessment, offering practical insights and concrete directions for future work. Code and data are publicly available.

title: PNEC-Mamba: Prototype-Guided Positive-Negative Evidence Calibration for Hyperspectral Image Classification
summary: In real-world hyperspectral scenes, pixel representations are often ambiguous due to factors such as spectral similarity, mixed pixels, and local context interference, which may simultaneously encode discriminative evidence and interfering information. Existing methods mainly focus on learning more powerful representations or modeling broader contexts, but rarely investigate whether the learned representations provide reliable evidence or introduce interference into classification decisions. To address this issue, we view hyperspectral image classification from the perspective of pixel-level evidence reliability modeling and propose PNEC-Mamba, a prototype-guided positive-negative evidence calibration framework. The framework progressively establishes semantic references, separates class-related evidence from interference, estimates pixel-level reliability, and performs selective calibration. First, a full-image state-space encoder extracts pixel representations, while dynamic class prototypes provide semantic references that evolve jointly with the feature space. Subsequently, positive and negative evidence is derived from pixel-prototype competition, explicitly separating discriminative cues that support classification from confusing signals associated with competing classes. Based on these evidence relationships, a multi-source uncertainty estimation strategy is introduced to assess pixel-level reliability, enabling stronger evidence calibration for uncertain regions. Finally, a full-resolution consistency refinement step is applied to recover local spatial details and improve boundary coherence in the final predictions. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that PNEC-Mamba achieves superior classification performance compared with state-of-the-art methods.

AI.tldr: PNEC-Mamba is a prototype-guided positive-negative evidence calibration framework for hyperspectral image classification that models pixel-level evidence reliability by separating class-related evidence from interference, estimating reliability via multi-source uncertainty, and performing selective calibration, achieving state-of-the-art performance on three benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Real-world hyperspectral pixels are often ambiguous due to spectral similarity, mixed pixels, and local context interference. Existing methods focus on learning stronger representations or wider contexts but fail to investigate whether learned representations provide reliable evidence or introduce interference into classification decisions.
AI.method: PNEC-Mamba progressively: (1) uses a full-image state-space encoder to extract pixel representations while dynamic class prototypes evolve jointly as semantic references; (2) derives positive and negative evidence via pixel-prototype competition to separate discriminative cues from confusing signals; (3) applies a multi-source uncertainty estimation strategy to assess pixel-level reliability, enabling stronger evidence calibration in uncertain regions; (4) applies a full-resolution consistency refinement step to recover spatial details and improve boundary coherence.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that PNEC-Mamba achieves superior classification performance compared with state-of-the-art methods.
AI.conclusion: Modeling pixel-level evidence reliability through positive-negative evidence separation and selective calibration is an effective new perspective for hyperspectral image classification, outperforming existing representation- and context-focused approaches.

title: CHOW-SLAM: Compact Hybrid Representation with Complementary Overlap Window Optimization for RGB-D SLAM
summary: Simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) based on Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) enables dense, continuous scene reconstruction. However, existing systems operating with limited online resources struggle to simultaneously construct two types of constraints, namely, compact yet discriminative spatial constraints derived from scene representations and persistent temporal constraints derived from historical observations. To address this challenge, we propose CHOW-SLAM, a dense RGB-D SLAM framework that explicitly constructs these complementary spatial and temporal constraints. Spatially, we propose a compact parametric-hash (P-H) hybrid representation that organizes components based on planes and grids across scales in P and H branches. A unified multi-output decoder further aligns the ray termination distributions induced by TSDF and density, preserving geometry and appearance under a compact parameter budget. Temporally, we propose a complementary overlap-window strategy to prevent optimization from being dominated by short-term overlap or weakly related historical observations. Within a fixed budget, the strategy retains recent frames, selects high-overlap local frames, and introduces temporally distributed historical keyframes. Loss-aware keyframe insertion and bundle adjustment scheduling further adapt optimization to tracking quality. In addition, ORB-based tracking and geometric pose estimation are used for pose initialization, followed by neural rendering optimization to improve tracking stability. Extensive evaluations on multiple datasets demonstrate that CHOW-SLAM outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both scene reconstruction quality and camera tracking accuracy. The source code is available at https://github.com/jinjidexiaohuoban/CHOW-SLAM.

AI.tldr: CHOW-SLAM is a dense RGB-D SLAM framework built on NeRF that explicitly constructs complementary spatial and temporal constraints. It uses a compact parametric-hash (P-H) hybrid representation with plane/grid components across scales, a unified multi-output decoder aligning TSDF and density ray termination, and a complementary overlap-window temporal strategy with loss-aware keyframe insertion and bundle adjustment scheduling. It achieves state-of-the-art scene reconstruction and camera tracking accuracy.
AI.motivation: Existing NeRF-based SLAM systems with limited online resources struggle to simultaneously construct compact yet discriminative spatial constraints from scene representations and persistent temporal constraints from historical observations, limiting their performance.
AI.method: Proposes a compact parametric-hash (P-H) hybrid representation organizing components by planes and grids across scales, a unified multi-output decoder aligning TSDF and density distributions, and a complementary overlap-window strategy retaining recent frames while selecting high-overlap local frames and temporally distributed historical keyframes. Uses loss-aware keyframe insertion, bundle adjustment scheduling, ORB-based tracking with geometric pose estimation, and neural rendering optimization.
AI.result: Extensive evaluations on multiple datasets show CHOW-SLAM outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both scene reconstruction quality and camera tracking accuracy.
AI.conclusion: The explicit construction of complementary spatial and temporal constraints within a compact representation enables superior dense reconstruction and tracking performance under limited online resources.

title: Recompute or Reuse? Diagnosing and Mitigating Textual Shortcuts in VLM Self-Reflection
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are expected to revise their reasoning when visual evidence changes. Failures to do so are often attributed to insufficient visual attention or contextual inertia, leaving unclear what models reuse instead of recomputing from the current image. We show that evidence-bearing reasoning in a prior chain of thought (CoT) can form a textual shortcut that competes behaviorally with visual recomputation. Across 16 VLMs, a matched counterfactual analysis identifies evidence-bearing content as the most robust carrier of prior-CoT influence. Removing this evidence-bearing content shifts answer preference more than removing length-matched non-evidence context or the final-answer span, with prior control weakening progressively as more stale evidence is removed. Reordering this evidence also weakens prior control, showing that its organization modulates shortcut strength. Beyond the immediate answer, the shortcut can retain residual influence after answer correction: weakening current-image support shifts preference back toward the prior answer, while repeated prior answers and reused premises arise mainly when the shortcut remains active. To limit this influence, we introduce Fresh-State Attention Firewall (FSAF), a training-free intervention that isolates fresh computation from the prior CoT. Across five VLMs, FSAF raises visual update rate from 35.28% to 53.61% and reduces prior-answer rate from 39.22% to 3.67%. Reliable VLM self-reflection therefore requires more than looking again: fresh visual recomputation must be protected from stale textual reuse.

AI.tldr: This paper reveals that evidence-bearing content in prior chain-of-thought reasoning acts as a textual shortcut that competes with visual recomputation in vision-language models, and introduces Fresh-State Attention Firewall (FSAF), a training-free intervention that isolates fresh computation from prior CoT, dramatically improving visual update rates and reducing prior-answer persistence.
AI.motivation: VLMs often fail to revise their reasoning when visual evidence changes, but previous work blames this on visual attention failures or contextual inertia without clarifying what models actually reuse instead of recomputing from the current image. The authors aim to identify the specific mechanism by which prior reasoning influences answers.
AI.method: The authors conduct a matched counterfactual analysis across 16 VLMs to isolate which content in prior chain-of-thought carries the most influence (finding evidence-bearing content is most robust). They perform removal and reordering experiments to measure how prior control weakens. They then introduce FSAF, a training-free attention-based intervention that separates fresh computation from stale prior CoT content.
AI.result: Evidence-bearing prior CoT content is the strongest carrier of prior influence; removing it shifts answer preference more than removing non-evidence context or final-answer spans, and reordering also weakens the shortcut. FSAF raises visual update rate from 35.28% to 53.61% and reduces prior-answer rate from 39.22% to 3.67% across five VLMs.
AI.conclusion: Reliable VLM self-reflection requires more than simply looking again at the image; fresh visual recomputation must be actively protected from stale textual reuse, as evidence-bearing prior reasoning forms a persistent shortcut that competes with visual updates.

title: CultureVidBench: Benchmarking Cultural Understanding in Text-to-Video Generation
summary: Text-to-video (T2V) generation models have advanced rapidly, yet their ability to represent diverse cultural contexts remains underexplored. Existing benchmarks mainly focus on perceptual quality, physical plausibility, and text-video alignment, but do not directly assess whether generated videos capture culturally specific objects, actions, rituals, visible text, or audio cues. We introduce CultureVidBench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating cultural understanding in T2V generation. CultureVidBench contains 1,000 curated prompts covering 12 countries, 6 continents, 8 cultural regions, and 14 cultural aspects organized into three categories: material culture, social practice & performance, and ritual & ceremony. Designed specifically for video generation, CultureVidBench emphasizes dynamic and multimodal cultural representation, including social interactions, ritual procedure, and culturally appropriate visible text and audio. We evaluate seven representative T2V models through human user studies and MLLM-based automatic assessment across cultural faithfulness, multimodal cultural rendering, semantic adherence, and perceptual quality. Results show that although current models achieve strong semantic adherence and visual quality, they often fail to faithfully capture fine-grained cultural details, particularly for underrepresented regions, rituals, and multimodal cultural cues.

AI.tldr: CultureVidBench is a new benchmark with 1,000 curated prompts spanning 12 countries, 6 continents, and 14 cultural aspects to evaluate cultural understanding in text-to-video (T2V) generation. Evaluation of seven T2V models via human studies and MLLM-based assessment reveals that while models achieve strong semantic adherence and perceptual quality, they struggle with fine-grained cultural fidelity, especially for underrepresented regions, rituals, and multimodal cues.
AI.motivation: Existing T2V benchmarks focus on perceptual quality, physical plausibility, and text-video alignment, but do not assess whether generated videos capture culturally specific objects, actions, rituals, visible text, or audio cues. This leaves a gap in understanding how well T2V models represent diverse cultural contexts.
AI.method: CultureVidBench is constructed with 1,000 curated prompts covering 12 countries, 6 continents, 8 cultural regions, and 14 cultural aspects across three categories: material culture, social practice & performance, and ritual & ceremony. The benchmark emphasizes dynamic and multimodal cultural representation, including social interactions, ritual procedures, and culturally appropriate visible text and audio.
