summary: In-context learning (ICL) has attracted increasing attention for enabling models to perform new tasks using only a few ``input--output'' prompt examples. However, existing approaches suffer from \textbf{shallow task adaptation}, where prompts are primarily used as contextual cues to implicitly infer task intent through semantic representations, while the underlying computational process remains unchanged. This limitation restricts task-specific adaptation and compromises inference interpretability. We argue that prompts should not only condition feature representations but also dynamically regulate the model's computation pathways. To this end, we propose \textbf{PromptPath}, an adaptive ICL framework that enables computation-level adaptation through prompt-conditioned dynamic pathways. Specifically, PromptPath introduces a prompt-driven routing mechanism to selectively activate and compose lightweight low-rank experts, forming task-specific computational pathways tailored to different prompts. By integrating prompt information directly into the inference process, PromptPath dynamically reconfigures model computation to enhance task specialization and interpretability. Extensive experiments on 3D point cloud and 2D visual recognition benchmarks demonstrate that PromptPath consistently outperforms state-of-the-art ICL baselines while exhibiting strong cross-domain and cross-task generalization.

AI.tldr: PromptPath is an adaptive in-context learning framework that moves beyond shallow task adaptation by using prompt-conditioned dynamic pathways—a routing mechanism that selectively activates lightweight low-rank experts to form task-specific computational pathways, enhancing task specialization and interpretability. It outperforms SOTA ICL baselines on 3D point cloud and 2D visual recognition benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing ICL approaches suffer from shallow task adaptation, where prompts serve only as contextual cues for feature representations while the underlying computational process remains static. This limits task-specific adaptation and compromises inference interpretability.
AI.method: PromptPath introduces a prompt-driven routing mechanism that selectively activates and composes lightweight low-rank experts, forming task-specific computational pathways. This enables computation-level adaptation by dynamically reconfiguring model computation based on prompts, integrating prompt information directly into the inference process.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on 3D point cloud and 2D visual recognition benchmarks show that PromptPath consistently outperforms state-of-the-art ICL baselines while demonstrating strong cross-domain and cross-task generalization.
AI.conclusion: Prompts should not only condition feature representations but also dynamically regulate model computation pathways. PromptPath achieves this through computation-level adaptation, improving both task specialization and interpretability in ICL.

title: Messages, Not Tokens: Grounded Coresets for Faithful VLM Compression
summary: Modern vision language models (VLMs) turn high-resolution images into long sequences of visual tokens. Every token traverses the language decoder and persists in its prompt KV cache, inflating inference cost and motivating aggressive visual compression. Existing score-based methods assign each token an independent importance score and retain the Top-K. However, text queries consume collective, signed attention messages from the visual population, not isolated patches. Consequently, equally sized Top-K sets can repeatedly cover one salient region, omit sparse but complementary evidence and discard information carried by the removed population. We therefore formulate faithful visual compression as constructing a compact coreset for decoder messages, and introduce our training-free Grounded Message Coreset Pruning (GMC) which jointly allocates support across query-grounded, appearance, and coordinate-aware evidence, then transports discarded states into selected representatives at their original multimodal positions before physical compaction and native attention resume. This decomposes faithful compression into two coupled components, including selecting carriers that cover the required message modes and realizing the signed population message on those carriers. We further derive bounds connecting their errors to signed-message distortion, visual innovation, and candidate-margin stability. Experiments across multiple VLM families and diverse benchmarks demonstrate strong performance, with GMC-H2 retaining 97.78% Full-relative mean capability on Qwen2.5-VL-7B using 80.2% fewer visual tokens, while GMC-L16 reaches 100.36%. Controlled interventions verify that collective support and population realization jointly drive these gains.

AI.tldr: GMC (Grounded Message Coreset Pruning) is a training-free visual token pruning method for VLMs that constructs compact coresets of decoder messages rather than scoring individual tokens independently, jointly allocating support across query-grounded, appearance, and coordinate-aware evidence, then transporting discarded states into selected representatives to preserve faithful visual compression.
AI.motivation: Existing score-based visual token pruning methods assign independent importance scores to each token and retain Top-K, but text queries consume collective, signed attention messages from the visual population rather than isolated patches. Top-K sets can redundantly cover one salient region, omit sparse complementary evidence, and discard information carried by the removed population, causing loss of faithful visual information during compression.
AI.method: GMC formulates faithful visual compression as constructing a compact coreset for decoder messages. It jointly allocates support across three evidence modes: query-grounded, appearance, and coordinate-aware. It then transports discarded states into selected representatives at their original multimodal positions before physical compaction and native attention resume. The method decomposes compression into two coupled components: selecting carriers that cover required message modes, and realizing the signed population message on those carriers. They also derive bounds connecting errors to signed-message distortion, visual innovation, and candidate-margin stability.
AI.result: Experiments across multiple VLM families and diverse benchmarks show strong performance. GMC-H2 retains 97.78% Full-relative mean capability on Qwen2.5-VL-7B using 80.2% fewer visual tokens, while GMC-L16 reaches 100.36%. Controlled interventions verify that collective support and population realization jointly drive the gains.
AI.conclusion: The collective, population-level nature of visual attention messages is key to faithful compression. By considering query-grounded, appearance, and coordinate-aware evidence jointly and realizing the full signed population message on selected carriers, GMC achieves near-full (or even slightly above) VLM capability with dramatically reduced visual tokens, outperforming existing score-based Top-K pruning approaches.

title: Two Sides of the Same Coin: Co-Evolving Search for Cross-Task Attacks on Vision-Language Models
comment: 15 pages, 7 figures, and 8 tables; includes supplementary material
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit strong generalization across multimodal tasks but remain vulnerable to adversarial perturbations. Existing attacks typically follow single-trajectory gradient optimization or task-specific objectives, limiting search-space exploration and cross-task transferability. We propose an evolutionary-computation-guided cross-modal attack framework for unified VLMs. The framework adaptively searches both textual and visual spaces. On the textual side, it evolves hard negative semantic embeddings around the source-category representation to provide diverse cross-modal repulsion. On the visual side, it maintains a population of object-region perturbations and combines momentum-based gradient updates with evolutionary selection, mutation, and crossover to more reliably explore multiple feasible trajectories. Jointly optimizing semantic negative guidance and localized perturbations generates adversarial examples that consistently shift source-object semantics toward target categories across vision-language tasks. Theoretical analyses show that the co-evolutionary search preserves perturbation feasibility, prevents degradation of the best observed fitness, and increases the probability of reaching high-margin adversarial regions compared with single-trajectory optimization. Experiments on Florence-2, OFA, and UnifiedIO-2 demonstrate strong overall attack performance across image captioning, object detection, region categorization, and object localization. Ablation studies further verify the complementary effectiveness of text-side semantic evolution and image-side perturbation evolution, as well as the framework's efficiency and cross-task transferability.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an evolutionary-computation-guided cross-modal attack framework for unified vision-language models (VLMs) that jointly evolves semantic text embeddings and visual object-region perturbations to generate adversarial examples with strong cross-task transferability across image captioning, object detection, region categorization, and object localization.
AI.motivation: Existing adversarial attacks on VLMs rely on single-trajectory gradient optimization or task-specific objectives, which limit search-space exploration and cross-task transferability. A more unified and robust attack strategy is needed.
AI.method: The framework employs a co-evolutionary approach: on the text side, it evolves hard negative semantic embeddings around source-category representations for cross-modal repulsion; on the visual side, it maintains a population of object-region perturbations using momentum-based gradient updates combined with evolutionary selection, mutation, and crossover to explore multiple feasible attack trajectories.
AI.result: Experiments on Florence-2, OFA, and UnifiedIO-2 demonstrate strong overall attack performance across image captioning, object detection, region categorization, and object localization. Ablation studies confirm the complementary effectiveness of text-side and image-side evolution, as well as efficiency and cross-task transferability. Theoretical analyses validate perturbation feasibility, preservation of best fitness, and increased probability of reaching high-margin adversarial regions.
AI.conclusion: The co-evolutionary search framework provides a principled and effective approach for generating transferable, cross-task adversarial examples against unified VLMs, outperforming single-trajectory optimization methods both theoretically and empirically.

title: HiResNets: Native Full-HD Video Recognition with Foveal Residual Streams
summary: Much of the recent progress in image and video recognition has come at the cost of memory: larger models, increased resolution, and longer temporal contexts. An inevitable component is the quadratic (or larger) growth of memory and compute based on image resolution, which is a property of the grid sampling used in convolutional networks and vision transformers. In this work we study residual networks whose convolutional blocks have logarithmic-square growth instead, enabling them to process very high-resolution video quickly. The key insight is to use a residual architecture's residual stream as a high-resolution buffer, to which convolutional blocks only read and write via log-polar image warp operations. Layers adaptively focus on different parts of each frame, with very high resolution only near the focus point. A complete high-resolution representation is built up in the residual stream, analogous to eye saccades creating a complete picture in biological vision, and a theoretical construction is presented that eliminates the quadratic dependency of the residual stream resolution. Experiments demonstrate that our proposed HiResNets learn to foveate around scenes similarly to human vision, and have superior performance in difficult egocentric video recognition tasks, especially egocentric video with small objects and fine-grained recognition.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces HiResNets, residual networks with convolutional blocks exhibiting logarithmic-square growth instead of quadratic growth with image resolution. Using the residual stream as a high-resolution buffer with log-polar image warp operations, these networks process very high-resolution video efficiently by adaptively foveating around scenes like human vision.
AI.motivation: Recent progress in image and video recognition is limited by memory and compute costs that grow quadratically (or worse) with image resolution due to grid sampling in CNNs and vision transformers. This quadratic dependency makes processing very high-resolution video impractical.
AI.method: HiResNets use a residual architecture's residual stream as a high-resolution buffer. Convolutional blocks read and write to this buffer via log-polar image warp operations, allowing layers to adaptively focus on different parts of each frame with high resolution only near the focus point. A theoretical construction eliminates the quadratic dependency of the residual stream's resolution.
AI.result: Experiments show HiResNets learn to foveate around scenes similarly to human vision and achieve superior performance in difficult egocentric video recognition tasks, especially those involving small objects and fine-grained recognition.
AI.conclusion: The residual stream can serve as an efficient high-resolution buffer, enabling logarithmic-square growth of convolutional blocks, which breaks the quadratic complexity barrier and improves high-resolution video recognition performance.

title: Quaternion Tensor Modeling for Joint Color-Polarization Demosaicking
summary: Division-of-focal-plane (DoFP) color polarization cameras enable snapshot acquisition of color polarization mosaic images, but the inherently sparse sampling pattern makes color polarization demosaicking severely ill-posed. Existing methods often fail to jointly exploit the correlations among polarization channels and the physical constraints inherent in polarization imaging, resulting in noticeable demosaicking artifacts. To address this issue, a quaternion-tensor-based color polarization demosaicking (CPDM) method incorporating Stokes-domain total variation (TV) regularization is proposed. Correlation analysis shows that the correlations among polarization channels are stronger than those among color channels. Accordingly, the color polarization images acquired at $0^\circ$, $45^\circ$, $90^\circ$, and $135^\circ$ are encoded into the four components of a third-order quaternion tensor, with the color channels organized along its third mode. A low-rank prior is then imposed on the quaternion tensor to exploit the global structural redundancy in the color polarization data. Moreover, spatial gradients are mapped to the Stokes domain through an orthogonal transformation to separate intensity, polarization and residual variations, with adaptive quaternion weights enabling component-specific regularization and preserving the energy consistency of the reconstructed Stokes vectors. An efficient optimization algorithm is derived for the resulting model. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superior demosaicking performance of the proposed method.

AI.tldr: A quaternion-tensor-based color polarization demosaicking method with Stokes-domain total variation regularization is proposed to jointly exploit polarization channel correlations and physical constraints, achieving superior demosaicking performance.
AI.motivation: DoFP color polarization cameras capture sparse mosaic images, making demosaicking severely ill-posed. Existing methods fail to jointly exploit correlations among polarization channels and physical constraints inherent in polarization imaging, leading to noticeable demosaicking artifacts.
AI.method: Color polarization images at four angles are encoded as four components of a third-order quaternion tensor with color channels along the third mode. A low-rank prior exploits global structural redundancy, while spatial gradients are mapped to the Stokes domain via orthogonal transformation with adaptive quaternion weights for component-specific regularization preserving energy consistency. An efficient optimization algorithm is derived.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrate superior demosaicking performance compared to existing methods, validating the effectiveness of jointly exploiting polarization channel correlations and Stokes-domain physical constraints.
AI.conclusion: The proposed quaternion-tensor CPDM method with Stokes-domain TV regularization effectively addresses the ill-posed nature of color polarization demosaicking and outperforms existing approaches.

title: UniqueSplat: View-conditioned 3D Gaussian Splatting for Generalizable 3D Reconstruction
summary: In this paper, we propose UniqueSplat, a view-conditioned feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting model to reconstruct customized 3D radiance fields for each view query. Existing feed-forward methods such as pixelSplat and MVSplat aim to generate fixed Gaussians across all views of each scene by minimizing the error between rendered views and ground-truth images. However, such fixed Gaussians generally render images from all views and lack the ability to adapt to specific viewpoints, as they do not incorporate target view information when predicting Gaussians. To address this, our UniqueSplat learns the view-conditioned information as a prior and incorporates this knowledge into network parameters, so that Gaussians are dynamically adjusted in accordance with different views. Specifically, we propose a two-branch view-conditioned hyperNetwork to simultaneously learn view-agnostic embeddings and view-specific knowledge, which not only explores the shareable knowledge from various views, but also adapts the model to specific views at test time. Extensive experiments on widely-used datasets including RealEstate10K, ACID and DTU demonstrate the superiority of UniqueSplat over the state-of-the-art methods. Moreover, UniqueSplat encouragingly outperforms existing methods in cross-dataset evaluation, showing its notable generalization ability.

AI.tldr: UniqueSplat is a view-conditioned feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting model that dynamically adapts Gaussian representations to specific target views, outperforming existing fixed-Gaussian methods like pixelSplat and MVSplat across multiple datasets.
AI.motivation: Existing feed-forward 3D reconstruction methods generate fixed Gaussians that are identical across all views of a scene, lacking the ability to adapt to specific viewpoints since they do not incorporate target view information during Gaussian prediction.
AI.method: UniqueSplat proposes a two-branch view-conditioned hyperNetwork that simultaneously learns view-agnostic embeddings and view-specific knowledge, incorporating target view information into network parameters to dynamically adjust Gaussians per view.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on RealEstate10K, ACID, and DTU show UniqueSplat outperforms state-of-the-art methods, and it also demonstrates superior cross-dataset generalization ability.
AI.conclusion: View-conditioned Gaussian prediction enables better adaptation to specific viewpoints and improved generalization compared to fixed-Gaussian approaches.

title: PhyCheck: Fine-Grained Evidence-Grounded Dataset for Physical Law Understanding in Video-LLMs
summary: Embodied intelligence and world models require video understanding systems to go beyond recognizing objects and actions and develop an understanding of physical regularities. However, despite their strong performance on general video understanding tasks, current video-language models still struggle to reliably determine whether an observed event conforms to specific physical laws. Existing benchmarks primarily assess the physical quality of generated videos, providing limited support for systematically evaluating and improving the physical-law understanding of Video Large Language Models (VideoLLMs). To address this gap, we introduce PhyCheck, a video question answering dataset organized at two complementary levels of granularity. The coarse-grained subset asks models to determine whether the phenomenon shown in a video conforms to or violates physical laws, while the fine-grained subset further examines whether models can capture physical details responsible for the violation or compliance. We use these subsets as structured supervision to improve physical understanding. In addition, the dataset contains a diagnostic subset with external causal context that reveal hidden factors affecting physical plausibility, assessing whether models can recalibrate their judgments accordingly. Experiments with Fine-tune Qwen2.5-VL show that training with the proposed data substantially improves the understanding of physical-consistency, while evaluations in the diagnostic subset reveal that current models still have difficulty incorporating additional causal conditions into their decisions. These findings highlight the gap between recognizing surface-level inconsistencies and understanding underlying physical mechanisms, and provide a foundation for evaluating and improving physical understanding in Video-LLMs.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces PhyCheck, a video question answering dataset designed to evaluate and improve VideoLLMs' understanding of physical laws, organized at coarse-grained (physical consistency judgment) and fine-grained (physical detail identification) levels, plus a diagnostic subset with external causal context. Fine-tuning Qwen2.5-VL on this data improves physical consistency understanding, but models still struggle with recalibrating judgments based on causal context.
AI.motivation: Current VideoLLMs excel at general video understanding but fail to reliably determine whether observed events conform to physical laws. Existing benchmarks focus on generated video quality rather than systematically evaluating physical-law understanding in VideoLLMs, leaving a gap in both evaluation and improvement of physical reasoning capabilities.
AI.method: The paper constructs PhyCheck, a video QA dataset with two granularity levels: (1) a coarse-grained subset for binary judgment of whether videos conform to or violate physical laws, and (2) a fine-grained subset for identifying specific physical details responsible for compliance/violation, plus a diagnostic subset with external causal context to assess whether models can recalibrate judgments. The authors use this data as structured supervision to fine-tune Qwen2.5-VL.
AI.result: Fine-tuning Qwen2.5-VL with PhyCheck substantially improves physical-consistency understanding. However, evaluations on the diagnostic subset show that current models still have difficulty incorporating additional causal conditions into their decisions.
AI.conclusion: The findings reveal a gap between recognizing surface-level physical inconsistencies and understanding the underlying physical mechanisms in VideoLLMs. PhyCheck provides a foundation for evaluating and improving physical understanding in video-language models, highlighting the need for further work on integrating causal context into physical reasoning.

title: AdaForensics: Learning A Characteristic-aware Adaptive Deepfake Detector
summary: In this paper, we propose a characteristic-aware adaptive network named AdaForensics for deepfake detection. Most existing methods learn a fixed network to detect deepfakes based on carefully-designed network architectures. However, these methods employ the same deepfake detector for all the images despite of various facial characteristic, which fail to provide customized forgery detection for different individuals. To address this, our AdaForensics simultaneously learns characteristic-agnostic and characteristic-specific embeddings, where the detector dynamically adapts to varying faces with our designed hypernetwork on the fly. More specifically, our AdaForensics not only explores the shareable abstractions from various deepfake images, but also adapts the detector to the given characteristic at test time. To achieve this, we propose a two-branch HyperNetwork to learn an adaptive deepfake detector, which automatically adjusts the parameters based on characteristic of the input. Extensive experiments on widely-used datasets including FaceForensics, Celeb-DF and DFDC demonstrate our AdaForensics outperforms the state-of-the-art works.

AI.tldr: AdaForensics is a characteristic-aware adaptive network for deepfake detection that uses a two-branch hypernetwork to dynamically adjust detector parameters based on facial characteristics, learning both characteristic-agnostic and characteristic-specific embeddings simultaneously. It outperforms state-of-the-art methods on FaceForensics, Celeb-DF, and DFDC datasets.
AI.motivation: Existing deepfake detection methods use a fixed network for all images regardless of facial characteristics, failing to provide customized forgery detection for different individuals. This lack of personalization limits detection performance.
AI.method: AdaForensics simultaneously learns characteristic-agnostic and characteristic-specific embeddings. A two-branch HyperNetwork is employed to learn an adaptive deepfake detector that automatically adjusts its parameters based on the characteristic of the input image, adapting the detector at test time on the fly.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on FaceForensics, Celeb-DF, and DFDC datasets demonstrate that AdaForensics outperforms state-of-the-art deepfake detection methods.
AI.conclusion: Characteristic-aware adaptive detection, where the detector dynamically adjusts to individual facial characteristics, is more effective than applying a fixed detector to all images for deepfake detection.

title: GSRAIN: Physically Calibrated High-/Low-Frequency Rainfall Synthesis for 3D Gaussian Driving Scenes
summary: Existing rainfall simulation methods for autonomous driving remain limited in physical controllability and multi-view consistency. This paper presents GSRAIN, a high-/low-frequency rainfall synthesis method for 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) driving scenes. GSRAIN constructs a high-frequency raindrop model from measured rainfall data and generates low-frequency rainy appearance using a geometry-aware single-step diffusion model. The two effects are then fused in a unified 3DGS scene, enabling rainfall-intensity control over the range of 0--13~mm/h. The proposed method achieves a Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) of 149.09, outperforming CycleGAN-Turbo (155.71) and WeatherEdit (157.94). Object-detection and closed-loop driving experiments further show that the generated scenes expose scene-dependent performance changes of the evaluated algorithms under controllable rainfall. These results indicate that GSRAIN provides an effective approach for constructing physically controllable, repeatable, and closed-loop-compatible rainy-weather test scenes for autonomous driving.

AI.tldr: GSRAIN is a high-/low-frequency rainfall synthesis method for 3D Gaussian Splatting driving scenes, enabling rainfall-intensity control (0-13 mm/h) and achieving superior FID scores (149.09) over existing methods while supporting closed-loop driving testing.
AI.motivation: Existing rainfall simulation methods for autonomous driving lack physical controllability and multi-view consistency, limiting their effectiveness for testing driving algorithms under rainy conditions.
AI.method: GSRAIN constructs a high-frequency raindrop model from measured rainfall data and generates low-frequency rainy appearance using a geometry-aware single-step diffusion model, then fuses both effects in a unified 3DGS scene.
AI.result: Achieves FID of 149.09, outperforming CycleGAN-Turbo (155.71) and WeatherEdit (157.94). Object-detection and closed-loop driving experiments show scene-dependent performance changes under controllable rainfall.
AI.conclusion: GSRAIN provides an effective approach for constructing physically controllable, repeatable, and closed-loop-compatible rainy-weather test scenes for autonomous driving.

title: SWINSleepNet: A Hierarchical Context-Aware Framework for Sleep Staging (v2)
comment: Report-no: SDUST-SLEEP-202608-V2; 10 pages, 7 figures, revised updated version of arXiv submit/7867870, conference submission draft
summary: Automatic sleep staging is a critical role in sleep disorder diagnosis, sleep quality assessment, and long-term health monitoring; however, existing approaches suffer poor performance on ambiguous and transition-related sleep stages, caused by inadequate modeling of fine-grained intra-epoch structures and complex cross-region spectral dependencies. Traditional epoch-level encoders commonly fail to extract subtle temporal microstructures and intra-epoch cross-region interactions, resulting in unsatisfactory recognition accuracy for hard categories such as the N1 stage. To tackle these drawbacks, we propose SwinSleepNet, a hierarchical context-aware dual-stream framework that separately optimizes intra-epoch representation learning and inter-epoch contextual modeling. Concretely, we characterize each sleep epoch from two complementary perspectives: raw time-domain EEG signal and its time-frequency transformation. The time-domain branch adopts convolutional encoders to capture fine waveform temporal details, and the time-frequency branch uses Swin Transformer to extract local spectro-temporal features, hierarchical multi-scale information and long-range spatial dependencies. The multi-branch extracted features are fused into integrated embeddings, which are optimized by a bidirectional context module to capture cross-epoch temporal dependencies for final sleep stage classification. Comprehensive experiments on Sleep-EDF-20, Sleep-EDF-78 and SHHS datasets verify that our method achieves competitive overall performance, and exhibits stronger robustness and stability on difficult N1 stages and transitional epochs. The results prove that optimized intra-epoch representation learning based on hierarchical architecture greatly benefits automatic sleep staging tasks.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes SwinSleepNet, a hierarchical context-aware dual-stream framework for automatic sleep staging that separately optimizes intra-epoch representation learning and inter-epoch contextual modeling using both raw time-domain EEG signals and time-frequency transformations, achieving competitive performance on Sleep-EDF-20, Sleep-EDF-78, and SHHS datasets with stronger robustness on difficult N1 stages and transitional epochs.
AI.motivation: Existing automatic sleep staging approaches perform poorly on ambiguous and transition-related sleep stages (e.g., N1) because traditional epoch-level encoders fail to extract fine-grained intra-epoch temporal microstructures and complex cross-region spectral dependencies.
AI.method: SwinSleepNet is a dual-stream framework with: (1) a time-domain branch using convolutional encoders to capture fine waveform temporal details, (2) a time-frequency branch using Swin Transformer to extract local spectro-temporal features, hierarchical multi-scale information, and long-range spatial dependencies, followed by (3) feature fusion into integrated embeddings and (4) a bidirectional context module for cross-epoch temporal dependency modeling.
AI.result: Comprehensive experiments on Sleep-EDF-20, Sleep-EDF-78, and SHHS datasets show competitive overall performance with stronger robustness and stability on difficult N1 stages and transitional epochs compared to existing methods.
AI.conclusion: Optimized intra-epoch representation learning based on a hierarchical architecture greatly benefits automatic sleep staging, particularly for hard categories and transitional epochs.

title: SPIRIT: Spatio-temporal Pairwise Relational Modeling of Instrument-Tissue Interactions for Surgical Action Triplet Recognition
summary: Fine-grained understanding of surgical activity is essential for context-aware assistance in the operating room, including safety monitoring, adverse event identification, and skill assessment. Surgical action triplets, defined as tuples of the form <instrument, verb, target>, provide a structured description of instrument-tissue interactions. A key open problem, however, is how to learn triplet representations that remain reliable across institutions, where surgical video varies in acquisition conditions, surgeon style, tool usage, and tissue handling, while existing triplet datasets do not support explicit evaluation of center-wise transfer. To address this problem, we propose \textbf{SPIRIT}, a structured framework for surgical action triplet recognition designed to learn interaction representations that transfer more reliably across centers. Instead of treating each triplet as a flat class label, SPIRIT first learns spatio-temporal representations for instruments, verbs, and targets, then models their pairwise relations, and finally composes them into coherent triplet predictions, with multi-head distillation used to stabilize learning. To evaluate this setting, we establish \textbf{MultiBypass-4C-T40}, a multi-centric dataset for dense surgical action triplet recognition in Roux-en-Y gastric bypass across four geographically distinct centers, with auxiliary phase and step annotations. Across multiple evaluation protocols, SPIRIT consistently outperforms strong recent baselines, highlighting the value of explicit relational reasoning for multi-centric triplet recognition. Code will be available at https://github.com/CAMMA-public/multibypass-4c-t40.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces SPIRIT, a structured framework for surgical action triplet recognition (<instrument, verb, target>) that improves cross-center transferability by explicitly modeling spatial-temporal relations between instruments, verbs, and targets rather than treating triplets as flat labels. They also introduce MultiBypass-4C-T40, a multi-centric surgical dataset from four geographically distinct centers, and demonstrate SPIRIT's superiority over existing baselines.
AI.motivation: Surgical activity understanding is crucial for context-aware OR assistance, but existing triplet recognition models fail to generalize across institutions due to variations in acquisition conditions, surgeon style, tool usage, and tissue handling. Current triplet datasets do not support explicit evaluation of center-wise transfer, making this a key open problem.
AI.method: SPIRIT decomposes triplet learning into three stages: (1) learning spatio-temporal representations for instruments, verbs, and targets separately, (2) modeling pairwise relations between them, and (3) composing these into coherent triplet predictions. Multi-head distillation is used to stabilize the learning process.
AI.result: The proposed MultiBypass-4C-T40 dataset (multi-centric, 4 centers, 40 classes, with phase and step annotations) enables evaluation across multiple protocols. SPIRIT consistently outperforms strong recent baselines across all evaluation protocols.
AI.conclusion: Explicit relational reasoning (decomposing triplets into components and modeling their relations) is more effective for multi-centric surgical triplet recognition than treating triplets as flat class labels, demonstrating the value of structured learning for cross-center generalization.

title: DerainSplat: Feed-Forward Clean 3D Gaussian Splatting from Sparse Rainy Views
summary: Although image deraining has advanced substantially, existing methods mainly focus on 2D image restoration. As spatial intelligence applications such as embodied AI and autonomous driving continue to emerge, reconstructing clean 3D scenes from sparse rainy views in a feed-forward manner becomes increasingly important. Existing feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) methods often assume clean inputs and collapse under rainy conditions. To this end, we present \textbf{\textit{DerainSplat}}, a feed-forward framework that reconstructs clean 3D scenes from only a few rainy views. To support this task, we build a large-scale multi-view derain dataset through a four-stage synthesis pipeline that sequentially models overcast illumination, depth-dependent haze, rain streaks, and lens raindrops, producing privileged weather factors. We introduce a weather net that predicts the weather factors from rainy context and yields two support maps. Scene support modulates cross-view cost-volume matching, while radiance support drives depth-aligned appearance fusion to fill corrupted pixels. The derived geometry evidence further attenuates Gaussian opacity to reduce spurious structures. A rainy cycle consistency re-renders clean views using the predicted factors and aligns them with rainy inputs. Extensive experiments show that \textbf{\textit{DerainSplat}} outperforms existing methods on various datasets, including RealEstate10K, ACID, Mip-NeRF360, and real-world rainy scenes, with strong cross-dataset generalization.

AI.tldr: DerainSplat is a feed-forward framework that reconstructs clean 3D scenes from sparse rainy views using 3D Gaussian Splatting, supported by a large-scale multi-view derain dataset with privileged weather factors and a weather net that provides scene and radiance support for robust geometry and appearance estimation.
AI.motivation: Existing feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting methods assume clean inputs and fail under rainy conditions, while image deraining focuses only on 2D restoration. As spatial intelligence applications (embodied AI, autonomous driving) demand clean 3D scene reconstruction from rainy views, a feed-forward method for 3D deraining is needed.
AI.method: The framework includes: (1) a four-stage synthesis pipeline building a large-scale multi-view derain dataset modeling overcast illumination, depth-dependent haze, rain streaks, and lens raindrops with privileged weather factors; (2) a weather net predicting weather factors from rainy context to produce two support maps—scene support modulating cross-view cost-volume matching and radiance support driving depth-aligned appearance fusion; (3) Gaussian opacity attenuation using geometry evidence to reduce spurious structures; (4) rainy cycle consistency that re-renders clean views with predicted factors and aligns them with rainy inputs.
AI.result: DerainSplat outperforms existing methods on RealEstate10K, ACID, Mip-NeRF360, and real-world rainy scenes, demonstrating strong cross-dataset generalization.
AI.conclusion: DerainSplat provides an effective feed-forward solution for reconstructing clean 3D scenes from limited rainy views, advancing 3D scene reconstruction under adverse weather conditions with robust generalization to real-world scenarios.

title: T$^2$exture: Sparsely Perturbed Thermal-to-Texture Imaging
summary: Thermal imaging remains effective under adverse illumination, yet passive long-wave infrared (LWIR) measurements often lack fine texture. Existing thermal texture imaging approaches commonly rely on spectral sensing or registered auxiliary modalities, incurring substantial data throughput or vulnerability to cross-modal degradation. We introduce T$^2$exture, a sparsely perturbed thermal texture imaging framework that aims to reconstruct temporally dense thermal texture sequences from densely sampled passive frames and a few actively perturbed keyframes. We define thermal texture as the residual between a source-on observation and its corresponding source-off passive state. Under sparse LWIR illumination and rapid quasi-steady paired acquisition, this residual attenuates the passive-emission background and approximates a source-induced reflected response, exposing localized material- and geometry-dependent texture. T$^2$exture reconstructs a dense sequence of this source-conditioned response through two stages. Stage 1 estimates the unobserved source-off passive state at each active instant from neighboring passive frames to obtain reliable differential texture anchors. Stage 2 combines sparse anchors with passive structural context near each target time to reconstruct the dense sequence. On the simulated benchmark, T$^2$exture adds only 0.20M parameters to AMT-L while improving PSNR by 6.66 dB. Extensive evaluations on simulated and real acquisitions further show clearer texture recovery and stronger structural preservation than representative VFI baselines. These results establish T$^2$exture as a practical framework for thermal texture imaging under sparse active acquisition.

AI.tldr: T²exture is a sparsely perturbed thermal texture imaging framework that reconstructs temporally dense thermal texture sequences from passive frames and a few actively perturbed keyframes, defining thermal texture as the residual between source-on and source-off observations. It uses a two-stage approach (passive state estimation + dense sequence reconstruction) and improves PSNR by 6.66 dB over AMT-L with only 0.20M added parameters.
AI.motivation: Passive long-wave infrared (LWIR) imaging lacks fine texture, while existing thermal texture imaging approaches rely on spectral sensing or registered auxiliary modalities that incur high data throughput or suffer from cross-modal degradation. The goal is to obtain fine thermal texture without these drawbacks.
AI.method: T²exture defines thermal texture as the residual between a source-on observation and its corresponding source-off passive state. Under sparse LWIR illumination with rapid quasi-steady paired acquisition, this residual attenuates the passive-emission background and approximates a source-induced reflected response. The framework uses two stages: (1) estimating unobserved source-off passive states at active instants from neighboring passive frames to obtain differential texture anchors, and (2) combining sparse anchors with passive structural context near each target time to reconstruct the dense sequence.
AI.result: T²exture adds only 0.20M parameters to AMT-L while improving PSNR by 6.66 dB on the simulated benchmark. Extensive evaluations on simulated and real acquisitions show clearer texture recovery and stronger structural preservation than representative VFI baselines.
AI.conclusion: T²exture establishes itself as a practical framework for thermal texture imaging under sparse active acquisition, effectively recovering fine texture while avoiding the drawbacks of existing spectral-sensing or cross-modal approaches.

title: RSC-GestureNet: Reliability-Aware Selective Causal Recognition of Chinese Traffic Police Gestures
summary: Traffic police gestures are safety-critical perception cues for autonomous driving. A deployable recognizer must infer commands causally from continuous full-frame video, remain stable around transitional arm motion, and avoid over-trusting corrupted pose measurements. This study presents RSC-GestureNet, a reliability-aware selective causal recognizer, for Chinese traffic police gestures. The model treats pose confidence as a first-class signal: unreliable joints are down weighted during graph reasoning, temporal evidence is aggregated causally, and calibrated predictions are selectively emitted through a reliability-aware inference rule. We further introduce CTPGesture-C, a reproducible feature-level corruption benchmark with seven pose/RGB degradation families, and an RGB-level diagnostic in which corrupted frames are reprocessed by MediaPipe before recognition. On the complete official CTPGesture v1 split (134,424 labeled frames and 33,451 causal windows), RSC-GestureNet achieves 93.33+-0.24% accuracy, 91.71+-0.27% macro-F1, 91.69+-0.29% online macro-F1, 98.80+-0.07% Early@10, 0.153+-0.013 s TTC, and the best robust macro-F1 among evaluated methods. Under the same split and causal protocol, it exceeds reproduced traffic-specific MD-GCN and HLP-GCN baselines by 3.23-4.11 macro-F1 points and 2.15-3.07 online-F1 points. These results, together with calibration, selective-risk, statistical, adaptive-branching, and image-level re-extraction analyses, indicate that explicit pose-reliability modeling improves early, stable, and robust traffic-command recognition.

AI.tldr: RSC-GestureNet is a reliability-aware causal recognizer for Chinese traffic police gestures that leverages pose confidence, causal temporal evidence aggregation, and selective prediction to achieve robust early recognition under corrupted inputs, outperforming baselines on the CTPGesture dataset.
AI.motivation: Traffic police gesture recognition is a safety-critical task for autonomous driving, but existing systems struggle with causal inference from continuous video, instability around transitional arm motion, and over-reliance on corrupted pose measurements.
AI.method: RSC-GestureNet treats pose confidence as a first-class signal: unreliable joints are down-weighted during graph reasoning, temporal evidence is aggregated causally, and calibrated predictions are selectively emitted via a reliability-aware inference rule. The authors also introduce CTPGesture-C, a feature-level corruption benchmark with seven pose/RGB degradation families, plus an RGB-level diagnostic pipeline.
AI.result: On the CTPGesture v1 split (134,424 frames, 33,451 causal windows), RSC-GestureNet achieves 93.33% accuracy, 91.71% macro-F1, 91.69% online macro-F1, 98.80% Early@10, 0.153s TTC, and the best robust macro-F1 among evaluated methods, beating MD-GCN and HLP-GCN baselines by 3.23-4.11 macro-F1 and 2.15-3.07 online-F1 points.
AI.conclusion: Explicit pose-reliability modeling improves early, stable, and robust traffic-command recognition, as validated by calibration, selective-risk, statistical, adaptive-branching, and image-level re-extraction analyses.

title: CLEAR: Conflict-aware Learning via Evidence-guided Adaptive Routing for Unified Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Super-Resolution
summary: Sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting Super-resolution is highly challenging since the sparse and low-resolution (LR) inputs lack sufficient geometric and high-frequency information for accurate reconstruction. To achieve high-quality reconstruction, existing sparse-view super-resolution methods adhere to two-stage pipeline that performs LR Gaussian reconstruction and then high-resolution (HR) Gaussian refinement, which directly results in stage-wise Gaussian transfer and reconstruction error accumulation. To this end, we propose CLEAR, a Conflict-aware Learning via Evidence-guided Adaptive Routing, as the first unified single-stage framework for Sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting Super-resolution. Specifically, CLEAR performs joint the optimization of authentic LR observations and external HR priors within a unified Gaussian representation. To mitigate the gradient conflicts introduced by sparse supervision during training, we propose a Gaussian-wise conflict-aware optimization strategy that regards the LR gradient as a reliable anchor and applies evidence-conditioned soft correction only to severe HR conflicts. Moreover, to recover high-frequency details, we introduce an evidence-guided Patch-to-Gaussian routing mechanism which estimates patch reliability and detail demand, lifts them into Gaussian space, and selectively routes high-frequency gradients and densification. Finally, we employ shared Gaussian dropout and a detached mid-training anchoring to enhance the robustness of training framework. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world $4\times$ super-resolution benchmarks demonstrate that CLEAR consistently achieves state-of-the-art rendering quality and superior geometric fidelity.

AI.tldr: CLEAR is the first unified single-stage framework for sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting super-resolution, jointly optimizing authentic LR observations and external HR priors within a unified Gaussian representation, with conflict-aware optimization and evidence-guided routing to achieve state-of-the-art rendering quality.
AI.motivation: Existing sparse-view super-resolution methods use a two-stage pipeline (LR Gaussian reconstruction followed by HR Gaussian refinement), which suffers from stage-wise Gaussian transfer issues and error accumulation. A unified single-stage framework is needed to avoid these problems.
AI.method: CLEAR proposes: (1) joint optimization of LR observations and HR priors in a unified Gaussian representation; (2) a Gaussian-wise conflict-aware optimization strategy treating LR gradients as anchors with evidence-conditioned soft correction for severe HR conflicts; (3) an evidence-guided Patch-to-Gaussian routing mechanism to selectively route high-frequency gradients and densification; (4) shared Gaussian dropout and detached mid-training anchoring for training robustness.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world 4x super-resolution benchmarks show CLEAR consistently achieves state-of-the-art rendering quality and superior geometric fidelity.
AI.conclusion: The unified single-stage framework effectively mitigates gradient conflicts from sparse supervision and recovers high-frequency details, outperforming existing two-stage approaches on sparse-view 3D Gaussian splatting super-resolution.

title: Self-supervised DXA representations encode multi-system disease risk, biological aging and heritability
summary: Whole-body dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) scans are routinely acquired to measure bone density and regional body composition, leaving their spatial structure largely unused. Here, we show that self-supervised learning (SSL) can convert raw DXA images into representations of systemic health. We introduce LeDXA, a vision model based on a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) that learns by predicting latent representations rather than reconstructing pixels. Trained from scratch on 11,540 unlabeled Human Phenotype Project scans, LeDXA was evaluated internally and on 47,400 external UK Biobank (UKBB) scans. It improved cross-cohort prediction of prevalent diseases and biomarkers beyond scanner-derived DXA measurements and DINOv3, a state-of-the-art general-purpose model, despite approximately 150,000-fold fewer training images and nearly 40-fold fewer parameters. Over a median 4.3-year UKBB follow-up, LeDXA improved incident disease prediction over tabular DXA measures, with the largest gains for hip and knee arthrosis and type 2 diabetes. For hip arthrosis, 66% of incident cases occurred in the highest-risk quartile versus 41% for tabular measures. Its representations predicted chronological age externally (r = 0.88; mean absolute error = 2.90 years), and the biological-age gap tracked broader disease burden and a 45% higher mortality hazard in the oldest-appearing quartile. The gap also decreased in women after starting hormone-replacement therapy, suggesting it may be modifiable. Genome-wide associations recovered mostly known body-composition and bone-density loci, and LeDXA embeddings were more heritable than DINOv3's. These findings reveal prognostic information in DXA images that conventional readouts discard, learnable with relatively little data and modest compute.

AI.tldr: LeDXA is a self-supervised vision model based on JEPA architecture that learns systemic health representations directly from raw whole-body DXA scans. Trained on only 11,540 unlabeled scans, it outperforms a state-of-the-art general model (DINOv3) and tabular DXA measures in cross-cohort disease and biomarker prediction, improves incident disease prediction (hip/knee arthrosis, type 2 diabetes), predicts chronological age with high accuracy, and derives a biological-age gap that tracks disease burden, mortality hazard, and is potentially modifiable.
AI.motivation: Whole-body DXA scans are routinely acquired for bone density and body composition measurement, but their rich spatial structure is largely discarded. The authors aim to unlock the hidden prognostic information in DXA images using self-supervised learning, showing that raw images carry systemic health signals beyond conventional tabular readouts.
AI.method: The authors introduce LeDXA, a vision model built on a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA). Instead of reconstructing pixels, it learns by predicting latent representations. The model was trained from scratch on 11,540 unlabeled Human Phenotype Project scans and validated internally and on 47,400 external UK Biobank scans. Evaluations included cross-cohort disease/biomarker prediction, incident disease prediction, age prediction, biological-age gap analysis, and genome-wide association studies.
AI.result: LeDXA outperformed both tabular DXA measurements and DINOv3 in disease and biomarker prediction despite far fewer training images (~150,000x fewer) and nearly 40x fewer parameters. It improved incident disease prediction, notably for hip/knee arthrosis and type 2 diabetes (66% of hip arthrosis cases in highest-risk quartile vs 41% for tabular). It predicted chronological age externally (r=0.88, MAE=2.90 years), and the biological-age gap tracked disease burden, showed 45% higher mortality hazard in the oldest-appearing quartile, and decreased in women after HRT. Its embeddings were more heritable than DINOv3's.
AI.conclusion: DXA images contain substantial prognostic information that conventional clinical readouts discard, and this information can be extracted with relatively little data and modest compute using SSL. This reveals a cost-effective path to enhanced disease prediction and potentially modifiable biological-age measurement from routinely acquired scans.

title: VARPose: Flexible 2D Pose Densification via Visual Autoregressive Modeling for Enhanced 3D Lifting
summary: Visual AutoRegressive Modeling (VAR) has excelled in natural image generation via next-scale prediction, but its use on topology-structured data like human skeletons is still unexplored. VARPose is proposed to adaptively densify 2D sparse poses, thereby enriching the anatomical information available for 3D lifting models. Our core contributions are twofold. First, we introduce a Granularity-agnostic Pose Tokenizer (GPT), which employs a single hybrid codebook and a residual quantization strategy to encode poses of varying densities into a unified, multi-scale discrete representation. Our results demonstrate the strong generalizability of this representation. By decoupling the representation from the projection, we can successfully decode novel pose granularities using a frozen codebook with a retrained decoder. Second, we propose UniSkelar, a unified autoregressive model that treats "joint density" as "scale". UniSkelar learns to predict the token sequence for the next density level in a coarse-to-fine manner, conditioned on the sparsest pose. VARPose not only outperforms state-of-the-art methods and generalizes to unseen granularities, but also confers tangible performance gains on downstream tasks, such as 3D Pose Estimation and Human Mesh Recovery, through 2D pose densification. Our code and model are available at https://github.com/BRL-SYSU/VARPose.git.

AI.tldr: VARPose applies Visual AutoRegressive (VAR) modeling to human skeleton data by treating joint density as scale. It introduces a Granularity-agnostic Pose Tokenizer (GPT) that encodes poses of varying densities into a unified multi-scale discrete representation using a hybrid codebook with residual quantization, and a unified autoregressive model (UniSkelar) that predicts next-density token sequences in a coarse-to-fine manner from the sparsest pose. The method improves 3D pose estimation and human mesh recovery via 2D pose densification and generalizes to unseen granularities.
AI.motivation: While VAR modeling has proven effective for natural image generation via next-scale prediction, its potential on topology-structured data like human skeletons remains unexplored. The paper aims to adapt VAR to 2D sparse poses by densifying them to enrich anatomical information for downstream 3D lifting tasks.
AI.method: Two core components: (1) Granularity-agnostic Pose Tokenizer (GPT) using a single hybrid codebook and residual quantization to encode poses of diverse densities into unified multi-scale discrete tokens, with decoupling of representation from projection to enable decoding of novel granularities via a frozen codebook and retrained decoder; (2) UniSkelar, an autoregressive model treating joint density as scale, predicting the next density level's token sequence in a coarse-to-fine manner conditioned on the sparsest pose.
AI.result: VARPose outperforms state-of-the-art methods, generalizes to unseen pose granularities, and provides tangible performance gains on downstream tasks including 3D Pose Estimation and Human Mesh Recovery via 2D pose densification.
AI.conclusion: The decoupling of discrete pose representation from projection, combined with density-as-scale autoregressive modeling, yields a flexible and generalizable framework for pose densification that benefits downstream 3D understanding tasks. Code and models are released publicly.

title: Local Margin Restoration for Test-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language Models
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) such as CLIP exhibit remarkable zero-shot capabilities, yet their performance frequently degrades sharply under unexpected test-time distribution shifts. While Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) offers a promising solution, continuously adapting VLMs over an unlabeled test stream presents fundamental challenges. Conventional top-1-centric updates often reinforce errors by corrupting the local semantic geometry among related classes, while iterative adaptation exacerbates progressive bias accumulation, ultimately driving the model toward mode collapse. To overcome these coupled vulnerabilities, we propose Local Margin Restoration (LMR), a lightweight, one-step TTA framework. At the sample level, our Protected Margin Restoration (PMR) objective recovers local semantic geometry by shielding plausible near-top candidates from external hard negatives. Concurrently, to combat stream-level degradation, we introduce a dual-stage stabilization mechanism, featuring an Adaptive Margin (AM) controller and Bias Correction (BC), to dynamically disrupt progressive bias accumulation and prevent mode collapse. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-C, ImageNet-C, and ImageNet variants demonstrate that LMR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art TTA baselines, proving exceptionally robust and efficient even in challenging low-batch test-time regimes. Our code is available at https://github.com/DennisHuangYan/LMR.

AI.tldr: LMR is a lightweight one-step test-time adaptation framework for vision-language models that restores local semantic geometry at the sample level via Protected Margin Restoration and prevents progressive bias accumulation at the stream level using an Adaptive Margin controller and Bias Correction, outperforming state-of-the-art TTA baselines on CIFAR-C, ImageNet-C, and ImageNet variants.
AI.motivation: VLMs like CLIP degrade sharply under test-time distribution shifts. Existing TTA approaches suffer from two coupled vulnerabilities: top-1-centric updates corrupt local semantic geometry among related classes, and iterative adaptation leads to progressive bias accumulation and mode collapse.
AI.method: LMR proposes (1) Protected Margin Restoration (PMR) at the sample level to recover local semantic geometry by shielding plausible near-top candidates from hard negatives, and (2) a dual-stage stabilization mechanism at the stream level with an Adaptive Margin (AM) controller and Bias Correction (BC) to disrupt progressive bias accumulation and prevent mode collapse, all in a lightweight one-step framework.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on CIFAR-C, ImageNet-C, and ImageNet variants show LMR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art TTA baselines, demonstrating robustness and efficiency even in challenging low-batch test-time regimes.
AI.conclusion: LMR effectively addresses the coupled vulnerabilities of conventional TTA by combining sample-level local semantic geometry restoration with stream-level stabilization, achieving superior and robust performance for VLM test-time adaptation under distribution shift.

title: VC-Tooler: Learning Compositional and Adaptive Visual Tool Use
summary: Agentic multimodal reasoning extends passive image understanding by allowing VLMs to actively acquire and refine visual evidence through visual tool interactions. Effective visual tool use requires three capabilities: grounding tool calls in visual context, composing tools across multiple steps, and adapting reasoning to tool-returned observations. However, existing approaches largely focus on grounding within fixed tool spaces and rigid invocation patterns, leaving composition and adaptation insufficiently addressed. We present VC-Tooler, which learns visual tool use as a compositional and adaptive capability. To this end, we first build a trajectory bank through a hierarchical synthesis pipeline covering three capability levels: single-tool grounding, multi-tool composition, and diverse tool contexts and interfaces. We then train the model in two stages: a supervised cold start that establishes these capabilities, followed by reinforcement learning that encourages accurate, efficient, and context-aware visual tool use. VC-Tooler achieves state-of-the-art performance among open-source models on both general-purpose and agentic benchmarks, including $95.8\%$ on V* and $35.3\%$ on VTC-Bench, and shows promising transfer under richer tool settings at inference time. Project page: https://w1zheng.github.io/VC-Tooler

AI.tldr: VC-Tooler proposes a method to train VLMs for compositional and adaptive visual tool use through a hierarchical trajectory synthesis pipeline and a two-stage training process (supervised cold start followed by reinforcement learning), achieving state-of-the-art performance on agentic multimodal reasoning benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing approaches to visual tool use in VLMs focus primarily on grounding within fixed tool spaces and rigid invocation patterns, leaving two critical capabilities insufficiently addressed: composition of tools across multiple steps and adaptation of reasoning to tool-returned observations. This gap limits the effectiveness of agentic multimodal reasoning.
AI.method: VC-Tooler first constructs a trajectory bank via a hierarchical synthesis pipeline spanning three capability levels: single-tool grounding, multi-tool composition, and diverse tool contexts/interfaces. The model is then trained in two stages: (1) supervised cold start to establish these capabilities, followed by (2) reinforcement learning that encourages accurate, efficient, and context-aware visual tool use.
AI.result: VC-Tooler achieves state-of-the-art performance among open-source models on both general-purpose and agentic benchmarks, including 95.8% on V* and 35.3% on VTC-Bench, and demonstrates promising transfer capabilities under richer tool settings at inference time.
AI.conclusion: Learning visual tool use as a compositional and adaptive capability through hierarchical trajectory synthesis and two-stage training (SFT + RL) enables state-of-the-art agentic multimodal reasoning, with strong generalization to unseen tool configurations.

title: GenPrior: Unleashing Text-to-Motion Generative Priors for Zero-Shot Skeleton-based Action Recognition
summary: Zero-shot skeleton-based action recognition (ZSAR) aims to recognize unseen action categories by aligning skeleton features with textual semantics. However, existing methods rely on text-derived prototypes that inherently lack geometric structure and physical constraints, resulting in a pronounced \textit{semantic-kinematic gap}. To bridge this gap, we propose \textbf{GenPrior}, the first framework to exploit generative priors from pre-trained Text-to-Motion (T2M) models for ZSAR. Specifically, we introduce Dispersion-Gated Feature Fusion, which distills kinematic prototypes and intra-class dispersion from generative motion sequences and employs a learned gating network to adaptively inject reliable structural cues into textual embeddings while suppressing synthetic artifacts. Furthermore, we propose Generative Prototype Refinement, which leverages these generation-enhanced prototypes as anchors to mine high-confidence unseen samples, calibrating class prototypes toward the true distribution and thereby unleashing strong performance gains. Extensive experiments on NTU-60, NTU-120, and PKU-MMD demonstrate that GenPrior achieves state-of-the-art performance under both zero-shot and generalized zero-shot settings. Code is available at https://github.com/jidongkuang/GenPrior.

AI.tldr: GenPrior is the first framework exploiting generative priors from pre-trained Text-to-Motion models for zero-shot skeleton-based action recognition, using Dispersion-Gated Feature Fusion and Generative Prototype Refinement to bridge the semantic-kinematic gap, achieving SOTA on NTU-60, NTU-120, and PKU-MMD.
AI.motivation: Existing ZSAR methods rely on text-derived prototypes that lack geometric structure and physical constraints, creating a pronounced semantic-kinematic gap that limits recognition of unseen action categories.
AI.method: Two key components: (1) Dispersion-Gated Feature Fusion distills kinematic prototypes and intra-class dispersion from generative motion sequences, using a learned gating network to adaptively inject structural cues into textual embeddings while suppressing artifacts; (2) Generative Prototype Refinement leverages generation-enhanced prototypes as anchors to mine high-confidence unseen samples and calibrate class prototypes toward the true distribution.
AI.result: State-of-the-art performance on NTU-60, NTU-120, and PKU-MMD benchmarks under both zero-shot and generalized zero-shot settings.
AI.conclusion: Generative priors from T2M models can effectively bridge the semantic-kinematic gap in ZSAR, providing a promising new direction for skeleton-based action recognition.

title: HarMoE: Multi-Source Chest Radiograph Pretraining with Dataset-Disentangled Experts
summary: Recent vision-language models for chest X-ray understanding are largely built on image-report alignment and therefore rely heavily on MIMIC-CXR as the dominant pretraining source. While effective at scale, this paradigm underexplores an important alternative source of supervision: a range of existing multi-label classification datasets, which provide cleaner and more explicit disease signals than free-text reports, and can offer broader pathology coverage when combined across sources. However, learning from such heterogeneous datasets is nontrivial, as differences in label ontologies, annotation protocols, acquisition pipelines, and report styles can cause models to entangle clinical semantics with dataset identity, leading to poor transfer despite increased scale. In this work, we revisit radiology VLM construction from the perspective of harmonized multi-source learning. We propose HarMoE, a dataset-aware mixture-of-experts framework that learns shared cross-dataset medical semantics while confining source-specific variation to lightweight residual experts in deeper decoder layers. To further exploit clean supervision from labeled datasets, we train in a unified disease vocabulary with masked multi-dataset supervision, enabling the model to leverage complementary annotations without introducing false negatives. Experiments on large-scale chest X-ray benchmarks show that HarMoE consistently improves zero-shot classification, out-of-distribution transfer, and grounding over strong baselines. Our results suggest that building robust radiology VLMs requires moving beyond single-source image-report alignment toward structured knowledge construction from heterogeneous datasets with cleaner supervision and broader coverage. Code and the 873k harmonized dataset will be released at https://github.com/Roypic/harmoe.

AI.tldr: HarMoE is a dataset-aware mixture-of-experts framework for radiology vision-language models that learns shared cross-dataset medical semantics from heterogeneous multi-label classification datasets while confining source-specific variation to lightweight residual experts, using masked multi-dataset supervision with a unified disease vocabulary to avoid false negatives. It consistently improves zero-shot classification, out-of-distribution transfer, and grounding over strong baselines on large-scale chest X-ray benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Current radiology VLMs rely heavily on MIMIC-CXR for image-report alignment, which underexplores multi-label classification datasets that offer cleaner, more explicit disease signals and broader pathology coverage. However, heterogeneous datasets with differing label ontologies, annotation protocols, and acquisition pipelines cause models to entangle clinical semantics with dataset identity, hurting transfer despite increased scale.
AI.method: HarMoE proposes a dataset-aware mixture-of-experts framework that shares cross-dataset medical semantics while isolating source-specific variation in lightweight residual experts within deeper decoder layers. Training uses a unified disease vocabulary with masked multi-dataset supervision to exploit complementary annotations across datasets without introducing false negatives.
AI.result: On large-scale chest X-ray benchmarks, HarMoE consistently outperforms strong baselines in zero-shot classification, out-of-distribution transfer, and grounding. The authors also release a harmonized 873k dataset and code.
AI.conclusion: Building robust radiology VLMs requires moving beyond single-source image-report alignment toward structured knowledge construction from heterogeneous datasets with cleaner supervision and broader coverage.

title: Open-Set Visual Text Forensics via Sparse-Constraint Rectified Flow
summary: Rapidly evolving Generative AI enables sophisticated visual text manipulations that increasingly evade current forensic detectors. Existing discriminative models often overfit specific forgery patterns, limiting their generalization to unseen, open-set attacks. To address this challenge, we propose a generative detector that localizes tampering by estimating the local restoration cost required to align a query image with authentic visual-text statistics, rather than by learning forgery-specific decision boundaries. Specifically, we introduce Sparse-Constraint Rectified Flow (SC-RF), a detector-oriented adaptation of Flow Matching for spatially sparse anomaly localization. We further mitigate data scarcity via self-supervised Artifact Injection and preserve high-frequency forensic traces using a pixel-space Forensic-DiT. Extensive experiments on three benchmarks show that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, surpassing the runner-up by 3.2 and 4.8 percentage points in F1 and IoU, respectively. In particular, the proposed detector demonstrates strong zero-shot performance on challenging unseen text editing patterns. We further provide an auxiliary stress-test analysis showing that local harmonization produced by our model can weaken the statistical cues relied upon by existing detectors, offering a complementary vulnerability-analysis perspective.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a generative detector (SC-RF) for visual text manipulation that localizes tampering by estimating local restoration cost against authentic visual-text statistics, rather than learning forgery-specific boundaries. It uses Flow Matching adapted for sparse anomaly localization, self-supervised Artifact Injection, and a pixel-space Forensic-DiT, achieving SOTA results (3.2 F1 and 4.8 IoU gains) with strong zero-shot generalization on unseen attacks.
AI.motivation: Existing discriminative detectors overfit specific forgery patterns and fail to generalize to unseen, open-set attacks from rapidly evolving Generative AI. A more robust approach is needed that does not rely on learning forgery-specific decision boundaries.
AI.method: The method introduces Sparse-Constraint Rectified Flow (SC-RF), a detector-oriented adaptation of Flow Matching designed for spatially sparse anomaly localization. It combines self-supervised Artifact Injection to mitigate data scarcity and a pixel-space Forensic-DiT to preserve high-frequency forensic traces. Detection works by estimating the local restoration cost needed to align a query image with authentic visual-text statistics.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on three benchmarks show state-of-the-art performance, surpassing the runner-up by 3.2 percentage points in F1 and 4.8 percentage points in IoU. The detector demonstrates strong zero-shot performance on challenging unseen text editing patterns.
AI.conclusion: The generative detection paradigm offers better generalization than discriminative approaches for visual text forgery localization. Additionally, the model's local harmonization capability provides a complementary vulnerability-analysis perspective by weakening statistical cues relied upon by existing detectors.

title: EOVSAM: Efficient Open-Vocabulary Segmentation with SAM 3 in One Pass
summary: Open-vocabulary segmentation identifies and segments objects from arbitrary textual descriptions. SAM 3 supports noun-phrase-guided segmentation and achieves competitive open-vocabulary performance through exhaustive vocabulary traversal, yet suffers from prohibitive computational overhead as target categories scale. In this paper, we propose an Efficient Open-Vocabulary segmentation framework with SAM 3 (EOVSAM), which adapts SAM 3 for single-pass prediction. EOVSAM removes prompt conditioning to turn SAM 3 into an efficient mask generator and introduces a new Attentional Aggregation strategy to optimize open-vocabulary classification end-to-end. This formulation avoids the multi-stage pipelines and post-processing heuristics commonly used by existing methods, while mitigating the closed-set collapse that can arise when classification is optimized directly. EOVSAM consistently improves segmentation accuracy over vanilla SAM 3 on all evaluated datasets and accelerates inference by up to 338$\times$. Furthermore, EOVSAM maintains high accuracy at lower resolutions while achieving even more remarkable inference speeds. Experiments on standard semantic and panoptic segmentation benchmarks show that EOVSAM combines competitive or state-of-the-art accuracy with a substantial speed advantage over existing open-vocabulary segmentation models. Code and models are available at https://github.com/hustvl/EOVSAM.

AI.tldr: EOVSAM is an efficient open-vocabulary segmentation framework built on SAM 3 that removes prompt conditioning to convert it into a single-pass mask generator, introduces Attentional Aggregation for end-to-end open-vocabulary classification, and achieves up to 338x faster inference while improving segmentation accuracy across all evaluated datasets.
AI.motivation: SAM 3 supports noun-phrase-guided open-vocabulary segmentation with competitive performance but suffers from prohibitive computational overhead due to exhaustive vocabulary traversal as target categories scale. Existing methods also rely on multi-stage pipelines and post-processing heuristics.
AI.method: EOVSAM adapts SAM 3 for single-pass prediction by (1) removing prompt conditioning to turn SAM 3 into an efficient mask generator, and (2) introducing an Attentional Aggregation strategy to optimize open-vocabulary classification end-to-end, avoiding multi-stage pipelines and mitigating closed-set collapse.
AI.result: EOVSAM consistently improves segmentation accuracy over vanilla SAM 3 on all evaluated datasets and accelerates inference by up to 338x. It maintains high accuracy at lower resolutions while achieving even more remarkable speeds, and demonstrates competitive or state-of-the-art accuracy with a substantial speed advantage over existing methods on standard semantic and panoptic segmentation benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: EOVSAM provides a single-pass, efficient solution for open-vocabulary segmentation that combines competitive accuracy with significantly faster inference, offering a practical alternative to computationally expensive exhaustive vocabulary traversal approaches.

title: Sen-Cap: Sensor-Flexible and Noise-Resilient Human Motion Capture via LiDAR-Camera Integration
comment: 16 pages, 8 figures, 4 tables. Accepted at ECCV 2026. Aoru Xue and Yujing Sun contributed equally. Yuexin Ma is the corresponding author
summary: We propose Sen-Cap, a Sensor-Flexible and Noise-Resilient 3D human motion Capture framework that integrates multi-modal data from LiDAR and camera. While multi-modal sensors provide richer information than single-modal sensors, existing approaches still suffer from two core challenges. First, multi-modal alignment/matching across arbitrarily deployed sensors is typically handled by explicit calibration, which propagates errors under changing viewpoints and in turn constrains deployment to fixed, highly overlapped layouts. Second, prior methods degrade under severe noise or partial sensor failures, which are common in real-world environments. To address these challenges, Sen-Cap introduces a Unified Across-Sensor Motion Estimator that reconstructs local pose and shape in a human-centric space without calibrations between sensors, supporting a flexible number of sensors, as well as a Noise-Resistant Trajectory Tracker that maintains robustness under severe point cloud noise through iterative refinement. These sensor-flexible and noise-resilient features make Sen-Cap more practical in real-world deployment. Notably, operating in real time, Sen-Cap achieves state-of-the-art performance on major metrics on Human-M3 and FreeMotion, as well as strong cross-domain performance on LiDARHuman26M and RELI11D. This combination of flexibility and robustness opens new opportunities for motion capture in real-world scenarios, e.g. sports analytics, field robotics, and large-scale immersive environments.

AI.tldr: Sen-Cap is a real-time, sensor-flexible, noise-resilient 3D human motion capture framework that integrates LiDAR and camera data without requiring calibration between sensors, achieving state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Multi-modal sensors offer richer information than single-modal ones, but existing approaches suffer from two core challenges: (1) explicit calibration for multi-modal alignment across arbitrary sensor placements propagates errors under changing viewpoints and limits deployment to fixed, highly overlapped layouts; (2) prior methods degrade significantly under severe noise or partial sensor failures common in real-world environments.
AI.method: Sen-Cap introduces two key components: (1) a Unified Across-Sensor Motion Estimator that reconstructs local pose and shape in a human-centric space without requiring calibration between sensors, supporting a flexible number of sensors; (2) a Noise-Resistant Trajectory Tracker that maintains robustness under severe point cloud noise through iterative refinement.
AI.result: Operating in real time, Sen-Cap achieves state-of-the-art performance on major metrics on Human-M3 and FreeMotion datasets, and demonstrates strong cross-domain performance on LiDARHuman26M and RELI11D benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: The combination of sensor flexibility and noise resilience makes Sen-Cap practical for real-world deployment, opening new opportunities for motion capture in applications such as sports analytics, field robotics, and large-scale immersive environments.
