title: Extended Field of View Analysis for VideoGAN-based Trajectory Generation
summary: Realistic and diverse trajectory generation is central to enabling higher levels of vehicle automation. While rule-based and classical learning-based methods may struggle to capture the complexity of traffic behavior, generative models have already demonstrated in other fields that they can handle a comparable level of complexity. In this paper, we build upon previous work on generative adversarial network (GAN)-based semantic bird's-eye-view traffic generation and extend the proposed framework in several key aspects. We improve the semantic representation, replace the trajectory extraction procedure with a graph-based association method, and systematically investigate increasingly larger fields of view. In addition, we introduce a quantitative evaluation framework to assess hallucinations and object permanence in generated videos. Our experiments demonstrate that the framework generalizes to larger and more complex traffic scenes while maintaining statistically realistic trajectories and coherent spatial relationships between traffic participants. Within 150GPU hours of training and with inference times below 20ms for scenes of up to 20s, our results demonstrate that video-based GANs remain an efficient and scalable approach for realistic trajectory generation, even in substantially larger traffic scenes, making them well suited for downstream tasks such as prediction, planning, and simulation in automated driving.

AI.tldr: This paper extends a GAN-based bird's-eye-view traffic generation framework by improving the semantic representation, replacing trajectory extraction with a graph-based association method, and scaling to larger field-of-view scenes. It introduces a quantitative framework to evaluate hallucinations and object permanence, demonstrating that video-based GANs can generate statistically realistic and coherent trajectories for scenes up to 20s in under 20ms inference time, with only 150 GPU hours of training.
AI.motivation: Realistic and diverse trajectory generation is essential for higher levels of vehicle automation, but rule-based and classical learning-based methods struggle to capture the complexity of traffic behavior. Generative models have shown promise in other fields, motivating their application to traffic scene generation.
AI.method: The framework builds upon a GAN-based semantic bird's-eye-view traffic generation approach with three key extensions: (1) improved semantic representation, (2) replacement of trajectory extraction with a graph-based association method, and (3) systematic investigation of increasingly larger fields of view. A quantitative evaluation framework is also introduced to assess hallucinations and object permanence in generated videos.
AI.result: The framework generalizes to larger and more complex traffic scenes while maintaining statistically realistic trajectories and coherent spatial relationships between traffic participants. Training requires only 150 GPU hours, and inference times are below 20ms for scenes up to 20 seconds.
AI.conclusion: Video-based GANs remain an efficient and scalable approach for realistic trajectory generation even in substantially larger traffic scenes, making them well suited for downstream tasks such as prediction, planning, and simulation in automated driving.

title: SpikeRestormer: Towards Energy-Efficient All-in-One Image Restoration via Unified Event Reasoning
summary: ANN-based All-in-One image restoration (AiOIR) unifies diverse degradation handling but incurs high computational costs, limiting its real-time deployment. While Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer a low-power alternative, applying them to static images remains challenging. This difficulty arises because explicit event signals are absent, and degradation cues are heavily entangled with scene structures, hindering the learning of reliable restoration-oriented spike events. To address these issues, we propose SpikeRestormer, an energy-efficient SNN for AiOIR that performs event reasoning over internally generated spike cues. Specifically, we propose a degradation-event perception process to extract spike-based degradation events through Subtractive Degradation Event Attention (SDEA). Moreover, we introduce Hierarchical Bayesian Skip Masking (HBSM) and Additive Restoration Event Attention (AREA) processes for event-reliability inference and restoration-event construction, respectively. By integrating these complementary processes, SpikeRestormer formulates restoration as a unified process of degradation-event perception, degradation-event reliability inference, and restoration-event construction, liberating the potential of SNNs for energy-efficient AiOIR. Extensive experiments show that SpikeRestormer delivers competitive performance against ANN-based methods and establishes new state-of-the-art results among SNN-based methods with significantly lower energy consumption.

AI.tldr: SpikeRestormer is an energy-efficient Spiking Neural Network (SNN) for All-in-One image restoration that generates and reasons over internally produced spike events, achieving competitive performance against ANN methods and state-of-the-art results among SNN methods with significantly lower energy consumption.
AI.motivation: ANN-based All-in-One image restoration (AiOIR) methods unify multiple degradation types but are computationally expensive, limiting real-time deployment. SNNs offer a low-power alternative, but applying them to static images is challenging because explicit event signals are absent and degradation cues are entangled with scene structures, making it hard to learn reliable restoration-oriented spike events.
AI.method: SpikeRestormer proposes a degradation-event perception process using Subtractive Degradation Event Attention (SDEA), a Hierarchical Bayesian Skip Masking (HBSM) process for event-reliability inference, and an Additive Restoration Event Attention (AREA) process for restoration-event construction. These processes jointly formulate restoration as degradation-event perception, reliability inference, and restoration-event construction.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show SpikeRestormer achieves competitive performance against ANN-based methods and establishes new state-of-the-art results among SNN-based methods while maintaining significantly lower energy consumption.
AI.conclusion: By liberating the potential of SNNs for AiOIR through internally generated spike-based event reasoning, SpikeRestormer offers an energy-efficient pathway toward real-time deployment of unified image restoration.

title: A General-Purpose VLM Can Teach an Astronomy Foundation Model to Better Recognize Galaxy Morphology
summary: Existing astronomy foundation models provide strong galaxy representations, but adapting them to new survey conditions and survey-specific morphology recognition tasks still requires substantial human supervision. We show that VLM-based VQA systems contain meaningful visual-semantic priors that can serve as weak supervision for downstream morphology classifiers and improve morphology classification under limited human-label budgets. We first introduce a survey-oriented VQA benchmark spanning two representative imaging regimes and evaluate state-of-the-art VLMs on galaxy morphology questions. The results show that these models capture useful morphology signals and informative uncertainty, but are not sufficiently reliable to replace human annotators. Motivated by this finding, we use a general-purpose VLM as a morphology teacher for Zoobot, an astronomy foundation model pretrained on large-scale Galaxy Zoo annotations. Across two survey domains and multiple annotation budgets, the VLM teacher consistently improves Zoobot's downstream morphology classification. These results demonstrate that a general-purpose VLM provides knowledge complementary to an astronomy foundation model and can teach it to better recognize galaxy morphology under limited human supervision. The resulting pipeline is designed for label-efficient adaptation to forthcoming large-scale surveys, including the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. The benchmark and code are publicly available at https://github.com/fw-ic/VLM-morphology-teacher.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates that general-purpose VLM-based VQA systems can serve as weak teachers for astronomy foundation models (Zoobot), improving galaxy morphology classification under limited human supervision across multiple survey domains and annotation budgets.
AI.motivation: Astronomy foundation models require substantial human supervision to adapt to new survey conditions and survey-specific morphology recognition tasks. The authors investigate whether VLM-based visual-question-answering systems, which contain visual-semantic priors, can provide weak supervision to reduce this human labeling burden.
AI.method: The authors introduce a survey-oriented VQA benchmark spanning two imaging regimes, evaluate state-of-the-art VLMs on galaxy morphology questions, and then use a general-purpose VLM as a morphology teacher to train Zoobot, leveraging the VLM's outputs as weak supervision signals.
AI.result: VLMs capture useful morphology signals and informative uncertainty but are not reliable enough to replace human annotators. When used as a teacher, the VLM consistently improves Zoobot's downstream morphology classification across two survey domains and multiple annotation budgets.
AI.conclusion: A general-purpose VLM provides complementary knowledge to an astronomy foundation model and can teach it better galaxy morphology recognition under limited human supervision, offering a label-efficient pipeline for forthcoming large-scale surveys like LSST and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.

title: The Push-Forward Transform for Continuous and Robust Comparison of Dynamic Shapes
summary: We introduce a mathematical framework for shape comparison based on mapping functions from the shape domain to a common reference domain. This Push-Forward Transform enables invariant and robust comparison of shapes, preserving intrinsic geometric information. Quantitatively comparing shapes and their temporal evolution is a fundamental challenge in image analysis. Meaningful shape comparison requires representations that are invariant to transformations that do not alter shape itself, such as translation, rotation, reflection, re-parametrization, and uniform scaling, while remaining sensitive to intrinsic geometric variation. Existing approaches often rely on sensitive parameterizations, landmark correspondence, or learned representations that are difficult to interpret and reproduce. We show that the Push-Forward Transform (PF-T) applied to Signed Distance Functions (SDFs) yields a continuous representation that captures both boundary and interior geometry. We derive an interpretable morphometric that quantifies shape similarity and reveals features such as skeletal topology and rotational symmetries. The push-forward transform applies consistently to two- and three-dimensional shapes, extends to time-evolving geometries, and supports the joint analysis of shape and additional scalar fields defined over shapes, such as intensity or molecular signals. We present the mathematical formulation, describe an efficient algorithm, and benchmark the approach on 2D, 3D, and temporal data sets.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces the Push-Forward Transform (PF-T) applied to Signed Distance Functions (SDFs) as a mathematical framework for invariant and robust shape comparison. This representation captures both boundary and interior geometry, enabling interpretable shape similarity quantification, supporting 2D/3D shapes, time-evolving geometries, and joint analysis with additional scalar fields.
AI.motivation: Shape comparison is a fundamental challenge that requires representations invariant to transformations (translation, rotation, reflection, re-parametrization, scaling) while sensitive to intrinsic geometric variation. Existing approaches rely on sensitive parameterizations, landmark correspondence, or hard-to-interpret learned representations.
AI.method: The method maps shape domains to a common reference domain via a Push-Forward Transform applied to Signed Distance Functions (SDFs). This yields a continuous representation capturing both boundary and interior geometry, along with an interpretable morphometric for quantifying shape similarity.
AI.result: The PF-T approach reveals features such as skeletal topology and rotational symmetries, applies consistently to 2D and 3D shapes, extends to time-evolving geometries, and supports joint analysis of shape with additional scalar fields (e.g., intensity or molecular signals). The method was benchmarked on 2D, 3D, and temporal datasets with an efficient algorithm.
AI.conclusion: The Push-Forward Transform on SDFs provides a principled, invariant, and interpretable framework for shape comparison that overcomes limitations of existing approaches while remaining computationally efficient and broadly applicable across dimensions and data modalities.

title: CalibBEV: LiDAR-Camera Calibration via BEV Alignment
summary: We present CalibBEV, a novel Bird's Eye View (BEV) alignment approach for LiDAR-camera calibration. Our method unifies LiDAR and camera data into a shared 3D spatial representation, enabling accurate and robust cross-modal calibration. CalibBEV extracts sensor-wise BEV features from each modality using domain-specific architectures and estimates the calibration matrix through a two-step alignment process. First, we perform an implicit alignment by regressing a coarse calibration matrix directly from the BEV features. To ease this alignment, we enforce semantic consistency between BEV representations across modalities using a contrastive loss inspired by CLIP, guiding both networks toward a unified feature space. In the second step, we leverage our BEV formulation to explicitly align the features of one modality with the other, refining the initial coarse estimate into a final, more accurate calibration matrix. CalibBEV significantly outperforms prior point-to-pixel matching methods, achieving state-of-the-art calibration accuracy. On the KITTI and nuScenes benchmarks, our method reduces the Relative Rotation Error (RRE) by 51% and 68%, and the Relative Translation Error (RTE) by 80% and 91%, respectively, compared to previous methods.

AI.tldr: CalibBEV is a novel Bird's Eye View (BEV) alignment approach for LiDAR-camera calibration that unifies both modalities into a shared 3D spatial representation, performs two-step alignment (coarse implicit regression followed by explicit refinement), and uses CLIP-inspired contrastive learning for semantic consistency, achieving state-of-the-art calibration accuracy on KITTI and nuScenes benchmarks.
AI.motivation: LiDAR-camera calibration is critical for autonomous driving and robotics, but existing point-to-pixel matching methods are limited in accuracy and robustness. The paper aims to overcome these limitations by proposing a unified BEV representation that enables more reliable cross-modal alignment.
AI.method: CalibBEV extracts domain-specific BEV features from both LiDAR and camera modalities, unifies them in a shared 3D spatial representation, and estimates the calibration matrix through two steps: (1) implicit alignment via direct regression of a coarse calibration matrix from BEV features, enhanced by a CLIP-inspired contrastive loss for semantic consistency; (2) explicit alignment that refines the coarse estimate by directly aligning features between modalities.
AI.result: On KITTI and nuScenes benchmarks, CalibBEV reduces Relative Rotation Error (RRE) by 51% and 68%, and Relative Translation Error (RTE) by 80% and 91% respectively, compared to prior methods, achieving state-of-the-art calibration accuracy.
AI.conclusion: CalibBEV demonstrates that a unified BEV representation combined with a two-stage alignment strategy significantly outperforms traditional point-to-pixel matching approaches, setting a new standard for LiDAR-camera calibration accuracy.

title: GEOID-Flood: A Large-Scale Multi-Modal Benchmark Dataset for Flood Segmentation
comment: Accepted at ECCV 2026 - Terrabytes II Workshop, 23 pages
summary: Geospatial foundation models aim to learn representations that transfer across regions and sensors, yet evaluating them on specific tasks requires large, high-quality, multi-modal benchmarks that measure how well such models extract value from data. Concerning flood mapping, existing datasets rarely combine bi-temporal SAR and co-registered optical imagery at scale, leaving the value of foundation models for this downstream task largely untested. We introduce GEOID-Flood, a large-scale multi-modal flood segmentation benchmark, derived from Copernicus Emergency Management Service activations, spanning 219 events across 65 countries over ten years. The dataset provides more than 14,000 tiles with co-registered pre- and post-event Sentinel-1, in GRD and RTC format, pre-event Sentinel-2 composite, and DEM, including manually validated labels that separate background from permanent water and flooded water. Using this benchmark, we evaluate foundation models against conventional encoders across single-image, multi-temporal, and multi-modal protocols. We report three main findings: foundation models offer a consistent but modest advantage; optical-SAR fusion with finetuning best resolves transient flooding; and models trained on GEOID-Flood transfer to unseen events better than those trained on existing datasets. Dataset and code available at https://github.com/links-ads/geoid-flood.

AI.tldr: GEOID-Flood is a large-scale multi-modal flood segmentation benchmark built from Copernicus Emergency Management Service activations, containing 14,000+ tiles across 219 events in 65 countries over ten years. It provides co-registered bi-temporal SAR (GRD and RTC formats), optical imagery, DEM, and manually validated labels. Evaluations reveal foundation models offer consistent but modest advantages, optical-SAR fusion with finetuning best resolves transient flooding, and models trained on GEOID-Flood transfer better to unseen events than those trained on existing datasets.
AI.motivation: Existing flood mapping datasets rarely combine bi-temporal SAR with co-registered optical imagery at scale, leaving the value of geospatial foundation models for flood segmentation largely untested. A large, high-quality, multi-modal benchmark is needed to properly evaluate these models' transfer capabilities across regions and sensors.
AI.method: The authors construct a benchmark from Copernicus Emergency Management Service activations spanning 219 events across 65 countries over ten years, providing over 14,000 tiles with co-registered pre/post-event Sentinel-1 (GRD and RTC), pre-event Sentinel-2 composites, DEM, and manually validated labels separating background, permanent water, and flooded water. They evaluate foundation models against conventional encoders across single-image, multi-temporal, and multi-modal protocols.
AI.result: Three main findings: (1) foundation models provide a consistent but modest advantage over conventional encoders; (2) optical-SAR fusion with finetuning is most effective for resolving transient flooding; (3) models trained on GEOID-Flood generalize better to unseen flood events than those trained on existing datasets.
AI.conclusion: GEOID-Flood provides a valuable large-scale, multi-modal benchmark for flood segmentation that enables systematic evaluation of geospatial foundation models, demonstrating that while these models offer advantages, fusion strategies and dataset quality for training are equally important for downstream flood mapping performance.

title: Global-Scale Self-Supervised Spatiotemporal Learning for NDVI Time-Series Reconstruction
summary: Accurate and efficient reconstruction of cloud-contaminated and noise-corrupted NDVI time series remains a challenge in remote sensing. Deep learning provides a promising solution for modeling complex spatiotemporal dependencies; however, its application is often limited by the difficulty of obtaining paired clear-sky and degraded NDVI data for identical spatiotemporal locations. To address this issue, we propose GloSSR, a Global-scale Self-supervised Spatiotemporal framework for NDVI Reconstruction. The framework constructs supervisory signals by artificially degrading relatively clean NDVI observations with realistic cloud contamination patterns, producing self-supervised training pairs that closely mimic real-world degradation. It further introduces an end-to-end spatiotemporal learning network that jointly captures long-range temporal dependencies and short-term spatiotemporal correlation through a bidirectional Transformer with a ConvLSTM architecture. A temporal-channel attention-based reconstruction module is incorporated to enhance informative features, while a spatiotemporal prior constraint is designed to preserve both fine-scale structures and long-term phenological trends during optimization. Extensive evaluations on MODIS NDVI data demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework across both artificial and real-world scenarios. In artificial degraded-pixel reconstruction experiments, GloSSR consistently outperforms the comparison methods. Time-series analyses based on real observations further demonstrate that the proposed framework can accurately characterize vegetation dynamics and capture the key phenological states. Long-term vegetation trend analysis and the transferability analysis to AVHRR data validate the scalability of the framework and illustrate its broad applicability for large-scale environmental monitoring.

AI.tldr: GloSSR is a self-supervised spatiotemporal deep learning framework for reconstructing cloud-contaminated and noise-corrupted NDVI time series at global scale, using artificially degraded training pairs and a bidirectional Transformer with ConvLSTM architecture.
AI.motivation: Accurate NDVI reconstruction is challenging, and deep learning methods are limited by the difficulty of obtaining paired clear-sky and degraded NDVI data at identical spatiotemporal locations.
AI.method: GloSSR constructs self-supervised training pairs by artificially degrading clean NDVI observations with realistic cloud patterns, then uses an end-to-end network combining bidirectional Transformer with ConvLSTM to capture long-range temporal and short-term spatiotemporal dependencies. A temporal-channel attention module enhances informative features, and a spatiotemporal prior constraint preserves fine-scale structures and phenological trends.
AI.result: Experiments on MODIS NDVI data show GloSSR outperforms comparison methods in artificial degraded-pixel reconstruction, accurately captures vegetation dynamics and phenological states in real observations, and demonstrates scalability and transferability to AVHRR data.
AI.conclusion: The framework delivers effective and scalable NDVI reconstruction for large-scale environmental monitoring, validated across both artificial and real-world scenarios.

title: Implicit Neural Representations for Multimodal Longitudinal Image Imputation and Interpolation
summary: Longitudinal multiparametric MRI is central to follow-up imaging in oncology, yet real-world clinical data are characterised by missing sequences, heterogeneous acquisition protocols, and varying spatial resolutions across time points. We propose a patient-specific conditional implicit neural representation (INR) that models multimodal longitudinal MRI as a continuous function of world coordinates, time, and modality conditioning. The model is trained with stochastic modality dropout to handle incomplete data, and its continuous coordinate-space formulation enables both spatial and temporal interpolation without resampling to a fixed voxel grid. A self-consistency-based confidence estimator is derived from cross-modal reconstruction performance at inference time. We evaluate the framework on longitudinal MRI from paediatric brain tumour patients, demonstrating statistically significant improvements over linear interpolation for T1CE and FLAIR (p < 0.05), with mean MS-SSIM of 0.95 $\pm$ 0.02 for T1CE. Predicted confidence correlates strongly with true reconstruction quality (Pearson r up to 0.996), suggesting reliable deployment potential in heterogeneous clinical settings.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a patient-specific conditional implicit neural representation (INR) that models longitudinal multiparametric MRI as a continuous function of world coordinates, time, and modality, enabling spatial and temporal interpolation of incomplete, heterogeneous clinical MRI data. It demonstrates significant improvements over linear interpolation on paediatric brain tumour data and introduces a self-consistency-based confidence estimator that correlates strongly with reconstruction quality.
AI.motivation: Real-world longitudinal multiparametric MRI in oncology suffers from missing sequences, heterogeneous acquisition protocols, and varying spatial resolutions across time points, making traditional approaches (which require fixed voxel grids and complete data) inadequate for clinical follow-up imaging.
AI.method: A patient-specific conditional INR models multimodal longitudinal MRI as a continuous function of world coordinates, time, and modality. Training uses stochastic modality dropout to handle incomplete data, and the continuous coordinate-space formulation allows spatial and temporal interpolation without resampling to a fixed grid. A self-consistency-based confidence estimator is derived from cross-modal reconstruction performance at inference.
AI.result: On longitudinal MRI from paediatric brain tumour patients, the method achieves statistically significant improvements over linear interpolation for T1CE and FLAIR (p < 0.05), with mean MS-SSIM of 0.95 ± 0.02 for T1CE. The predicted confidence correlates strongly with true reconstruction quality (Pearson r up to 0.996).
AI.conclusion: The framework demonstrates reliable deployment potential in heterogeneous clinical settings, offering a robust solution for longitudinal multiparametric MRI follow-up despite incomplete and heterogeneous real-world data.

title: Context-Aware Mixture of Domain Experts for Bodily Expression of Emotion in the Wild
comment: Submitted to "IEEE Transactions on Affective Computing"; 10 pages, 6 figures, 6 tables. To facilitate reproducibility, the PyTorch implementation of CA-MoDE is publicly available at https://github.com/dehshibi/CA-MoDE
summary: The same body posture can convey entirely different emotions depending on its surrounding context, yet most methods for recognising bodily emotions treat scene and object cues as auxiliary feature augmentations rather than as structured priors over the plausibility of emotions. We introduce the Context-Aware Mixture of Domain Experts (CA-MoDE) for bodily emotion recognition. CA-MoDE incorporates dedicated scene and object experts to generate soft distributions over emotion categories conditioned on their respective domains. These domain-conditioned soft predictions serve as structured contextual priors that modulate the body expert's predictions at the distributional level rather than at the feature level. To fuse these multi-domain signals, we propose a task-tailored max-endorsement gating strategy that selects the strongest contextual signal across experts for each emotion dimension. Our gating strategy mitigates the signal dilution that typically occurs when conflicting or uninformative context distributions are averaged. CA-MoDE achieves an Emotion Recognition Score of 0.3269 on the Body Language Database. By outperforming existing temporal models using only single still images, our framework demonstrates that explicitly modelling structured spatial context can serve as a complementary discriminative proxy for the behavioural dynamics typically captured by video.

AI.tldr: CA-MoDE is a context-aware framework for bodily emotion recognition that uses domain-specific experts (scene and object) to generate structured contextual priors over emotion categories, combined with a task-tailored max-endorsement gating strategy to modulate body expert predictions at the distributional level.
AI.motivation: Existing methods for bodily emotion recognition treat scene and object cues as auxiliary feature augmentations rather than structured priors over the plausibility of emotions, ignoring the fact that context fundamentally shapes how body postures are interpreted emotionally.
AI.method: CA-MoDE uses dedicated scene and object experts to produce soft distributions over emotion categories conditioned on their domains, which serve as structured contextual priors that modulate the body expert's predictions at the distributional level. A max-endorsement gating strategy selects the strongest contextual signal across experts for each emotion dimension to mitigate signal dilution from averaging conflicting or uninformative contexts.
AI.result: CA-MoDE achieves an Emotion Recognition Score of 0.3269 on the Body Language Database, outperforming existing temporal models using only single still images.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly modelling structured spatial context can serve as a complementary discriminative proxy for the behavioural dynamics typically captured by video, even when only static images are available.

title: Loop-Mamba: A Loop Mamba with Degradation-Aware and Shared Memory for Old Photo Restoration
summary: Old photographs often suffer from multiple coupled degradations, including scratches, cracks, fading, blur, noise, and missing regions, severely degrading both visual quality and semantic content. We propose Loop-Mamba, a lightweight loop-based state-space framework that formulates old photo restoration as progressive state evolution, where a persis- tent restoration state is continuously propagated and refined through iterative computation. Specifically, we introduce a Semantic-Guided Degradation Estimator (SGDE) to explicitly model heterogeneous degradations by jointly predicting local degradation maps and global degradation scores, providing degradation-aware guidance for state evolution. We further develop a Shared Structural Memory Mamba (S$^2$M- Mamba), which maintains a persistent restoration state across iterations, enabling persistent state evolution through shared structural memory for robust long-range structural reconstruction. Benefiting from first-order state recursion, Loop-Mamba propagates latent restoration states through recurrent tran- sitions instead of repeatedly stacking deep feature transformations, thereby alleviating gradient dilution while avoiding the computational overhead inherent in iterative CNN- and Transformer-based restoration frameworks. A lightweight multi-directional scanning strategy further enhances direc- tional information aggregation and preserves structural continuity. To better evaluate restoration quality, we introduce the task-oriented Old Photo Damage Recovery Score (ODRS), which jointly measures degradation recovery and structural reconstruction fidelity. Experimental results on the public SynOld benchmark demonstrate that Loop-Mamba consistently outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods across both conventional restoration metrics and the proposed ODRS.

AI.tldr: Loop-Mamba is a lightweight loop-based state-space framework for old photo restoration that treats restoration as progressive state evolution, using a Semantic-Guided Degradation Estimator (SGDE) and Shared Structural Memory Mamba (S2M-Mamba) to handle multiple coupled degradations, achieving SOTA results on the SynOld benchmark.
AI.motivation: Old photographs suffer from multiple coupled degradations (scratches, cracks, fading, blur, noise, missing regions) that severely degrade visual quality and semantic content. Existing iterative restoration frameworks based on CNN and Transformer architectures suffer from gradient dilution and high computational overhead.
AI.method: Loop-Mamba formulates old photo restoration as progressive state evolution with a persistent restoration state propagated through iterative computation. It introduces (1) SGDE to explicitly model heterogeneous degradations via local degradation maps and global degradation scores, and (2) S2M-Mamba which maintains persistent restoration state across iterations via shared structural memory. A lightweight multi-directional scanning strategy enhances directional information aggregation. It also proposes the task-oriented ODRS metric.
AI.result: On the public SynOld benchmark, Loop-Mamba consistently outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods across both conventional restoration metrics and the proposed ODRS metric.
AI.conclusion: By leveraging first-order state recursion with recurrent transitions instead of deep feature stacking, Loop-Mamba effectively alleviates gradient dilution and avoids computational overhead of iterative CNN/Transformer frameworks while achieving superior restoration quality on old photos.

title: GROVE: Growing and Reasoning over Temporally Stratified Memory from Streaming Video Experience
comment: 7 pages and 4 figures in the main paper
summary: A wearable assistant should both answer questions about its visual history and recognize when that history is useful to the present situation. Existing video-memory systems primarily support question-conditioned recall, whereas proactive assistants typically use separate memory and control mechanisms. We introduce GROVE, a training-free framework that supports both behaviors with one memory grown causally from a continuous video stream. GROVE retains fine-grained perceptual evidence and incrementally consolidates it into time-stamped moments, coherent episodes, and recurring cross-day patterns. Each stratum is paired with a scale-native retrieval skill for locating an observation, replaying an activity, or traversing long-range regularities. Reactive QA and proactive assistance share this memory and access interface, differing in whether retrieval is initiated by a user query or the current situation. Across multiple benchmarks including the challenging MM-lifelong and EgoServe, GROVE achieves the best results among the compared methods. Controlled ablations show that the temporal strata and their access skills are complementary, with patterns providing the largest benefit when evidence spans multiple days. Code will be available at https://github.com/SitongGong/GROVE.

AI.tldr: GROVE is a training-free framework for wearable assistants that builds a single causal memory from continuous video, supporting both reactive question answering and proactive assistance through multi-scale temporal strata (observations, episodes, patterns) each paired with native retrieval skills.
AI.motivation: Existing video-memory systems support only question-conditioned recall, while proactive assistants rely on separate memory and control mechanisms. The paper aims to unify reactive QA and proactive assistance in one coherent memory framework for wearable assistants.
AI.method: GROVE grows a causal memory from continuous video with three temporal strata: fine-grained perceptual evidence consolidated into time-stamped moments, coherent episodes, and recurring cross-day patterns. Each stratum has a scale-native retrieval skill—locating an observation, replaying an activity, or traversing long-range regularities. Reactive QA and proactive assistance share this memory and access interface, differing only in whether retrieval is triggered by a user query or the current situation.
AI.result: GROVE achieves the best results among compared methods across multiple benchmarks including MM-lifelong and EgoServe. Controlled ablations show the temporal strata and access skills are complementary, with the patterns stratum providing the largest benefit when evidence spans multiple days.
AI.conclusion: A unified hierarchical memory with scale-native retrieval can effectively support both reactive and proactive wearable assistance without training, and cross-day pattern consolidation is particularly valuable for long-horizon evidence.

title: Does Explainability Transfer? A Controlled Benchmark of Attribution Methods on Vision Transformers and CNNs
summary: Most evidence on the effectiveness of explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) attribution methods has been established on convolutional neural networks (CNNs), with limited investigation into whether these conclusions generalize to the diverse Vision Transformer (ViT) architectures that now dominate computer vision. This paper presents a controlled benchmark that evaluates attribution quality across five dimensions: faithfulness, localization, robustness, complexity, and computational cost. A standardized framework assesses 13 attribution methods from four algorithmic families on eight representative backbones spanning CNNs, isotropic ViTs, hierarchical transformers, hybrid architectures, and linear-attention transformers. The results show that attribution performance is strongly architecture-dependent and that rankings established on CNNs do not reliably transfer to transformer-based models. CAM-based methods achieve the highest scores under the conventional bounding-box localization metric on CNNs and most ViTs but perform poorly on linear-attention architectures. Pixel-level dense-mask evaluation further reveals that these gains largely reflect metric saturation rather than accurate localization. CAM-based methods also exhibit limited robustness on global-attention transformers, whereas attention rollout provides consistently stable explanations with poor localization. Furthermore, faithfulness correlation offers limited discrimination between attribution methods, highlighting the limitations of single-metric evaluation. These findings challenge prevailing conclusions on attribution performance and demonstrate the need for architecture-aware, multi-dimensional evaluation. The open-source code for the evaluation framework and benchmark results is available at https://github.com/Nishan-Charlie/VIT_XAI_Bench.

AI.tldr: A controlled benchmark evaluating 13 XAI attribution methods across 8 architectures (CNNs, ViTs, hybrid, linear-attention) reveals that attribution performance is strongly architecture-dependent, and CNN-established rankings do not transfer to transformer-based models.
AI.motivation: Most XAI evaluation evidence is based on CNNs, but Vision Transformers now dominate computer vision. It is unclear whether existing conclusions about attribution method effectiveness generalize to diverse ViT architectures.
AI.method: A standardized framework benchmarks 13 attribution methods from four algorithmic families on 8 backbones spanning CNNs, isotropic ViTs, hierarchical transformers, hybrid architectures, and linear-attention transformers, evaluated across five dimensions: faithfulness, localization, robustness, complexity, and computational cost.
AI.result: CAM-based methods score highest on bounding-box localization for CNNs and most ViTs but fail on linear-attention architectures. Pixel-level dense-mask evaluation shows these gains reflect metric saturation rather than accurate localization. CAM methods have limited robustness on global-attention transformers, while attention rollout offers stable but poorly localizing explanations. Faithfulness provides limited discrimination between methods.
AI.conclusion: Attribution performance conclusions established on CNNs do not reliably transfer to transformer architectures, challenging prevailing assumptions and demonstrating the need for architecture-aware, multi-dimensional evaluation of XAI methods.

title: USP-Mamba: Unmixing-Derived Spectral and Structural Prompting for Hyperspectral Image Super-Resolution
summary: Hyperspectral image super-resolution aims to reconstruct high-resolution imagery while preserving dense spectral information. Recently, Mamba-based models have shown promising potential for this task by capturing long-range dependencies with linear computational complexity. Nevertheless, their causal sequence modeling requires two-dimensional hyperspectral features to be unfolded along predefined scanning orders, which disrupts spatial adjacency and restricts the effective propagation of contextual information. Moreover, state-space parameterization of existing models is predominantly derived from generic learned representations, without explicit alignment with the intrinsic characteristics of the hyperspectral image. To address this issue, we propose an Unmixing-derived Spectral and Structural Prompting Mamba framework, termed USP-Mamba, which adapts Mamba state evolution through composition-aware spectral priors and image-dependent structural prompts. Specifically, an unmixing-informed spectral prompt captures the global material composition of the input image and provides persistent conditioning throughout reconstruction. Injected into the Mamba sequence and progressively adapted across layers, it steers state evolution toward composition-consistent reconstruction. We introduce feature-level structural prompts comprising spatial and frequency components to provide image-dependent local guidance. The spatial prompt promotes structure-sensitive state encoding for local detail preservation, while the frequency prompt enables region-adaptive transitions between homogeneous regions and high-frequency details. Finally, complementary Hilbert and Semantic-Guided Neighboring scans preserve spatial continuity and strengthen non-local semantic dependency modeling. Extensive experiments on different datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms representative approaches.

AI.tldr: USP-Mamba is an Unmixing-derived Spectral and Structural Prompting Mamba framework for hyperspectral image super-resolution. It addresses limitations of existing Mamba-based methods by using unmixing-informed spectral priors (capturing global material composition) and feature-level structural prompts (spatial and frequency components for local guidance), along with complementary Hilbert and Semantic-Guided Neighboring scans to preserve spatial continuity and semantic dependency.
AI.motivation: Existing Mamba-based hyperspectral super-resolution models have two key limitations: (1) causal sequence modeling requires unfolding 2D features along predefined scanning orders, which disrupts spatial adjacency and restricts contextual information propagation; (2) state-space parameters are derived from generic learned representations without explicit alignment with intrinsic hyperspectral image characteristics.
AI.method: The framework introduces: (1) an unmixing-informed spectral prompt capturing global material composition for persistent conditioning throughout reconstruction, steering state evolution toward composition-consistent results; (2) feature-level structural prompts with spatial components (structure-sensitive state encoding for local detail preservation) and frequency components (region-adaptive transitions between homogeneous regions and high-frequency details); (3) complementary Hilbert and Semantic-Guided Neighboring scans for spatial continuity and non-local semantic dependency modeling.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on different datasets demonstrate that USP-Mamba consistently outperforms representative approaches in hyperspectral image super-resolution.
AI.conclusion: By coupling unmixing-derived spectral priors with image-dependent structural prompts, and improving scanning strategies, the proposed method effectively adapts Mamba state evolution to the intrinsic characteristics of hyperspectral imagery, achieving state-of-the-art super-resolution performance.

title: Loggia dei Lanzi: AI Thermography Enhancement Comparisons through 3D Photogrammetry
comment: 19 pages, 10 figures, to be presented at the 8th International Symposium on Cultural Heritage Conservation by Digitization (CHCD2026) in Beijing
summary: The Loggia dei Lanzi in the Piazza della Signoria is one of Florence's most prominent structures visited by millions every year. Its construction history spans multiple centuries of modification. This paper presents the results of a thermal imaging campaign conducted in December 2025, using a FLIR T1020 HD camera, revealing hidden architectural features including walled-up openings and material transitions beneath the plaster surface. The favorable winter ambient conditions provided a feature-rich benchmark upon which to compare the results of enhancement algorithms and artificial intelligence models. We evaluate the application of AI-based image enhancement to thermal heritage documentation through a comparison of three tiers of image resolution in a photogrammetric Structure-from-Motion (SfM) pipeline: native resolution, FLIR's hardware-based pixel-shifted super-resolution (UltraMax), and state of the art AI-upscaled imagery models. We quantify the effect of each resolution tier on feature detection and tie-point generation, assessing whether the additional detail produced by super-resolution, whether hardware or AI-derived, translates into meaningfully denser and more accurate 3D thermal models. Our results contribute to the emerging intersection of artificial intelligence and heritage thermography by providing a direct comparison of hardware microscanning and AI super-resolution within a thermal photogrammetric workflow for cultural heritage. All datasets are made publicly available and accessible within an interactive 3D archival framework, and integrated into a custom citywide extended reality overlay application.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a thermal imaging campaign of Florence's Loggia dei Lanzi using a FLIR T1020 camera, revealing hidden architectural features beneath plaster. It compares three image resolution tiers (native, hardware-based UltraMax pixel-shifting, and AI upscaling) within a photogrammetric SfM pipeline, quantifying their impact on feature detection and 3D thermal model density/accuracy for heritage documentation.
AI.motivation: The Loggia dei Lanzi is a historically significant structure with a multi-century construction history, yet its hidden architectural features (walled-up openings, material transitions) remain undocumented. The authors aim to explore whether super-resolution techniques—both hardware and AI-derived—meaningfully improve thermal photogrammetric reconstruction for heritage documentation, addressing a gap at the intersection of AI and heritage thermography.
AI.method: A thermal imaging campaign was conducted in December 2025 using a FLIR T1020 HD camera under favorable winter ambient conditions. Three resolution tiers were compared in a photogrammetric Structure-from-Motion (SfM) pipeline: native resolution, FLIR's hardware-based pixel-shifted UltraMax super-resolution, and AI-based upscaling models. The effect on feature detection and tie-point generation was quantified for each tier.
AI.result: The campaign revealed hidden architectural features such as walled-up openings and material transitions beneath plaster. The study quantified differences in feature detection and tie-point density across the three resolution tiers, assessing whether super-resolution translates into denser and more accurate 3D thermal models. Datasets are publicly available and integrated into an interactive 3D archival framework and citywide extended reality overlay.
AI.conclusion: The paper contributes a direct comparison of hardware microscanning versus AI super-resolution within a thermal photogrammetric workflow for cultural heritage, providing empirical evidence on whether increased resolution meaningfully improves 3D thermal reconstruction outcomes. All data is publicly shared to support further research in AI-enhanced heritage thermography.

title: DF$^3$: World Modeling via Decoder-Free Feature Forecasting in Autonomous Navigation
summary: Forecasting future states from video sequences is a critical challenge for autonomous robotic systems and a fundamental objective of world modeling. Prior generative methods operating at the pixel level inevitably overemphasize task-irrelevant details, leading to prohibitive computational overhead. While latent-based approaches attempt to mitigate this by predicting features directly, the persistent reliance on heavy decoders for state-to-task mapping remains a computational bottleneck. In this work, we propose Decoder-Free Feature Forecasting (DF$^3$), a novel framework that models world evolution entirely within the latent space and directly derives task outputs, completely eliminating the need for a decoder. Specifically, DF$^3$ injects learnable spatial queries into the terminal blocks of a frozen vision foundation model to extract future state representations directly. By employing a lightweight, unified Motion-Aware Context Fusion (MACF) mechanism that seamlessly integrates coarse flow warping with fine-grained latent cross-correlation, these queries interact with historical token representations to explicitly align and forecast the feature of the next frame. Subsequently, a specialized set of task queries probes these forecasted features for the downstream task. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks and zero-shot deployment in a robotic simulator demonstrate that DF$^3$ achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods while offering superior efficiency and flexibility for integrated perception and control.

AI.tldr: DF³ proposes a decoder-free feature forecasting framework that models world evolution entirely in latent space, using spatial queries with a frozen vision foundation model and a Motion-Aware Context Fusion mechanism to directly derive task outputs without any decoder.
AI.motivation: Pixel-level generative forecasting methods overemphasize task-irrelevant details and incur prohibitive computational costs, while latent-based approaches still rely on heavy decoders for state-to-task mapping, creating a persistent computational bottleneck.
AI.method: DF³ injects learnable spatial queries into the terminal blocks of a frozen vision foundation model to extract future state representations directly in latent space. A lightweight Motion-Aware Context Fusion (MACF) mechanism combines coarse flow warping with fine-grained latent cross-correlation to align and forecast next-frame features. Task queries then probe the forecasted features for downstream tasks, eliminating decoders entirely.
AI.result: Experiments on public benchmarks and zero-shot deployment in a robotic simulator show DF³ achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods while offering superior efficiency and flexibility for integrated perception and control.
AI.conclusion: DF³ demonstrates that forecasting and task derivation can be performed entirely within latent space without decoders, achieving competitive performance with significantly improved computational efficiency.

title: Learning to Tessellate: Point Cloud Generation via Recursive Spectral Partitioning
comment: Accepted by ECCV2026, project page: https://huggingface.co/Mo-nan/PointRSP
summary: Autoregressive models have emerged as an effective paradigm for point cloud generation. However, most existing approaches rely on heuristic tokenization strategies, such as spatial sorting or stochastic downsampling, which often disrupt intrinsic point cloud topology and weaken the structural coherence of the generated shapes. In this paper, we present PointRSP, an autoregressive framework that reformulates point cloud generation as a topology-preserving tessellation process via recursive spectral partitioning. Instead of constructing token sequences heuristically, we introduce a topology-aware partitioning autoencoder that decomposes an unstructured point cloud into a non-balanced binary tree through a hybrid recursive spectral partitioning strategy. This hierarchical representation provides a deterministic geometric blueprint that preserves topological relationships while capturing multiscale structural dependencies within a quantized latent space. To synthesize shapes in this space, we propose a dual-stream cascaded generator that jointly models structural evolution and feature synthesis. In addition, we design a geometry-calibrated positional encoding mechanism that anchors latent embeddings using multi-scale structural centers, which stabilizes cascaded generation during the early stages of structural formation. Extensive experiments show that PointRSP achieves state-of-the-art performance in generation quality and diversity, demonstrating strong generalization across complex 3D topologies.

AI.tldr: PointRSP is an autoregressive point cloud generation framework that reformulates generation as a topology-preserving tessellation process via recursive spectral partitioning, using a topology-aware partitioning autoencoder and a dual-stream cascaded generator to achieve state-of-the-art generation quality and diversity.
AI.motivation: Existing autoregressive point cloud generation methods rely on heuristic tokenization strategies (e.g., spatial sorting or stochastic downsampling) that disrupt intrinsic point cloud topology and weaken structural coherence of generated shapes.
AI.method: PointRSP introduces: (1) a topology-aware partitioning autoencoder that decomposes point clouds into a non-balanced binary tree via hybrid recursive spectral partitioning, preserving topology in a quantized latent space; (2) a dual-stream cascaded generator that jointly models structural evolution and feature synthesis; (3) a geometry-calibrated positional encoding mechanism that anchors latent embeddings with multi-scale structural centers to stabilize cascaded generation.
AI.result: PointRSP achieves state-of-the-art performance in generation quality and diversity, with strong generalization across complex 3D topologies.
AI.conclusion: Topology-preserving tokenization via recursive spectral partitioning is a more effective paradigm than heuristic tokenization for autoregressive point cloud generation, improving structural coherence and generation performance.

title: InfiniSplat: Implicit Gaussian Decoding for Large-Baseline Monocular View Synthesis
comment: Accepted to SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 (Journal Track). Project page: https://zju3dv.github.io/InfiniSplat
summary: Single-image feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) aims to directly generate a renderable 3D scene representation from one input image, avoiding the cost of multi-view capture and per-scene optimization. However, existing methods are often constrained by a pixel-aligned representation, where Gaussians are predicted from fixed image-grid locations. Such pixel-aligned primitives can produce promising nearby-view renderings, but they remain weakly coupled to underlying scene surfaces and struggle to preserve coherent structures under large viewpoint shifts. We present InfiniSplat, a feed-forward single-image 3DGS framework that moves from a pixel-aligned representation toward a surface-aligned representation. InfiniSplat constructs this representation by first using geometry-guided sampling to place 2D supports according to depth-induced local surface structure, and then applying a query-conditioned implicit decoder to predict Gaussian attributes from the image features queried at these supports.By grounding support locations in geometry while decoupling Gaussian prediction from fixed pixel centers, InfiniSplat produces Gaussian layouts that better follow scene surfaces and reduce scattered primitives caused by grid discretization.Across multiple cross-dataset NVS evaluations, InfiniSplat achieves state-of-the-art performance compared with single-image feed-forward baselines, and demonstrates zero-shot generalization from Hypersim indoor synthetic training to complex open-world scenes.Project page: https://zju3dv.github.io/InfiniSplat.

AI.tldr: InfiniSplat is a feed-forward single-image 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that shifts from pixel-aligned to surface-aligned Gaussian representation, using geometry-guided sampling and a query-conditioned implicit decoder to achieve state-of-the-art novel view synthesis and zero-shot generalization.
AI.motivation: Existing single-image feed-forward 3DGS methods use pixel-aligned representations where Gaussians are predicted from fixed image-grid locations. These primitives are weakly coupled to scene surfaces and struggle to maintain coherent structures under large viewpoint shifts.
AI.method: InfiniSplat uses geometry-guided sampling to place 2D supports according to depth-induced local surface structure, then applies a query-conditioned implicit decoder to predict Gaussian attributes from image features queried at these supports, decoupling Gaussian prediction from pixel-grid locations.
AI.result: InfiniSplat achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple cross-dataset NVS evaluations compared with single-image feed-forward baselines, and demonstrates zero-shot generalization from Hypersim indoor synthetic training to complex open-world scenes.
AI.conclusion: By grounding support locations in geometry and decoupling Gaussian prediction from fixed pixel centers, InfiniSplat produces Gaussian layouts that better follow scene surfaces and reduce scattered primitives caused by grid discretization, enabling robust single-image 3D reconstruction and novel view synthesis.

title: UAV-Based Environmental Monitoring of Rip-Current Indicators Using Wavelet-Derived Texture Features
summary: Rip currents are recurrent coastal natural hazards that threaten beachgoers and create operational challenges for lifeguards and coastal managers. Reliable monitoring from standard RGB (red-green-blue) imagery acquired by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) remains difficult because hazardous channels often appear as subtle gaps in breaking waves, foam texture, or sediment patterns, and these signatures are affected by illumination, sea state, and environmental noise. This study presents a physically informed coastal environmental monitoring workflow for detecting visually expressed rip-current indicators that integrates wavelet-derived spatial-frequency texture features with deep learning. We evaluate multiple strategies for incorporating Discrete Wavelet Transform features into convolutional architectures, from computationally efficient channel replacement to dual-stream fusion with attention mechanisms. Performance is assessed against a standard RGB baseline using a task specific convolutional neural network for image-level presence classification and a YOLOv8 model for object-level localization. Under the evaluated dataset conditions, integrating wavelet derived texture features improves performance over RGB-only models. The dual-stream architecture achieves the strongest classification performance, exceeding 95% accuracy with high recall, while channel replacement is most effective for YOLOv8 object detection, reaching 94% mAP@50 for localization. Explainable artificial intelligence analyses provide qualitative evidence that the models attend to visually plausible wave-gap regions associated with rip currents. These results suggest that under the conditions of the evaluated dataset, physically informed wavelet integration may support UAV-based decision-support tools for interpretable beach-safety risk mitigation.

AI.tldr: This study presents a physically informed workflow for detecting rip-current indicators from UAV RGB imagery by integrating Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) texture features with deep learning models. Dual-stream fusion with attention achieves >95% classification accuracy, while channel replacement boosts YOLOv8 object detection to 94% mAP@50 for localizing rip-current zones.
AI.motivation: Rip currents are hazardous coastal phenomena that are difficult to reliably detect from standard UAV RGB imagery because their visual signatures (gaps in breaking waves, foam texture, sediment patterns) are subtle and heavily affected by illumination, sea state, and environmental noise. Reliable automated monitoring is needed for beach-safety risk mitigation.
AI.method: The authors integrate wavelet-derived spatial-frequency texture features (via Discrete Wavelet Transform) into convolutional architectures. They evaluate multiple integration strategies: (1) computationally efficient channel replacement, and (2) dual-stream fusion with attention mechanisms. They use a task-specific CNN for image-level presence classification and YOLOv8 for object-level localization, benchmarking against RGB-only baselines, with explainable AI for interpretability.
AI.result: Wavelet-derived texture features improve performance over RGB-only models. The dual-stream architecture achieves the strongest classification performance (>95% accuracy, high recall), while channel replacement is most effective for YOLOv8, reaching 94% mAP@50. XAI analyses confirm models attend to visually plausible wave-gap regions associated with rip currents.
AI.conclusion: Under the evaluated dataset conditions, physically informed wavelet integration can support UAV-based decision-support tools for interpretable beach-safety risk mitigation, offering a promising approach for operational rip-current monitoring.

title: MoRAL: Sensor-Grounded BEV Reasoning for Compact VLMs toward Edge-Oriented Autonomous Driving
comment: 7 pages, 5 figures, 6 tables. Accepted to the 14th IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Mobile Computing (IEEE IMC 2026), Fukuoka, Japan, July 27-30, 2026
summary: Deploying vision-language models (VLMs) for safety-critical spatial reasoning on resource-constrained autonomous driving platforms requires both compact model size and reliable metric grounding. We present MoRAL (Multimodal Reasoning for Autonomous Language Models), a two-stage fine-tuning pipeline that teaches Cosmos-Reason2-2B to first read a physics-encoded Bird's Eye View (BEV) representation and then reason over it for driving decisions. The BEV image encodes LiDAR metric distance as color bands, object class as cluster morphology, and radar Doppler velocity as directional wedge overlays, externalizing spatial perception into the input image so that no learned 3D backbone is required at inference. Stage 1 fine-tunes the vision encoder on 60,000 grounding records; zero-shot baselines produce no parseable BEV outputs, confirming the vocabulary requires explicit training. Stage 2 fine-tunes the full model (52M parameters, 2.4% of total) on 57,696 chain-of-thought records generated by Cosmos-Reason2-8B as teacher, spanning eight driving question types. On 2,304 held-out nuScenes frames evaluated by Gemma 4 (31B) calibrated against human review, MoRAL wins seven of eight question types over a zero-shot 8B baseline despite using four times fewer parameters, with the largest margins on question types requiring structured multi-step physics reasoning. Emergency braking recall improves from 10.8% to 47.8%, output degeneration falls from 94.1% to 20.8%, and the full pipeline fits a consumer 8 GB GPU at 42 tok/s without quantization. These results establish a reproducible foundation for compact, physics-grounded VLM reasoning on mobile edge platforms.

AI.tldr: MoRAL is a two-stage fine-tuning pipeline that teaches a compact 2B vision-language model to read physics-encoded Bird's Eye View (BEV) representations for driving decisions, achieving superior spatial reasoning on nuScenes benchmarks with 4x fewer parameters than an 8B baseline while running on a consumer 8 GB GPU.
AI.motivation: Deploying VLMs for safety-critical spatial reasoning on resource-constrained autonomous driving platforms requires both compact model size and reliable metric grounding, which existing large-scale VLMs fail to provide.
AI.method: A two-stage fine-tuning pipeline: (1) fine-tunes the vision encoder on 60,000 grounding records to teach it to parse physics-encoded BEV images (LiDAR distance as color, object class as cluster morphology, radar Doppler as wedge overlays); (2) fine-tunes the full model (52M parameters) on 57,696 chain-of-thought records generated by an 8B teacher model across eight driving question types.
AI.result: MoRAL wins seven of eight question types over a zero-shot 8B baseline despite 4x fewer parameters; emergency braking recall improves from 10.8% to 47.8%, output degeneration drops from 94.1% to 20.8%, and the pipeline runs at 42 tok/s on a consumer 8 GB GPU without quantization.
AI.conclusion: MoRAL establishes a reproducible foundation for compact, physics-grounded VLM reasoning on mobile edge platforms by externalizing spatial perception into the input image rather than relying on learned 3D backbones.

title: ISRS-DETR: Detection-Guided Click Propagation for Remote Sensing Interactive Segmentation
summary: Interactive segmentation reduces the prohibitive cost of pixel-level annotation by allowing users to delineate objects with a few clicks. However, applying this paradigm directly to remote sensing imagery is non-trivial: ultra-high resolutions, small object sizes, and sparse spatial distributions all degrade segmentation quality. Recent work has addressed the resolution barrier and achieved competitive results in interactive segmentation for remote sensing (ISRS). However, they treat all instances of a class within an image as a single objective target. Consequently, interactions spent on one object contribute nothing to its same-class neighbours, and satisfactory masks may demand up to 40 clicks per image, hindering the practicality of these frameworks. We observe that remote sensing scenes exhibit markedly strong inter-object correlation, meaning a single clicked object is highly informative about the rest of its category. Building on this, we propose ISRS-DETR, a detection-guided interactive segmentation framework that injects object-level evidence into both training and inference. Our ISRS-DETR employs an RF-DETR decoder with the interactive segmentation backbone to localise co-occurring same-class objects, and introduces a Dynamic Top-K Click Selection strategy that retains only reliable proposals and converts each into a simulated click, so one user interaction propagates across an entire class. Experiments on three standard remote sensing benchmarks show that ISRS-DETR achieves state-of-the-art accuracy while substantially reducing Number of Clicks per Image (NoC-I). All codes and data splits will be released for reproducibility upon acceptance.

AI.tldr: ISRS-DETR is a detection-guided interactive segmentation framework for remote sensing that leverages inter-object correlation to propagate a single user click across an entire object class, reducing the number of clicks needed while achieving state-of-the-art accuracy.
AI.motivation: Current interactive segmentation methods for remote sensing treat all instances of a class as a single target, so interactions on one object don't help segment its same-class neighbors, requiring up to 40 clicks per image. The authors observe that remote sensing scenes exhibit strong inter-object correlation that can be exploited to reduce this burden.
AI.method: ISRS-DETR uses an RF-DETR decoder with an interactive segmentation backbone to localize co-occurring same-class objects. It introduces a Dynamic Top-K Click Selection strategy that retains only reliable object proposals and converts each into a simulated click, enabling one user interaction to propagate across an entire class during both training and inference.
AI.result: Experiments on three standard remote sensing benchmarks show ISRS-DETR achieves state-of-the-art accuracy while substantially reducing the Number of Clicks per Image (NoC-I).
AI.conclusion: The proposed detection-guided approach effectively addresses the efficiency bottleneck of interactive segmentation in remote sensing by exploiting inter-object correlation, improving practicality of the framework.

title: Calibrated Similarity and Graph Clustering for Open-Set Animal Re-Identification
summary: AnimalCLEF26 addresses discovery-oriented animal re-identification, where systems must both attach query images to known individuals and discover unseen individuals by clustering them correctly. We present a similarity-to-clustering pipeline for this setting across Eurasian lynx, fire salamander, loggerhead sea turtle, and Texas horned lizard images. The method first isolates the target specimen using segmentation and then applies lightweight species-specific preprocessing for lynx, sea turtle, and salamander images to enhance identity-relevant visual cues, while Texas horned lizard images are used after segmentation only. Pairwise similarities are then estimated with WildFusion by calibrating and combining a MiewID global descriptor with two local matching branches, ALIKED + LightGlue and DISK + LightGlue. The resulting query-query similarities are refined and converted into identity clusters using graph-based clustering, while query-database similarities are used to attach confident samples to known identities. We evaluate training-free and fine-tuned MiewID variants, including Dynamic ArcFace and SphereFace2-Focal adaptations, and combine them in the final ensemble. Our selected ensemble substantially improves on the WildFusion baseline, achieving the best public ARI of 0.72124 and a private ARI of 0.70393, while a simpler preprocessing-before-calibration variant achieves the best private ARI of 0.71087. These results indicate that calibrated global-local fusion with species-aware preprocessing choices is effective for open-set wildlife re-identification under challenging field conditions and visual variation. The implementation code is available on GitHub.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a similarity-to-clustering pipeline for open-set animal re-identification across four species (Eurasian lynx, fire salamander, loggerhead sea turtle, Texas horned lizard), using segmentation, species-specific preprocessing, calibrated global-local feature fusion (WildFusion with MiewID global descriptor and ALIKED/DISK+LightGlue local branches), and graph-based clustering. The method achieves the best public ARI of 0.72124 and private ARI of 0.70393, substantially improving over the WildFusion baseline.
AI.motivation: AnimalCLEF26 requires systems to both identify known individuals and discover unseen individuals via clustering, which is challenging in open-set wildlife re-identification due to visual variation and field conditions. The authors aim to effectively combine global descriptors with local matching and species-aware preprocessing to handle this dual discovery and identification task.
AI.method: The pipeline comprises: (1) segmentation to isolate the target specimen, (2) species-specific lightweight preprocessing for lynx, sea turtle, and salamander images (horned lizard images use segmentation only), (3) pairwise similarity estimation via WildFusion, combining a MiewID global descriptor with two local matching branches (ALIKED+LightGlue and DISK+LightGlue), (4) calibrated query-query similarity refinement followed by graph-based clustering for unseen individual discovery, and (5) query-database similarity for attaching confident samples to known identities. Both training-free and fine-tuned MiewID variants (Dynamic ArcFace and SphereFace2-Focal) are evaluated and ensembled.
AI.result: The selected ensemble achieves the best public ARI of 0.72124 and private ARI of 0.70393, substantially improving on the WildFusion baseline. A simpler preprocessing-before-calibration variant achieves the best private ARI of 0.71087.
AI.conclusion: Calibrated global-local fusion combined with species-aware preprocessing choices is effective for open-set wildlife re-identification under challenging field conditions and high visual variation. The implementation is open-sourced on GitHub.

title: Grounding Agentic VLMs with Dedicated Segmentation for Fine-Grained Vehicle Damage Assessment
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly deployed as reasoning agents in real-world visual assessment pipelines, yet their spatial grounding remains unreliable for fine-grained, visually ambiguous targets. We study this gap in the context of automated vehicle damage assessment, where fine-grained defects such as scratches and hairline cracks occupy few pixels, produce weak gradient signal, and are easily confused with reflections and surface texture. We show that a state-of-the-art VLM (Qwen-VL) achieves strong semantic classification accuracy (87.3%) on this task but is systematically ungrounded at the spatial level: it hallucinates damage in reflective regions, misses elongated scratches entirely, and produces spatially inconsistent outputs when prompted for localization. We propose TinyDamage, a hybrid architecture that delegates spatial grounding to a dedicated multi-task segmentation model while reserving the VLM for semantic reasoning and report generation. On the segmentation side, we find that the choice of loss function has an outsized and underexplored effect on tiny-object grounding: focal loss, widely used for class imbalance, collapses tiny-damage detection to zero, while a supervised contrastive objective measurably improves damage/background separability. We integrate the segmentation model into a 7-node LangGraph agent pipeline that grounds every VLM generation step in the segmentation output, and show that this grounding reduces the report hallucination rate from 92% (text-only) and 78% (image-only) to 31% in a controlled evaluation on 100 human-verified reports. We introduce DET_l, a permissive per-category detection metric for evaluating tiny-object grounding under class imbalance, and report latency and reliability characteristics of the deployed pipeline.

AI.tldr: VLMs (e.g., Qwen-VL) achieve high semantic accuracy but poor spatial grounding on tiny visual targets like vehicle damage. The authors propose TinyDamage, a hybrid architecture combining a multi-task segmentation model (with supervised contrastive learning) for spatial grounding and a VLM for semantic reasoning, integrated via a 7-node LangGraph pipeline. This reduces report hallucination from 92%/78% to 31% and introduces DET_l, a per-category detection metric.
AI.motivation: VLMs deployed in visual assessment pipelines have unreliable spatial grounding for fine-grained, visually ambiguous targets. In vehicle damage assessment, tiny defects (scratches, hairline cracks) occupy few pixels, produce weak gradients, and are confused with reflections and surface texture, leading to systematic spatial hallucinations and inconsistent localization.
AI.method: Proposes TinyDamage, a hybrid architecture that separates concerns: a dedicated multi-task segmentation model handles spatial grounding while the VLM handles semantic reasoning and report generation. Key findings include that focal loss collapses tiny-damage detection to zero, while a supervised contrastive objective improves damage/background separability. The segmentation model is integrated into a 7-node LangGraph agent pipeline that grounds every VLM generation step, and a new metric DET_l is introduced for per-category tiny-object detection under class imbalance.
AI.result: Qwen-VL achieves 87.3% semantic classification accuracy but is systematically ungrounded spatially (hallucinates in reflective regions, misses elongated scratches, inconsistent localization outputs). The hybrid pipeline reduces report hallucination rate from 92% (text-only) and 78% (image-only) to 31% on 100 human-verified reports, with latency and reliability characteristics reported.
AI.conclusion: Spatial grounding should be delegated to dedicated segmentation models rather than expected from VLMs for tiny-object tasks. Loss function choice is critical for tiny-object segmentation (contrastive > focal), and grounding every VLM generation step in segmentation output substantially reduces hallucination in automated visual assessment pipelines.

title: Action-grounded tissue affordance enables anticipatory auto-framing that lowers surgeon cognitive workload during laparoscopic surgery
comment: Preprint. 54 pages, including supplementary information and 7 main figures
summary: Computational attention models could help surgeons manage the visual demands of laparoscopy, but they require dense spatial labels that are difficult to obtain because surgical intent is highly specialized and tacit. Here, we introduce DiffeoAfford, an action-grounded tissue affordance framework that retrospectively derives visual attention supervision from completed surgical procedures. By combining diffeomorphism-constrained tissue tracking with instrument trajectory analysis, DiffeoAfford generates affordance hotspot labels without manual per-frame annotation. A real-time prediction model trained on these labels anticipates relevant surgical regions and enables AffordView, an assistive auto-framing system for laparoscopic visualization. The proposed framework aligns with expert annotations and intraoperative surgeon gaze, and reduces surgeon cognitive workload during real-world evaluations using subjective, physiological, and behavioral measures.

AI.tldr: DiffeoAfford is a framework that automatically generates visual attention supervision labels for surgical laparoscopy by retrospectively analyzing completed procedures using diffeomorphism-constrained tissue tracking and instrument trajectories, eliminating the need for manual annotation. It powers AffordView, an assistive auto-framing system that reduces surgeon cognitive workload.
AI.motivation: Computational attention models could help surgeons manage visual demands during laparoscopy, but training them requires dense spatial labels that are extremely difficult to obtain because surgical intent is highly specialized and tacit knowledge, making manual annotation impractical.
AI.method: DiffeoAfford combines diffeomorphism-constrained tissue tracking with instrument trajectory analysis on completed surgical procedures to retrospectively generate affordance hotspot labels without manual per-frame annotation. These labels train a real-time prediction model that powers AffordView, an assistive auto-framing system for laparoscopic visualization.
AI.result: The framework aligns with expert annotations and intraoperative surgeon gaze, and reduces surgeon cognitive workload during real-world evaluations measured through subjective, physiological, and behavioral metrics.
AI.conclusion: Action-grounded tissue affordance labels derived from completed procedures can serve as effective supervision for surgical attention models, enabling practical assistive systems that improve surgical visualization and reduce cognitive burden.

title: EchoCache: Energy-Guided Cross-Modal Caching for Efficient Audio-Driven Video Generation
comment: EchoCache is honored to be accepted by ACM MM 2026
summary: Audio-driven video generation (A2V) has achieved promising progress in synthesizing temporally coherent and audio-visually aligned videos, yet its inference remains expensive due to the iterative denoising process of diffusion models. Existing caching methods mainly exploit temporal redundancy in visual features while overlooking the cross-modal alignment of A2V, where audio drives visual generation with highly non-uniform temporal importance. In this paper, we identify two levels of misalignment in existing A2V caching methods: temporal-semantic and computation-storage misalignment. To address them, we propose EchoCache, an energy-guided cross-modal caching framework for efficient A2V generation.
